Las letras pueden imprimirse de varias formas, aunque recomiendo imprimirlas en posición vertical. De esta manera se conserva mejor el efecto volumétrico del diseño y se obtiene una superficie más limpia. Para garantizar una buena adhesión a la base, especialmente si se imprimen varias letras a la vez, es recomendable utilizar un brim amplio. Las letras mostradas en las fotografías se han impreso con filamento tricolor. Si utilizas este tipo de material, conviene prestar atención a la orientación de cada pieza, ya que el ángulo de impresión influirá directamente en la distribución de los colores y en el resultado final. Para obtener el mejor acabado posible, recomiendo utilizar una altura de capa reducida o, preferiblemente, altura de capa variable. El efecto globo se basa en superficies curvas y transiciones suaves que pierden definición cuando se utilizan capas demasiado gruesas. También es posible imprimir las letras en horizontal, pero en ese caso es especialmente importante utilizar una altura de capa muy fina o altura de capa variable para mantener el aspecto redondeado y evitar que se pierda parte del efecto característico del diseño. description: Edit 7/14/2026** Now Also check out “Big Chap” in a huge, detailed print!: https://makerworld.com/en/models/3052357-big-chap-alien-detailed-xenomorph-statue#profileId-3433924 Xenomorph (Alien) Ultra Detailed Display This one is by far one of my largest, and definitely the most detailed model that I've worked on to date.. This is an Ultra Detailed Xenomorph statue that stands 19 inches (48cm) tall in the largest form! This statue pulls inspiration from the unbelievably awesome Sideshow Collectibles Vinyl model, which if you are familiar with their models, are next level in detail.. but next to impossible to get! There are 2 size profiles being made available at the time of the model upload - 19" tall version as well as a 10" tall version. Please note that the 19" tall version is printed in pieces, and is maximized in size to fit the P/X series printer beds. The 10" tall version is printed a simplified one-piece print. I should know that I have printed 6 different size variants and will note that you can easily scale this between 10" and 19" tall models. **Please be aware that the print times are lengthy. I had 4 machines running test prints none stop. I promise though, it is worth it at the end. **Please also be aware that the model images you see are 100% real, with 0 use of AI, but they have been post-process colored using some Rub'n Buff waxes, along with some gloss clear coat layer application at the end. ASSEMBLY REQUIRED ** The 19" tall, multipiece print will require some glue. I have used both super glue, as well as hot glue. Hot glue was my preference. With all the parts printed, and supports cleaned up (TAKE YOUR TIME REMOVING THE SUPPORTS AS THE PARTS ARE HIGHLY DETAILED AND FRAGILE ) do a dry-fit of all the parts to ensure proper fitment. You may need to file down some pieces if they do not fit. All 4 of my models went together with no issues, but different printers/filaments may have some tolerance issues. Assembly is very straightfoward, with the exception of the tail. DO NOT mount the tail to the model until the Xenomoprh is placed onto the base display. The tail loops around the display and needs to be installed afterwards. Install the tail by turning is 90 degrees and carefully looping the tip around the back of the base and then gently rotating it up into the reciever cutout on he back of the xenomorph (Yes, it looks like a butt ). With the Dry fitting completed, if you are satisfied with the fitment you can take the piees apart and proceed to glue them together. As with the above test-fit process, you can assemble everything together, just leave the tail to the end. If you are planning to paint/apply color to the model I highly advise doing so with Xenomorph OFF of the base. For final assembly, apply some glue to the foot mounting peg as well as some glue to the toes of the left foot (there is no peg here) and firmly place the model on to the base. Proceed with snaking the tail into position, and then apply some glue onto the peg of the base of the tail. There is a small mounting support for the tail at the back of the base that also requires a small application of glue to help it from bouncing around with the model fully assembled. COLOR APPLICATION I used a very straightforward process for my coloring via application of some Rub'n Buff Antique Gold wax for the Xenomorph, and Brass color for the base. Wear gloves and apply the wax to a towel and gently go over the details. Avoid pressing really hard so that the void remain black/dark, this helps with final contrast of the model. As you can tell from these two photos the difference between the plain model and the colored one is pretty phenomenal and I HIGHLY recommend going through the effort!

EDIT 2026/07/10 Please note that this is not your everyday casual 3D print! If interested in printing, read everything below! It requires some experience and I advise everyone to think everything through before blindly starting to print. Post-processing is needed after assembling. Read through my description below! It will take roughly 12-15kg of filament and probably several months of work including post-processing, painting and adding details. The parts are without infill and without top- and bottom layers. 6 wall loops. Adjust the parameters to your liking, also depending on your choice of post-processing! With this update, I tweaked the print profiles by adding a few more modifiers. They are placed in rather flat areas and have the top layers re-enabled so these areas turn out more smooth. - - - - - Yes, I’m insane. Regular-sized figures and statues just aren’t my thing - So I modelled Batman from scratch and printed him…life sized. After printing, assembling and painting, I gave him a batcape, glass eyes, metal screwhead details and a glossy surface finish for his metal parts. I modelled him after the design in the arkham origins game because I think this is one of the sickest batsuit designs. Who agrees? If you happen to be equally crazy as I am and to actually download and print your own life-sized statue, here’s a few additional information: Print overview Batman himself consists of 40 parts which can be printed on every Bambu printer except for the A1 mini. His accessories on the belt as well as the batarang add another 11 parts making it a total of 51 parts. To identify each part, I created a general overview below. You can identify each part in the print profiles too - I named the print bed labels and the parts on it according to the overview. Because Bambu Studio won’t let me create more than 36 plates, I divided the parts into “Lower body”, “Torso & Head” and “Shoulders, arms & Accessories”. Each print profile has its own overview with the parts it contains. Assembling, Post-processing For assembling, there’s no connectors, screw holes or anything like that - Like a typical cosplay prop, the print itself just serves as the base and is then further refined, making the seams invisible and giving it a nice finish which will also hold everything together properly. I used a heated sculpting tool called Modifi3D to melt the seams together, which added a lot of strength already while also making the seams barely noticeable. And from this point on, it’s entirely up to you how far you want to take the surface finishing process. I coated everything in fiberglass which was a sh!tload of work but it really paid off in terms of both durability and appearance. And because there’s so many different ways, techniques and methods for the entire post-process, there’s no right or wrong when it comes to slicing and printing. I printed everything without infill and without top- or bottom surface (with a few exceptions), leaving the parts hollow, made of 6 wall loops. Sort of a vase mode. Adjust the parameters to your liking. Really curious to see if there’s ANYONE who will actually go for this project. And if so, I need pictures! Este diseño de mariposa está pensado para ser una pieza versátil que puede servir como una delicada decoración o como un marcapáginas único. El modelo está diseñado específicamente para ser impreso directamente sobre tela de tul, lo que le otorga un fondo transparente y una textura muy especial. Instrucciones de Impresión (Técnica sobre tela) Para lograr que la mariposa quede adherida a la tela, es necesario seguir un proceso de impresión con pausa. Aquí están los pasos clave: Pausa programada: El archivo de impresión debe configurarse en el laminador (slicer) para que genere una pausa automática exactamente al terminar la primera capa . Colocación de la tela: Durante esta pausa, el cabezal se apartará. Es el momento de colocar la tela de tul estirada sobre la cama de impresión, justo por encima de la capa base que se acaba de imprimir. Fijación con imanes: Para evitar que el cabezal arrastre la tela o se formen arrugas, utiliza imanes en los bordes para fijar el tul firmemente a la base metálica de la impresora. Asegúrate de que los imanes queden fuera de la trayectoria del extrusor. Reanudación de la impresión: Una vez que la tela esté tensa y asegurada, reanuda la impresión. El plástico de las siguientes capas se fundirá a través de los agujeros de la malla del tul, encapsulando la tela y uniendo el diseño de forma permanente.

model_name: Mecha Pokemon Series — Beedrill Hyper-Real Statue
description: Mecha Pokémon Statue Series — Mecha Beedrill Hyper-Real Steel Sculpture 1. Concept & Design This sculpture reinterprets the iconic, lethal airborne assassin through the lens of heavy mechanical re-forging (Mecha Reforge). As the newest chapter of our "Mecha Pokémon Series," we turn our focus to the legendary high-speed apex predator of the Kanto region— Beedrill . This creation reimagines Beedrill’s aggressive biological silhouette into a heavy armored exoskeleton statue brimming with industrial rigidity. The design transforms its naturally lightweight abdomen and segments into layered, curved armor plates packed with dense mechanical panel lines, exuding immense physical mass and weaponized tension within a static warrior pose. Structurally, due to Beedrill's defining biological trait of having extremely small feet , achieving balance in large-scale monolithic FDM printing posed a significant challenge. To counter this, we engineered the right arm to drive its massive lance directly into the ground , establishing a rock-solid triangular base. However, this required a compromise: visually, it looks as though half of Beedrill's iconic twin stingers are missing. To fix this, we included an extra loose lance accessory just for you guys ! This bonus lance gives you complete display freedom—you can hang it on the raised left hand to create a gripping effect, holding it facing forward or backward. (Note: If you wish to completely lift it overhead, you will need to utilize an aftermarket action figure display stand for support). Of course, you can also get creative and print multiple extra lances to scatter around him, replicating an epic "infinite weapon arsenal" scene from certain anime series (lol). 2. Engineering & Printability The statue is highly optimized for large-scale FDM stability, prioritizing ballast physics and center-of-gravity compensation over part articulation: Support Removal & Structural Integrity: The primary printing hurdle with this model is that the supports beneath both arms are somewhat tricky to remove , requiring patience. On the flip side, the supports for the wings detach very easily. However, because the joint area connecting the wings to the main body is quite small , please handle them with care during cleanup so you don't accidentally snap the entire wing section off. The remaining parts should be smooth sailing for experienced makers. Minor Artifact Correction: If your print suffers from a slightly warped or misaligned pinky finger on the left hand , there's no need to scrap the print. Simply use a heat gun to gently soften the plastic, realign it, and secure it with a drop of glue. Geometric Shadow Readability: At 0.2 mm layer heights, the mechanical compound eyes, the layered armor on the torso, and the sweeping taper of the giant lances catch ambient light perfectly, throwing deep dual-density shadows that eliminate the absolute need for immediate painting. 3. Display & Customization With its sweeping, aggressive wingspan, Mecha Beedrill naturally commands a premium presence when staged inside industrial mecha bays, barren desert ruins, or post-apocalyptic military outposts. For advanced miniature painters and makers, the model offers limitless creative room for custom finishing: The expansive metal surfaces are perfectly suited for heavy weathering, grease-staining, and metallic edge dry-brushing. The deep recesses between the armor plates and the main lances are ideal for dropping high-contrast vivid hive-amber or neon toxic-green paints to simulate a lethal weapon system charging up. By printing several extra copies of the lance and staking them into a custom clay or foam terrain base, you can flawlessly recreate a "Gate of Babylon" styled boundless armory effect that dramatically elevates the visual impact. Whether positioned as a standalone desk centerpiece or integrated into a sci-fi diorama, its silhouette delivers superb stylized plausibility from every angle. 4. Conclusion The Hyper-Real Mecha Beedrill statue stands as a definitive showcase piece, proving that high collectible impact isn't born from moving parts, but from raw sculptural presence. It transforms a childhood memory into tangible awe—blending menace, mass, and sharp industrial geometry into an essential collector’s centerpiece that completely dominates the space it commands. Quick Tips: Avoid using photography/timelapse travel modes for this print to minimize stringing or failure risks around the delicate antennae and sweeping wing overhangs. Crucial Warning: If you plan on using a mini-torch or a heat gun to clear stringing and print residue from the wings, remember that the wings are extremely thin—please exercise extreme caution ! To prevent the thin geometry from softening and warping instantly upon heating, it is highly recommended to steady the wing with one hand while keeping the heat source moving rapidly. My absolute go-to filament for reading these industrial mechanical details remains the Bambu Lab gray series . When removing tight supports from beneath the arms, needle-nose pliers combined with Bambu’s FAC002-N scraper will be your ultimate soulmates.

description: 🍬 Big Mom - Charlotte Linlin - Whole Cake Island Statue "Life or Treat! There is no one in this world who can stop me when I crave sweets!" Bring the terrifying and magnificent presence of the Yonko Charlotte Linlin , famously known as Big Mom , to your One Piece collection. Captured during the Whole Cake Island arc, this detailed statue features Big Mom in her most iconic attire—her polka-dot dress, pirate hat (Napoleon the Homie), and holding the Homie umbrella in her hand. She stands on a detailed rocky base littered with treasure and debris. Standing at a substantial 130mm tall , this figure is a premium display piece that showcases her massive presence and dynamic design. 📐 Print Specs & Geometry Advantages Total Height: 130mm (13cm) (A significant scale to match her Yonko status). Layer Height: 0.16mm (Optimized for perfect surface texture definitions, hiding layer lines effectively across her elaborate dress and hair). 🧠 Advanced Slicer Engineering (Exclusive 3MF Profile): Due to Big Mom's top-heavy design and tiny contact points (her heels), the provided .3mf file is heavily optimized with embedded modifier primitives. These modifiers increase infill density and wall counts in critical anchoring zones, particularly around the ankles and heels, ensuring structural stability without wasting material on the body. 🛠️ Support Removal & Critical Cleanup Guide 🧹 CLEANUP NOTE: This model has very specific support requirements. A patient, experienced hand is required, and the file provided is optimized to help with this. Expect a meticulous cleanup. 🌂 The Homie Umbrella (High Caution Zone): The umbrella is extremely delicate. The supports in this area are optimized, but proceed with maximum caution. Cleanup Strategy: Snip the support interface points underneath the umbrella dome with fine flush cutters. Note: If the handle snaps, it can be reincollated cleanly, as with my test print, but work slowly to avoid it. 🎩 The Hat Pennant & Hair: The decorative pennant (ribbon detail) on the side of Napoleon the hat is close to her hair. A tree support pillar will be trapped in this gap. Cleanup Strategy: Use pliers to gently twist the support pillar away from the hair, not the hat. The pennant is thin and may feel unstable until it is fully cured and glued, if necessary. 👗 Under-Robe Cavity (Legs & heels Risk): This is the most complex support area. Due to the tiny contact points (heels), the base is integrated with the body for stability. Cleanup Strategy: Work from underneath the scenic base. Use a standard metal hook or scraper, insert it through the base cavity underneath the skirt, and apply gentle downward leverage. Take extreme care near the ankles and tiny heels. description: Stormwing – Windswept Owl Sculpture The idea behind Stormwing came from my fascination with driftwood sculptures and how nature and time shape everything they touch. I wanted a model that looks like raw power and motion, which lead to this windswept owl—an animal pushing forward while almost getting torn apart. The current height of the sculpture is ~ 16 cm (~6.3 in) in height. I would not print it smaller as the thin edges would become rather thin and increase the risk of not forming as it should. For the easiest support removal, keep the model in the provided vertical position. This helps reduce the amount of support required and makes the supports as manageable as possible to remove. Printing Use a clean print plate with some glue (unless you are using a super tack plate) Use dried out filament (Different filament and printers impacts the print differently, please adjust your settings accordingly.) Keep the model in the provided vertical position Support Removal Instructions Allow the print to cool completely before removing it from the build plate. Use small flush cutters, needle-nose pliers, and tweezers to remove the support branches in smaller pieces. Support removal will take a little bit of time. Patience and careful handling are important for protecting the thin driftwood details. Be especially careful around the talons of the owl. Start by removing the larger support sections around the base and outside edges. Break the smaller branches into smaller sections and alternate around each supported section as needed. I needed to alternate between the front and backside as some of the support was built up from both sides for the same section. After removing the supports, clean up potential rough contact points with a precision knife, small file, or fine-grit sandpaper if needed. Light sanding and gentle, controlled heat may be needed to clean up areas where the supports were attached. I used a handheld mini torch, but apply heat carefully to avoid warping or damaging the print. Wood PLA is very sensitive to heat! Cookie Monster Godzilla "Cookie Blast" Edition "Cookie...zilla breathes cookies!" What happens when Cookie Monster Godzilla unleashes his ultimate attack? You get the Cookie Monster Godzilla "Cookie Blast" Edition! Instead of a traditional monster breath attack, this version features Cookie Monster Godzilla standing on a detailed base while blasting a stream of cookie dough from his mouth. Some might call it a cookie-powered attack... others might say it looks like he's having a bit of a cookie-related incident. Either way, it's a hilarious and unique addition to any monster, cookie, or 3D printing collection. The model includes a custom base designed to add stability, along with a detailed flowing "cookie flame" effect that gives this version a completely different look from the original Cookie Monster Godzilla Duck. Design Process This model was created using a hybrid workflow of AI-assisted generation and traditional 3D modeling. I began with an original mashup concept, then used AI-assisted tools to explore different forms and proportions. After selecting the strongest base design, I refined the model to improve the details, clean up geometry, and optimize it for reliable FDM printing. Print Settings Layer Height: 0.20 mm Infill: 15% Gyroid Supports: Tree Supports (required) AMS Required: Yes Base Modifier A modifier is included that increases part of the base to 30% infill . This adds extra weight to the bottom of the print and helps prevent the model from becoming top-heavy and tipping over. Color Changes This print uses 6 colors and requires two pauses for filament swaps . The pauses are already in the file, but be sure to check that after slicing. If you change the size for a larger or smaller printer, you'll need to change the pauses. Layer 350: Swap Gray for Light Brown Layer 949: Swap Black for Dark Brown Filaments Used Anycubic PLA+ Black Anycubic PLA+ White Kingroon Blue PLA Kingroon Light Brown PLA Elegoo PLA+ Gray Sunlu PLA+ Coffee Brown Post-Processing Notes Support removal on this model can be a little challenging. The area underneath the tail can be difficult to access when removing supports, so take your time and be careful. The cookie drips at the very top of the "cookie fire" effect are also extremely delicate and can break during cleanup. I broke a few of mine during testing, but thankfully they were fairly easy to repair. Small pieces can usually be reattached with glue or bonded back together by carefully heating the plastic. If one of the cookie drips breaks off and you don't want to repair it, remember... it's a melting cookie! You can carefully heat the broken end slightly to soften it and let it resolidify into a natural-looking melted edge. The entire cookie flame effect is fairly fragile, so handle it carefully after printing. Notes for Future Versions I may create a larger version of this model in the future that separates at least part of the cookie flame effect into an assembly piece. This would make the effect more durable while also allowing for an even larger and more detailed version. Print Testing I always print my models before releasing them so I can make sure they actually work and look good in real life. Most of the time, I start with a simple single-color test print first. That lets me check the overall geometry, supports, and printability without burning a ton of filament. If everything comes out clean, I'll move on to the full multicolor AMS version. My prototyping and testing setup includes two Bambu Lab P1S printers and two Snapmaker U1 printers , which lets me quickly iterate between test prints and full-color versions depending on what I'm working on. That said, if I'm already confident in the design—usually from similar prints or earlier versions—I might skip straight to the multicolor print. A fossil-hunter's dream on your shelf — this Spinosaurus skull prints at a display-ready, museum detail included. What to expect Comes in 7 simple parts: upper jaw, lower jaw, 4 cylindrical pegs and 1 plate printed separately for easy assembly Distinctive elongated, narrow snout with interlocking conical teeth — a hallmark of the Spinosaurus's fish-eating skull shape Supports are required for the fine details, but they're easy to remove — no need to stress over fragile connections here Print time & printer note (important) Since this model prints in 2 separate parts (upper and lower jaw) rather than as one large, connected piece, print time is more manageable than you'd expect for a 250mm skull — each part can be printed on its own, so you're not committing to one massive multi-day print. Support removal tips Supports on this model are refreshingly manageable: Crush or snip supports close to the contact point first, then remove gently Take a bit of extra care around the teeth, since the snout is narrow and the teeth are fine If something resists, don't pull — remove a bit more support instead Assembly Once both jaws are printed and cleaned up, join the upper and lower jaw and mount on the included stand for display. Take your time and you'll be rewarded with a clean, impressive skull. description: Rococo Chair & Setee VEF-CHR-0035 1:12 Dollhouse How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Download it Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊

description: Il personaggio raffigurato è Aang , il protagonista della celebre serie animata Avatar: La leggenda di Aang (Avatar: The Last Airbender). Ecco una panoramica dei dettagli principali del personaggio e della sua posa: Descrizione del Personaggio L'aspetto : È riconoscibile per la testa calva contrassegnata dal caratteristico tatuaggio a forma di freccia azzurra , simbolo che identifica i Maestri del Dominio dell'Aria. L'abbigliamento : Indossa i tipici abiti dei Nomadi dell'Aria, caratterizzati dai colori zafferano, arancione e rosso, completati da un mantello corto sulle spalle, una fascia in vita e calzari marroni con stringhe. Nello specifico, la posizione delle gambe è una variante della Posa del Gallo d'Oro (nota in cinese come Jin Ji Du Li - 金鸡独立, o "The Golden Rooster Stands on One Leg" ): L'equilibrio : Il corpo è interamente bilanciato su una sola gamba (la sinistra), mentre la gamba destra è sollevata con il ginocchio alto per proteggere il busto o prepararsi a sferrare un calcio. La dinamicità : Sotto la base del diorama sono visibili vortici di polvere ed effetti di vento stampati in 3D, che enfatizzano la natura aerea e l'agilità del personaggio durante un movimento difensivo o di attacco.

description: Karpen GOLD Armchair: VEF-CHR-0050 1:12 Dollhouse How I established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model BONUS IMAGE: Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale . Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊

description: Gothic Revival Desk: VEF-DSK-0044 1:12 Dollhouse How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale (and you can do it too) The image above is an example showing how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for the Dollhouse models I upload. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image, (the item I want to scale), into a Victorian room reference image, (the wall with the fireplace, window and door). Most important is to set the wall image to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image at the bottom of this description, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Download & Scale your Models to 1:12 Bambu Settings for this Model

description: Carved Walnut Parlor Suite VEF-SUITE-0053 1:12 How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model To Change the Scale: Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊 [End]

Insert your games, clip your Kanto badges ( Easily found on Amazon and AliExpress) , and enjoy your ultimate retro-gaming display! _____________________________ C'est mon tout premier design ! description: Victorian Cottage 6 Drawer Dress VEF-DRS-0036 1:12 How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model For those of you who want the model but in a different scale: Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊 [End]

description: “Big Chap” (Alien) Ultra Detailed Sculpture Staying on the recent Xenomorph Theme, here is another absoutley awesome, and highly detailed, “Big Chap” Xenomorph Sculpture! There are 2 size profiles being made available at the time of the model upload - 18" tall version as well as a 10" tall version. Please note that the 19" tall version is printed in pieces, and is maximized in size to fit the P/X series printer beds. The 10" tall version is printed a simplified one-piece print. I should know that I have printed 6 different size variants and will note that you can easily scale this between 10" and 19" tall models. **Please be aware that the print times are lengthy. I had 4 machines running test prints none stop. I promise though, it is worth it at the end. **Please also be aware that the model images you see are 100% real, with 0 use of AI, but they have been post-process colored using some Rub'n Buff waxes, 2-part epoxy resin, and then some gloss clear coat layer application at the end. ASSEMBLY REQUIRED ** Discard the small round cylinder that prints on the 2nd plate with the arms and foot. It is an uneeded part that was a result of slicing the model in the studio* The 19" tall, multipiece print will require some glue. I have used both super glue, as well as hot glue. Hot glue was my preference. With all the parts printed, and supports cleaned up (TAKE YOUR TIME REMOVING THE SUPPORTS AS THE PARTS ARE HIGHLY DETAILED AND FRAGILE ) do a dry-fit of all the parts to ensure proper fitment. You may need to file down some pieces if they do not fit. All 4 of my models went together with no issues, but different printers/filaments may have some tolerance issues. Assembly is very straightfoward, The tail loops around the display and needs to be installed afterwards. Install the tail by turning is 90 degrees and carefully looping the tip around the back of the base and then gently rotating it up into the reciever cutout on he back of the xenomorph (Yes, it looks like a butt ). With the Dry fitting completed, if you are satisfied with the fitment you can take the piees apart and proceed to glue them together. As with the above test-fit process. If you are planning to paint/apply color to the model I highly advise doing so with Xenomorph OFF of the base. For final assembly, apply some glue to the foot mounting pegs and firmly place the model on to the base. COLOR APPLICATION I used a very straightforward process for my coloring via application of some Rub'n Buff Antique Gold wax for the Xenomorph, and Brass color for the base. Wear gloves and apply the wax to a towel and gently go over the details. Avoid pressing really hard so that the void remain black/dark, this helps with final contrast of the model. As you can tell from these two photos the difference between the plain model and the colored one is pretty phenomenal and I HIGHLY recommend going through the effort!

description: Bitte die Druckhinweise (weiter unten) beachten! Über dieses Modell Es ist jetzt mehr als 23 Jahre her das ich Vater geworden bin. Doch leider durfte ich meinen Sohn erst vor einigen Monaten kennenlernen. Vor wenigen Tagen war sein erster Geburtstag zu dem ich ihm wirklich gratulieren konnte. Meine größte Frage war aus diesem Grund: Was kann ich ihm schenken? Nach vielen Stunden des nachdenkens und grübelns sind meine Frau und ich zum Schluss gekommen das wir das wertvollste verschenken wollen das wir haben: Zeit Sicherlich hätte ich auch einfach Geld in einen Umschlag stecken können, reinschreiben: "Für eine schöne Zeit" aber das war mir zu unpersönlich und zu einfach. Immerhin habe ich sein ganzes Leben bisher verpasst. Aus diesem Grund war gemeinsame Zeit in meinen Augen das wertvollste was ich zu geben habe. Doch wie verpackt man Zeit? Diese Frage hat mich nichtmehr losgelassen und da wir uns bereits für einen gemeinsamen Freizeitpark Besuch entschieden hatten war es klar! Ich musste irgendwas drucken das den Freizeitpark verkörpert. Doch auch nach mehreren Tagen des suchens bin ich auf nichts gestoßen das mich zufrieden gestellt hätte und die Zeit wurde langsam immer knapper. Also entschied ich mich kurzerhand etwas selbst zu entwerfen und zu drucken. Als Basis diente hier ein Foto des Fahrgeschäfts Talocan aus dem brühler Phantasialand, das mittels Google Gemini zu einem Diorama umgestaltet wurde, das druckbar war. Der Vibe des Modells war mir dabei wichtiger als Detailtreue und so entstand ein grober Entwurf Natürlich könnt ihr euch ganz schnell ausrechnen das eine 1:1 Umsetzung, selbst mit einer guter Bild zu 3D KI nahezu unmöglich ist. Nach lediglich 2 Versuchen hatte ich aber bereits eine Basis mit der ich arbeiten konnte. Viele Stellen mussten mit Nomad Sculpt und einem CAD Programm noch ausgebessert werden um das Ganze druckbar zu machen, aber ich denke das Ergebnis ist ganz gut geworden, dafür das ich lediglich knappe 8 Stunden Arbeit reinstecken musste. Da die Zeit gedrängt hat und ich lediglich noch 3 Tage hatte bevor ich das Modell verschenken wollte musste das an dieser Stelle reichen. Das Filament also schnell bei Amazon über 24h Lieferung bestellt und losgedruckt... die Druckzeit betrug nämlich in Multicolor mehr als 42 Stunden (Singlecolor weitaus schneller!), nur für das Fahrgeschäft. Mein größter Fehler hierbei: Das Modell in 2 Hälften zu teilen um es "schneller" (mit 2 Druckern" drucken zu können. Der Fehler dabei: Ich hatte nur eine Rolle Material... wer nachdenkt ist klar im Vorteil! Da waren Gutscheine und Basis, Schublade und Knopf noch nicht mit eingerechnet. Da ich zum Glück derzeit noch 5 Drucker in Benutzung habe war das allerdings kein so extremes Problem, Basis und Schublade konnte ich separat drucken! DRUCKHINWEISE WICHTIG! Wenn ihr dieses Modell druckt nehmt euch Zeit und Werkzeug zum entfernen der Stützen! Seid Vorsichtig beim entfernen der Stützen um nichts abzubrechen! Das Geländer im Hintergrund des Fahrgeschäfts hat bei mir nicht vernünftig gedruckt, ich habe es einfach entfernt nach dem Druck! Vielleicht habt ihr ja mehr Glück! Da ich mit mattschwarz die Basis gedruckt habe musste ich die Schublade ein wenig herunterskalieren. Die in der Konstruktion eingrechneten Toleranzen hatten nicht gereicht. Das sollte bei normalem Material nicht passieren. Bitte denkt daran das ihr eventuell die Schublade skalieren und neu drucken müsstet. Verwendete Materialien: PLA Mattschwarz: https://amzn.to/4y933tY PLA Stein Farbverlauf: https://amzn.to/4yel9uE PLA Silk Blau: https://www.dr3dcrazymonkey.com/products/lotactree-pla-silk-1-75mm-1kg?variant=57444533731660 HINWEIS: Dieses Projekt ist mit viel Liebe entstanden und auch wenn es zu einem großen Teil aus einer generativen KI stammt wurden noch einige Arbeitsstunden in das entfernen der klumpigen Passasgiermasse, dem begradigen von unebenheiten, dem ersteller der individualisierbaren Gutscheine und vielem mehr gesteckt. Ich hoffe ihr wisst dieses Modell und die Arbeit, die ich mir auf die schnelle gemacht habe zu schätzen. Der gesamtaufwand lag bei 4-5 Tagen arbeit bis Alles fertig war.

*** Images are actual photographed Prints. This is a fully 3D-printable eyewear design that you can print, finish, and assemble entirely at home. It requires no screws, hinges, or extra hardware—all you need is some super glue and a bit of post-processing to get a clean, functional pair of glasses. This model is designed to support standard and prescription lenses, making it both a stylish accessory and a practical daily wear option. For ordering lenses in the EU: I found Lens4Glasses to be an affordable option that ships across the EU. Important: Please ask your optician not to heat the frame when fitting the lenses. The frame is designed to fit the lenses without heating—and yes, they will deform your eyewear and send it back! 🙂 Key Features Two Sizes Included: Comes in two different sizes to help ensure a proper fit for different face shapes. Lens-Ready: Designed to accommodate both standard non-prescription lenses and prescription lenses. 100% Hardware-Free: No need to source tiny screws or specialized hinges. Easy Assembly: Simple joint design secured with a small amount of super glue. Recommended Print Settings To ensure the best surface finish and structural strength, the following settings are recommended: Layer Height: 0.10mm to 0.15mm (highly recommended for smoother curves and easier sanding) Infill: 40% – 50% Supports: Required. You will need to enable supports for the curved sections of the temples (the arms that go behind the ears). Material Compatibility This model has been tested with several filaments, and you can print it using almost any standard material: Bambu PLA-CF: Highly recommended. The carbon fiber texture provides a premium matte finish and excellent structural rigidity. Wood PLA: Gives a unique, organic aesthetic. It looks great but will require extra sanding and finishing to get a smooth feel. Standard PLA/PETG: Works well and offers a wide range of color choices. Assembly & Post-Processing Sanding: To achieve a comfortable fit and clean look, thoroughly sand the frames and temples. Start with a coarser grit (like 220) to smooth out print lines, and finish with a wet sand (400 to 1000 grit) for a smooth surface. Dry Fit: Test-fit the temples into the frame joints before applying any glue to ensure they align properly. Gluing: Apply a very small drop of super glue (cyanoacrylate) to the connection points. Hold the pieces firmly in place Lens Installation How to install: Standard scanned or custom-cut lenses can be snapped directly into the frame from the inside. Important Note: Do not apply heat (such as hot water or a hairdryer) to the frame during installation. Heating the plastic can cause the printed frame to warp or lose its shape. The lenses are designed to snap into place easily at room temperature.

Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. But like a cooler version of myself in a fantasy setting? YES. 💅🏼✨ 📌What do you need to know? (Before printing) This is a multipart design, with two separate frame looks that you can choose between. One of the frames has a clean/industrial steampunk look, and the other has a more ornate Victorian look with foliage patterns. Both frames are included in the design profile on separate plates. I designed the assembly first for compatibility with laser-cut 3 mm PMMA (acrylic) lenses, but then I decided to make it more accessible to everyone by including an FDM-printable version of the lenses. So you can print this full design even without laser cutting. Just keep in mind that the FDM version is mostly a prop for wearing overhead, since I personally couldn't see anything behind the printed lenses. :D Also, these goggles are gigantic by design. :D Please don't scale them up or down, by doing that the assembly won't be possible anymore. 📌What about additional components? I put the DXF file for the laser-cut acrylic lenses in this model if you'd like to cut your own see-through lenses. You can find them under the “Download STL/CAD files” section. For the forehead lights, I used mini battery-powered LEDs of 10x15 mm (Dxh). You can see an example here . Although I didn't include them yet in my versions, the movable mechanical assembly on the side is there to integrate a magnifying lens with a diameter of 20 mm into your glasses if you want. You can see an example here . 📌Print notes: Since this design has several print plates and objects with various settings, I suggest you open the 3MF directly in Bambu Studio and check out the requirements for each group of objects. 📌Post-printing and assembly: This design requires only minimal support, and most of the clean-up is for the brims (since there are quite a few small and separate components). However, there is a small “bridge” that you'll need to clean up before the assembly. Push it open with a hot or sharp tool to have access to the back of your LED and printed insert, so you can push them out from behind if needed. After cleaning, assembling the goggles is quite straightforward. You won't need any glue or additional joining components. Here are some additional guides. Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: 缠绕灵蛇镯戒两用配饰（3D 打印款） 一、项目主要特点 盘绕灵蛇一体环绕造型 整条蛇身环形缠绕成环，蛇头、蛇尾立体卷曲，全身复刻细密蛇鳞纹理，复古神秘、暗黑小众风格，缩放尺寸可做戒指或手镯，造型独特吸睛。 一体式闭环环形结构 整体无缝一体成型，环形壁厚均匀，可按需缩放内径适配手指、手腕，佩戴贴合肌肤，受力不易断裂，开合弧度舒适不硌肤。 高精度全身蛇鳞细节 完整雕刻蛇头部五官、鳞片纹路、蛇身褶皱与尾尖造型，3D 打印层纹强化雕刻肌理，素模可打磨抛光、手工上色做旧，DIY 创作空间充足。 多场景多功能设计 缩小内径可做个性灵蛇戒指；放大内径可做复古蛇形手镯；闲置也可作为 cos 装扮道具、桌面迷你摆件、拍摄装饰、创意定制礼品。 低支撑友好打印模型 仅蛇头、蛇尾尖端少量悬空，仅需局部简易支撑，环形主体无大面积悬空，FDM 打印机成型稳定，新手打印成功率高。 两种打印材质可选 PLA 性价比高，适合静态摆件、短期搭配使用；PETG 韧性更强，抗弯折、耐汗水侵蚀，长期贴身佩戴不易脆裂变形。 二、适用场景 & 适配人群 1. 日常穿搭佩戴 缩小款：灵蛇个性戒指，复古、暗黑、小众风穿搭指环；放大款：缠绕蛇形手镯，潮流亚文化手环、个性穿搭配饰；适配人群：潮流穿搭爱好者、cos 玩家、手工涂装 DIY 玩家、创意首饰定制人群 2. 道具装饰用途 万圣节 / 奇幻题材 cos 装扮道具、桌面小众潮玩摆件、静物摄影拍摄道具、节日小众送礼成品 3. 二次加工衍生 金属首饰翻模原型、树脂浇筑复刻白模、丙烯手绘上色创作素材 三、3D 打印设置（0.4mm 标准喷嘴通用参数） 方案 A：PLA（低成本、摆件 / 短期搭配） 层高：0.15mm（完美还原细密蛇鳞纹理；赶工期快速打印可选 0.2mm 层高） 壁厚 / 周长：3–4 圈（壁厚≥1.2mm，提升环身抗弯折强度） 填充率：15% 蜂窝填充，兼顾结构强度，节省耗材 喷嘴温度：200–210℃ 热床温度：首层 65℃，后续 60℃，防止环身底部翘边变形 打印速度：外壁 35mm/s，内部填充 55mm/s 支撑：仅蛇头、蛇尾尖端开启局部支撑，环形主体无需支撑 底部厚度 1.2mm，顶部封层 1.0mm 适用局限：不耐长期汗水浸泡，高温环境易软化形变，不适合长期贴身佩戴 方案 B：PETG（长期贴身佩戴推荐款） 层高：0.15mm 壁厚 / 周长：3–4 圈（1.2–1.6mm，韧性更强，弯折不易断裂） 填充率：15%–20% 蜂窝填充 喷嘴温度：240–250℃ 热床温度：全程 70–75℃持续加热 风扇：首层关闭，第 3 层后风扇全开 打印速度：外壁 30mm/s，填充 45mm/s 支撑：仅蛇头、蛇尾尖端添加简易支撑 优化设置：开启熨烫功能，环身内壁光滑平整，佩戴不磨皮肤 核心优势：防水抗汗、耐摔不易开裂，温差环境不易变形，适合日常长期佩戴 补充打印小贴士 尺寸缩放参考戒指款：内径 18–22mm；常规手镯款：内径 60–68mm；宽松道具镯：70–78mm；摆件放大款 90–120mm 后处理优化打印完成后用细砂纸逐层打磨支撑残留毛刺，可喷涂金属漆、做旧古铜漆，打造复古灵蛇质感；也可抛光做仿银、仿金效果 保养说明PETG 款可清水直接擦拭清洁；PLA 款避免长期接触汗液、阳光暴晒、暖气等高温热源

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Bring a touch of nature and elegance to your wrist with this Orchid Lace Bracelet . This design combines the precision of 3D printing with a simple and fun post-processing technique (thermoforming) to create a perfectly curved, comfortable piece of wearable art. It features a delicate, lace-like pattern inspired by the beautiful silhouettes of orchids, making it a perfect accessory or a unique gift. 💡 The Concept & Credit This model is designed to be printed completely flat on your print bed and then shaped using hot water. While this is an original design made from scratch, the brilliant concept of using flat-printed patterns to thermoform bracelets was inspired by the work of @ G-ODA and their excellent Organic Wave Bracelet . I highly recommend checking out their work, which taught me this wonderful technique! 🛠️ How to Make It (Post-Processing Guide) Shaping the bracelet is incredibly easy and takes less than 2 minutes. Follow these simple steps: Print the file completely flat. Prepare hot water: Fill a mug or container with hot water. It doesn't need to be boiling, just hot enough to soften the plastic. Shape it: Carefully wrap the bracelet around the outside of the mug. 🖨️ Recommended Print Settings Material: PLA works perfectly for this technique as it softens at accessible temperatures. (The one in the photos is printed in Matte Olive Green). Layer Height: 0.16mm or 0.20mm for clean details. Bed Adhesion: A clean bed is recommended due to the detailed first layer. No brim needed. description: One customizable OpenSCAD generator for everyday personalized tags: keychains, luggage tags, fridge magnets, screw plates, bin labels, door signs, and desk nameplates. Universal Personalized Tag Generator Pro expands a simple winning keychain label into a broader personal-label generator. Choose a mode, type your text, and generate a practical tag for keys, bags, storage bins, fridge notes, tool panels, doors, desks, and workshop organization. The first build includes seven fast MakerWorld-ready modes: `keychain` , `luggage_tag` , `fridge_magnet` , `screw_plate` , `bin_label` , `door_sign` , and `desk_nameplate` . Each mode has sensible default size, shape, text layout, and mounting, while manual overrides let you tune the width, height, thickness, shape, mount type, and text style. Mounting options include single ring hole, double ring holes, strap slot, blind magnet pockets, screw holes with counterbores, adhesive tape recess, and no-mount plates. The default text style uses raised lettering so color changes near the top layers are easy on a standard FDM printer. Optional text styles include engraved, recessed, and inlay-ready lettering for paint, resin, or filament-fill workflows. The desk nameplate mode prints as a simple support-free wedge with text on the sloped face. Customization Notes - Use `tag_mode` first, then leave `size_preset` , `mount_type` , `text_layout` , and `shape_style` on `mode_default` for a quick printable result. - Leave `color_style` on `raised` for the easiest two-color print with a filament swap near the top layers. - Use `inlay_ready` for deeper lettering pockets that can be filled after printing. - Use `fridge_magnet` or `magnet_pockets` for blind underside magnet pockets; glue magnets in after printing. - Use `screw_plate` or `door_sign` for screw holes with counterbores. - Use `back_side` for simple underside ID text such as phone number, serial number, property label, or emergency info. - Keep very long labels short or reduce the font size for narrow tags.

description: A functional, aesthetic charging and display stand based around the Pebble Time 2! Includes an indent for the heart rate sensor and a non-slip TPU 95A foot. HARDWARE This project requires a couple things: Your Pebble magnetic charger. If you don't want to use the one that came with your watch, I have had luck with this one from Amazon . There are a few like this, but if you buy one without the USB C port make sure it has a thin (preferably flat), flexible cable. Right-angle USB-C adapter. If you don't use a charger with an attached cable, you will need one of these. Make sure it is slim. The fitment was modeled after one similar to these from Ugreen . USB-C cable, if you aren't using a charger with one attached. Just use one of the hundreds you have laying around at this point! 4x M3x25mm self-tapping screws. Mine came from this set . These are optional, but I like the look of screws instead of using glue and it's easier to take apart. PRINTING TIPS I have carefully painted supports, infill & walls on the included print profiles. There should be no need to tweak them. Ironing is enabled on the Pebble logo to look nice and smooth. This can be tweaked or disabled to your preference. If printing from the step files, note the following: The stand is best printed on its side so that the curves are smooth and the inset on the bottom is accurate. Ensure that your bridging is calibrated and well-tuned Ensure that the widest part of the stand at least is supported; tree supports can angle into the cavity about 10mm while remaining on the build plate and I found that to be sufficient Ensure that the inset at the bottom of the stand for the foot is supported; I had to paint on supports manually since the slicer kept wanting to print that as an overhang. The inlay side (pebble logo) of the watch holder should be printed face down and should not need supports - they're hard to remove. However, the cantilever for the heart rate sensor does need support. Print the stand and foot at 100% infill (or 1000 walls, your preference). This is to ensure they are weighty enough to offset the high weight when the watch is on the stand. Print the foot on a textured PEI plate if using TPU. I recommend 95A TPU or SEBS. The texture on the plate, when applied to the foot, greatly enhances grip. Assembly Print and Gather your parts Insert the charger (with right angle connector if applicable) into the cavity. There is an indent for the lanyard if you do not want to remove it. The lanyard can also be used to add some friction by sliding it underneath the magnetic charger. Plug the cord in and feed it through the cavity in the stand. Slide the stand onto the watch holder. Fitment is tight, so a small amount of force may be necessary. It may be easiest to slide the watch holder onto the stand, feeding the charger into the cavity as you do so. Secure 4x M3x25mm self-tapping screws into the four holes on the side of the stand. Screw them all the way in so their heads are flush to ensure that they have secured the holder to the stand. Click the logo inlay into place. It should not require glue, but a little dab does not hurt. Insert the foot into the inset in the bottom. The small peg should align to the small hole next to the cord cutout. Do not glue this in or the cord will be impossible to remove later. Fill your coffee!

description: I designed these for my daughter who wanted multiple sets to wear on her trip to Disneyland. Instead I created a single set with inserts that could be changed out easily. This is done with the magic of magnets holding a front ear frame with an insert to the back part of the ear housing on the headband. For the desings its as simple as changing the color of the ear plate and/or adding a design. I used Maker Lab’s Image to Keychain and glued them on the front, or you can even embed it with the blank earpiece for a flat printed look. Along with this I also created carring case for ear inserts, which can be found here . Additional Items used: Battery operated lights from Amazon: Fairy Battery Operated Lights Magnet set from Amazon: 400 Piece 8 Sizes Magnet Set (12 - 5*3mm & 2 - 12*3mm Magnets from set used) Hot Glue: To hold lights in place and to secure magnet holder to the bow Super Glue: To secure the magnets in place. I use Gorrila Glue Super Glue Gel Assembly: Lights: Insert the light’s battery pack, wire side to the bottom, into the battery box on the headband. The battery pack should fit snuggly in the battery box, but if desired a small dot of hot glue could be used to hold it in place. Test to see that the battery box cover slides down and you feel it ‘lock’ into place once closed. Now take the wire and dry run it (not glueing yet) to the right ear and string half the lights (10) around the ear, assuring when you complete you can run blank wire across to the other side. String the lights around the left ear and once you are sure about how they are strung, glue them in place with a small dot of hot glue. You can also place a small dot of glue on the wire crossing between the ears to bottom center of where the battery box connects to the headband. *Note: the wire on the that crosses from ear to ear will be covered by the bow. Magnets: Place a small drop of super glue into each recessed spot before inserting the magnets. 6 of the 5*3mm are used for each ear on the headband. Assure you are placing the magnets in place with the same polarity facing out. Repeat the process with the other 6 of the 5*3mm magnets for the front ear frames, assuring that the outside facing magnet polarity is attracted to the headband ears. For the bow, place a drop of super glue in the recessed spot on the cover of the battery holder and instert a 12*3mm magnet. Repeat this for the magnet holder that would go on the bow with the other 12*3mm magnet. *Note more bow magnet holders and 12*3mm magnets would be required if you want to add/change out your bows. Ears: Insert the ear plate of your choice into the front ear frame. Notches on the ear frame and plact should match up and should snap into place with slight force around the edges. Attach the front frame to the headband and repeat for the other side. To remove or change the place reverse the process appling slight force near one of the notches from the front side. Bow: The magnet cover while small is important to assure the bow does not slide off from the battery box magnet. The cover is designed to only allow pulling vs sliding of the magnets to remove the bow. To attach the magnet cover to the bow, use a small dollop of hot glue on the back of the bow near the center and attach the magnet cover. *Note it is easier to insert the magnet into the bow magnet cover prior to attaching the cover to the bow.

Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. How to Customize Your Pin Follow these simple steps using Bambu Lab's MakerLab "Image to Keychain" tool to create your own custom pin. Powered by MakerWorld-Image to Keychain (https://makerworld.com/makerlab/imageToKeychain) Step 1: Image Preprocessing Upload your desired image and adjust the crop and background options. Change the Crop Ratio to Shape and select the circle icon ❶. Toggle Keep Background to ON ❷. Set the Image Thickness to 1 mm ❸. Use the slider ❹ to adjust the zoom and center your character within the circle. Step 2: Fine-Tune the Plate & Thickness Settings Once inside the editor, navigate to the Plate & Thickness tab on the right side of the screen. Set the Plate Thickness to 1 mm ❶. Set the Image Thickness to 0.5 mm ❷. Step 3: Choose Your Nozzle & Download Click the green Download button in the top right, which will bring up the download prompt. Under "Choose your nozzle", select 0.2mm (Recommended) ❶. Click the final green Download button ❷ to grab your customized .3MF file. Step 4: Import and Adjust Colors in Bambu Studio Open the downloaded file in Bambu Studio. Map your AMS filament slots ❶ to match the colors of your design. Tip: For crisp details on small pins, the recommended 0.10mm Standard layer height layer profile with a 0.2mm nozzle yields the sharpest results! description: Create a whole custom bracelet bead set in one download. Enter up to 12 bead labels, choose cube, coin, or barrel beads, set the size and hole diameter, then pick raised or recessed lettering. Make personalized letter beads for friendship bracelets, craft projects, classroom name strings, zipper pulls, gift tags, and keychain accents. This parametric OpenSCAD generator creates a full batch of matching beads with adjustable size, thickness, stringing hole, and per-bead face lettering, so you can generate a complete name/word bracelet instead of downloading each letter as a separate file. Features: - Cube, coin, and barrel bead styles. - Adjustable bead size, thickness, bead count, and spacing. - Up to 12 separate label fields, one per bead. - Horizontal side-stringing hole by default for classic bracelet-bead layouts. - Optional vertical hole mode, offset below the letter, for name-string or tag layouts. - Raised or recessed label text. - Optional back-side label. - Rounded cube corners and optional barrel rib detail. - Cutaway preview mode for checking hole and label depth. The default prints a small `FRIEND` bracelet-bead set with horizontal side-stringing holes. The default 3 mm holes bridge cleanly on normal tuned printers, so it can print without supports while looking more like classic bracelet beads. For bracelet stringing, test your cord/elastic against `hole_diameter` ; different filaments and printers can make small holes tighter than expected. Safety note: these are small parts. Not for children under 3, and not for any use where broken or loose beads could become a choking hazard. Customization Notes - `bead_style` : choose cube, coin, or barrel. - `bead_count` : number of beads in the batch, up to 12. - `bead_size` / `bead_thickness` : bead face size and height. - `hole_diameter` : string/elastic hole size. Bring your favorite football memes to life on your wardrobe! This unique DIY project features the iconic silhouette of Erling Haaland, 3D printed with an ultra-thin thickness of 0.4 mm . How It's Made (PLA+ Method): For this specific shirt, PLA+ was used. Since this filament is tougher to melt, it requires a specific technique combining high heat and immediate pressure: Setup: Lay the t-shirt perfectly flat on a smooth, heat-resistant surface (like floor tiles). Placement: Position the main Haaland design, then carefully place the 2 or 3 small detached pieces that aren't connected to the rest. Protection: Cover the entire design with tightly stretched baking paper. Heating: Use a heat gun to melt the filament onto the fabric through the baking paper. Pressing (The key step): Immediately after heating, firmly press a wooden cutting board directly onto the hot baking paper to force the melted filament into the fabric mesh for a solid bond. ⚠️ Warning: Do not stay in one spot for too long with the heat gun! Heat evenly and keep moving, then press immediately to avoid deforming the plastic. 💡 Pro Tip: Which filament should you use? Standard PLA with a household iron (Possible, but not recommended): You can technically try using regular PLA with a standard iron (no steam) and baking paper, but the result isn't great. The plastic doesn't bond well to the fabric and tends to peel off easily. TPU Filament (The absolute best option): For the best results, we highly recommend using TPU (flexible filament) instead. It works beautifully with a regular household iron (no steam) . When heated, the TPU melts right into the fabric mesh, blending with the textile. This gives you maximum flexibility, a softer feel, and incredible longevity. 🧼 Care Instructions: To ensure your design lasts as long as possible, always wash the t-shirt at a low temperature and inside out .

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

This project is a premium parametric Cotton Pad Dispenser (Porta Algodão Dispensador) with a vertical U-shaped front slot. It allows you to load a stack of circular cotton pads from the top and easily pull pads out one-by-one from the bottom. Fully parametric in OpenSCAD, it features three standard capacities, optional screw-on lid configuration, and deep aesthetic customization. --- UNLIMITED CUSTOMIZATION --- With over 30 texture patterns and adjustable scales, this project offers hundreds of unique combinations for you to create an exclusive dispenser. --- PARAMETER GUIDE --- 1. Size & Capacity - Size Selection: Choose between three height capacities: - Small (P): Height 80mm (Holds approx. 20 cotton pads) - Medium (M): Height 120mm (Holds approx. 35 cotton pads) - Large (G): Height 160mm (Holds approx. 50 cotton pads) - Has_Lid: Option to include a screw-on lid. - Enabled (Yes): Adds a top thread to the base and exports the lid. - Disabled (No): Removes threads entirely, leaving a clean open-top dispenser with a smooth, rounded upper rim. 2. Dispenser Slot Settings - Cutout Width: Controls the width of the vertical dispensing slot (Default: 35mm). It is optimized to be wide enough for your fingers to easily pull a pad out, but narrow enough to keep the pads stacked securely inside. - Bottom Lip: Height of the bottom retaining wall that supports the stack (Default: 8mm). 3. Aesthetics and Texture - Surface Pattern: Applies geometric textures in high/low relief to the outer face (Default: Grid Diagonal). - Pattern Depth: Controls how pronounced the texture is (recommended: 0.6mm). - Pattern Scale: Adjusts the size of the texture tiles. Small variations in this scale dramatically transform the visual effect, essentially creating entirely new textures from a single base pattern. You can fine-tune the look from bold geometric shapes to fine, intricate details. Scale effects on the same pattern - Text Bands: Show customized text at the top (Default: "COTTON"). - Logo Patch: Creates a smooth, centralized area on the base for logos or custom labeling. --- TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS & PRINTING --- - Support-Free Design: Both the dispenser base and the lid print completely without supports. The bottom of the U-slot is a semi-circle that prints cleanly in mid-air, and the inside has straight 62.0mm cylinder walls to prevent soft cotton pads from catching or tearing. - Smart Lidless Finishes: When printing without a lid, the top edge of the dispenser is automatically detailed with a smooth, 1.0mm double-rounded rim (both inner and outer lips). This ensures that cotton pads don't snag when loading and the top is completely safe and pleasant to touch. - Perfect Thread Synchronization: When the lid is enabled, the metric threading system includes a hardcoded thread phase (angular offset). This guarantees that when you fully tighten the lid, the texture patterns on the lid and the base align flawlessly, even with the vertical slot cutout. --- RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- - Layer Height: 0.16mm (Optimal) - Wall Generator: Arachne (Required for sharp texture details) - Line Width: 0.6mm (Outer & Inner walls) - Infill: 10 Gyroid or Cross Hatch - Speed: 100 mm/s (Outer & Inner walls for premium finish) - Supports: No supports needed!
