model_name: Rope Paracord Ratchet Tensioner Outdoor Tie-Down
description: A fully 3D-printed rope ratchet tensioner that tightens your line one satisfying click at a time, and releases with a thumb press. No knots, no fiddling, no metal ratchet wheel to source. Pull the cord, let the ratchet do the holding, and dial in tension with one hand. Inspired by the little aluminum rope-tensioner pulleys you see on tent guylines and grow-light hangers, but reimagined so almost everything comes off your printer . The grip comes from the cord wrapping the knurled wheel (capstan effect) combined with a directional ratchet that only lets the wheel turn one way. Honest performance - Read this first I test my functional models to failure and I tell you the real numbers, not marketing ones. Recommended working load: 3–4 kg (or 20+ kg with a backup knot, read below). Slip point observed in my tests: 5–7 kg , depending on the cord. It does not break under load, when overloaded, the cord slips on the wheel rather than the part snapping. The limiting factor is grip between cord and printed wheel , not the mechanism (the ratchet and clicker themselves hold far more). A steel wheel like the commercial versions grips harder, a printed wheel can't fully match that, and that's the honest trade-off of an all-printed design. Tip to squeeze out more grip: printing the wheel in a slightly abrasive or matte/porous filament increases surface friction and can push the slip point higher. Smooth glossy filament grips the least. Tension is cord-dependent, different cord material, diameter and sheath change the grip. Always test with your own cord before trusting a load. Backup stopper knot — a big safety margin Here's the trick that changes the game for the rare high-load moment: tie a simple stopper knot on the tail (the free end running through). If the cord ever starts to slip, the knot jams against the tensioner and can't pass, and from that point the load is carried by the structure of the part , not by friction grip. In my own testing, with a backup knot I pulled it to 20 kg one-handed with zero drama, and that was the limit of what I could safely pull by hand, not the limit of the part. Beyond that it's the shell and anchor taking the load, and there's clearly more headroom. Real-world use: tensioning a line with a backup stopper knot on the tail for extra security. With a backup stopper knot, it held 20+ kg in hand-testing without failure Where it works well (≈3–4 kg working) Tent and tarp guylines - the core use Tarp ridgelines , camp clotheslines, drying lines Hanging grow lights, lanterns, camp lights (1–3 kg) - the classic rope-ratchet job Hanging planters, bird feeders / birdhouses Backpack compression and lashing light gear Kayak / canoe deck rigging for light gear Tensioning banners, bunting, light signs, shade cloth, awnings Where NOT to use it (please respect this) ❌ Climbing or anything a person hangs from, never. This is not safety equipment. ❌ Hammock body (80–150 kg). Tarp suspension over a hammock is fine; the hammock itself is not. ❌ Primary vehicle / roof cargo tie-down. Use as a light positioning aid only, never as the load-bearing restraint. ❌ Leash or tie-out for medium/large dogs, a single lunge exceeds the working load instantly. ❌ Anything overhead where a drop could injure someone or damage something. Print settings Layer height: 0.16 mm, or adaptive (adaptive is set in the included profile), this matters for the printed closure-screw threads to come out clean. Supports: optional , only for the retention-screw holes . The rest prints support-free. Material: PETG recommended for outdoor UV/heat durability; PLA is fine for indoor / light use. Preparing the torsion spring The spring needs a quick manual tweak (real photos included in the model gallery): Cut one leg to ~5 mm . Keep the other leg at ~10 mm and bend a 90° angle at the end, like this: That's it, no special tools, just cutters and pliers. Assembly 1. Build the wheel (4 parts). The wheel is split into four pieces so each prints cleanly: the bottom piece that seats into the base shell, the first knurled half of the wheel, the second knurled half, these two slide together on the central hex pin , the clicker gear on top. Stack all four onto the M2.5 SHCS and secure with the M2.5 hex nut . 2. Wrap the cord. Route the cord around the assembled wheel. 3. Seat it. Place the wheel assembly into the base shell . 4. Add the pawl + spring. Insert the pawl together with the prepared torsion spring, as shown in the gallery. 5. Close it up. Fit the cover , then drive the 4 × M2 closure screws . 6. Anchor point. Finally insert the M3 × 14 screw (with its M3 nut) — this is where the carabiner clips on. Cord notes Tested with 3 mm Nylon Paracord 425 and 4 mm cord, results were very similar between the two. Thicker cord may grip better but I didn't have any on hand to test. If you try thicker or different cord, please leave feedback in the comments, I'll collect real numbers and add a grip table. Companion carabiner My Classic Spring Carabiner is a separate print-in-place model designed to pair with this tensioner: clip it on, tension your line, done. Disclaimer This is a printed functional accessory for light tensioning only . It is not rated safety equipment and must never be used for climbing, fall protection, lifting people, or any application where failure could cause injury or serious damage. Real-world holding force depends on your filament, cord, print quality and assembly. Always test with your own setup and stay well within the recommended working load. Use at your own risk.

description: Motivation If you're curious about the motivation behind 3D-printed FPV drone frames, check out the [BETA] ManaFly 3" Generative FPV Drone Frame project: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2000546-beta-manafly-3-generative-fpv-drone-frame?from=search#profileId-2154440 That page goes into much more detail on the motivation, use cases, crash resistance, frame-swapping, and the overall advantages of a 3D-printed frame over a traditional carbon fiber one. This project follows the same idea and versatility, scaled up to fit most common components used on 7-inch drones. Compatibility Flight Controller - 20 x 20 mm FPV stack - 30.5 x 30.5 mm FPV stack VTX - 20x20 mm (M2) — small VTX mounts, fits most modern analog and compact digital systems - 25.5x25.5 mm (M2) — standard mount for DJI digital VTX units (Air Unit / O3 / O4) - 30x30 mm (M3) — larger mounts for older or high-power VTX units with better heat handling Camera - Analog Mini / Micro / Nano - A custom mount can be made for any camera smaller than 21 mm Prop Size - 7-inch props (standard) Filament I used ABS for its stiffness, but the frame can also be printed in PETG or PA6-CF. A detailed breakdown of each filament option, along with a comparison against a carbon fiber frame, is available on the [BETA] ManaFly 3" Generative FPV Drone Frame project page linked above. IMPORTANT — Print Settings, Please Read Filament: ABS, PETG Infill: 50% Gyroid (50-70% range recommended) Wall loops: 8 Filament use: ~170 g Print orientation: Flat / horizontal, for maximum strength Support type: Automatic tree supports Infill — 50% Gyroid: Going higher 70%+ has only a low effect on strength. Wall loops — 8: this setting has a major effect on final mass while greatly increasing rigidity. For reference, with the same 50% gyroid infill, 2 wall loops give a mass of ~121 g, while 8 wall loops give ~157 g. Bed adhesion matters. Apply a bed adhesive before printing, and set the bed temperature to 110°C (the recommended setting for ABS) — otherwise the frame risks delaminating from the bed mid-print. Printer configuration — required for this frame's size: Because of this frame's large footprint (251 x 251 mm), some default printer settings need to be changed before slicing, or the print head can physically collide with the part and damage the printer: 1. Remove the bed exclusion zone from your printer configuration, so the part fits within the build area. 2. On a Bambu Lab P1S, increase the printable height from 250 mm to 256 mm. 3. Bend the Filament Cutter Lever Actuator out of the way . Once the exclusion zone is removed, the print head can collide with this component during printing. It's spring-mounted, so it can safely be bent aside — for example, secured with a cable tie. FEA Validation Before printing, the frame geometry was validated using FEA (Finite Element Analysis) simulation to check the safety factor across the structure and identify weak points before committing to a print. Assembling Top Plate — Important For ease of assembly, the top of the frame is left open, and the top plate is a separate part. However, this plate is not optional — it carries and transfers the load from the arms holding the motors. Before every flight, make sure the top plate is fitted in place and securely fastened with its bolt and nut. Oscillating Desktop Fan – 3D Printable Design This project is a compact oscillating desktop fan designed for 3D printing. It uses two 12V fans, adjustable fan speed control, and an automatic left-to-right oscillation mechanism. The vertical angle of the fan can be adjusted manually. The airflow speed can be controlled using the knob located on the side of the body. The oscillation mechanism is powered by a small N20 geared motor, providing a slow and smooth left-to-right movement. Features Automatic left-to-right oscillation Adjustable fan speed Manually adjustable vertical angle Compact desktop design Two 12V fans 3D printable body and mechanical parts Easy access to the controls and electronic components Suitable for desks, workshops, and hobby rooms Electronic Components 2 × 12V fans N20 6V 30 RPM geared motor DC-DC step-down converter PWM fan speed controller 12V power supply On/off switches Wires, screws, and basic electronic components I used an N20 6V 30 RPM geared motor for the oscillation mechanism. The motor is powered at approximately 3V through a DC-DC step-down converter. In my setup, 3V provides a suitable and balanced oscillation speed. The motor can also be operated at 3V, 3.5V, or 4V depending on the desired movement speed. Increasing the voltage will increase the oscillation speed. You can also use an N20 10 RPM or 15 RPM geared motor if one is available. Since lower-RPM motors may behave differently depending on the applied voltage, I recommend testing the motor speed before completing the final assembly. Electrical Wiring I recommend connecting the 12V power input to the switches first, and then distributing power from the outputs of the switches to the relevant components. With this wiring method, no power will be supplied to the fans, speed controller, step-down converter, or other electronic components when the switches are turned off. In my video, I distributed the power before the switches. However, for anyone building the project, placing the switches between the 12V input and the electronic components is the better wiring method. The general connection order should be: 12V power input → Switches → Related circuits and components This prevents unnecessary power consumption and ensures that the connected circuits are not continuously powered when the switches are off. Printing Notes I divided the project into a total of six build plates. The plates are named according to the type of print surface that should be used. In the project files: Plates named Smooth Plate should be printed on a smooth print surface. Plates named Textured Plate should be printed on a textured print surface. It is especially important to print certain sliding, rotating, or contact parts on a Smooth Plate. These parts require smooth contact surfaces for the oscillation mechanism to operate correctly. If the contact surfaces are too rough, the additional friction may cause: Excessive load on the N20 motor Irregular oscillation movement The mechanism to jam The motor to become unable to move the mechanism For this reason, please check the build plate names carefully before printing and use the specified print surface. Most parts can be printed using PLA or PETG. PETG is recommended for parts located close to the motor or electronic components, especially if the fan will be operated for extended periods. I recommend keeping the prepared print orientations and plate layouts where possible. However, always check support requirements and inspect the slicer preview before starting the print. Assembly and Mechanism Notes Depending on your printer calibration and dimensional tolerances, some parts may require light sanding or minor adjustment. All moving, rotating, and contacting areas of the oscillation mechanism should be lightly lubricated using a plastic-compatible lubricant. Pay particular attention to: Rotating connection points Shaft and bearing areas Plastic surfaces that slide against each other Moving joints in the oscillation mechanism Only apply enough lubricant to create a thin layer on the contact surfaces. Excessive lubrication is not necessary. Make sure that the lubricant is safe for plastic parts. After completing the assembly, check the following: The oscillation mechanism should move freely when operated by hand Moving parts should not rub against the housing Fan wires should not restrict the oscillation movement Wires should not enter or become trapped inside moving parts The motor should be mounted securely Screws in moving joints should not be overtightened Electrical connections should be properly insulated The mechanism should not jam at the left or right movement limits Before powering the motor, move the mechanism slowly by hand and check for excessive friction, resistance, or jamming. If the mechanism does not move freely by hand, do not operate it with the motor. First locate the source of the friction or obstruction. Lightly sand the contact surfaces if necessary and apply lubricant again. Important This project requires basic knowledge of electronics, soldering, and mechanical assembly. Before connecting the power supply, always check the voltage, polarity, and all electrical connections. During the first test, operate the oscillation motor at a low voltage and make sure that the mechanism moves freely. Do not leave the device unattended during the initial tests. Feel free to share your prints, improvements, and modifications on MakerWorld. I would be happy to see your version of the fan.

description: Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 4-part mould (3 sides and a small insert for the base) to cast round tumblers/mugs with a smooth design. You need to cast plaster in the larger mould three times for the sides, for every one cast of the small insert. This gives a complete plaster mould. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, with most casting slips this should give a final tumbler size of 6.5cm diameter and 7cm height, or a capacity of around 150ml. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 350ml of plaster for the side pieces and around 75ml for the base insert, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast. This uses the updated 3 part mould design, which is compatible with other updated 3 part moulds but not the original ornament moulds. This new design has slots added to the back to allow the mould to bend slightly when releasing the plaster, making the process much easier.

After the Modular Bricks Remote, I’ve been wanting to design other CyberBrick hardware into modular bricks. I believed a complete vehicle project would make this concept far more engaging, so lots of development work was required beyond designing basic modular bricks. The project is now finished — the Modular Bricks Kart, available in the Mecanum Wheel Version. Mecanum wheel vehicles are incredibly fun. They can drive like ordinary cars and also perform omnidirectional lateral sliding. Modular Bricks feature easy assembly and disassembly, allowing quick swapping between different toy models. Even children can assemble them with little difficulty. Once you have the full set of basic modular bricks, assembling any subsequent model becomes quick and hassle-free. This kart adopts exactly this design. Except for the wheels, the entire chassis and body require no screws or adhesive — assembly is just like stacking building blocks. It’s compatible with the official standard remote. If you are interested, I recommend trying my previously released Modular Bricks Remote, which lets you own a full set of modular brick toys. Some future models will rely on the unique advantages of the modular brick system to deliver functions unavailable with standard remote controllers. The remote links are in the Assembly Guild. Controlling a Mecanum wheel vehicle normally requires four motors, yet the CyberBrick receiver only supports two. Fortunately, it comes with four servo ports, so I opted to use four servos for power. This setup allows full vehicle functionality with a single receiver unit, while servos also deliver superior torque output. · Download the assembly guide for detailed build instructions, covering three manuals: Basic Modular Bricks, Chassis and Body, Mecanum Wheels. · The printing profiles are split into three sets matching the assembly guides; all three must be printed. Layouts are optimized for the A1 mini 3D printer and compatible with all other printer models. · Download JSON Files for Modular Bricks Mecanum Kart. Pair your transmitter and receiver in the app, then upload this file to operate the vehicle. · Purchase Recommendations Required hardware: 1 set Beginner Hardware Kit - ZK004 1 set Extra Rechargeable Battery Upgrade Kit - ZL003 3 extra 9g Continuous Rotation Digital Servo-360°- PG002 (4 servos total per kart; ZK004 includes 1 servo) 4 packs of 2×33 mm Brass Dowel Pin- DA006 (10 pieces per pack) For printing filaments: TPU90A is mandatory for printing Mecanum wheel rollers. All other parts can be printed with PLA in your preferred color; white PLA is recommended for the LED lamp cover. Have fun building and driving!

description: Da ich für mein Dachfenster keine passende Lösung gefunden habe, habe ich diesen Adapter selbst konstruiert. Der Adapter ermöglicht es, den Abluftschlauch einer mobilen Klimaanlage durch ein Dachfenster zu führen, während das Fenster nahezu vollständig geschlossen bleiben kann. Dadurch wird der Luftaustausch mit der warmen Außenluft reduziert und die Kühlleistung verbessert. Eigenschaften Passend für 125 mm, 130 mm und 150 mm Abluftschläuche Integrierte Aussparung für den Fenstergriff Große Auslassfläche für einen möglichst geringen Strömungswiderstand Mehrteilige Bauweise für eine einfache Herstellung auf handelsüblichen 3D-Druckern Für verschiedene Schlauchdurchmesser stehen passende Anschlussstücke zur Verfügung Version 2 Ich habe bereits eine V2 des Modells erstellt. Hier wurden zusätzlich 6 Verstärkungsrippen ergänzt, die nach dem Druck eingeklebt werden. Hintergrund ist, dass der Adapter während eines längeren Betriebs der Klimaanlage durch die warme Abluft leicht erwärmt wird. Je nach Material kann sich der Auslassbereich mit der Zeit minimal verformen. Die Verstärkungsrippen erhöhen die Stabilität deutlich und halten den Auslass dauerhaft in Form. Zusammenbau Der Adapter besteht aus: 2 Auslassteilen 1 Schlauchadapter 6 Verstärkungsrippen (V2) Alle Teile habe ich mit einem hochwertigen Sekundenkleber verklebt. Durch die mehrteilige Bauweise lassen sich sämtliche Komponenten auch auf Druckern mit normaler Baugröße problemlos herstellen. Druckempfehlung Bei mir wurde das Modell erfolgreich mit Bambu PETG HF und dem Standard-Bambu-Profil gedruckt. Ein Druck mit normalem PETG hat ebenfalls gut funktioniert. Da es sich jedoch um einen langen Druck handelt und PETG zu leichter Tropfenbildung neigt, verwende ich zusätzlich einen selbst eingebauten Nozzle-Cleaning-G-Code , der die Düse regelmäßig reinigt. Dadurch konnte ich die Druckqualität nochmals verbessern. Natürlich kann der Adapter auch aus anderen temperaturbeständigen Materialien gedruckt werden. Hinweise Da Dachfenster und mobile Klimaanlagen sehr unterschiedlich sind, kann ich keine universelle Passgenauigkeit garantieren. Bitte prüft vor dem Druck die angegebenen Maße und wählt den passenden Schlauchdurchmesser (125 mm, 130 mm oder 150 mm). Dieses Modell wurde ursprünglich für meinen eigenen Anwendungsfall entwickelt und anschließend so aufbereitet, dass möglichst viele Nutzer davon profitieren können. Feedback Ich freue mich über jedes Feedback! Solltet ihr Verbesserungsvorschläge, Ideen oder Anpassungswünsche haben, schreibt diese gerne in die Kommentare. Ich bin jederzeit offen für konstruktive Kritik und werde sinnvolle Verbesserungen gerne in zukünftige Versionen einfließen lassen. Viel Spaß beim Drucken – und ich hoffe, der Adapter hilft euch dabei, auch an heißen Sommertagen einen kühlen Kopf zu bewahren! 😊

description: Description This is my replica of the famous Rapala Jointed Floating 7 cm , designed and modeled directly from a precise 3D scan of an original 4-gram Rapala Jointed lure. Known for its broken-back design and unmistakable, hyper-active swimming action, the Jointed Floating is a legendary choice when fish are finicky or biting short. This 3D-printed version brings that exact lively, snake-like presentation directly to your tackle box, making it perfect for targeting perch, trout, pike, and zander. A massive amount of engineering and testing went into recreating the physics of a two-part jointed balsa lure in 3D-printed plastic. Because the action depends entirely on the freedom of movement between the two sections, the internal balance has been meticulously tuned to achieve the exact same characteristic swimming motion as the original classic. Design Notes 3D Scanned Precision: Modeled directly from a physical 3D scan of a real Rapala Jointed Floating 7 cm to ensure perfect proportions and flawless hydrodynamics. True-to-Original Weight: Engineered to match the compact 4-gram profile of the original, providing excellent buoyancy and a highly responsive action on light tackle gear. Finetuned Slicer Modifiers: The lively and chaotic swimming action of this lure relies heavily on custom internal weight distribution. I have integrated multiple precise slicer modifiers inside the model to perfect the center of mass for both sections. It is crucial that you do not change these settings , as they have been heavily tested and tuned across numerous prototypes. Crucial Support-Free Lip Design: The diving lip is oriented to print completely flat on its own separate plate. To handle the steep overhangs successfully without supports, it is highly recommended to print the lip at a 0.08 mm layer height . Printing it at a standard 0.2 mm layer height will cause print flaws on the curved edges. Strength & Testing 6.8 kg+ Load Capacity: Despite the jointed design, this lure uses the exact same robust internal hardware connection system as my other models. It has been thoroughly tested to lift at least 6.8 kg with absolutely no issues. The internal structure is rock-solid and fully prepared to handle heavy, hard-fighting predators. Strength & Finishing (Crucial Step) Applying a clear coat is highly recommended to ensure the model is 100% waterproof and to add structural strength. ⚠️ IMPORTANT FINISHING NOTE: Unlike my other models, do not dip this lure in your clear coat! Instead, I highly recommend applying your UV resin or epoxy clear coat with a brush . It is extremely important that you keep the central joint connection completely clean. If resin or epoxy gets inside the "link" where the two screw eyes connect, it will lock up the joint and ruin the lure's unique swimming action. Assembly The lure consists of three printed parts: the front body, the rear tail section, and the separate diving lip. Prep the Parts: Clean up any print lines or imperfections. Secure the diving lip into the front body slot using a strong 5-minute epoxy or superglue. Assemble the Joint (The Link): To create the jointed action, take two stainless steel screw eyes. Gently bend one of the eyelets slightly open with a pair of pliers, loop the second screw eye into it, and bend it completely shut again. Install the Joint: Screw the ends of this connected pair into the pre-modeled holes linking the front body and tail section together. Make sure the joint moves freely and smoothly. Install Remaining Hardware: Install the remaining 3 screw eyes (nose, front belly, and tail) into their pilot holes. (Tip: Use my 1mm Handdrill Handle tool from my profile to pre-drill the holes, or gently heat the screw eyes with a lighter before screwing them in for maximum strength). Rig the Hooks: Attach your split rings and size #8 treble hooks to the designated belly and tail screw eyes. Hardware Requirements To fully assemble the lure, you will need the following hardware: 5x Screw Eyes: Stainless steel. 1.3 mm thread thickness, 12 mm full length, 5 mm outer eye diameter, 8 mm shaft length. (Can be bought very cheaply on sites like Temu or AliExpress). 2x Split Rings: Size 5 mm. 2x Treble Hooks: Size #8. Important Print Profile Notice To make printing as easy as possible, the included print profile is split onto two plates : Plate 1: Contains the main body parts set to a standard 0.2 mm layer height . Plate 2: Contains the diving lip set to the required 0.08 mm layer height to handle the steep overhangs perfectly. (Note: If your printplate is big enough, you can easily combine these onto a single plate and utilize "Print by Object" to print both parts in a single run). Tight lines!!

description: Ratchet Scroll Frame – Embroidery Frame with Directional Lock An innovative embroidery scroll frame featuring a mechanical system for effortless canvas tensioning and scrolling. By utilizing rotating aluminum profiles where the canvas is attached, combined with a directional locking mechanism, tightening and advancing your fabric is easier than ever. The rotation direction is fully adjustable, allowing you to scroll seamlessly in both directions. How it Works The direction of rotation is controlled by small switches located on each end of the side pieces. Each switch has 3 positions: Center position: Rotation is locked in both directions. Side positions (Left / Right): The switch points to an arrow indicating the allowed direction of rotation. 💡 Pro Tip: Once your canvas is properly tensioned, always return the switch to the center position. When you are not actively scrolling, keep the switches centered to prevent premature wear on the locking mechanism. Bill of Materials (BOM) Item Specification Quantity Notes Aluminum Profile 20x20 mm (500 mm length used in proto) 2 pcs Must be tapped on both ends for M5 screws. M5 Screws Length depends on the depth of the profile thread 4 pcs For mounting the aluminum profiles. Self Tapping Screw BT2.6x8 SHCS 12 pcs Standard screws from the Bambu Lab store. ⚠️ Important Note on Aluminum Profiles The aluminum profiles must be tapped on both ends to accept M5 screws. Many sellers offer this as a custom cutting service, so keep this in mind when ordering. If you plan to tap the threads yourself, proceed with caution: breaking a tap inside the profile is easy to do and will ruin the part. Profile Specifications Used in this Project: Height / Width: 20 mm x 20 mm ( Actual size: 19.7 x 19.7 mm — see note below) Length: 500 mm (50 cm) Slot Width: 5.15 mm 📏 Aluminum Profile Tolerance Note: Aluminum profiles don't always have perfect dimensions. In my case, the actual measured size of the profiles was 19.7 x 19.7 mm . The entire project was designed around these exact measurements. If your profiles are larger and don't fit, please let me know! I will make the necessary adjustments to the design and publish an updated version for larger profiles. 3D Printing & Assembly Guidelines Spring Element (Colored RED in the photos): CRITICAL – This part must be printed in PETG to maintain its flexibility and spring tension over time. Canvas Clips: These clips should also be printed in PETG for durability and flexibility. Remaining Parts: Can be safely printed in standard PLA . ⚠️ Test Your Clips First! The clips that lock the canvas onto the profiles are designed to be quite tight. Before printing the entire set, please print just one clip as a test and check the fit together with your canvas. I have already included a looser version in the print profile. If it is still too tight for your specific canvas/profile setup, let me know and I will upload an even looser version.

Microgroove turns the $30 M5Stack Cardputer-ADV into a four-track groovebox: three synth tracks (each switchable between a mono 303-style voice with slide & accent, and 3-voice polyphony for chords), eight drum lanes of 808/909 synthesis or sample playback, live mic sampling, and resampling of its own output. This listing is the shell and keycap label system that makes it playable — the free, open-source firmware lives on GitHub: https://github.com/matoslav/MicroGroove It fits the M5Stack Cardputer- ADV specifically. The screen, USB-C port, and headphone jack all stay fully accessible after the swap. Printing Print with a 0.2 mm nozzle (strongly recommended). A 0.4 mm nozzle works, but the fine label text won't come out clean. The parts: Top + label top — the two-piece face. The label top is multi-color (blue / red / white). Keys — the keycaps, also multi-color. Bottom — optional. Table stand and box with instructions — optional extras. The label top and keys need a multi-color setup (AMS / multi-material or manual filament swaps). If you only print in one color, you'll still get a working shell, just without the colored labels. Assembly Glue the top and the label top together, slide in the keys, and swap the assembly for the original top your Cardputer-ADV came with. Two screws hold it in place — gluing the two face pieces matters because without it the edges lift. What the firmware does Three acid synth voices — saw/square/tri/sine plus 16 wavetables through a resonant 303 filter. Flip any track from mono squelch to 3-voice chords. Eight drum lanes — 808 and 909 synthesis or your own samples, side by side. Tune, decay, and choke each one. Sample the room — hold one key, watch the level meter, release. It's already playing on a lane. Resample yourself — bounce the live mix onto a pad and build the next layer on top. Sequence and arrange — 8 patterns of 16 steps, clone with a hold, chain up to 64 into a full song. Ready to play out of the box — the SD image on GitHub ships a five-pattern demo track and a CC0 sample pack.

Hallo an alle die den EduColon Kapselautomaten gedruckt haben oder drucken wollen, (übrigens die Fensterteile findet ihr hier: https://makerworld.com/de/models/3020347-3d-window-parts-for-the-educolon-vending-machine#profileId-3393353 ) Mein Upgrade ist passend für: https://makerworld.com/de/models/1646388-remixed-full-vending-machine-200-scale#profileId-1740186 von Naddou oder https://makerworld.com/de/models/1258546-remixed-capsule-holder-for-200-scale-educolon?from=search#profileId-1282437 von Amenthyst3D. Ich habe ihn auch voller Freude gedruckt und musste schnell feststellen, dass ein paar Verbesserungen nötig sind um den Funktionsbereich zu erweitern, die Haltbarkeit des Materials zu verlängern und mehr Coins einwerfen zu können. Als erstes stellte ich fest, dass das innen liegende Fach, welches die Coins auffängt, ein sehr kleines Volumen hat. Die Coins an sich sind ja schon mit fast 5cm im Durchmesser und 6mm dicke recht klobig und groß. So kam es bei uns nahezu immer vor, dass schon nach etwa 5 Münzeinwürfen, der Münzausgang versperrt war. Die Münze blieb dann einfach unten stecken und es verklemmte sich entweder das Drehrad, oder die Münze blieb stecken und drehte einfach durch und fuhr noch einmal mit. Das sah dann so aus: Eine sehr ungünstige Situation, gerade weil ich es für Kinder gedruckt habe und das Drehen immer leichtgängig sein muss. Dreht man dennoch mit Gewalt weiter, so bricht die Mechanik die vom Drehrad gesteuert wird und man muss den Automaten wieder mühevoll auseinander nehmen und das Teil ersetzen. Die andere Option, wenn der Coin mehrfach seine Runden in der Mechanik dreht, ist das ebenfalls blöd, denn jedes Kind möchte ja seine eigene Freude am Münzeinwurf finden. Abgesehen davon, fand ich es auch blöd, dass ich etwa 20-25 Kugeln (5cm) effektiv in den Kugelbehälter einfüllen kann (bei mehr mischt und bewegt es nicht mehr so gut) aber nur etwa 5 Münzen einwerfen kann bevor das System ins stocken gerät. Ich wollte es nicht immer nach 5 Münzen schütteln oder ausleeren. Das macht keinen Spaß. Also öffnete ich den Automaten wieder und überlegte wie ich es Verbessern kann. Dann setzte ich mich an Fusion 360 und fing an meine Gedanken in einen Volumenkörper zu verwandeln. Mein Upgrade löst diese Probleme zuverlässig und beinhaltet: 1) Eine größere Münzauffangschale als Unterbau. Der fertig gedruckte Automat kann einfach auf das zusätzliche Fach drauf gestellt werden. Der Deckel an der Unterseite des Automaten muss geöffnet werden, er wird für diesen Unterbau nicht benötigt und kann bei Seite gelegt werden. In Verbindung mit der größeren Rutsche aus 2) fallen die Coins direkt durchs Loch nach unten in die große Auffangschale. Wie ein Abfluss. So können unendlich viele Coins gesammelt werden, das Volumen ist riesig. 2) Eine größere Rutsche zum nachträglichen Einkleben (doppelseitiges Klebeband reicht schon, oder Sekundenkleber) die einen zuverlässigen und schwungvollen Abgang der Coins gewährleistet und den Ausgang vor dem Steckenbleiben schützt. Die Coins bleiben also nicht mehr am Ausgang liegen und türmen sich dort, sondern bekommen mehr Schwung, um weiter nach hinten direkt durch die Öffnung im Boden zu verschwinden und von der Auffangschale aus 1) aufgefangen zu werden. Die Rutsche ist später von außen nicht mehr sichtbar, die Farbe ist daher unwichtig. 3) Eine Transport- und Ordnungsbox mit Deckel, passend für 20 Coins. Wer mehr Coins verstauen will, kann die Box in der Höhe skalieren. Berechnungsgrundlage ist, dass 1 Coin eine Höhe von 6mm hat. Meine Coins haben einen Durchmesser von 49mm. Sie passieren die Mechanik des Automaten perfekt und passen perfekt in die Box hinein. Jedes Fach kann, dank eines integrierten Schlitzes Coin für Coin geleert werden. Man muss nicht alle zusammen ausschütten. Die Aussparungen für die Coins haben einen Durchmesser von 52mm falls ihr etwas größere Coins habt, passen diese auch. 3 kurze Hinweise zum Drucken: - der Unterbaubehälter besteht aus 2 Teilen, die mit 4 Verbindern zusammengesteckt und an den Kanten geklebt werden müssen. Die Verbinder ermöglichen eine passgenaue Ausrichtung. Der Druck benötigt keine Stützen. - Ihr könnt auch die Füllung reduzieren, damit es schneller druckt (z.B. 5% Infill mit Gyroid, das ist stabil genug) - wartet bis das Druckbett abgekühlt ist, sonst reißt ihr euch die Oberfläche runter. Hier ein direkter Vorher und Nachher Vergleich als GIF: Mit und ohne mein Upgrade: Likes, Kommentare und Bewertungen werden täglich gelesen und beantwortet. Teilt gerne Fotos eurer Drucke. Ich sehe gerne wenn meine Profile zum Leben erweckt werden.

description: Diese modulare Halterung ist die professionelle Lösung für das saubere Trocknen Ihrer bemalten oder mit Airbrush besprühten Modellteile. Das System basiert auf quadratischen und rechteckigen Platten, die mit speziellen, im Lieferumfang enthaltenen Verbindern (Connectors) beliebig erweitert werden können. Ein wesentlicher Vorteil ist zudem die Doppelfunktion der Verbinder: 1. Platten verbinden: Um die Station beliebig zu erweitern. 2. Stabilisieren: Wenn keine weitere Platte angeschlossen wird, können die Verbinder als seitliche "Stützbeine" eingesteckt werden. Dies verhindert effektiv, dass die Platte kippt, falls Sie sehr schwere oder große Teile an der gegenüberliegenden Seite zum Trocknen platzieren. ZK-1002T Amp Enclosure / “Happy Meal” Style Box This is my own version of the compact amp enclosure style often called a “Happy Meal” box. It was inspired by Bang Box Speakerz, but designed from scratch to give builders a clean, protected way to mount a ZK-1002T amplifier inside a custom speaker build. Feed the control shafts through the holes in the support plate, then reinstall the washers and nuts that came with the amp. This secures the amplifier to the outside support. The inside support uses two M4 heat inserts. Once the amp is mounted, use screws through the outside support plate to fasten everything together. For the lid, install six M4 heat inserts into the enclosure’s top mounting points, then secure the lid with M4 screws. Use a soldering iron tip or heat-insert tool to install the inserts slowly and straight. Print settings may need slight adjustment depending on your printer and insert brand. I recommend using a stronger material such as PETG or ABS/ASA if this will live inside a speaker box that may see heat, vibration, or outdoor use. description: This is a kumihimo wheel, a thing to help weave friendship braclets, regular braclets or keychains. Works best printed in TPU, but works in PLA too. How to weave? First, grab 4 strings about the same lenght and tie a knot in the middle as shown, then you will have 8 strings in total. Pull the knot through the middle of the wheel, through the biggest hole. Then, put the strings on the wheel in a cross pattern, as shown in the picture below. Now, the weaving begins. put the top left string to the bottom left. Next, put the bottom right string to the top right. Rotate the entire wheel 90 degrees counter-clockwise. Do the same thing to the other set of strings. Rotate 90 degrees, and repeat until you are happy with your keychain's length. Remove from the wheel and tie a knot at the top. Thank you for reading. Happy printing and making! description: HALO GP — MotoGP Desktop Companion Case Always know when the next session starts. No apps, no aggressive ads, no searching. Born from the foundations of Halo F1 . What is Halo GP? Halo GP is a sleek, always-on desktop companion for MotoGP fans. Built around the JC4827W543 , an ESP32 all-in-one board from Guition with a 4.3" capacitive touch display. It sits on your desk and gives you everything you need about the current MotoGP season at a glance: 🏁 Session times for the next race weekend, automatically converted to your local timezone 🏆 Drivers' championship standings , updated live 📋 Session results: qualifying, race and sprint at the moment they're published 📰 Latest MotoGP news headlines , fetched directly from the web (experimental, only english for now) 🌙 Night mode with configurable time window and brightness 🌍 Many languages : English, Italian, Spanish, French, Dutch, German and counting… No subscription. No app. No aggressive ads. Just plug it in and glance at it. About this case This is the official case for the Halo GP project. It's designed to be simple to print, simple to assemble, and good-looking on a desk. The case is a two-piece snap fit : the front and back halves slide-in together and hold the board securely with no screws, no glue, and no inserts. Disassembly takes seconds if you ever need to reflash or tinker. Designed specifically for the JC4827W543 board with its integrated 4.3" capacitive touch TFT display. Print settings Setting Recommendation Material PLA or PETG Layer height 0.2 mm Infill 15–20% gyroid Supports Yes Brim Not necessary Print time is approximately 3 hours on a typical FDM printer. No post-processing needed beyond removing the supports. Getting started with Halo GP Print this case Flash the free firmware directly from your browser (no drivers, no software) at halof1.com (select Halo GP FW) On first boot, connect to the Halo-MotoGP Wi-Fi hotspot from your phone or PC and enter your home Wi-Fi credentials Snap the case shut and put it on your desk That's it. The whole setup takes under 5 minutes. Hardware you'll need 1× JC4827W543 board with capacitive touch ( you can buy it from Aliexpress from this link ) 1× USB-C cable and a phone charger to power it Important Before You Assembly: This is the items you should receive when ordering the board. The black thing on the left is a WiFi antenna with an Ipex connector. It is very important you connect it on the back of the board, otherwise it will not get a stable connection on the WiFi. If you don't receive an antenna with your board, you can buy any Ipex Antenna from Aliexpress, Amazon, Temu, … To install the antenna, simply align it on the connector on the corner of the main chip, then press firmly. It should slot into place and stay attached. Once you place the screen into the case, simply bend the antenna to fit it in the free space at the top. Common Troubleshooting: Connect to the PC via a USB A → USB C cable, USB C → USB C cables usually don't work. Check that your cable is a data cable, otherwise you won't be able to upload the firmware. Once the firmware is uploaded you can use a power only cable to power it, if you prefer. To flash the firmware connect to halof1.com and connect your board to the PC. Go to the “Install Firmware” section and press “Connect”, then select your device's COM port from the dialog and proceed with the installation wizard. Links 🌐 Project website & firmware installer: halof1.com 💻 GitHub: github.com/FabioRoss/Halo-F1 📸 Instagram: @fabiotechgarage 👾 Discord: Discord Server If you make one, please share a photo — it genuinely makes the project worth building. Questions and feedback are always welcome. This project is a rework of the Halo F1 project and is currently hosted on the same website and GitHub repository.

description: This is a Tweak Station used to help you remove tweak from your RC 1/28th scale chassis. There are a lot of tweak videos on youtube to show you what tweak is and how to remove it from your chassis, every chassis is slightly differnt in the way this can be achieved. This design was influenced buy a few other designs already out there and by my previous setup board also available here https://makerworld.com/en/models/2449239-1-28-mini-z-setup-board#profileId-2688656 . Usage : Adjust the leveling screws to make the bubble levels in the middle centered which should mean the platform is level, then place the car with the front axel on the pivoting section at the front or the rear depending on your preference, or what you are adjusting, then adjust the car until the front bubble level is centered, which should make the car de tweaked. Required Hardware: 3 x Bubble level inserts 29x10x10mm (I'm using these: https://www.amazon.com.au/dp/B01L4PUVHQ?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title ) 5 x Flanged bearings 4x8x3mm (I'm using these: https://www.amazon.com.au/dp/B0CGXF888Y?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title&th=1 ) 1 x Carbon fibre rod 57.5-58x4mm Or a 60x4mm steel dowel pin and file it down to size, Amazon stock it but expensive probably cheaper in local hobby shop. As many as needed 4x6mm shims of various thicknesses to space out the floating plate so it wont bind or flop around to much, can be had on Amazon but might be cheaper in local hobbyshop. Assembly: 1. Start by installing the 5 flanged bearings once installed they should sit flush into the face of the print, the fit should be snug but easy to push in or with slight persuation from the back end of a set of tweezers or something else flat pushing on the flanged side of the bearing, try to keep it parallel with the face of the print. 1.1 Push both of the bearings in the main plate in from the back side. 1.2 On the flaoting plate at the back push the bearing in from the back side. 1.3 On the front of the floating plate push both bearings in from the front. 2. To assembled both parts you can line it up as shown below then push the main plate forward and it should just fall into each other, to unassembled requires a similar process in reverse, just be careful it will pull appart with no force just have to line it up, forcing can break the bearing carrier part of the main plate at the front. Thats a bad day. 3. Once the bearings are all in place and the main parts assembled you can slide the shaft in fron the front, just take it easy and use a pair of tweezers to insert the shims if you are using them as you feed the shaft through, the shaft will be captured on both ends by the bubble level inserts so the shaft must fit flush with both bearings it cannot stick out beyond the bearings or the bubble level inserts will not fit. 4. Once the shaft is installed make sure the floating plate can pivot left to right freely and inserts the bubble level inserts very carefully, they need to be lined up perfecly flat at the top of the slots and then pushed in evenly into the slots, if they start going in at an angle they wont fit and could cause damage, better to pop them out again and slide them in flat. The photo below shows the location of the shims if used via the bown arrows, they go in between the floating plate main body and the main plate body. The last step is to screw in the leveling screws, they are designed to be slightly tight the first time you insert them but will free up after that. Don't force it and make sure they are starting on a thread and will go in nicely. Thats it, enjoy.

description: DIY Handheld Wärmebildkamera – ESP32 + AMG8833 + 8×8 LED Matrix Mit diesem Projekt kannst du eine kleine DIY-Wärmebildkamera nachbauen. Zusätzlich erstellt der ESP32 ein eigenes WLAN, über das die Wärmebilddaten auch im Browser angezeigt werden können. Montagevideo Montagevideo auf YouTube ansehen Benötigte Bauteile Bauteil Menge Link ESP32 Dev Board 1× click me AMG8833 / Grid-EYE Wärmebildsensor 1× click me WS2812B 8×8 LED-Matrix 1× click me Dünne Kabel / Dupont-Kabel mehrere click me Screw M3 x 6mm 8x click me Pinbelegung Verbindung ESP32 Pin Bauteil-Pin LED-Datenleitung GPIO 5 DIN der WS2812B Matrix LED-Stromversorgung 5V / VIN 5V der WS2812B Matrix LED-GND GND GND der WS2812B Matrix AMG8833 Datenleitung GPIO 21 SDA AMG8833 Taktleitung GPIO 22 SCL AMG8833 Stromversorgung 3V3 VIN / VCC AMG8833 GND GND GND Wichtig: Alle GND-Leitungen müssen miteinander verbunden sein. Also ESP32-GND, AMG8833-GND und LED-Matrix-GND. Die LED-Matrix wird mit 5V betrieben. Der AMG8833 sollte mit 3,3V betrieben werden. Firmware vorbereiten Für die Firmware brauchst du die Arduino IDE oder PlatformIO. Benötigte Libraries: Adafruit AMG88xx FastLED ESP32 Board Package Nach dem Hochladen startet der ESP32 automatisch ein eigenes WLAN. WLAN-Name: ThermalCamera Danach mit Handy oder Laptop mit diesem WLAN verbinden und im Browser diese Adresse öffnen: http://4.3.2.1 Dort wird die Wärmebildanzeige angezeigt. Außerdem kannst du die Ausrichtung der Webansicht und der LED-Matrix direkt im Browser drehen oder spiegeln. Wichtige Code-Parameter Diese Werte kannst du im oberen Bereich des Codes anpassen: Parameter Standard Bedeutung LED_PIN 5 Datenpin der WS2812B LED-Matrix NUM_LEDS 64 Anzahl der LEDs, bei 8×8 also 64 I2C_SDA 21 SDA-Pin für den AMG8833 I2C_SCL 22 SCL-Pin für den AMG8833 SERPENTINE false Auf true setzen, wenn deine Matrix meanderförmig verdrahtet ist ORIGIN_TOP_LEFT true Legt fest, ob die erste LED oben links sitzt FLIP_X false Spiegelt die LED-Ausgabe links/rechts FLIP_Y false Spiegelt die LED-Ausgabe oben/unten BRIGHTNESS 16 Helligkeit der LEDs, 0–255 MAX_MILLIAMPS 450 Strombegrenzung für die LED-Matrix FRAME_MS 100 Bildrate, 100 ms entspricht ca. 10 FPS DEADBAND_C 3.0 Temperaturbereich um die Referenztemperatur, der schwarz bleibt MIN_SIGNAL_C 2.5 Mindest-Skalierung, reduziert Flackern bei gleichmäßiger Temperatur REF_SMOOTH 0.90 Glättung der Referenztemperatur PRINT_EVERY_N 5 Gibt jedes fünfte Frame im seriellen Monitor aus AP_SSID ThermalCamera Name des WLANs, das der ESP32 erstellt Empfindlichkeit einstellen Wenn du mehr Temperaturdetails sehen willst: #define DEADBAND_C 2.0f Wenn nur starke Wärmequellen sichtbar sein sollen: #define DEADBAND_C 4.0f Wenn die Anzeige flackert: #define REF_SMOOTH 0.95f Wenn die Reaktion schneller sein soll: #define REF_SMOOTH 0.80f Ausrichtung der LED-Matrix Falls das Bild verdreht oder gespiegelt ist, gibt es zwei Möglichkeiten: Direkt im Browser unter http://4.3.2.1 die LED-Matrix drehen oder spiegeln. Im Code diese Werte anpassen: #define SERPENTINE false #define ORIGIN_TOP_LEFT true #define FLIP_X false #define FLIP_Y false Viele 8×8 LED-Matrizen sind unterschiedlich aufgebaut. Wenn die Anzeige nicht passt, zuerst SERPENTINE ändern. Danach bei Bedarf FLIP_X oder FLIP_Y testen. Zusammenbau Gehäuseteile drucken. ESP32, AMG8833 und LED-Matrix probeweise ins Gehäuse legen. AMG8833 mit 3V3, GND, SDA und SCL verbinden. LED-Matrix mit 5V, GND und GPIO 5 verbinden. Alle GND-Leitungen miteinander verbinden. Firmware auf den ESP32 laden. Vor dem Verschließen testen, ob Sensor und LEDs funktionieren. AMG8833 so einsetzen, dass der Sensor nach vorne zeigt. LED-Matrix hinter die Frontöffnung bzw. den Diffusor setzen. Kabel sauber verlegen und Gehäuse verschließen. Mit dem WLAN ThermalCamera verbinden und http://4.3.2.1 öffnen. Falls nötig, Ausrichtung der Anzeige im Browser anpassen. Fehlerbehebung Problem Mögliche Ursache / Lösung AMG8833 wird nicht gefunden SDA/SCL vertauscht, falsche Spannung, GND fehlt LED-Matrix bleibt dunkel 5V/GND prüfen, DIN prüfen, Richtungspfeil der Matrix beachten ESP32 startet ständig neu Stromversorgung zu schwach, Helligkeit reduzieren Bild ist gespiegelt FLIP_X, FLIP_Y oder Browser-Einstellungen anpassen Bild ist um 90° verdreht Rotation im Browser ändern WLAN erscheint nicht ESP32 neu starten, Code erneut hochladen, seriellen Monitor prüfen Browser zeigt keine Daten Mit dem WLAN ThermalCamera verbinden und http://4.3.2.1 öffnen Hinweise Diese Wärmebildkamera ist ein DIY-Maker-Projekt und kein kalibriertes Messgerät. Die Anzeige eignet sich zum Visualisieren von Temperaturunterschieden, aber nicht für präzise oder sicherheitskritische Messungen. Die LED-Matrix kann je nach Helligkeit relativ viel Strom ziehen. Bei USB-Betrieb ist eine niedrige Helligkeit sinnvoll. Im Code ist die Helligkeit deshalb standardmäßig auf 16 und die Strombegrenzung auf 450 mA gesetzt.

A holder for your section style fishing rods that lets you fold up a rod with line still on so you can get back to fishing quicker when at your new location. It was made for longer flyfishing rods to make it easier to move down or upstream with a 14 foot rod by folding it in half or quarters. Assembly: Materials. All parts of the cookie, Superglue, 3mm diameter bungee cord. Step 1. Measure out a length of bungee cord around 25% shorter than the circumference of the middle of the cookie and loop it through the hole in the part. Step 2. Tie a knot on the side facing away from the “claw” and pull it inside of the cookie, Make sure the knot is about the same size as the hole there is a lip inside to hold it. step 3. loop the cord around the cookie and tie a knot at an appropriate length to hook into the “claw”, keep in mind it will need some stretch to be able to hold bigger rod sections so don't go too tight. step 4. Glue on the sides of the cookie using the pins to align them, The pins can be kept or removed when gluing is done. step 5 (extra). If you loop some normal cord through the pins holes and tie it off you can use it to hang from the ceiling or anywhere to store it. Thanks for any support and happy fishing!

If you make your own resin beads for jewellery making, you will know that nothing lets them down more that drilling the hole off centre. This tool holds your beads and ensures that when you drill them, the drill bit goes through perfectly centrally. description: Who doesn’t want Macklin Celebrini as a large brick figure!? Here is a fully articulated Macklin Celebrini brick figure that is about 8 ½” tall (20 cm). Boostez l'admission de votre moteur classique avec ce cornet d'admission (velocity stack) 100% paramétrique ! Conçu initialement pour le standard 40 mm (entraxe 65 mm) des carburateurs légendaires comme les Weber DCOE, Dell'Orto DHLA ou Solex ADDHE (ex: BX Sport, Alfa Romeo, etc.), ce modèle est entièrement modifiable via l'outil de personnalisation MakerLab pour s'adapter à n'importe quel projet . Que vous cherchiez un simple cornet droit pour votre boîte à air ou un design expérimental pour optimiser le flux d'air, tout est à portée de clic. ✨ Fonctionnalités Uniques et Personnalisables Grâce au générateur paramétrique, vous pouvez ajuster absolument toutes les cotes de la pièce sans logiciel de CAO complexe : 📏 Dimensions sur mesure : Modifiez la hauteur totale, le diamètre d'entrée (l'évasement), le diamètre intérieur de la base et l'épaisseur de la paroi. 🔧 Platine adaptable : Ajustez l'entraxe des goujons, le diamètre des trous et l'épaisseur de la platine pour correspondre à vos carburateurs ou corps papillon (ITB). 🌪️ Option "Vortex" (Style TMAX) : Cochez une simple case pour générer des ailettes internes torsadées ! Le générateur sculpte des pales parfaitement plaquées contre la paroi courbe de la trompette pour créer un flux d'air tourbillonnaire. Vous pouvez régler le nombre d'ailettes, leur épaisseur, leur profondeur et leur angle de torsion. ⛳ Option "Dimples" (Effet Balle de Golf) : Activez cette option pour creuser un motif de petites sphères en quinconce sur toute la surface interne. Cet effet aérodynamique est pensé pour perturber la couche limite et améliorer la vitesse des gaz (comme sur une balle de golf !). ⚙️ Paramètres d'Impression Recommandés Pour une utilisation dans le compartiment moteur, le choix du matériau et des paramètres est crucial pour résister à la chaleur et aux hydrocarbures. Matériau : ASA, ABS, PETG ou Nylon-Carbone (PA-CF). Évitez absolument le PLA , qui se déformerait rapidement avec la chaleur du moteur. Orientation : Imprimez la pièce à plat sur sa platine de fixation (côté moteur vers le bas). Hauteur de couche : 0.12 mm ou 0.16 mm maximum pour garantir une surface interne la plus lisse possible (crucial pour le flux d'air). Supports : Normalement inutiles si l'évasement (courbure) n'est pas trop extrême. Si vous activez l'option "Dimples", une ventilation adéquate est recommandée. Remplissage (Infill) : 100% ou un nombre important de murs (Wall loops : 4 à 6) pour garantir la solidité au niveau de la fixation. 🛠️ Assemblage Ce modèle (dans ses dimensions par défaut de 40mm) utilise la visserie M6 standard des carburateurs concernés. N'hésitez pas à partager vos réalisations, vos réglages de Vortex/Dimples, et les véhicules sur lesquels vous avez monté ces cornets dans les commentaires ! Avertissement : Pièce destinée à un usage sur circuit, compétition ou prototypage expérimental. La modification de l'admission peut nécessiter un nouveau réglage de la carburation (gicleurs) ou de la cartographie.

EcoFlow Wave 2 Wall Vent Adapter / Wanddurchführung Die EcoFlow Wave 2 ist eine fantastische mobile Klimaanlage, aber die Abluftschläuche lose aus einem Spalt im Fenster zu hängen, ist oft unpraktisch und ineffizient. Mit diesem maßgeschneiderten Wandanschluss-Set schaffst du eine saubere, permanente und professionelle Lösung – perfekt für Gartenhäuser, Werkstätten, Camper oder Tiny Houses! Das System sorgt für einen perfekten Luftaustausch durch die Wand und ersetzt provisorische Lösungen durch ein robustes, verschraubbares Design, das innen wie außen hervorragend aussieht. ✨ Design-Highlights Maßgeschneiderte Passform: Exakt auf die Abluft- und Zuluftschläuche der EcoFlow Wave 2 abgestimmt. Die Schläuche sitzen fest und sicher. Zweiteiliges System: Das Design umfasst den inneren Befestigungsring für die Schläuche sowie eine schicke Lamellenblende für die Außenwand. Integrierter Wetterschutz: Die nach unten abgewinkelten Lamellen der Außenblende verhindern zuverlässig, dass Regenwasser, Laub oder Schmutz in den Raum eindringen. Sicherer Halt: Durch die integrierten Schraublöcher lässt sich das System bombenfest im Holz oder in Gehäusewänden verankern. 🖨️ Druck-Empfehlungen Wichtiger Hinweis zur Hitze: Die Abluft der Klimaanlage wird im Betrieb sehr heiß. PLA ist für dieses Projekt ungeeignet, da es sich schnell verformen würde. Material: ABS ist für dieses Modell die absolute Top-Wahl. Es ist extrem hitzebeständig, UV-resistent (für die Außenseite) und sehr robust. Durch einen geschlossenen Bauraum lässt es sich verzugsfrei drucken. Alternativ funktioniert PETG ebenfalls hervorragend. Schichthöhe: 0.20 mm bietet die beste Balance aus Stabilität und einer sauberen Optik für die Lamellen. Wandlinien (Wall Loops): Verwende mindestens 4 bis 5 Wandlinien. Das gibt dem Adapterring die nötige Festigkeit, wenn die dicken Schläuche bewegt werden, und verhindert, dass die Schraublöcher ausreißen. Infill: 15–20% (Gyroid) sind optimal. Tipp für perfekte Überhänge: Gerade bei den Lamellen der Außenblende und den Anschlüssen ist trockenes Filament entscheidend. Frisch aus dem Filamenttrockner gedruckt, werden die Überhänge und Kanten absolut sauber, was die spätere Montage der Schläuche extrem erleichtert. 🔧 Zubehör & Montage Du benötigst: Holz- oder Blechschrauben (je nach Wandbeschaffenheit) Ich persönlich habe M-Schraubgewinde eingeschmolzen, ist aber kein muss. Optional: Etwas Silikon oder Dichtband, um die äußere Blende komplett wetterfest gegen die Wand abzudichten. Die Montage ist unkompliziert: Kreisrunde Ausschnitte an der gewünschten Stelle in die Wand sägen (z. B. mit einer Lochsäge oder Stichsäge). Die äußere Lamellenblende von außen in die Öffnung setzen und verschrauben. Den inneren Adapterring von innen fluchtend ansetzen und ebenfalls festschrauben. Die dicken EcoFlow-Schläuche in den Ring stecken. Klima an, Hitze raus!

Universal Motorcycle Chain Cleaner Box Keep your motorcycle chain clean with minimal mess. This is a 3D printable chain cleaning box designed primarily for 525 motorcycle chains (tested on my Yamaha MT-09), but it may also work with similar chain sizes. The cleaner is designed to be used with white petrol (or kerosene) , which is commonly recommended because it effectively removes grease while not damaging O-rings when used appropriately. Material: Printed in PLA . After my first intensive use with white petrol , I haven't experienced any problems or visible damage to the printed parts. Features Adjustable design that accepts many different toothbrush head shapes. Controlled cleaning fluid flow using a standard medical IV set . Easy and inexpensive to build. Compact and reusable. Required Hardware 10 × M2 x 5 mm cross recessed dome head screws 4 × toothbrush heads I used inexpensive heads purchased from Lidl. Spirograph This collection of templates represents a comprehensive set of spirographs useful for drawing curves of all kinds. What is a spirograph and how does it work? A spirograph is an instrument used to draw curves called hypotrochoids. It is based on a simple concept: a circumference that rotates in a bigger circumference in a specified ratio. In fact what is important to understand how it works is to know the number of teeth of the bigger wheel, which we call R and the number of teeth of the smaller wheel, which we call r . The nominator of fraction reduced to its lowest terms between R and r tells us the number of petals that our hypotrochoids will have while the denominator, the number of revolutions the smaller wheel will do in the bigger one. The higher the numerator and denominator, the denser hypotrochoids will be, this is likely to happen when the denominator is high and a prime number since it will not be possible to reduce the fraction. How to draw? To draw, you must select and position the large circle (the one with teeth facing inward) in the center of the sheet. Then, choose a small circle (the one with teeth facing outward) and place it inside the large circle so that the teeth mesh. Finally, insert the pen into the desired hole and begin making elliptical movements, trying to follow the path of the small circle while ensuring it never separates from the large one. How to print the model? Each print profile features a wheel R —named after the profile itself—along with smaller wheels r designed to produce a particularly interesting result when combined with that R wheel. You can therefore print the large wheel and any or all of the small wheels included in the print profile. There is nothing to stop you from using small wheels "r" from other print profiles to achieve endless variations. Documentation Before printing, you can view a preview of the designs that can be created using various combinations of large wheels (R) and small wheels (r). This is an example of what you will find in the preview; this way, you can identify a design you like and know exactly which wheel size and which wheel hole to use.
