Hi everyone, this is a personal project of mine. Please read below for more details, and feel free to reach out if you need any help with this model. TLDR: A custom-built 4-DOF desktop robotic arm designed in Solidworks. Build : Turntable base (3D-printed ball bearing race, MG996R servo) → shoulder (MG996R) → elbow (SG90) → wrist (SG90) → gripper (fingers/lever reused from a GrabCAD reference, everything else original). Code : Arduino sketch, keyboard nudges servos via a generic moveServo(index, delta) function, parallel arrays for servos/pins/angles, constrain() for safety, recenter-to-90° key. No feedback or interrupts — kept deliberately simple. Hardware : Everything is intended to be assembled with M3 hardware, sizes up to you. Whatever works best. You will need 2 SG90 and 2 MG996R servos along with the various attachments. Servos can either be superglued or screwed directly into the plastic (I tried an iteration with holes, but the hold seemed worse than just screwing the screws directly into the plastic. DISCLAIMER: Size is often not consistent for these servos and their attachments. I bought some really cheap SG90s and they were way off from the spec I was expecting. This is why I have given you access to actual CAD models, as I highly recommend tinkering, making improvements, and customizing this model to your specs. Even in my models I just found publicly available servo models which did not exactly match the ones I bought. Robotic Arm A 4-DOF desktop robotic arm designed and built from scratch as a personal engineering project. All structural components were custom-modeled in SolidWorks and 3D printed, with servo geometry measured directly from physical hardware using digital calipers. The arm is capable of planar reach-and-grasp tasks within an approximate 15–20 cm workspace and is controlled via keyboard input over serial. CAD & Mechanical Design All structural components were designed from scratch in SolidWorks/Inventor, modeled from physical hardware measurements taken with digital calipers. The arm is a 4-DOF serial manipulator with a total reach of approximately 15–20 cm. Additionally, all parts were designed for M3 hardware. While those are not found in the model, please use M3 washers on the gripper and screws throughout to ensure the best fit. For servo attachments, use the provided screws and screw them directly in the plastic. I’ve experimented drilling into holes and drilling directly in the plastic, the latter holds significantly better. Base: The circular turntable base is fully custom-designed and integrates a 3D-printed ball bearing race using 1/8" diameter balls, enabling smooth continuous rotation driven by an MG996R servo. The two-tier disc profile houses the servo internally, keeping the footprint compact. Arm Links: The shoulder and elbow joints are custom-designed structural links. The shoulder is actuated by an MG996R servo for higher-torque lifting; the elbow uses an SG90. Joint geometry and servo mounting pockets were modeled directly from caliper measurements of the physical servos — as dimensions vary slightly between manufacturers, printed parts may require minor tolerance adjustment for servos from different suppliers. Wrist & Gripper: The wrist rotation is driven by an SG90. The gripper leverages the lever arm and finger geometry from an existing GrabCAD reference design ( gripper-servo-sg90-1 ) with direct reuse of those components, modified only to adjust mounting hole sizing for fit. All surrounding structure — wrist housing, servo mounts, and interface brackets — is original. Design Inspiration: Structural layout and proportions drew loose reference from a robotics arm with feeding spoon on GrabCAD. No geometry from that model was reused directly. Programming The arm is controlled via an Arduino Uno running a keyboard-control sketch written in Arduino IDE. Each keypress nudges the corresponding servo by a fixed angle step. The four joints are mapped to two-key pairs (increase/decrease) across the keyboard, with an additional key to recenter all servos to 90°. Servo state is managed using a Servo array alongside parallel pin and angle arrays, with a single generic moveServo(index, delta) function handling all joints. Angles are clamped with constrain() to prevent out-of-range writes. The architecture is intentionally minimal — no interrupt-driven input, no position feedback. In the future, if I have time, I will add a dual-sense controller mode since joysticks tend to feel more natural. Note : The circuit diagram provided comes directly from this project which makes a 6 DoF arm. The same logic applies for a 4 DoF arm, just make sure that you are not providing power to the servos directly from the Arduino as this can potentially fry the Uno. Another future iteration would be to change the elbow joint to a more powerful servo, as the SG90 can struggle with the load when lifting an object in addition to the weight of the arm

# 🚐 Haltegriff-Upgrade für VW T5 / T6 / T6.1 – Airline-Fitting-Aufnahme & Kleiderhaken Die serienmäßigen Kunststoff-Haltegriffe im Dachhimmel sind konstruktiv nur für kurzes Zugreifen beim Einsteigen ausgelegt – nicht für dauerhaftes Anhängen von Jacken, Handtüchern oder einer quer durch den Bus gespannten Wäscheleine. Genau da setzt dieses Modell an: Es wird **unter den originalen Angstgriff** geschraubt und macht ihn zum vollwertigen Camper-Ausstattungspunkt – **ohne** die eigentliche Haltefunktion einzuschränken, ohne Bohren, ohne Kleben. Ideal für alle, die ihren California, Multivan, Caravelle, Transporter, Kombi, Kasten oder Beach zum echten Reisemobil ausbauen wollen. Mit den Original-Schrauben, in drei Minuten montiert. --- ## ✨ Features - **2× Airline-Bohrungen im Standard-Raster** – nimmt jedes handelsübliche Airline-Fitting direkt auf. Ösen-, Haken-, Ring- oder Karabiner-Fittings werden eingesteckt und verriegelt. Damit lässt sich eine Wäscheleine quer durch den Bus spannen, ein Netz einhängen oder eine schwere Jacke sicher fixieren. - **1× integrierter Kleiderhaken** – für den kleinen Alltagskram: Schlüsselbund, Sonnenbrille, Halstuch, Kappe, leichte Jacke. Immer griffbereit, ohne Zusatzhardware. - **Passgenaue Aussparungen für die Original-Schraubpunkte** – das Teil legt sich sauber um die Fixierpunkte des originalen Angstgriffs. Keine sichtbaren Modifikationen an der Verkleidung. - **Angstgriff-Funktion bleibt 100 % erhalten** – der Griff fühlt sich beim Zugreifen an wie ab Werk. Die Erweiterung wird geräusch- und rüttelfrei zwischen Dachhimmel und Griff eingeklemmt. - **Werkzeugloses Umrüsten** – Airline-Fitting kann jederzeit entnommen oder gewechselt werden (z. B. Ösen-Fitting fürs Wochenende, Haken-Fitting im Alltag). --- ## 🚗 Passend für folgende Fahrzeuge Alle VW T5, T6 und T6.1 in sämtlichen Ausbaustufen: `California` · `California Beach` · `California Ocean` · `California Coast` · `Multivan` · `Multivan PanAmericana` · `Multivan Highline / Comfortline / Trendline / Startline` · `Caravelle` · `Transporter / Kombi / Kasten` · `Shuttle` ⚠️ **Wichtig – zwei Griff-Sub-Typen im T5/T6/T6.1:** - **Version A (dieses Modell):** Passt auf den serienmäßigen Standard-Haltegriff **ohne** bereits integrierten Kleiderhaken (meist im vorderen Fahrzeugbereich verbaut). - **Version B (kommt bei entsprechender Nachfrage separat):** Für den Haltegriff **mit** werkseitig integriertem Kleiderhaken (typischerweise im hinteren Fahrzeugbereich). 👉 Bitte vor dem Druck einen Blick auf euren eigenen Griff werfen. --- ## ⚠️ Materialwahl – bitte unbedingt lesen Dieses Teil wird **im KFZ-Innenraum verbaut** und muss unter zwei Bedingungen zuverlässig funktionieren, die viele Standard-Filamente überfordern: **1. Temperatur im Fahrzeug-Innenraum** Ein VW Bus wird im Sommer hinter der Windschutzscheibe und im Dachhimmel schnell **60 °C und mehr**, in praller Sonne auch deutlich darüber. Filamente, die in diesem Bereich weich werden, verlieren unter Zuglast schlagartig ihre Formstabilität. **2. Mechanische Zugbelastung** Eine nasse Jacke, eine quer gespannte Wäscheleine mit Handtüchern oder ein Karabiner mit dranhängendem Rucksack erzeugen dauerhaft Zugkräfte – genau dort, wo das Filament am heißesten Punkt sitzt. Deshalb bitte **nur folgende Filamente** verwenden: | Filament | Empfehlung | Warum | |---|---|---| | ✅ **ASA** | **empfohlen** | UV-, temperatur- und schlagfest – Standardmaterial für Automotive-Interior | | ✅ **ABS** | empfohlen | Wärmeformbeständig bis ~95 °C, zäh | | ✅ **PA-CF / PET-CF / PAHT-CF / ASA-CF** | Premium-Wahl | Maximale Steifigkeit und Temperaturstabilität, ideal bei dauerhaft eingestecktem Airline-Fitting mit Zuglast | | ⚠️ **PETG** | **nicht empfohlen** | Wird ab ca. 70–80 °C weich (Glasübergang) – im Sommer im Bus grenzwertig, unter Zuglast riskant | | ❌ **PLA / PLA+** | **nicht verwenden** | Wird ab ca. 55–60 °C weich – im geparkten Bus im Sommer garantiert kritisch, Bauteil kann kriechen und versagen | Wer keinen gehärteten Nozzle für CF-Filamente hat: reines ASA reicht für den normalen Camping-Einsatz vollkommen aus. --- ## 🔩 Montage (3 Minuten) 1. Die beiden Torx-Schrauben des Originalgriffs herausdrehen 2. Druckteil **unter den Originalgriff** setzen – die Aussparungen im Druckteil legen sich exakt um die Original-Schraubpunkte 3. Original-Schrauben wieder eindrehen und mit Gefühl anziehen (nicht in den Dachhimmel würgen) 4. Bei Bedarf Airline-Fitting oder Karabiner einstecken – fertig 💡 **Schrauben-Hinweis:** Bei mir haben die **Originalschrauben mit Standard-Länge** einwandfrei gereicht. Sollte durch Fertigungstoleranzen oder Farbabweichung bei euch die Klemmlänge knapp werden: zwei minimal längere Torx-Schrauben mit demselben Gewinde und Kopf aus dem Baumarkt besorgen (typischerweise ~5 mm länger als Original genügt). **Sicherheitshinweis:** Während der Fahrt eingesteckte Airline-Fittings oder Karabiner entfernen – bei einem Unfall besteht sonst Verletzungsgefahr für Insassen. Das gedruckte Teil ist Zubehör für den stehenden Betrieb (Camping, Übernachten, Rangieren im Stand), keine sicherheitsrelevante Komponente. --- ## 📦 Optional erweiterbar mit - **Airline-Fitting deiner Wahl** (25-mm-Raster, EU-Standard): - **Ösen-Fitting** → für Karabiner, Seile, Wäscheleine - **Haken-Fitting** → für schwere Jacken, Handtaschen - **Ring-Fitting** → für Wäscheleine und Gurte gleichzeitig Bezugsquellen: Camper- und Bootsausrüster (Suchbegriff: „Airline Fitting", „Airline Zurrmulde", „Airline Bodenschiene Fitting"). Preis meist 3–8 € pro Stück. - **Karabinerhaken 6–8 mm** direkt für die Fitting-Öse - **Wäscheleine 3–4 mm mit zwei Karabinern** – klassisch quer durch den Bus gespannt zum Handtuchtrocknen Werkzeug für Montage: Torx (T20 oder T25, je nach VW-Baujahr). --- ## 💛 Wenn dir das Modell gefällt Ich freue mich riesig über **Make-Fotos**, ehrliche Rückmeldung und einen 👍 – und wenn dir das Modell wirklich weitergeholfen hat, würde ich mich extrem über einen **Boost** freuen. Das kostet dich nichts außer einem Klick, hilft aber enorm dabei, dass ich weiter neue Camper-Teile veröffentlichen kann. 🚀 Konstruktive Kritik, Verbesserungsvorschläge oder Fitment-Rückmeldungen zu speziellen Sub-Varianten: jederzeit gerne in die Kommentare – ich iteriere aktiv weiter. Happy printing & safe travels!

model_name: Tempest Putter - Low-Torque / Modular / High MOI
description: Tempest - A Modular 3D Printed Putter with Everything You Need Looking for a customizable putter without the price tag of today's premium designs? This project combines the flexibility of 3D printing with design features inspired by modern high-performance putters. The putter head is designed to incorporate removable weights, allowing the majority of the mass to be positioned around the perimeter. This increases the moment of inertia (MOI), helping improve stability on off-center strikes while reducing twisting through impact. One of the key features of this design is its modular construction. The shaft insert is a separate component that bolts into the main putter head, allowing different putter head designs to be swapped without needing to remove or reinstall the shaft. Simply remove a few screws, install a new head, and you're ready to go. The shaft insert has a lie angle of 74 degrees and a static loft angle of 3 degrees to match the feel of many center-shafted putters. The design of the head of the putter has been carefully made to ensure that the center of mass is aligned with the center of the face. It sits slightly in front of the center of the shaft, providing little torque when swinging. Therefore, the design of this putter naturally eliminates the majority of the torque that can open or close the face while putting. This can make it significantly easier to keep the face square at impact. To improve feel, the striking face is printed from TPU, providing a soft but responsive impact that closely resembles the insert faces found on many premium putters. Including the printed parts, added weights, screws, and epoxy, the total mass of the head of the putter is right around 320g. Features Large integrated putting alignment aids High-MOI perimeter-weighted design Center of Mass positioned to produce Low Torque when swinging Modular construction with interchangeable putter heads TPU face insert for a soft, responsive feel Removable shaft adapter secured with screws Designed for commonly available hardware and weights Inexpensive and creative alternative to traditional putters Hope you can have as much fun with this project as I did and get to give it a try out on course! For instructions, materials, and a list of parts to purchase/use, see the information below! Happy printing! Modular Design: Find other compatible putter heads here! Eclipse Putter - Low Torque / Modular / High MOI Striker Putter - A Center-Shafted Modular Putter Material Selection Body / Shaft Insert - PETG is recommended for outdoor use and to withstand higher temperatures while being relatively easy to print. Face Insert - TPU provides a soft yet confident feel when striking the ball. Assembly Be sure to read all the following steps before beginning assembly of your putter! The order in which some of these steps are taken is very important! Print all required components in your favorite colors. Be sure to print each component in its recommended material. Support removal. This step can be rather difficult due to the way the model must be printed, so my recommendation is to work from the outside inwards. I've used normal supports for the flat-bottomed sections to allow for each of the gaps for the weights to be cleared in a singular piece. Press the TPU face into the putter body. Secure it by using super glue or epoxy. Install the weights. All weights should sit flat within the head of the putter when installed correctly. A total of 30 individual 0.25oz weights are to be inserted, with 4 stacked near the face and 2 stacked in all other locations. While removing the film on the weights (making them stick) is recommended, it is not required for the putter to work great. Doing so may reduce noises heard when making contact with the ball slightly but will make it more difficult to remove the weights if interchanging putter heads. Prior to installing the bottom plate, it can be helpful to lay a layer of tape over the bottom plate and cut to size. This will reduce some noise made when putting. Install the bottom plate to the putter head at the 5 holes around the perimeter. Ensure that the side which features cutouts matching the position of the weights is facing the inserted weights. Use 5x M3 x 3/8" wood screws (link provided below for the ones used). Screws should only be hand tight, and do not over-tighten them! Cut down the putter shaft to your desired length (I cut mine down to 36in for my height). For a great step-by-step process to complete this, check out this YouTube video: How to Shorten a Putter with a Steel Shaft . Install the grip to your putter shaft. I recommend completing this step before installing the shaft adapter and putter head as there is less time to work and straighten out the grip in comparison. For a great guide to doing this, check out this other YouTube tutorial: How to Install a Putter Grip (jump to 3:00 in the video). Bolt the shaft adapter/insert into the putter head after sliding the shaft adapter into place from the top. Using 3x M3 x 3/8" wood screws, secure the bottom plate, main body, and adapter together through the bottom in the three central holes. Then, complete the installation by using one more screw in the hole near the top of the putter towards the back. Screws should only be hand tight, and do not over-tighten them! Epoxy the shaft into the adapter by applying epoxy to the shaft and sliding it in from the top. The epoxy which is suggested has a long working time which allows you to rotate the putter shaft so the the grip precisely lines up with its correct orientation. My recommendation for alignment of the grip is as follows: look down the shaft and line up the flat part of the grip with the line on top of the putter which is parallel to the direction of your stroke. Once aligned properly, wipe away any excess epoxy from the top of the putter. Let the putter sit overnight so that the epoxy can fully cure. Next step, rolling putts! Hardware & Non-Printed Parts Required Purchased Components: I've added direct links here so you can source everything needed. Shaft: 0.370in Tip Diameter Straight Stepless Putter Shaft ( Amazon Link ) - $29.95 Grip: Any putter grip should do, but the one seen in all images here is a SuperStroke Zenergy Tour 3.0 ( Amazon Link ) - $34.39 Weights: Important to uses these weights due to their exact size and 1/4oz weight ( Amazon Link ) - $6.99 Screws: M3 x 3/8" Wood Screws ( Amazon Link ) - $6.79 Required Tools/Adhesives: Links are provided in case you may need to get these. If you don't already have some of these, they are also great to have in general for a variety of projects. Epoxy: Simple JB Weld 2-Part Epoxy ( Amazon Link ) - $5.93 Steel Tube Cutter: I used a copper pipe cutter (although it worked, not recommended), but using a proper steel pipe cutter is advised if possible ( Amazon Link ) - $13.99 Total (For Required Components and Printed Parts): ~$80 USD Future Plans This modular platform was designed with expansion in mind. I plan to release additional interchangeable putter head designs that will all use the same shaft adapter, allowing you to experiment with different shapes and weight distributions without building an entirely new putter. If you build one, I'd love to see your make! Feel free to leave feedback or suggestions for future head designs. Happy printing, and good luck on the greens!

80mm to 120mm Low-Profile Fan Adapter: Short Description: This is a precision-engineered duct adapter that mounts an 80mm pc fan to a 120mm case opening. This can also be used to attach a 120mm fan to an 80mm case opening. Why this design? A flat blanking plate creates a sharp orifice that kills static pressure. A full-length funnel solves that but wastes filament and print time. This adapter splits the difference: a conical bore tapering gives you a smooth, low-turbulence airflow in a compact form factor of just 28mm that is fully self-supporting in PETG with zero internal supports. Quick specs: 120mm mount (105mm hole spacing) ↔ 80mm intake (71.5mm hole spacing) · 28mm tall · ~55g PETG · ~2 hrs print time CAD drawing: This is my first time doing a cad drawing, please forgive me for any mistakes (NOT TO SCALE) Print profiles included: PLA (0.4mm nozzle) — included for convenience, but not recommended due to risk of warping and melting PETG (0.4mm nozzle) — the recommended profile. Best balance of strength, print speed, and detail. PETG (0.6mm nozzle) — for maximum strength. Thicker extrusion lines add rigidity to the bore walls and bosses if you want extra durability or are running the adapter under mechanical stress. Test fit first — some 80mm fans and 120mm openings vary by 1-2mm from spec. Verify your hardware before printing a full batch, you can look at the cad drawings provided. Questions or fit issues? Drop a comment — happy to help troubleshoot. Thanks for taking your time to read this, and happy printing!

Supporto telefono per bicicletta e moto - versione 2.0 Questa è una nuova versione del supporto telefono che ho progettato qualche mese fa ( https://makerworld.com/it/models/2877387-phone-holder-for-bicycle-motorcycle-scooter#profileId-3213255 ). Ho migliorato un po' l'estetica e ho reso più pratico l'aggancio e lo sgancio quando si cambia l'orientamento del telefono. Rispetto al modello precedente che era fatto di soli tre pezzi, per quello attuale ho scelto di separare le graffe che avvolgono il telefono, stampandole in modo che la trazione a cui sono sottoposte agisca nel senso della lunghezza del filamento, invece che dei layer sovrapposti. Ho introdotto una nuova molla elicoidale, che migliora l'apertura delle due parti laterali, e aumentato l'infill al 90% per gli snodi e le leve di serraggio. Per unire le diverse parti ho utilizzato sia i ganci a scatto già presenti nel precedente modello, sia un nuovo sistema di inserimento con profilo a coda di rondine e bloccaggio a fine corsa. Descrizione del modello Il supporto telefono è composto da 7 particolari: morsetto di fissaggio al manubrio base fissa del supporto base mobile leva di serraggio molla elicoidale graffe laterali “A” (2 pezzi) graffe inferiori “B” (2 pezzi) Il morsetto snodato si applica al manubrio della bicicletta o della moto. L’apertura è regolabile e si adatta a barre con diametro compreso tra circa 18 e 22 mm. Per migliorare l’aderenza sulla superficie liscia del manubrio, è previsto l’utilizzo di un comune elastico di gomma, come mostrato nelle istruzioni di montaggio. Il serraggio iniziale avviene tramite la vite integrata nel morsetto; una volta raggiunta la presa corretta, il bloccaggio finale viene fatto con la leva a scatto. L'estremità del morsetto va inserita in una delle due basi del supporto per mezzo di due profili a coda di rondine, permettendo di scegliere l’orientamento del telefono in verticale o in orizzontale. La due basi scorrono tra di loro per mezzo di una guida e una barra filettata che consente la regolazione della distanza fra le graffe laterali, in base alle dimensioni dello smartphone. La barra è dotata di una leva con eccentrico e molla di contrasto per il blocco e sblocco rapido, così da poter inserire e rimuovere il telefono in modo pratico. Caratteristiche principali Supporto telefono per bici, scooter e moto leggere Morsetto regolabile per manubri da circa 18 a 22 mm Orientamento del telefono verticale o orizzontale Larghezza regolabile in base allo smartphone Leva di blocco e sblocco rapido Nessun attrezzo necessario per il montaggio Solo parti in stampa 3D, nessun altro componente in metallo Design ottimizzato per aumentare resistenza a trazione Materiali e attrezzi necessari Per completare l’assemblaggio è sufficiente aggiungere un comune elastico di gomma con diametro indicativo di circa 30-40 mm. Non sono necessari attrezzi. Consigli di stampa Il supporto è stato progettato per poter sfruttare al massimo le caratteristiche di resistenza nel senso della lunghezza del filamento, anche con materiali poco performanti. Io l'ho stampato con un comune PLA e l'ho testato sulla mia bici. Per renderlo ancora più robusto, ad esempio per l'utilizzo su moto, si può stampare in PETG, o, per chi ha stampanti più performanti della mia A1, anche in PET, ABS o PC. Istruzioni di montaggio 1. Assemblaggio dei particolari Dopo aver stampato tutti i particolari, rimuovere i supporti delle parti a sbalzo ed eliminare le piccole imperfezioni, aiutandosi se necessario con una limetta per unghie. Avvitare e svitare completamente un paio di volte le barre filettate, per eliminare gli impuntamenti. Inserire le graffe laterali “A” negli inserti a coda di rondine delle basi, spingere a fondo fino a che si avverte il “clic” del bloccaggio. Inserire i ganci delle graffe inferiori “B” nei fori delle basi, applicando una pressione uniforme (si, ci vuole parecchia forza, è normale) Accoppiare fra loro le due basi, inserendo la guida, la barra filettata e la molla. Basta avvitare la barra solo per pochi millimetri, la regolazione finale sarà fatta in seguito in base alle dimensioni del telefono. 2. Montaggio del morsetto sul manubrio Aprire lo snodo del morsetto e agganciare l’elastico di gomma tra il filetto della vite e l’estremità opposta del morsetto, facendogli fare mezza torsione in modo che rimanga in posizione. Inserire il morsetto aperto sotto il manubrio e, mentre lo si richiude, sfilare l’elastico dall’estremità opposta e agganciarlo al filetto della vite, vicino all’altro capo. Avvicinare tra loro le due estremità del morsetto e iniziare a serrare la vite girando la leva di bloccaggio. Non serrare subito a fondo: quando il morsetto inizia a fare presa sul manubrio, utilizzare la leva a scatto per il bloccaggio definitivo. Verificare che a morsetto montato, la scritta “UP” sia in alto. 2. Aggancio e sgancio del supporto A seconda che si voglia orientare il telefono in orizzontale o verticale, inserire dall'alto il supporto sul morsetto, utilizzando gli scassi a coda di rondine presenti su una o sull'altra base. Far scorrere verso il basso il supporto, fino a che si avverte il “clic” del bloccaggio. Se si desidera cambiare l'orientamento del telefono, basta tirare verso l'alto il supporto, tenendo fermo il morsetto, sfilarlo e inserirlo nello scasso dell'altra base. 3. Regolazione apertura e blocco del telefono Iniziare a serrare la barra filettata per avvicinare le graffe laterali. Inserire il telefono e continuare la regolazione fino a lasciare lo spazio sufficiente per poterlo estrarre facilmente. Verificare infine che il telefono venga bloccato correttamente agendo sulla leva. Note di sicurezza Prima di usare il supporto su strada, verificare sempre che tutte le parti siano ben agganciate, che il morsetto sia stabile sul manubrio e che il telefono sia trattenuto correttamente. Trattandosi di un oggetto stampato in 3D, la resistenza finale dipende dal materiale utilizzato, dalle impostazioni di stampa e dalla qualità della stampa stessa. Per maggiore sicurezza, soprattutto su moto, scooter o strade sconnesse, consiglio di usare anche un laccetto o un sistema di sicurezza aggiuntivo per evitare la caduta accidentale dello smartphone.

model_name: RC Trailer for WPL 1:16. scale model
description: I made this trailer to tow behind my WPL-C24 RC car. It started as a hot glued mess of random prints, and a different failed trailer. I decided I wanted to make my own design, and so this was born. I didn't go with functioning suspension for simplicity sake. That way you don't need to worry about printing fiddly leaf springs, or having to buy extra parts, and if you don't care 100% about scale accuracy, it's a lot more straight forward I've used a pin style hitch again for simplicity, you can just use a long screw or piece of wire to hold it on to the cars hitch. To attach it to a vehicle, it will need a hitch similar to the one I've provided on my rear bumper bar design for the WPL-C24 This version of the trailer uses quite a few m3 screws to hold it together. It was a trade off between ease of printing, and assembly. Depending on the response from this trailer, I'm contemplating redesigning the model to print in fewer parts, so it uses fewer screws, but I might need to think how it goes together. Printing: The model is pretty straight forward to print. PLA has been fine for my versions. Some parts will need supports, like the suspension mount, and around the lip of the trailer tray, but they are minor, and mostly any support scarring is hidden from view. You have the option of printing the tray & fenders from one colour, while printing the chassis & suspensions from a secondary colour. I've separated them onto two seperate plates Parts / BOM As well as the printed parts, you need a couple of other things. A bunch of M3 screws, and some wheels. M3 Button head screws: 4x m3x6mm for fenders 15x m3x8mm for everything else 2x 5mm hex drive wheels with a max diameter of 65mmfrom the likes of a WPL C24 kit, or replacements. 2x m2 screws to hold the wheels on. Assembly: The main assembly is pretty straight forward, screw everything together as pictured. One thing I recommend doing is attaching the hitch swivel first with the screw in the back of the cap. It is easier to do it before you attach the trailer neck to the chassis / tray. The 4 m3x6mm screws are for the fenders. If you use 6mm screws, they will fit perfectly, and not protrude into the model's tray. It's best for clearance to use button head screws for these. The rest of the screws will be the m3x8mm screws. You can get away with using up to 10mm screws for most joints if you have them, apart from the 4x holding the tray to the chassis. These screws also don't need to be button head screws, but for the sake of consistency, that is what I've used. I hope you can enjoy this model. As always, feel free to get in touch if you have suggestions to improve it, or run into issues with printing or assembling it.

Features: *Rotating turret! *Moving barrel! *Heavily detailed model with high accuracy! *Supports modified to be easy to remove *Perfectly scaled to be the size of your pocket! 😀 the hull (not including barrel) is 3.25 in (82.55 mm) long (about 1/87 scale) PRINT/ASSEMBLY ADVICE (READ BEFORE ASSEMBILING) Once the plate has cooled, gently remove the supports. They’re designed to come off easily, but take extra care around the barrel. Make sure you clear the support under the breech where the barrel meets the turret. After the supports are off, hold the connection point between the barrel and turret and move it up and down until it moves smoothly. Avoid bending the thin part of the barrel—if you must, only handle it right where it meets the turret. When it’s moving freely, click the square pin into the lower turret section. You can press it in with needle‑nose pliers or by pushing it straight down against a table. Next, place the top half of the turret on and press until the seam disappears. Historical Reference: The Dukhov KV‑4 (Object 224) was the winning SKB‑2 entry in the spring 1941 KV‑4 competition: an enlarged KV‑series hull fitted with a single large turret mounting the 107 mm ZiS‑6 gun, heavy frontal armor, and an estimated mass in the low‑to‑mid 80‑ton range. The design emerged from a rapid, internal Kirov works contest that produced some 20–27 competing proposals—many wildly different in layout and weight—as engineers raced to counter reports of new German heavy tanks, and Dukhov’s entry is the best documented because it won and left the clearest drawings. Functionally intended as a breakthrough/counter‑heavy vehicle, the Dukhov KV‑4 traded mobility and production practicality for survivability and punch, envisaging thick frontal protection, large crews and powerful engines, but like the rest of the KV‑4 family it remained a paper project cancelled after the June 1941 shift in wartime priorities. description: 🎤 VocalAIR™ – Adjustable Vocal Resistance Warm-Up Trainer Your voice is an instrument. Just like any instrument, it performs best when it's warmed up properly. After a week of prototyping, testing, refining, and obsessing over tiny details, I designed this adjustable vocal resistance trainer to provide consistent back pressure for humming, lip trills, and vocal exercises. Whether you're a singer, voice actor, public speaker, or simply someone who wants a healthier, more controlled warm-up, this tool is designed to become part of your daily routine. Unlike fixed-resistance designs, this model features 4 adjustable airflow settings , allowing you to gradually increase or decrease resistance depending on your exercise or comfort level. ✨ Features 🎚 4 Adjustable Airflow Levels Dial in the amount of resistance that feels right for your warm-up. Perfect for different vocal exercises and experience levels. 👄 Lip Retention Bump A subtle raised feature on the mouthpiece helps keep the device comfortably positioned during use without feeling intrusive. 🔑 Built-In Lanyard Loop Clip it onto your keys, backpack, microphone case, or gig bag so it's always ready before rehearsals or performances. 🧩 Simple Two-Piece Design Prints quickly. No supports. No AMS required. ⚙️ Precision Engineered Designed in Fusion 360 with extremely tight tolerances for a satisfying, secure sliding mechanism. 🖨️ Recommended Print Settings For the intended fit and feel: Recommended Layer Height: 0.08 mm Produces the smoothest slider action and most accurate fit. Acceptable Layer Height: 0.12 mm Still works well if you prefer a faster print. 🧵 Material Recommendations The main body looks fantastic in carbon fiber composite materials , but there is one important recommendation: Print the slider from a NON-carbon-fiber material such as standard PETG. Carbon fiber filaments are slightly abrasive. While a carbon fiber slider will still function, the carbon fibers rubbing against each other create noticeably more friction, resulting in a rougher sliding action. For the smoothest, most satisfying movement: Main Body → Carbon Fiber Composite (optional) Slider → Standard PETG (recommended) 🔧 Assembly Assembly only takes a few seconds. Print both pieces. Apply a thin coat of food-grade lubricant to: the inside slider track both sides of the slider A food-safe lubricant designed for meat slicers or food-processing equipment works perfectly and is inexpensive online. Using a small paintbrush makes application quick and even. Although the device will function without lubrication, it was intentionally designed with very tight tolerances. Lubrication transforms the movement from slightly grippy into a smooth, crisp, satisfying click between airflow settings. 📥 Installing the Slider Insert the slider with the wide, flat end first. Once fully installed, the retention feature locks it into place so it cannot accidentally fall out during use. This is intentional. If you ever need to remove it: Move the slider to Setting 4 Pull upward on the thumb tab Push forward until it clears the retention bump Removal requires a little force by design to prevent accidental disassembly. ❤️ Designed With Care This wasn't modeled in an afternoon. It represents roughly a week of design iterations, print testing, tolerance adjustments, and refinement to achieve a smooth mechanism, reliable fit, comfortable ergonomics, and an enjoyable user experience. Every revision taught something new, and the final design reflects countless small improvements that most people will never notice—but will absolutely feel when using it. ⭐ If You Enjoy It... If this design helps your vocal warm-ups, I'd truly appreciate: ⭐ Rating the model 👍 Leaving a Like 📸 Sharing a Make 💬 Leaving feedback or suggestions for future versions Seeing people print and use something I created is incredibly rewarding, and your support helps motivate future projects. Happy printing—and happy singing! 🎶

I designed this robotic arm from scratch to bridge that gap. My goal was to maximize structural rigidity while keeping the entire build strictly under an ultra-affordable $75 USD budget (including all 3D printing filament, electronics, bearings, and hardware). description: Improve your caravan refrigerator performance during hot summer days with this 3×120 mm fan adapter designed for Hobby caravan refrigerator ventilation grilles . Absorption refrigerators often struggle when outside temperatures become very high. Without active airflow, heat builds up behind the refrigerator, reducing cooling efficiency and causing internal temperatures to rise significantly. This adapter allows you to mount three standard 120 mm PC fans directly behind the refrigerator ventilation grille, creating a strong airflow that efficiently removes hot air from the cooling unit. For the best results, I recommend using a temperature-controlled fan controller , so the fans automatically adjust their speed depending on the refrigerator heatsink temperature. This keeps noise levels low while maximizing cooling performance when needed. During summer camping, this upgrade can significantly improve refrigerator performance, helping maintain safe food temperatures even during extended periods of hot weather. Installation requires almost no permanent modifications to the caravan. The adapter simply fits into the original ventilation grille and can easily be removed again if required. It will be installed first into the ventilation frame, then the oem grill and the oem outside shutter part. The FAN Adapter only needs a bit of the plastic support on the fwd (RH) side to be trimmed away. Due to the size printed in two parts, with alignment pins to be glued together. ⭐ Features Designed for Hobby caravan refrigerator vents (might fit others) Holds 3×120 mm fans Cable Holders for all fans plus temp. probe. I'm usually not someone who enters competitions or tries to show off my work. But the moment I saw the MakerWorld contest for the Insta360 Luna Ultra , I simply couldn't resist. Ideas started flooding my mind. I first imagined designing a complete docking station inspired by a Star Wars droid , or maybe WALL·E , since the Luna Ultra immediately reminded me of their iconic eyes. Then I considered turning the camera handle into a lightsaber hilt. There were so many possibilities... But after thinking about it for a while, I realized that wasn't the direction I wanted to take. One of the things I love most about the Insta360 Luna Ultra is its elegant simplicity and the incredible freedom of movement of its camera. I didn't want to hide those features behind a bulky accessory. Instead, I wanted to create something that would naturally become part of the camera while preserving everything that makes it special. That's how this Magnetic C-Clamp was born. The clamp easily attaches around the camera without restricting its signature movement, adding personality while keeping the original functionality completely intact. The feature I'm most proud of is the interchangeable magnetic badge system. The clamp includes a slot designed for 1×3 mm magnets , allowing you to swap decorative badges in just a few seconds. Whether you prefer something elegant, funny, geeky, minimalist or completely unique, you can change the appearance of your Luna Ultra whenever you like. As a gift, this download includes the Moon badge shown in the photos, together with a blank magnetic badge template . The blank template isn't just an extra file—it's an invitation. Design your own symbols, logos, characters, favorite games, movies, anime, pets, or anything your imagination can come up with. Print as many badges as you want and build your own collection. Because every maker has their own personality, and everyone should be free to customize their Insta360 Luna Ultra in their own way. I truly hope this project inspires you to create something even cooler than what I imagined. Magnet Slot The magnetic badge system is designed for 1×3 mm round magnets . The magnet recess has a diameter of 3.4 mm , intentionally made slightly larger than the magnet itself. This provides enough clearance to insert the magnet easily and leaves just enough room for a small drop of glue (such as CA glue or epoxy) to securely hold it in place. This makes assembly quick, simple, and reliable without requiring excessive force when inserting the magnets. Printing Recommendations For the best long-term durability, I recommend printing this model using materials that can withstand higher temperatures, such as: • ABS • ASA • PETG (good alternative) • Any other heat-resistant engineering filament PLA is suitable for testing, but if the camera is left inside a hot car or exposed to direct sunlight for extended periods, it may soften or deform over time. If you create your own magnetic badges, I'd love to see them! Feel free to share your creations and inspire other makers. #PrintForLuna #BambuLab #Insta360LunaUltra

description: Built for potters who want repeatable, precise mug sizing without performing the math themselves!! Stop eyeballing paper templates. This tool calculates the exact flat pattern for a tapered or straight-sided mug, compensates for your specific clay's shrinkage, and outputs a ready-to-print cutter - sharp blade, comfortable press rim, and built-in bracing so it holds its shape under real hand pressure. How it works Enter your target top diameter, bottom diameter, and height (or just tell it the volume you want - in mL or oz - and it'll solve the height for you, with headroom left below the rim so your coffee doesn't spill). Punch in your clay body's shrinkage percentage, and the tool mathematically "unrolls" the cone shape into the precise 2D pattern, then oversizes it so the fired mug comes out at your intended size. Features True cone-development math (not an approximation) - works for tapered mugs and straight-sided cylinder mugs alike Shrinkage compensation for any clay body (stoneware, porcelain, whatever you're working with) Set height directly, or calculate it from a target fill volume (mL or fl oz) with adjustable headroom Sharp cutting blade with a durable (non-fragile) edge, tapering up to a flared rim you can press with your palm Structural cross-ribs keep the loop rigid so it doesn't flex out of shape mid-cut Cutter has clean, rounded corners, no print artifacts Prints rim-down for the strongest bed adhesion, auto-centered and auto-rotated to fit your plate Optional bed-size check with an unmissable warning if your mug size won't fit your printer Quick start Set your top and bottom diameter and height (or switch to volume mode) Enter your clay's shrinkage % from the spec sheet Generate, print, and press into a rolled slab Trim the seam, join, and you've got a perfectly sized mug blank Want more control? Open the Advanced sections in the customizer — blade sharpness, rim grip width, rib count/bracing, and the bed-fit checker all live there. The four basics up top get you a great mug fast, but the advanced tabs are where you fine-tune it exactly to your studio and printer. Notes before you print Ignore the build plate graphic shown in the preview - it's a fixed generic size and doesn't reflect your actual printer or update with your settings. Changing a value doesn't update the model automatically - after adjusting any option, click Generate to see it reflected in the preview. Once it looks right, click Download in the top right to get your 3MF or STL. Want a real fit check for your printer? Turn on the bed-size checker in Advanced - Printer Bed Size Check - it's off by default. Print settings PETG or PLA, 100% infill on the walls (they're already thin), no supports needed. A taller cutter wall (default 20mm) makes it easier to keep your cut vertical through a thick slab. Got changes or suggestions? Want another parameter parametized? Drop me a comment below and I will see what I can do! Enjoy!

Really easy to assemble this in some minutes. a few drops of glue is needed to secure the 2 body parts, the axis caps and maybe the black keyboard keys. on top of the bottom body there are some reliefs (the golden ones). I have placed them there so if some folks have problems with wrapping on the model then this will be hide after assembly. about the profiles: One profile for the name plate. this is if you wish to make the piano more personal with the custom text. One profile for the feeder. this is the stock feeder that features 9 mm holes. if this doesn't fit your treats please customize the holes and print your feeder. the main profile has 5 plates. print them with the colors you wish! the main profile use an ams but its not necessary. you can swap the filaments for the bottom body that features another color on top and do the same with the axis caps. almost all the parts are support free! the only profile that uses some minor supports is the feeder how to customize holes: There is only one parameter you can change and this is the diameter holes of the feeder. There are 3 rows of holes and every row is configurable sepperattly. This means that if you want to slow down the food at every press you can turn tha row to have very small holes. To determine the size of holes take a caliper and measure your pet's favorite treats. click customize button. and again customize button resize the diameters on customization window at least 0,5mm to 1mm bigger than the treats. Mine max dimension was 11 so i went finally to 11,5mm diameter for the holes. It was tricky cause they are heart shaped… Now you are ready to download your custom feeder from the download button up rioght the customizer: It took me 3 tries to figure out the best holes for my cats food. So if at first you don't see move customize accordingly. how to customize text on nameplate: in the name plate profile go to objects and right click on text shape and hit edit text. this will open the text tool where you can change the text according your needs finally center the text to the sign plate by right clicking on the text_shape. note that you can change the color by right click on the text_shape object and then change filament. Assembly guide: watch the assembly video below: post process the feeder so not to have any stringing or small particles. If you will use a name plate glue it on the front face relief. glue the upper body on the bottom body. There are joints that will help you with this. tap one side of the keyboard axis with one piece of the axis cap. a drop of glue is needed. insert the piano keys one by one while pushing the key's axis to pass through the holes of the keys. attach the second axis cap with a drop of glue. Load the feeder with the food and finally slide the upper cap. The feeder is ready for your pet! how to train your cat! caspers video below: at first load the feeder and while she is hungry push the keyboard keys to drop some food. Your pet will see this some times and will eat the treats! so she will understand the function of the feeder fast! let it push your fingers if needed… Maybe this way will not be afraid of it… After 5 more tries mine learned how much force is needed for the food to drop while pressing the keyboard keys… just have some patient according to your pet. Mine is really clever cause i always make puzzles for her…. MAKE SURE TO TEST THE FEEDER BEFORE THE TRAINING! How to train you! Adjust any parameter — font, size, border, underline, or base height — and the entire model updates instantly with zero manual fixes. Whether you're producing a single custom desk sign or batch‑printing names for customers, this generator delivers consistent, professional results. 🛠️ What can you customize? ✏️ Custom Text & Fonts Choose any word and apply any installed system font. This makes filament swapping extremely easy — ideal for two‑color prints with a bold contrast between base and text. ⚙️ Automated Parametric Structure The generator uses a fully modular architecture: Main text and border are built as synchronized 2D modules Underline length is computed from text size and font metrics Base and top layers share unified Z‑height logic All positioning is handled through synchronized translation modules This ensures every part stays perfectly connected — no floating elements, no misalignment, no manual tweaking. description: I wanted to make a simple enrichment toy that would keep my cats entertained for a little longer without needing batteries or anything complicated. It also works well for other small pets that enjoy chasing treats. The 12mm dispensing holes are ideal for small kibble, although the amount released will vary depending on the size and shape of the food you use. I designed this for my own cats and it's been great watching them chase it around the room, never quite knowing where the next piece of kibble will appear. I hope your pets enjoy it too!

description: A modular picture frame system that fits any canvas size. Print the corners and connectors once, then generate custom rail segments to match your artwork dimensions. Canvas clips lock the artwork in place from the back without glue. A small drop of CA glue on the connector pins is recommended for a permanent frame joint. Works with canvas depth of 10mm or more. Four plate types included in default print profile Corners are fixed parts that connect the frame at 90 degrees. Each corner takes up 65mm on each side it connects to. Print 4 for any frame. Connectors are the printed pins that join rails to corners. Print one connector per part, corners and rails combined. For example, 4 corners and 6 rails need 10 connectors total. Canvas clips are retaining pins that hold the artwork securely in the frame recess from the back. Each corner has 2 clip holes and each rail has 1. Print one clip per hole for maximum hold. Note: one hole on the top rail is reserved for wall hanging. Frame rails are the straight segments generated to your dimensions. Two generators are included Frame Side Generator calculates the rail length from your canvas size, Single Frame Rail Generator lets you enter an exact length for replacement parts or custom segments. How to use Frame Side Generator Enter your canvas side length in mm. Minimum 170mm. Enter the number of rail segments for that side. Aim for at least 40mm per segment, otherwise the connector pins won't fit. The generator calculates the segment length: (canvas length - 130) / number of segments. Click a generated part in the preview to confirm its exact length before printing. Repeat for the other side if your frame is not square. How to use Single Frame Rail Generator Enter the exact rail length you need. Minimum 40mm. Use this for replacement parts or when you already know the dimensions. Material notes PLA works well for most sizes. For larger frames (above approximately 400mm per side) consider PETG or a stronger material for better rigidity. Assembly Apply a small drop of CA glue to each connector pin before pressing into the corner sockets and rail ends. Slide the rails and corners together and let the glue set. Place your canvas in the recess and insert the canvas clips to lock it in place. If you print it, please leave a rating - it helps a lot.

Basic Settings - Tray Length & Width: Maximum exterior dimensions of the tray (mm). - Base Thickness: Thickness of the base along the Z-axis. - Cut Inner Hearts: Enables boolean subtraction to remove the inner portion of the hearts, yielding a smooth interior wall. - Alternating Layers: Enables horizontal offset (half-step) on even layers, aligning geometry in a brick pattern. - Number of Layers: Quantity of heart rings stacked along the Z-axis. - Heart Base Size: Size of the heart (mm). The script recalculates the perimeter and automatically adjusts the instance count. 2. Engraving & Text Settings - Enable Top Text: Adds embossed (raised) text to the center of the base's top face. - Enable Bottom Logo: Adds debossed (engraved) text to the base's bottom face. 3. Advanced Settings For users who want fine-grained control over mesh and placement: - Heart Width / Thickness / Height Ratio: Individual scale of the heart on its local X, Y, and Z axes. - Heart Size Multiplier: Global scale (XYZ) applied to the heart. - Heart Facing Rotation: Angular rotation (local Z-axis) of each heart at its origin. - Heart Z Offset: Z-axis displacement of the heart layers. Negative values intersect with Z=0 (cut plane), generating a flat bed adhesion area. - Heart Radial Offset: Radial displacement of the anchor line. Negative values increase volumetric intersection with the base. - Lateral and Vertical Overlap Factor: Interpenetration rate between adjacent instances. --- TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS & PRINTING --- - Clean Printing Base: The parametric bottom is cut perfectly flat on the Z-axis, ensuring maximum bed adhesion without the fragility of the heart tips. - Support-Free: The design ensures progressive overhangs without the need for any supports in FDM printing. - Premium Finish Tip: For a wonderful textured ceramic look, enable the "Fuzzy Skin" option on the outer contour in your slicer! description: BONBON Capsule Cooling Surprise | Mini Ice Pack + Real Reward Concept A slim reusable refillable ice pack concept designed for cooler bags, lunch boxes, camping, travel, outdoor family use, and simple DIY summer cooling setups. BONBON contest concept This entry is designed as a capsule surprise idea with two versions: a mini capsule-size version that fits inside the BONBON capsule as the surprise item a larger real-size version that can be used as a practical reusable ice pack The mini version represents the small capsule surprise, while the larger version shows the real functional cooling product that the surprise can unlock, represent, or be redeemed for. Important Capsule Fit Note This model is designed for the BONBON 2.7-inch capsule contest. https://makerworld.com/uk/models/2566374-bonbon-2-7-inch-capsule-content-checker The capsule checker shown in the photos was taken from the contest host/creator’s MakerWorld profile and used to test the model size. The model was checked inside the contest-size checker to confirm the fit. How to use Fill it partly with water, leave enough empty space for ice expansion, freeze it, and use it as a flat cooling block. The slim rounded shape makes it easy to place inside a cooler bag, lunch bag, backpack pocket, or near small DIY cooling setups where a flatter ice pack is more convenient than a bulky block. This design uses a recessed filling area and a separate cap, helping keep the overall shape compact and easy to handle. The ice pack uses an internal honeycomb-style structure to help divide the water volume into smaller sections and support the flat walls during freezing. This helps reduce deformation and stress from ice expansion while keeping the model slim and lightweight. Important Do not fill completely. Water expands when frozen. Always leave empty space inside before freezing. The internal structure does not mean the model can be filled completely. It only helps support the shape and divide the water volume. This is a 3D printed container, so always test for leaks before using it near electronics, food, bags, or temperature-sensitive items. Leak / material preparation note Possible leaks are not automatically caused by the model design. This is a functional 3D printed container, so water-tightness depends heavily on the material, printer condition, slicer settings, and calibration. Before using the ice pack, make sure your filament is properly dried, especially PETG, and that your printer is calibrated for that exact material. Incorrect flow, too high or too low temperature, poor layer bonding, wet filament, under-extrusion, weak walls, dirty nozzle, or modified print settings can all cause leaks. description: # macOS Folder Desk Organizer - 2-Slot Invoice Tracker A desk organizer inspired by the classic macOS folder icon — but with a purpose: track invoices and receipts through a simple two-step workflow instead of letting them pile up. ## The idea Two separate slots, one clear workflow: - **Slot 1**: invoices/receipts submitted to your health insurance - **Slot 2**: invoices/receipts submitted to your private/supplemental insurance Move a document from slot 1 to slot 2 (or wherever fits your process) and always know at a glance what's been submitted where — no more digging through a drawer to check if something's already been filed. Please note that the structural grip in this V1 isn't perfect, precisely because the thin walls required for illumination make it tricky to design robust joints at this scale. 🛠️ Assembly Instructions Before starting: If you feel you need glue, use it! If you don't plan on taking the rocket apart, gluing is the best option. 🧴 Joystick: Assemble the joystick background together with its buttons. 🕹️ Wiring: Remove the power cable from the levitation kit's motherboard, but leave the mini-board (touch button) connected. ⚡ Power plug: Insert the power plug into the back cover (as shown in the photo) and route it upwards through the internal hole. If you swipe your finger on the outside of that area, the button will activate when the UFO is levitating on the base! 👆💡 Base: Assemble the walls to the base of the rocket (glue is recommended). 🏗️ Floor: Next, cover the magnetic base with the floor piece you decided to print ( DO NOT GLUE THIS PART! ). 🚫🧴 Claw: If the tolerance is too loose, you can glue the claw to the top of the rocket; otherwise, just snap it into place. I recommend placing the open claws facing forward, as seen in the photo. 🦞 Top section: Join the top part with the walls (glue recommended). 🚀 🛸 Let's build the UFO! (It's very simple) Place the copper piece at the bottom, followed by the spacer, and then the metal piece with the magnet. Leave the light on top and cover it with the cap so it doesn't move. 💡 Drop the top shell onto the bottom one, adjust it slightly, and you're done! As mentioned before, it's designed this way to allow the light to shine through. I’ll try to create an improved V2 later. 🔄 FOR NON-AMS ONLY: You will need a tiny drop of glue for both the floor and the windows. Be careful, I know it can be a bit tricky! 🤏 🎯 Final Setup Once everything is assembled, carefully lower the UFO right in the center, as close to the claw as possible. You'll hear a characteristic sound when it locks into the levitation point. Then, just place your favorite mini-figure on top!!! 🤠👾 I have created quite a few of them » HERE « , take a look and print whichever ones you like! 🖨️ ✨I hope you all like it! 🦖 Best regards. 🟢Don't forget you can follow me on Instagram as @Jotas3D ^^ 📸 ⚠️ » HERE « for Toy Story Logo ⚠️

Modeled after a vintage mechanical typewriter, it completely encloses a standard paper towel roll, feeding it perfectly through the top slot. description: Check out my newly released models: Product Description Meet the Self-Locking Towel Holder — a minimalist, wall-mounted accessory that keeps your towel exactly where you want it, using nothing but gravity and a clever internal ball mechanism. No hooks to snag on, no clips to fiddle with, no adhesives on the fabric. Just push the towel in, and it holds itself. How It Works Inside the arched body sits a free-rolling ball housed in a tapered channel. The mechanism works in three intuitive steps: Insert — Push the edge of the towel upward into the slot from below. The ball lifts out of the way, letting the fabric pass through easily. Lock — As soon as you let go, the towel naturally pulls downward. The ball rolls down with it and wedges the fabric against the tapered wall of the channel, gripping it firmly. The harder the towel pulls, the tighter the hold. Release — To remove the towel, simply pull it sideways (horizontally) instead of down. This motion disengages the ball from the wedge zone, instantly releasing the fabric with zero effort. It's a purely mechanical, gravity-driven design — no springs, no magnets, no moving parts to wear out beyond a single ball. Key Features 🪝 One-handed operation — insert and release with a single motion 🎨 Warm brown finish — pairs beautifully with neutral, Japandi, or earth-tone bathroom interiors 🧺 Universal fit — works with hand towels, tea towels, dish cloths, and thin bath towels 🌊 Bathroom & kitchen ready — great next to the sink, shower, or by the stove 🔩 Minimal footprint — the compact arched profile takes up almost no wall space 🛠️ Easy install — double-sided tape Why You'll Love It No more towels sliding off hooks or bunching up on bars. This holder embraces the beauty of simple physics — the more your towel wants to fall, the more securely it stays. A tiny piece of engineering that quietly does its job, every single day.

description: # 🌿 Philodendron Melanochrysum Selbstbewässerungs-Topfset – S, M, L & XL Dieses Set wurde speziell entwickelt, damit die Töpfe **nicht skaliert werden müssen**. Wer schon einmal dekorative Pflanzentöpfe mit aufwendigen Blattmotiven skaliert hat, kennt das Problem: Wandstärken verändern sich, Details werden unsauber und das Design verliert an Wirkung. Deshalb erhältst du hier vier separat angepasste Größen, die jeweils speziell für ihre Größe optimiert wurden. Jeder Topf trägt ein plastisch ausgearbeitetes **Philodendron Melanochrysum Blatt**, das besonders bei einfarbigen Drucken hervorragend zur Geltung kommt und den Töpfen ihren charakteristischen Look verleiht. --- # 💧 Selbstbewässerungssystem Alle Größen wurden für die Nutzung als Selbstbewässerungstopf ausgelegt. Der eigentliche Pflanztopf sitzt im oberen Bereich. Darunter befindet sich ein separates Wasserreservoir. Über einen Kapillardocht, der durch die Bodenöffnungen des Orchideen- oder Aroid-Topfes geführt wird, kann die Pflanze selbstständig Wasser aus dem Reservoir aufnehmen. Dadurch wird eine gleichmäßige Wasserversorgung ermöglicht und die Gießintervalle können deutlich verlängert werden. Bei allen Größen wurde darauf geachtet, dass die Innentöpfe bequem von oben entnommen werden können, ohne im Topfinneren hantieren zu müssen. --- # 👀 Sichtfenster (optional) Auf der Rückseite befindet sich ein Sichtfenster, durch das sich Wasserstand und Wurzelentwicklung bequem kontrollieren lassen, ohne den Innentopf herausnehmen zu müssen. Das Sichtfenster ist als optionales Negativ ausgeführt und kann im Bambu Studio bei Bedarf aktiviert oder deaktiviert werden. ### Mit Sichtfenster ✅ Kontrolle des Wasserstands ✅ Kontrolle der Wurzelentwicklung ✅ Ideal für Orchideen, Alocasien und andere Aroid-Pflanzen ### Ohne Sichtfenster ✅ Geschlossene Außenwand ✅ Nutzung als Dekoration ✅ Nutzung als Vase ✅ Nutzung als Stiftehalter ✅ Nutzung als allgemeines Aufbewahrungsgefäß --- # 📏 Größen ## Größe S * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **6 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **100 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Einfaches Einsetzen und Herausnehmen des Innentopfes --- ## Größe M * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **7,6 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **200 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Einfaches Einsetzen und Herausnehmen des Innentopfes --- ## Größe L * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **9 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **400 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Ideal für größere Pflanzen mit höherem Wasserbedarf --- ## Größe XL * Passend für einen **10 cm Aroid-Topf** * Der Aroid-Topf ist tiefer und ragt bewusst leicht über den oberen Rand hinaus * Dadurch lässt sich der Innentopf besonders komfortabel entnehmen * Wasserreservoir: **500 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Aroid-Topf geführt werden zum Beispiel: Becher: https://amzn.eu/d/01GtIsBM https://www.variegata.de/produkt/toepfchen-der-toepfe/ AROID TÖPFE https://www.sybotanica.com/de-de/products/dursichtiger-plfanzentopf S und m 9 cm Klarsicht-Orchideentopf https://www.obi.de/p/2807519/ --- # ⚠️ Wichtiger Hinweis Die Druckdateien enthalten ausschließlich die dekorativen Außentöpfe. Dieser Topf löst beides. Das Prinzip: Im Boden des Außentopfs sitzt ein großes Wasserreservoir. Der Innentopf steht darüber; sein Boden hat Belüftungs- und Drainagelöcher. Drei Erdsäulen reichen vom Innentopf in den Wasserspeicher – die Erde in ihnen dochtet selbst, ganz ohne Zusatzmaterial, das faulen kann. Ein Überlauf hält den Wasserstand knapp unter dem Innentopf-Boden: Das Reservoir kann nicht in die Erde überlaufen, überschüssiges Gießwasser läuft ab. Ergebnis: konstant feucht, nie nass, Wurzeln bekommen Sauerstoff. Genau die Bedingungen, unter denen Basilikum zum Busch wird statt einzugehen. Praxistest bestanden: Ein handelsüblicher Supermarkt-Basilikum ist darin innerhalb weniger Wochen zum kompletten Busch herangewachsen (siehe Vorher/Nachher-Foto). Features Echtes SIP-Prinzip – Wasser und Erde getrennt, Wasseraufnahme nur über die Erdsäulen; kein Wurzelfäule-Risiko durch Staunässe Selbst-dochtende Erdsäulen – kein Baumwolldocht, nichts, was verrottet Überlaufschutz – hält den Wasserstand knapp unter dem Innentopf-Boden, kann nicht überlaufen; überschüssiges Gießwasser läuft ab Füll-Kerbe am Rand zum sauberen Nachgießen ins Reservoir Belüftungs-/Drainagelöcher im Innenboden für Sauerstoff an den Wurzeln Großes 2L-Reservoir – Standzeit gut eine Woche ~130 mm Erdtiefe – echtes Wurzelvolumen für Basilikum, Minze, Petersilie & Co. Facettiertes Design – modern, druckt sauber Technische Daten Außendurchmesser 202 mm (facettiert, rund) plus einseitig 17mm für die Eingießtülle Innendurchmesser 183 mm Gesamthöhe: 206 mm Erdtiefe: ca. 130 mm Überlauf: 66 mm ab Innenboden Reservoir (nutzbar bis Überlauf): ca. 2L → Standzeit gut 1 Woche, je nach Pflanzengröße und Standort Teile Außentopf – Reservoir + facettierte Wand Innentopf – Erde, Belüftungslöcher, Aufnahmen für die Erdsäulen Erdsäulen (3 Stück) – separate Dochtsäulen, werden in den Innentopf eingesetzt (können eingeklebt werden, müssen aber nicht – siehe Montage) Montage Erdsäulen in die vorgesehenen Aufnahmen des Innentopfs einsetzen. Einkleben ist optional – wenn der Innentopf im zusammengesetzten Zustand (im Außentopf sitzend) mit Erde befüllt wird, hält der Erddruck die Säulen von selbst an Ort und Stelle. Innentopf in den Außentopf setzen – der Flansch liegt auf dem Rand des Außentopfs auf. Erde einfüllen, dabei die Erdsäulen mit Erde füllen (nicht hohl lassen – sie sind der Docht ins Reservoir). Erste Bewässerung von oben angießen, damit sich die Erdsäulen vollsaugen. Danach übers Reservoir über die Füll-Kerbe nachfüllen. Pflege-Tipps Etwa wöchentlich über die Füll-Kerbe nachfüllen, bis Wasser am Überlauf austritt – der Überlauf verhindert Überfüllen von selbst. Kurze Trockenphasen sind gesund, das Reservoir nicht dauerhaft randvoll halten. Für buschigen Wuchs die Haupttriebe über einem Blattpaar auskneifen. Blütenstände früh abknipsen – blühender Basilikum wird bitter.

description: PhotoMag – Turn Your Images into Printable Fridge Magnets for free PhotoMag is an image-to-3MF generator, it turns a PNG, JPG or SVG into a print-ready 3MF with hidden magnet cavities. You do not need CAD, and the image is processed locally in your browser. Completely free, with no account or sign-up required. Link to Generator: here How to use the tool: This guide covers the main web page, the settings worth changing, what PRINT FROM means, and how to insert magnets safely. The Image parts section is intentionally not covered yet. 1. Upload your artwork Click Upload or drop PNG, JPG, or SVG , or use the sample to learn the controls first. For the cleanest result: - Use a clear subject with a simple or transparent background. - Keep Remove background on for most isolated subjects. Turn it off if it removes pale or white details that you want to keep. - The current base shape is Silhouette , so the outside edge of the artwork becomes the magnet outline. - Dark pixels are raised by default. Turn on Invert relief if you want the light areas to be raised instead. 2. Choose the size and artwork depth Width is the final width of the magnet in millimetres. The height follows the image aspect ratio automatically. Artwork depth controls how far the artwork rises from the base. Start at the default 0.8 mm . A practical starting range is 0.6 to 1.0 mm. Very tall relief can make fine artwork steeper and harder to print, and the generator warns above 1.6 mm . 3. Set the magnet cavities PRINT FROM means which face touches the build plate and is printed first. Artwork first is the recommended default: - The artwork face sits on the build plate. - The model may look face-down in the slicer. That is intentional . - The printer pauses while the cavities are still open from the back. - You insert the magnets and resume the print, then the final back layers seal them inside. Back first : - The sealed back face sits on the build plate. - The artwork is printed later on top. - Use this ONLY when you deliberately prefer that surface or filament sequence. Diameter and thickness Measure the real magnet with callipers rather than trusting the packet. For a magnet sold as 4 x 2 mm, start by entering : - Diameter: 4.0 mm - Thickness: 2.2 mm (please leave 2mm for better sitting, it will be explained later) note: Magnets, printers and first layers all vary slightly. Do not design the overall print to exactly the advertised magnet size. Leave roughly 0.2 mm of real-world headroom and test the fit on your own printer before committing to a large print. Diameter clearance is added to the magnet diameter to make the pocket wide enough. - If the test pocket is too tight, increase the diameter clearance by 0.1mm a time. - If the magnet is very loose, do the opposite. - Remember to change this in small steps and test again. 4. Generate the model and print Click Generate clean 3MF . Inspect the artwork preview and make sure the outline and relief look sensible. Open the downloaded 3MF in Bambu Studio, slicer the plate and double check that the pause is added to the correct location, at the pause, the magnet cavities should be fully open. The next layers should begin sealing them. 5. Insert magnet at pause Prepare the magnets before the print reaches the pause. If you use more than one, mark one face so their polarity stays consistent. When the printer pauses: Leave the bed and toolhead in their paused positions. Put a TINY drop of super glue in each cavity. Too much glue can stop the magnet sitting flat. Insert each magnet with a non-metallic tool if possible. Press it fully into the cavity. It must sit flush or slightly below the surrounding plastic, never in the nozzle path. Give the glue a moment to hold . This matters because metal around the toolhead can pull a loose magnet back out . If a magnet rocks, floats or sits proud of the cavity, do not resume . Remove it, correct the fit and make sure the nozzle path is clear first. Hope you get a good printing result and don't forget to share your creation!

I've been growing herbs and strawberries in hydroponic towers at home for a long time. But classic tower models had many drawbacks: they were too noisy due to the sound of falling water, poorly irrigated the upper tiers of plants due to their imperfect design, have no lights and took up a lot of space. So I decided to develop my own design that eliminated these drawbacks. I combined NFT hydroponics and a traditional tower to create a spiral plant nutrition system. I also designed the tower for corner installation so it would take up a quarter of the space of a traditional circular tower. I also added many improvements, which I detailed in my YouTube video: For assembly, you will need: 1) a water tank. I used a plastic bucket from a local marketplace with a diameter of 295 mm and a capacity of 18 liters https://ozon.ru/t/yCqJQjw. 2) a pump with a capacity of 800 liters per hour and a water lift of 160 cm https://ali.click/jlwlg1u. 3) a silicone hose with an internal diameter of 12 mm and a length of 150 cm https://ali.click/z0xlg1z. 4) two 45-watt grow lights 105 x 40 x 35 cm, or four 55cm length with metal buckles https://ali.click/1sxlg16. 5) a 1-meter cable for connecting the lights and a 3-pin timer https://ali.click/pfylg19 https://ali.click/8sylg1v. 6) 45 x 45 mm agrowool plugs for green seeds, or foam glass for strawberries. You'll need total 3 kg of PETG plastic for printing, and I recommend using Bambu Lab PETG HF. I'm not sure why, but the locks on the parts work better with it than with PETG Basic. For now, all the tower parts are designed for printing on H2 series printers. But you can support my project using the link in my profile, and I'll make a model for printing on standard Bambu Lab A1/P/X series printers.

To ensure the best performance and durability, please keep the following recommendations in mind. Filament Choice Choosing the right filament is essential. Filaments with additives such as silk, matte, wood, or similar effects are generally more brittle and less durable than standard materials, making the opener more likely to fail under load. For the most reliable results, standard PLA is highly recommended. Recommended Material The opener base performs best when printed in regular PLA . It is stiff, resists bending, and provides the precise fit needed to open bottles reliably. PETG is also suitable, but keep in mind that it is significantly more flexible and will bend more under load. Wer schon einmal dekorative Pflanzentöpfe mit aufwendigen Blattmotiven skaliert hat, kennt das Problem: Wandstärken verändern sich, Details werden unsauber und das Design verliert an Wirkung. Deshalb erhältst du hier vier separat angepasste Größen, die jeweils speziell für ihre Größe optimiert wurden. Jeder Topf trägt ein plastisch ausgearbeitetes **Alocasia Nobilis Blatt**, das besonders bei einfarbigen Drucken hervorragend zur Geltung kommt und den Töpfen ihren charakteristischen Look verleiht. --- # 💧 Selbstbewässerungssystem Alle Größen wurden für die Nutzung als Selbstbewässerungstopf ausgelegt. Der eigentliche Pflanztopf sitzt im oberen Bereich. Darunter befindet sich ein separates Wasserreservoir. Über einen Kapillardocht, der durch die Bodenöffnungen des Orchideen- oder Aroid-Topfes geführt wird, kann die Pflanze selbstständig Wasser aus dem Reservoir aufnehmen. Dadurch wird eine gleichmäßige Wasserversorgung ermöglicht und die Gießintervalle können deutlich verlängert werden. Bei allen Größen wurde darauf geachtet, dass die Innentöpfe bequem von oben entnommen werden können, ohne im Topfinneren hantieren zu müssen. --- # 👀 Sichtfenster (optional) Auf der Rückseite befindet sich ein Sichtfenster, durch das sich Wasserstand und Wurzelentwicklung bequem kontrollieren lassen, ohne den Innentopf herausnehmen zu müssen. Das Sichtfenster ist als optionales Negativ ausgeführt und kann im Bambu Studio bei Bedarf aktiviert oder deaktiviert werden. ### Mit Sichtfenster ✅ Kontrolle des Wasserstands ✅ Kontrolle der Wurzelentwicklung ✅ Ideal für Orchideen, Alocasien und andere Aroid-Pflanzen ### Ohne Sichtfenster ✅ Geschlossene Außenwand ✅ Nutzung als Dekoration ✅ Nutzung als Vase ✅ Nutzung als Stiftehalter ✅ Nutzung als allgemeines Aufbewahrungsgefäß --- # 📏 Größen ## Größe S * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **6 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **100 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Einfaches Einsetzen und Herausnehmen des Innentopfes --- ## Größe M * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **7,6 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **200 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Einfaches Einsetzen und Herausnehmen des Innentopfes --- ## Größe L * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **9 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **400 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Ideal für größere Pflanzen mit höherem Wasserbedarf --- ## Größe XL * Passend für einen **10 cm Aroid-Topf** * Der Aroid-Topf ist tiefer und ragt bewusst leicht über den oberen Rand hinaus * Dadurch lässt sich der Innentopf besonders komfortabel entnehmen * Wasserreservoir: **500 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Aroid-Topf geführt werden zum Beispiel: Becher: https://amzn.eu/d/01GtIsBM https://www.variegata.de/produkt/toepfchen-der-toepfe/ AROID TÖPFE https://www.sybotanica.com/de-de/products/dursichtiger-plfanzentopf S und m 9 cm Klarsicht-Orchideentopf https://www.obi.de/p/2807519/ --- # ⚠️ Wichtiger Hinweis Die Druckdateien enthalten ausschließlich die dekorativen Außentöpfe. Folgende Komponenten sind **nicht Bestandteil der STL-Dateien**: * Orchideentöpfe * Aroid-Töpfe * Kunststoffbecher für die Wasserreservoirs * Kapillardocht Diese Komponenten müssen separat beschafft werden. Die benötigten Orchideentöpfe, Aroid-Töpfe, Kunststoffbecher sowie Kapillardochte sind problemlos beim großen A erhältlich. Die Außentöpfe dienen als dekorative Hülle und verwandeln einfache Pflanzgefäße in ein optisch ansprechendes Selbstbewässerungssystem. --- # 🖨️ Druckhinweise * Kein Skalieren erforderlich * Jede Größe wurde separat angepasst * Optimierte Wandstärken für jede Größe * Optimierte Blattdetails für jede Größe * Für PLA, PLA+, PETG und vergleichbare Materialien geeignet * Für optimale Ergebnisse wird eine feine Schichthöhe empfohlen --- # 📜 Lizenz Diese Dateien sind grundsätzlich ausschließlich für den privaten Gebrauch bestimmt. Achtung, 2 Punkte sind wichtig! Ich wurde gefragt, ob ich Größe VI erstellen kann. Das habe ich gerne getan, allerdings habe ich keine Pumpe bzw. Lay-Z-Spa-Kartuschenhalter hier, um Funktion und Passgenauigkeit zu prüfen. Falls etwas nicht passt, gebt mir bitte schnellstmöglich eine Rückmeldung und ich bessere nach. Da ich den inneren Bereich nicht verjüngen kann und nach außen hin wohl auch kein Platz ist, ist der Raum für die Filterbälle recht klein. Wenn Filterbälle hineinpassen: Perfekt! Wenn nicht, dann müsst Ihr nach Alternativen Ausschau halten; ich denke da an Schaumstoff-Filtereinsätze oder Ähnliches. In meinem Fall (siehe Bild) bekomme ich die Bälle gerade so in den Korb gedrückt. Und nun mein Standard-Text… Ich bin diese nervigen Kartuschenfilter einfach leid gewesen. Auf Sandfilter wollte ich nicht unbedingt umsteigen, da die “normalen” Filterpumpen an sich ja gut funktionieren; vor allem bei kleineren Pools sind diese auch vollkommen ausreichend. Ich dachte mir daher, dass ich das Problem einfach mittels CAD und 3D Drucker selber löse. Herausgekommen sind Filterkörbe in den Größen I, II, III, IV und nun auch in Größe VI. Das Teil hat bei den ganzen Löchern natürlich unglaublich viele Außenwände, so dass bei 0,2mm Schichthöhe recht lange Druckzeiten entstehen. Ich stelle Euch das Modell mit meinen Einstellungen zur Verfügung - fühlt Euch frei, z.B. die Schichthöhe und/oder die Druckgeschwindigkeit zu erhöhen (natürlich auf eigene Gefahr 😉). Über Bilder und Bewertungen freue ich mich natürlich sehr! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
