🌐 Internet Connection Monitor 24H The project that finally proved my Internet provider was wrong. Have you ever had random Internet dropouts that magically disappeared every time the technician arrived? I did. For almost three weeks my Internet connection kept randomly disconnecting. Video calls froze, downloads stopped, smart home devices went offline... but every time I called my ISP the answer was always the same: "Everything looks perfect from our side." And of course... When the technician came to my house... The connection was perfect. So I decided to build something that could monitor my Internet connection 24 hours a day , collect real data, and prove what was really happening. That is how this project was born. After a few days of continuous monitoring, the graphs clearly showed that the connection randomly died for short periods before automatically recovering. Those historical logs finally convinced the provider to investigate further. The real culprit? A faulty modem/router that randomly crashed and reconnected. Three weeks of frustration... Solved thanks to a tiny ESP32. What does it do? This standalone monitor continuously checks your Internet connection without requiring a PC. It periodically performs: ✅ HTTP connectivity tests ✅ Ping / Latency measurements ✅ Wi-Fi RSSI monitoring ✅ Connection Health calculation ✅ 24-hour historical logging Everything is displayed on a beautiful touchscreen interface. HOME Screen The main page always shows: Internet status (UP / UNSTABLE / DOWN) Connection Health (%) HTTP Connectivity Network Latency (Ping) Wi-Fi Signal Strength (RSSI) IP Address Immediate RGB status indication 24-Hour History Touch the display to open the historical graphs. You can instantly see: Internet quality over the last 24 hours Ping history Connection stability Drops and recovery events Sometimes a connection that "looks fine" at the exact moment you're checking it tells a completely different story over an entire day. And that's exactly the purpose of this project. RGB Status LED The rear RGB LED lets you understand the connection status from across the room. 🟢 Green → Stable connection 🟡 Yellow → Unstable connection 🔴 Red → Internet unavailable No need to look at the display. Hardware ESP32 Cheap Yellow Display (ESP32-2432S028R) 2.8" ILI9341 Touch Display XPT2046 Touch Controller Integrated RGB Status LED Why I decided to share it Someone else is probably experiencing the exact same problem I had. Instead of arguing with your provider... collect the data. Numbers and graphs are much harder to ignore than words. If this project helps even one person solve an "impossible" Internet problem, then it has already achieved its purpose. Printing Tips For the best visual result: Print the front panel vertically . This produces a much smoother curved surface below the display. PETG is recommended for better temperature resistance, although PLA also works well indoors. Source Code The complete Arduino (.ino) project is included. You are welcome to study, modify and build this project for: Personal use Educational purposes Learning and experimentation Commercial use is not permitted. If you wish to manufacture, sell, or integrate this project into a commercial product, please contact me first. ⭐ If this project helped you troubleshoot your Internet connection, please consider leaving a Like, Download, Boost or Make. It really helps support future open-source ESP32 projects! 🛠 Required Components To build this project you will need: 1× ESP32-2432S028R (Cheap Yellow Display - 2.8" TFT Touch Display) 1× TP4056 Li-Ion Battery Charging Module (USB-C or Micro-USB version) 1× 18650 Li-Ion Battery 1× 18650 Battery Holder 5× M3 × 6 mm Screws 1× JST 2-Pin Mini Connector (usually included with the ESP32 Cheap Yellow Display board) 🧰 Assembly The enclosure has been designed with snap-fit joints , so no screws are required to assemble the case itself . The only screws needed are the five M3×6 mm screws used to secure the electronic components inside the enclosure. Only basic soldering skills are required to complete the project. 📦 What's Included Printable enclosure (3MF / STL) Arduino source code (rename the .txt in .ino) Complete assembly-ready design Educational documentation The template you downloaded is free; if you encountered any difficulties, please let me know and I will try to resolve them. What happens when my most successful design meets one of my newest design series? My firefighting pen holders have become a huge part of my MakerWorld journey – and my Fog Nozzle Pen Holder is still my most successful design ever . At the same time, MPAS has grown into a complete modular pool accessory system, now including its own series of pool fountains. So... it was probably only a matter of time before these two worlds collided. 😄 The result is the MPAS Pool Fountain “FireHero” . 🚒💦 Based on the design language of my popular Fog Nozzle Pen Holder and combined with the MPAS Pool Fountain “Pure” , FireHero turns your pool fountain into a firefighting-themed highlight. And yes – this time, the nozzle actually sprays water. 😄 Important – “Pure” is required FireHero is not a standalone MPAS Pool Fountain. It is an extension for my MPAS Pool Fountain “Pure” and requires Pure as its base. The complete FireHero assembly is attached to the front of Pure and should be glued in place as securely and watertight as possible. The water supply is connected externally to Pure via its 1" thread . Please keep in mind that FDM printed parts are not automatically watertight. Before use, I strongly recommend sealing all water-carrying printed parts with clear coat, Dichtol or another suitable sealing product. All connections should also be glued as watertight as possible. Use a sufficient amount of suitable adhesive – in this case, a little too much glue is better than too little. 😄 Even small gaps between the parts may cause water to leak. Assembly The connector part installed inside the coupling and glued to the neck of Pure has an “UP” marking on one side. This marking must face upwards during assembly! The orientation of this part determines the final position of the complete nozzle assembly and ensures that the fog nozzle is positioned the right way up. So before applying glue: Find “UP”, check the orientation, then glue. 😄The red lever on top of the nozzle is purely decorative and has no function . It does not start, stop or regulate the water flow. Water Pattern The spray pattern and range shown in the photos were created with my own pool setup. The actual result may vary depending on pump performance, water flow and the complete hose setup. About the MPAS - Modular Pool Accessory System The MPAS aims to provide a simple solution for attaching a range of accessories to different pools. The installation is done through standardized brackets, to which various modules can be attached. you will find all available MPAS Modules in my Maker World MPAS Collection . Note: The models in the pictures were printed from PLA. For outdoor use, ASA filament should be used due to its UV resistance. You can also use PETG for more strength.

OCEAN ILLUMINATED BIG WALL DECO - 3D PRINTABLE FILE OBVIOUSLY I BASED MY IDEA ON THE MOON ILLUMINATED DECO THAT IS PUBLISHED IN MAKERWORLD. I JUST WANTED A MORE RELAXING THEME, AT LEAST TO ME. SO I CHOSE THE OCEAN. I PAINTED MINE JUST SO IT ALSO LOOKED LIKE WATER WHEN THE LED IS OF. BUT IF YOU DON´T HAVE THE SKILLS, THE TIME OR JUST DON´T WANT IT PAINTED, YOU CAN PRINT IN ANY COLOR AND LET THE LED DO THE WORK. I SUGGEST WHITE OR LIGHT BLUE. HERE IS AN IMAGE GUIDE OF HOW TO PUT TOGETHER. BUT ITS PRETTY EASY EVEN WITHOUT THE GUIDE: THESE SHOULD BE THE RESULT OF EVERY PRINTED. REMEMBER THAT I PAINTED MINE SO I DIDNT CARE ABOUT THE OCEAN FILAMENT COLOR. I USED WHAT I HAD LEFT OF A JADE WHITE FROM BAMBU LAB AND FINISHED IT IN GRAY. THE FRAME PRINTED BLACK SO I DIDN´T HAVE TO PAINT THAT. FIRST PUT TOGETHER THE BACK “CROSS” MAKING SURE THE HANGGING SUPPORT IS IN THE CORRECT POSITION. PRESENT THE 4 PARTS OF SEA SLIDING THE ON THE CROSS TO MAKE SURE EVERY THING MATCHES. IF EVERYTHING IS CORRECTLLY PLACED YOU CAN JOIN THEM ALL AND GLUE THE FOR PARTS. I SUGGEST TO DO A PLASTIC WELDING ON THE BACK SIDE, THAT WAY EVERYTHING HOLD TOGETHER ALOT BETTER. I DIDN´T WELD IN THE PART THE CROSS FITS. THIS IS THE MOMENT OF SELECTING THE ORIENTATION YOU WANT YOUR OCEAN TO BE IN. MAKE SURE TO GLUE THE CROSS WITH THE WALL MOINT HOLE IN THE CORRECT PLACE AND HERE AGAIN I SUGGEST DOING A PLASTIC WELD BETWEEN OCEAN PARTS AND CROSS. PUT TOGETHER THE 4 FRAME PIECES, GLUE THEM AND AGAIN, IF POSSIBLE, DO A PLASTIC WELD. NOW YOU CAN ADD THE LED STRIP OF YOUR CHOICE. YOU´LL NEED EXACTLY 1.5 METERS OF LED STRIP. I USED A 5050 LED MULTICOLOR SELECTOR OF 60 LEDS PER METER THAT IS CHEAP AND EASY TO FIND ON ANY SITE. GLUE IT TO THE UPPER PART OF THE SIDE WALL OF THE FRAME AND PASS THE CONNECTION THROUHG THE OPENNING OF THE FRAME. THE OPENNING SHOULD BE THE PART YOU´LL PUT LOOKING DOWNWARD OR TOWARD YOU POWER CONNECTION. YOU NOW HAVE EVERYTHING DONE. ALL THAT REST IS PUTTING THE FRAM AND THE OCEAN PART TOGETHER. THIS IS WHAT IT SHOULD LOOK LIKE ONCE FINISHED (IF YOU DECIDE TO PAINT IT). FOR THOSE INTERESTED IN PAINTING IT, I USED REGULAR ACRILIC PAINT. FIRST DID AN ENTIRE COAT OF A MEDIUM TONE OF BLUE. THEN WITH A LIGHTER BLUE I STARTED PAINTING WITHOUT COVERING THE DEEP PARTS. LAST STEP WAS TO PUT A VERY WHITE TONE OF BLUE TO THE HIGN SPOTS. I HOPE ANYONE TAKING A TRY TO THIS PROYECT HAS THE SAME FUN I DID. IT´S EASIER THEN IT LOOKS AND FOR THE SIZE (ALMOST 50CM OF DIAMETER), IT TAKES LESS THEN A ROLL OF FILAMENT. ENJOY!

Automatic Trash Bin Lid Opener – String and Hook for IKEA Cabinet A practical upgrade for a cleaner kitchen workflow: open the cabinet, and the trash bin opens with it. A simple mechanism that automatically opens the trash bin lid when you open or pull out the cabinet. The string is attached to the moving cabinet front, door, or drawer. As the cabinet opens, the string becomes tensioned and pulls the hook mounted on the trash bin lid, lifting it automatically. When the cabinet closes, the lid returns to its normal position. This model was designed for an IKEA cabinet and a trash bin with a similar lid design, but it can also be adapted to other bins and cabinets with comparable construction. Attach the second hook to the fixed upper or side section of the cabinet using double-sided tape. Loop the cord over the hooks. !!!! When mounting the hooks, adjust the cord length so that there is a bit of slack when the cabinet is closed. Open the cabinet and check that the cord lifts the lid smoothly. Adjust the mounting position or cord length if necessary. Recommended Materials PLA for hooks TPU for cord You can use ordinary string if your basket requires a different length. Simply tie it to the printed hooks. Notes The exact position of the hook and the string attachment point may need small adjustments depending on the bin lid weight, cabinet travel, and available space. description: A simple, highly effective, and reusable ant trap designed for easy baiting and safe disposal. This two-part, screw-together design features a unique threading system. When screwed halfway on, it exposes ant-sized entry holes and a built-in ramp, allowing ants to easily access the bait. When you are done with the trap, simply screw the lid down 100% to seal it completely. This allows you to safely transport the trap to the bin without spilling the powdery bait inside, or save it for next ant season! Key Features: Pet-Safe Overhang: A large top overhang restricts access, keeping curious cats and dogs away from the bait inside. Easy-Access Ramp: Built-in ramps ensure ants can easily climb in and find the bait. Sealable Disposal: Fully tighten the lid to lock the trap, preventing messy spills when throwing it out or storing it. Indoor & Outdoor Use: Low-profile design fits perfectly along kitchen baseboards, on patios, or directly in garden soil. Reusable: Easily empty, wash, and refill year after year. The "Cocktail" (DIY Ant Bait): You can use standard commercial liquid or gel ant poison, but a great DIY, non-toxic alternative is a 50/50 mix of powdered sugar and baking soda (about a teaspoon in total). The sugar attracts them, and the baking soda eliminates them. You can also use coffee grounds or a splash of apple cider vinegar as repellents. Print Settings & Material Recommendations: Layer Height: 0.12mm is highly recommended . The threading is designed with tight tolerances to ensure a good seal, and thicker layer heights may cause the threads to bind. Material: For indoor use, PLA is perfectly fine. If you plan to use these outdoors in direct sunlight, it is highly recommended to print in PETG, ABS, or ASA . High outdoor temperatures can warp PLA and permanently fuse the threads together! Profile: A pre-configured print profile is included for guaranteed success. Supports: No supports required.

The model is optimized for FDM 3D printing , producing crisp details and a smooth finish. It looks fantastic in white PLA , but you can also print it in matte black, silk gold, marble, or wood-filled filaments for a unique appearance.

Este extensor de tarjetas es la solución definitiva. Ideal para parkings públicos, comunitarios o peajes. Está diseñado en dos piezas (mango y brazo portatarjetas) para facilitar su impresión y maximizar la resistencia. 🛠️ Consejos de Impresión y Materiales Para garantizar que el objeto dure y resista el trote diario, te recomiendo encarecidamente la siguiente combinación de materiales: Brazo / Portatarjetas: ¡Usa PETG! ⚠️ Los coches aparcados al sol se convierten en auténticos hornos. Al ser una pieza maciza y estar en la zona baja, aguanta mejor, aunque si prefieres curarte en salud, el PETG siempre es bienvenido. 🔧 Montaje El diseño cuenta con un encaje a presión muy firme. description: 🌱 MICROGREENS TRAY Grow fresh, nutritious microgreens at home with this reusable 3D-printed Microgreens Tray . Large seeds (peas, sunflower, beans, corn, etc.): Place the seeds directly on the grid —no cotton or growing medium is required. Keep the water level consistent so the roots always have access to moisture. During germination, keep the tray in a warm place. Features 🌱 Reusable 3D-printed design 💧 Separate water reservoir for consistent moisture 🧼 Easy to clean and reuse ♻️ Printed from environmentally friendly PLA 🌿 Suitable for a wide variety of microgreens 🏡 Perfect for kitchens, apartments, classrooms, and indoor gardening Stackable Design The trays are fully stackable , making storage simple and efficient. Recommended Print Settings For the best performance and a watertight tray, the following print settings are recommended: Material: PLA Layer Height: 0.20 mm Walls / Perimeters: 3–5 (recommended) Bottom Layers: 5–8 Supports: Not required Using 3–5 wall perimeters creates a strong, durable shell and greatly improves the tray's waterproof performance , minimizing the chance of leaks. The soft tissues—including ligaments, menisci, and articular cartilage—were then meticulously 3D modeled by hand, based on in-depth studies of MRI scans and anatomical literature. It serves as a premium medical-grade educational tool, perfect for students, orthopedic professionals, physical therapists, or 3D printing enthusiasts. Included Anatomical Structures The model features all critical bony and soft tissue structures necessary to understand the complex biomechanics of the knee: 🦴Skeletal Structure (CT Extracted): Femur, Tibia, Fibula, and Patella (kneecap), featuring accurate reproductions of condyles, epicondyles, and articular surfaces. 🔗Ligamentous Apparatus (MRI Modeled): Cruciate Ligaments (Anterior Cruciate Ligament - ACL & Posterior Cruciate Ligament - PCL). Collateral Ligaments (Medial Collateral Ligament - MCL & Lateral Collateral Ligament - LCL). Patellar System (including the patellar tendon/ligaments). 🦵Cartilage & Cushioning (MRI Modeled): Menisci (Medial and Lateral menisci). Articular Cartilage covering both the femoral and tibial contact surfaces. Intended Use Education & Didactics: An excellent tactile and visual aid for anatomy classrooms, medical schools, and healthcare training. Patient Communication: Ideal for orthopedic clinics and physiotherapy practices to visually explain injuries (e.g., ACL tears, meniscus damage, osteoarthritis) and surgical procedures to patients. Advanced 3D Printing Showcase: A great project to showcase your printer's capability with complex, high-detail organic geometries. 💡 Print Settings & Recommendations Material: This model has been fully designed and optimized for PLA . No flexible filaments are required, making it easy and reliable to print on any standard 3D printer. Optimized for Single AMS (4 Colors): The model is structured to use exactly 4 colors, making it perfectly compatible with a single Bambu Lab AMS unit. To maximize visual contrast and educational value, the recommended color mapping is: Bone White: Skeletal structures (Femur, Tibia, Fibula, Patella) Red: Ligaments Blue: Menisci Beige: Articular Cartilage Disclaimer: This model is intended strictly for educational, illustrative, and hobbyist purposes. It is not a clinical tool and does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.

Overview This kinetic sculpture has linkages that cause the ball to be always centered in the exact same position. Due to each hinge axis passing through the center, no matter how each link is moved, it will cause the entire structure to articulate around a stationary center. It features a print-in-place and thread-together design that requires no glue or additional hardware. It requires no supports and is extremely fascinating and satisfying. The base can also be filled with sand or other materials to provide a more premium feel. I have also created a soccer version that is completely compatible with all of these parts. You can find the soccer version here: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2977052-soccer-football-fixed-center-kinetic-sculpture#profileId-3339654 For printing Standard setting can be used for printing. No AMS is required and no supports are needed. For the print profiles, there is one with all parts on separate plates for different colors for each part and two that have all the parts on a single plate (one includes the funnel and the other does not). All materials should work; however, for the ball to stay more centered, avoid flexible materials like TPU. Features The model prints in three pieces: the ball, the base, and the print-in-place linkages. Additionally, a funnel can be printed to more easily fill the base with sand or another material. The hole for filling the base is the same hole that the linkage structure threads into. The entire structure is about 95 mm in diameter and about 105 mm tall. All parts are compatible with the other versions. Assembly Assembling this model is very simple. Optionally, the funnel can be threaded into the hole in the base and the base filled. After the funnel is removed, the linkage structure can be threaded into that same hole until it stops. The location of where the threads stop should position the linkage structure properly. Lastly, the ball can be threaded onto the rod at the center of the ring. The links may be slightly stiff and not want to move after printing, but with some slight pressure, the links can be broken free. Versions with Themes I currently plan on making more variations of this model with specific themes. I have already created a soccer version that you can find here. https://makerworld.com/en/models/2977052-soccer-football-fixed-center-kinetic-sculpture#profileId-3339654 Other versions may include but not be limited to: A space theme with the ball being a planet or the moon. A version themed around a sport such as basketball, baseball, tennis, golf, volleyball, or American football. A moving object-themed version that could be a motorcycle, racecar, airplane, or rocket. An outdoor activity-themed version that could have a surfboard, skateboard, or fishing bobber or lure. A larger version that had a light using the led light kit. There are many possible versions that I could create. Let me know which ones you want to see, and let me know of any other ideas that you have. Other notes If you have any questions or comments, feel free to ask in the comments or send me a private message. This is actually sort of the second version of one of these that I have created. After creating the other one, I found that it had limited movement, was a little bit weak, and could have looked better. That partially inspired me to create this model. TrailMark3D Turn Your Trail Into a Trophy TrailMark3D is a web application that generates 3D printable terrain models from GPX files. Upload any GPX track from Strava, Garmin, Komoot, or other tracking apps and get a detailed topographic model ready for 3D printing, zero setup, no software to install, no CAD skills required. Whether it's the summit you finally bagged, a century ride, a multi-day thru-hike, or your local loop, TrailMark3D turns the route you recorded into a physical object you can hold, display, or gift. Who It's For Hikers & trail runners who want a tangible keepsake of a route or summit Cyclists commemorating a big climb, gran fondo, or tour Gift-givers looking for something personal for the outdoor enthusiast in their life, or organizers and gift shops producing them in small batches for events and races. 3D printing hobbyists who want real-world terrain data without wrangling GIS tools How it Works Upload your GPX file to TrailMark3D.com Choose your preferred model shape, size , rotation, map features, printing style Generate your 3D terrain model (processing takes minutes depending on features, size, and resolution) Download the STL/3MF file for 3D printing Core Features Web application - No installation or boilerplate setup needed. Just upload, tweak, and generate. Shape options - Square, Circle, Hexagon Map features - Terrain, Buildings, Roads, Water Bodies, Trail (from GPX) Separated objects - Map features are separate objects inside the 3MF file, so objects can be printed separately. NO AMS NEEDED. Multi-day adventure workflow - Upload up to 5 GPX files to combine your multi-day hike, ride, or any recorded adventure. Job storage - Your latest generated 3D mesh is always stored in the database under your account, so you can always come back to redownload or modify your model. Persistent 3D mesh generation - 3D mesh generation can take time. This feature lets you close your browser and come back anytime to download the generated 3D model. Interactive 2D map view - Resize, rotate, or drag your choice of shape on a 2D map view. Selective water body removal - You may or may not want to print some of the fetched water bodies. This tool lets you exclude water body segments from being generated. Extension tiles - A single GPX is a single tile by default. You can extend the tiles by adding new tiles in the Interactive 2D Map View. Jigsaw puzzle - Generate up to a 20×20 jigsaw terrain puzzle with full control over the jigsaw shape parameters and randomness. Preset (Experimental) - Skip the tweaking by selecting the type of adventure for your GPX. Free & Pro Tiers The core features of TrailMark3D are completely free - no credit card, no expiry. With the free tier you get up to 10 downloads per month, grid resolution up to 200, all three shape options (Square, Circle, Hexagon), water features (Seas, Lakes, Rivers), through-hole water slots, water preview, tree line, activity presets, 3D trail animation, 3MF export, and custom colors. The free tier limits are set around what the server can sustainably handle - 10 downloads/month and a resolution cap of 200 keep things running smoothly for everyone without blowing past my hosting budget. Pro upgrades go directly toward the server capacity that makes higher limits possible. Upgrading to Pro unlocks everything in the free tier plus: unlimited downloads, grid resolution up to 500, shelf mode and water exclusion, shrink-below-trail, buildings and roads, multi-day trips (up to 5 days), priority processing, and early access to upcoming features. Why TrailMark3D From data to object - Your recorded route becomes a real, printable model with accurate terrain. Full control - Tune shape and which map features to include before you generate. Print-friendly - Separated objects mean clean multi-part prints without needing an AMS. Come back anytime - Generation runs server-side, and your jobs are saved to your account. Free to start - The core features are completely free, with Pro available when you need more power. Zero setup - No software to install, no CAD skills required. description: The Great Pyramid Cross-Section Explore the secrets of the Great Pyramid of Giza with this detailed cross-section display, revealing the intricate chambers that have fascinated humanity for millennia. What Lies Within? While traditionally understood as a grand tomb for Pharaoh Khufu, the Great Pyramid remains an enigma. Beyond the famous King’s Chamber —home to the enigmatic red granite sarcophagus—and the Queen’s Chamber , the pyramid contains the breathtaking, corbelled-roof Grand Gallery . Hidden shafts, mysterious voids discovered via muon tomography, and an unfinished Subterranean Chamber carved deep into the bedrock all point to a level of engineering sophistication that continues to challenge our understanding of the Old Kingdom. Are these voids hidden burial sites, or part of a larger, lost architectural plan? A New Discovery Beneath the Sands Recent, cutting-edge research using satellite imaging and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has suggested the existence of an extensive, deeper subterranean complex beneath the Giza Plateau. Reports indicate potential anomalies, including vertical shafts and structured, geometric patterns reaching deep into the bedrock beneath the major pyramids. While these findings have sparked intense debate among archaeologists regarding their nature and origin, they offer a tantalizing glimpse into what may still be hidden beneath our feet. Inspired by these findings, I have designed a model of the subterranean structures that some researchers believe may be part of this deep network, featuring complex pillars with coiled sections and block-like bases. description: Support young learners in mastering correct letter formation with this all-in-one stencil plate featuring the complete lowercase alphabet! Based on the NSW Foundation font and designed for early writers, each letter features directional arrows and stroke numbers cut into the surface to guide proper handwriting formation - all 26 letters on a single, easy-to-use board. Thoughtfully Designed for Young Learners In stencil letters like a, b, d, e, g, o, p, q and others, small bridge points are needed to keep the inner parts of the letter connected to the plate. In many stencils these bridges are placed arbitrarily, interrupting the natural flow of the letter mid-stroke. In this design, the bridges are deliberately positioned at each letter's starting or ending point — so when a child begins tracing, they start at the bridge and follow the letter all the way around. The result is an uninterrupted tracing experience that teaches correct stroke formation, not just the shape of the letter. Print Options The arrows and stroke numbers are cut out of each letter — in a single colour they're still clearly visible and functional. For the best visual result, the colour change is already set in the slicer file at the correct layer height, so no manual configuration is needed. If you have an AMS , it will handle the filament swap automatically. No AMS? No problem — your printer will pause and prompt you to swap filament manually at the right moment. The result is a contrasting colour on the arrows and stroke numbers, making the letter outlines really pop. Print Tips Due to the fine details in this model, good bed adhesion is critical — poor adhesion can cause lifting or warping and ruin the small details. 🧼 Clean your plate thoroughly with hot water and dishwashing liquid before printing and allow to dry completely 🖼️ An outer brim is included in the slicer profile to prevent warping and lifting on this large, flat print. If you have adhesion issues on the insides of the letters, reslice with inner brims turned on. 🗼 Prime tower is disabled — this is intentional, so don't be alarmed when you don't see one in the preview Coming Soon A face-down version with coloured inserts is in development; the same great stencil with a premium finish. Follow my profile so you don't miss it! description: Hold a medically accurate piece of human anatomy right in your hands! (Read the last sentence for a curiosity question!) 🩻 Overview 🩻 This advanced 3D model is a highly detailed representation of the human shoulder (glenohumeral) joint, developed through a hybrid medical and digital workflow. The skeletal framework was extracted directly from real CT scans to ensure an anatomically correct bone morphology. The surrounding soft tissues were subsequently hand-modeled in Blender, carefully crafted based on anatomical studies and medical literature. To ensure the best possible 3D printing experience and educational clarity, this model focuses on the primary structures. Some minor or overlapping anatomical elements were intentionally omitted, providing a clean, understandable, and highly printable display piece without overwhelming the slicer or the viewer. 🦴 Included Anatomical Structures The model highlights the key bony landmarks and major soft tissues crucial for understanding shoulder biomechanics: Skeletal Framework (CT Extracted): Scapula (Shoulder Blade), Clavicle (Collarbone), and Humerus (Upper arm bone), featuring accurate articular surfaces and bone topography. 💪 Muscular System (Blender Modeled): Key musculature, including major components of the rotator cuff and biceps, which are essential for shoulder stability and movement. 🔗 Ligaments & Connective Tissue (Blender Modeled): Essential stabilizing ligaments and capsular elements highlighting the articulation points. 🎯 Intended Use Education & Study: A brilliant hands-on visual aid for medical students, anatomy classes, and healthcare professionals. Clinical Communication: Perfect for physical therapists and orthopedic specialists to easily explain shoulder mechanics, impingements, or rotator cuff injuries to their patients. Advanced 3D Printing Showcase: A fantastic display piece that highlights the precision of your printer on complex organic shapes. 💡 Print Settings & Recommendations Material: This model has been fully designed and optimized for standard PLA . No flexible or exotic filaments are required. Versatile Print Profiles: To make this model accessible to everyone, I will be uploading dedicated print profiles for both AMS and non-AMS setups . The multicolor profile is organized to maximize visual contrast and educational value. Based on the provided images, the recommended color mapping is: Bone White: Skeletal structures (Scapula, Clavicle, Humerus) and tendons. Red: Musculature (Rotator cuff and supporting muscles). Blue: Ligaments, and capsular structures. Different colors are presented in the non-AMS setup for printing reasons. SIMPLY INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE NO-AMS PROFILE ⚠️ Disclaimer: This model is intended strictly for educational, illustrative, and hobbyist purposes. It is not a clinical tool and does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. For the most interested ones, a bit of anatomy! 🤓🫀🔬 The shoulder, or shoulder girdle, is a complex system designed to give the upper limb a very wide range of motion, with bones, muscles, tendons, and ligaments working together. In my model, the labeled parts show both the supporting framework and the soft tissues that stabilize movement. Bones 🦴 The scapula is a flat triangular bone at the back of the thorax, and it provides attachment for many shoulder muscles. The humerus is the upper arm bone, and its rounded head articulates with the scapula to form the glenohumeral joint, which is the main shoulder joint. The clavicle acts like a strut between the sternum and the scapula, helping keep the shoulder positioned away from the chest wall so the arm can move freely. Soft tissues 💪 The rotator cuff is made of four muscles and their tendons, and its main job is to keep the head of the humerus centered while the arm moves and rotates. The tendons connect muscle to bone, and the long head of the biceps tendon also contributes to shoulder stability as it passes near the joint. The ligaments connect bone to bone and reinforce the joint capsule, helping prevent excessive movement and instability. The subacromial bursa is a small fluid-filled sac that reduces friction between the acromion and the rotator cuff tendons during arm elevation. A question for the more curious viewer: Why does the biceps tendon anchor to the scapula instead of attaching directly to the humerus? Let me know in the comments!

description: A fully 3D-printable Push-to-Open mechanism with 4 tactile click stages and a completely new rotating locking wheel concept. Snap-fit assembly No supports required No additional hardware No tools required 4 parts 1 printing plate Approx. 3 hours print time Approx. 110 g filament Tested with PLA, standard print settings and the printer X1E and X1C I designed a completely new Push-to-Open (Push-to-Lock / Push-Push) mechanism. This model is intended as a functional demonstration of the working principle and can be assembled quickly using snap-fit connections. I plan to use this Push-to-Open principle in future projects. Unlike other 3D-printed Push-to-Open mechanisms, this new concept is based on a wheel with movable print-in-place contact pins. To make the mechanism easier to understand, I added viewing windows to the model so every movement step can be observed clearly. The mechanism creates 4 distinct click sounds that provide both tactile and audible feedback during every cycle🔔: The first click indicates that the button can be released The second click confirms that the mechanism is locked Pressing again creates the third click, indicating that the button can be released. The fourth click confirms that the mechanism is open and the cycle can start again Additionally, the spring elements inside the mechanism are not permanently loaded in the locked or unlocked position, which increases durability (This does not apply to the spring that retracts the sliding latch). The locking wheel rotates 90° during each open-close cycle. Suitable Applications This functional model is suitable for: Educational and demonstration purposes Mechanical concept studies DIY projects Prototype development for Push-to-Open systems Just to have fun with the mechanism 😉 I believe this mechanism has potential for many different applications and further development. For example: Different spring forces for opening and closing could be implemented Different actions could be triggered after each 90° rotation The mechanism could be activated from all four sides I am open to application ideas, improvement suggestions, and remixes.👐 Print Settings and Material The mechanism can be printed without any special print settings. I tested the mechanism using PLA for all parts. Other materials may require adjustments and were not tested. In my tests, the spring elements of the locking wheel were stiffer when printed in standard PLA, which made the click sounds more noticeable. PLA Tough+ for the locking wheel was more flexible and allowed the mechanism to run slightly smoother, but the click sounds were less pronounced. Assembly The functional model consists of four parts: Housing ① Base plate ② Locking wheel ③ Spring-loaded sliding latch ④ Do not heavily load the spring elements immediately after printing. Allow the parts to cool down completely first. Check if the spring elements inside the locking wheel can move freely. Sometimes a small amount of plastic may fuse inside the gap during printing. This can usually be separated easily. Press each pin toward the center as shown in the image. 2. Insert the spring-loaded sliding latch into the housing as shown in the image. Make sure the guide rails are aligned correctly. 3. Place the locking wheel into the housing. The locking wheel must sit flush inside the housing as shown in the image. 4. Slightly press down the spring-loaded sliding latch at the push point while inserting the base plate from the top until the snap-fits lock into place. 5. Finished!🥳 Do not store the spring of the sliding latch in a permanently preloaded position, as this may reduce the spring force over time. From my experience, the mechanism runs smoother after several cycles. It is important that the locking wheel can rotate freely. Too much friction may cause the mechanism to malfunction. This was a problem in my first prototypes, but the newer versions worked reliably. If you experience any issues, feel free to leave feedback.🤔 Detailed Function Description (Now things start getting a bit more technical😉) I marked the most important elements with colors: The housing contains: First locking position (pink) Second locking position (purple) The locking wheel contains: First contact pin (red) Second contact pin (yellow) These pins can move toward the center and spring back afterward. The locking wheel also contains: Spring-loaded locking sliders (blue) Rotation stops (green) The following section explains the closing and opening sequence of the mechanism. The circled numbers correspond to the images shown below. Closing Process During closing, the spring-loaded sliding latch is inserted from the top by hand and presses against the first contact pin, causing the locking wheel to rotate clockwise ①. At the same time, the second contact pin is pushed toward the center by the side wall of the sliding latch and becomes preloaded, creating enough space for the sliding latch to move to the end position②. As soon as the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the first locking position ③. This prevents the locking wheel from rotating backward. The spring-loaded sliding latch can now move backward slightly using the spring force (spring not shown). Due to the previous rotation of the locking wheel, the return path of the sliding latch is blocked by the rotation stop ④. Because of this, the sliding latch can only move back to the rotation stop position and the mechanism is now locked ⑤. In this position, the preloaded second contact pin can move back into the matching recess of the sliding latch ⑥. Once this happens, the Push-to-Open mechanism can be opened again. Opening Process Opening is performed by pressing the sliding latch a second time by hand. The sliding latch pushes the second contact pin downward until the end stop is reached ⑦. The required travel distance is only 5 mm. During this movement, the first contact pin is preloaded against the side wall of the sliding latch ⑧. When the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the second locking position to again prevent the locking wheel from rotating backward ⑨. The sliding latch can now be fully pulled out of the mechanism by the spring force (spring not shown) ⑩. Since the first contact pin is no longer pressed against the side wall of the sliding latch, it can spring back into its original position ⑪. The system is now back in its starting position and the cycle can begin again. Thanks for checking out the project! 😁

description: ✨ 设计初衷 传统的蒙特梭利触觉教具通常使用砂纸、布料或木材手工制作，工艺繁琐且纹理单一。本项目跳出了传统 3D 建模的固有思维， 完全基于 FDM 3D 打印机切片软件（Bambu Studio）的底层走线与填充算法 ，将枯燥的几何体转化为 8 种截然不同的物理肌理。这不仅是一套好玩的亲子感官教具，更是对 3D 打印切片工艺美学的一场深度探索。 在外观上，整体造型遵循极简主义美学，线条纯粹、圆润安全，能够让孩子摆脱色彩和复杂造型的视觉干扰，全神贯注于指尖的触觉感知。 🧠 教育价值与交互玩法 感官拓展 ：8 个积木的顶部及对应底座孔位分别拥有同心圆、希尔伯特曲线、八角星、蜂窝、直线等不同的几何肌理 (可以按照切片填充图案任意修改) 。 指尖大侦探 ：将积木打乱放入不透明袋子中，让孩子闭上眼睛（或戴上眼罩）。孩子需要仅凭手指触摸，分辨出“粗糙、细腻、波浪、网格、凹陷”等触感反馈，并在脑海中构建几何空间图像，最终将其与底座中拥有相同肌理的孔位进行精准配对。 核心能力培养 ：极其适合 3-6 岁儿童，能有效锻炼专注力、指尖微运动触觉灵敏度，以及早期空间几何想象力。 🚀 核心工艺创新点 本模型在 3D 建模软件中保持了最基础的几何形态，所有的触觉“魔法”均在 Bambu Studio 中通过修改“局部对象参数”一键生成： 稀疏填充算法 ：通过将部分积木及底座特定区域的“顶部外壳层数”设置为 0 ，直接暴露出 15% 密度的内部填充。 异构材料无缝剥离 ： （可选工艺玩法） 本设计支持使用 PLA 与 PETG 互不相融 的物理特性。通过在切片中将积木与底部纹理片之间加入 多层 PETG 作为零公差分离层，可实现“一体打印、咔哒掰开”，完美确保了配对两面的纹理 100% 同轴且丝丝入扣。

description: Modular Articulated DNA Educational Model Let your students build, connect, and explore the DNA with this colourful modular model designed for hands-on learning. Each nucleotide piece represents one of the DNA/RNA bases, while the blue connector parts form the sugar-phosphate backbone. This model is great for classrooms, STEM projects, biology demonstrations, or anyone who wants a fun physical way to understand nucleotide pairing and DNA structure. I also plan on extending this model with a couple of more pieces for better demonstration of topics like Transcription and Translation . Feel free to leave a like and follow if you'd like to stay updated. Parts You can print as many of the individual parts as you like and connect them with each other! Each nucleotide piece represents one of the DNA/RNA bases and the blue connector parts form the sugar-phosphate backbone: Cytosine Guanine Adenine Thymine Uracil Assembly & Colouring The backbone pieces can be clicked together with a little bit of force. It is recommended to use 5x2 (dxh) magnets for both the backbone pieces and nucleotides, to better hold them in place. Place the magnets into the slot (make sure you have them oriented all in the same way!) and use a paper clip, a scredriver, or something similar to push the magnet all the way into the slot. You can also remove the magnets if needed using a paper clip from the other side. Feel free to adjust the colouring of the pieces to your needs. My file uses the colours according to the Wikipedia nucleic acid image: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid#/media/File:Difference_DNA_RNA-EN.svg Versions There are two Versions of nucleotides: Standard Set (recommended!) nucleotides have no chamfer/fillet on the connection pin. This makes them harder to separate from their counterparts, but results in a more stable double strand. Rounded Nucleotide Set contains nucleotide pieces with a rounded down connection pin. This makes them easier to separate, e.g. when demonstrating something, but obviously also reduces the stability of the entire double strand in terms of base pairs disconnecting when you move the double strand around. If you have any suggestions, feel free to let me know!

This model is completely press-fit, no glue, no tape, no magnets, just plain old PLA, modeled with the intent of being easy and fun to assemble and mess with, for experts to beginners to people who just enjoy messing around with cool contraptions. Additionally, those who have previous experience with vacuum engines can attempt to performance tune it, by changing the offset the camshaft has on the crankshaft. Simply print out all the parts (don't forget to boost with that free boost token ;), assemble with the easy assembly instructions, and enjoy! Note: You will need six 608 bearings, either 3D printed versions from Makerworld, or the metal versions which I have included in the Bill of Materials from Makersupply. Also note that the tolerances are very good for a Bambu Lab A1, but I cannot guarantee perfect fits with other printers, although they should be pretty close. Operation Instructions: Operation is easy, simply stick a vacuum up to the cone on the exhaust manifold, and watch it rip! You may need to give it a rotate or two to help it get started. Tips for success: Be sure that the camshaft if offset by a quarter turn from the crankshaft (explained in the instructions). Try lubing all of the areas where there is filament on filament contact, to reduce friction and increase speed and power. Clean out your vacuum's filter, or remove it entirely to improve your vacuum performance. Be sure there is little friction inside the crank case, as in make sure there are tiny gaps between all of the moving parts to ensure they move freely. Updates: I have many updates planned, from gaskets cutouts, to new exhaust manifolds for different vacuums. I will include links to them here as they are developed. I just finished a throttle body for this engine, and you can find it here Thank you for checking this model out, and if you enjoyed, please share with your friends and family! I love designing models like this, and yall's support keeps me going. It takes a lot of time and trial runs to design new models. This model was no exception! Instructions: This model can be a bit complicated, as there are many pieces, but personally I found it very fun to assemble, and very satisfying. Step One: Connect the piston heads to the connecting rods with the two pins. Next assemble the crankshaft. This can be a bit tricky, with all the pieces looking identical, but pay attention to the photo, and you'll do fine. Note, the the position of the two cranks should be opposite, but I accidently had them the same in the first photo. The parts include are the five crankshaft pieces, three 608 bearings, the two piston assemblies, the flywheel, and one of the two gears with a hexagon cutout. Step Two: Connect the two valves to the connecting rods with the two pins. Now assemble the camshaft, this can also be a bit tricky, since there are so many pieces that make up the camshaft. Again, just pay careful attention to the photos and you'll do great. Note: If you get the crankshaft and camshaft pieces mixed up just remember the camshaft has a shorter stroke than the crankshaft, meaning the pieces are smaller. The pieces used here are the five camshaft pieces, three 608 bearings, the two valve assemblies, and one of the two gears with a hexagonal cut out. Step Three: Attach the cylinder heads to the block. There are a different amount of each size of screw included in the file, and throughout the rest of these instructions I will refer to each screw by the amount of them that are included. The set of three screws go in the three holes in a line in the head, and the single screw goes in the single hole on the other side of the head. VERY IMPORTANT: The screws included with this file are FRAGILE and cannot take very much twisting force at all. To avoid breaking off screws inside of the engine block or oil pan, finger tighten or lightly tighten with a flat-head screwdriver until its not easy and then STOP SCREWING. Note that the screwheads are also 10mm, and you may be able to fit a socket on them, but you must still be very careful to not over tighten the screws. Step Four: Now it is time to lay the crankshaft, the camshaft, and the middle gear into the engine block. This step can be tricky, and must be done correctly or the engine will not function. The secret to vacuum engines is to have the camshaft a one quarter (0.25, 90 degrees) turn AHEAD of the crankshaft, in the direction you want it to rotate. In a simpler sense, this means that while the valve is completely open (Top Dead Center) the piston must be halfway up. When the piston reaches Top Dead Center, the valve with already be half closed. Additionally, since this engine has two cylinders, the pistons and valves must be in opposite positions to be most efficient. Finally, if you would like to mess around with tuning the engine for higher speeds, try changing the amount that the camshaft leads the crankshaft. Basically, try a lead of maybe a sixth of a turn or a third of a turn, instead of a quarter turn. Step Five: Once you've got those in place, you can carefully screw the oil pan to the engine block with the set of four screws included in the file. Be sure the quarter turn amount does not change while you set the engine block and the oil pan together. Step Six: Finally, attach the exhaust manifold to the heads with the set of two screws, and the nuts. This may take some finagling to get them on. Once again remember to not overtighten, I advise only finger tightening. Congrats! Your finished! Don't forget to share a comment with a photo about your experience, I love to hear about it, whether success or failure. Also don't forget to boost!

This 3D printable SEL tool gives children a simple finger tracing path to support calm breathing, focus, and emotional regulation. However, for the scaled-down versions, I recommend using the fully 3D-printed, bearingless configuration. At smaller scales, the printed bearing system generally rotates more smoothly because it produces less friction than a standard 608ZZ bearing. A traditional bearing may still work well if a high-quality, low-friction bearing is used. Sections Story & Background Engine Info Printing Tips & My Modifications Assembly Instructions Final Notes 1) Story & Background This model was originally designed for a special MTU event in the DFW area — a tribute to the engineers and technicians who work on and around one of the most advanced jet engines flying today. It was built for a friend who works there, and for the incredible team around them. Building this model meant diving deep into the real engineering behind the LEAP-1B, and coming out the other side with an even deeper respect for what CFM International has achieved. It was a labor of love from first sketch to final print, and sharing it with the maker community feels like the right next step. 2) Engine Info The CFM International LEAP-1B is the exclusive powerplant for the Boeing 737 MAX , designed and produced by CFM International — a 50/50 joint venture between GE Aerospace and Safran Aircraft Engines , established in 1974. It represents a massive leap forward in efficiency and sustainability over its predecessor, the CFM56. MTU & the LEAP-1B This model was created for an MTU event — and MTU's connection to this engine runs deep. MTU Aero Engines is directly involved in MRO (Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul) services for both the LEAP-1A and LEAP-1B, helping keep this massive global fleet airworthy and operational. 3) Printing Tips & Modifications I made targeted modifications on a per-component basis rather than applying global settings — for example, on the engine body I adjusted print speeds for better surface quality and used support enforcers and blockers on specific areas to avoid unnecessary supports elsewhere. If you use your own print profile, you will still get a good result. However, if you have a Bambu A1 like mine, you'll get the best results using my specific print profile. Since the A1 is a Cartesian (bed-slinger) printer , outer surface quality can sometimes suffer — my speed adjustments help mitigate this, though it may not be perfect. Alternate Parts & Customization I have also uploaded an alternate parts profile for those who want additional options or a cleaner look. This includes: Clean engine variant — a version free of decals for a sleek, minimal finish Alternate display stands — additional stand styles as shown in the figures below Blank logo plates — fully blank plates that you can customize by importing SVGs directly in Bambu Studio or your preferred CAD software Bearing Options The shaft supports are designed to accommodate several bearing configurations. Choose whichever works best for you: Option Specs Notes Bambu-sourced bearing (6000ZZ) ID/OD/W: 10 × 26 × 8 mm Recommended Common Amazon bearing ID/OD/W: 8 × 22 × 7 mm Easy to source 3D printed bearing — Works, but not ideal Custom / your own bearing — Blank shaft support included Bearingless option Surprisingly works well A blank shaft support is included if you'd like to fit your own bearing or design a custom solution. Orient the shaft correctly — the flat side faces a specific direction as shown in the photo. ⚠️ If installed backwards, the fan blades will not seat in the correct position. Apply a small amount of glue into the alignment hole only — do not over-apply. Applying glue here (rather than on the shaft body) prevents glue from migrating to the shaft collar, which must remain free to spin. The completed fan core must be able to rotate freely — confirm this before the glue sets. Step 2 — Install Fan Core into Engine Body Apply glue to the designated glue area on the engine body interior as shown in the photo. Insert the fan core sub-assembly into the body. Align the notches on the shaft holder with the corresponding notches inside the engine body — this is critical for correct positioning. Do not proceed until the notches are fully seated and glue has cured. Step 3 — Fan Blades & Dowels Once the engine body assembly is fully cured, apply glue to the alignment hole of the fan blades and install them. Insert the dowels into their holes around the face ring — these may require a small amount of glue depending on fit tolerance from your printer. My Educational Mechanical Examples Series This model is one of my educational mechanical mechanism examples on 80mm x 80mm base plates. You can find all models of the series in this collection => [Mechanical Mechanism Examples] The present model This is an educational model of a Hart's A-frame, which is one of the exact straight-line linkages. Brief Description The approximate straight-line mechanisms introduced so far — Watt's linkage, the Chebyshev linkage, and the Grasshopper linkage — are all based on four-bar linkages. The coupler point need not lie at a joint between two links; it may sit at the midpoint of a link or on its extension. Even so, these simple linkages confine the coupler point to a path that is only approximately straight — and they do so without any linear guide or prismatic pair. A four-bar linkage, however, cannot trace an exactly straight line. Hart's A-frame achieves exact straight-line motion by raising the number of links to six. Five of them move; the sixth is the base plate itself, which serves as the hidden ground link. Laid out as the capital letter A, each slanted side is built from a long link and a short link half its length, joined end to end, and the two short links meet at the apex. The lower end of each long link is pinned to the base plate, and these two fixed pivots are spaced apart by twice the length of the crossbar. The crossbar — the horizontal stroke of the A — joins the two long links at the points that divide them in a 3:1 ratio, with the longer portion toward the fixed pivot. Only these two lower pivots are anchored; every other joint is free to move. Under this arrangement the apex of the A, which is the coupler point, is constrained to travel along a perfectly straight line: the vertical line engraved on the base plate, which is the perpendicular bisector of the two fixed pivots. Move the coupler point by hand and you can feel it being held to this line. As you play with the model, though, you will find that this is not the only path open to the coupler point: the motion branches at the midpoint between the two pivots. There, the coupler point can leave the straight line for a second, skewed path that traces a distorted triangle, also engraved on the plate. Pushing on the coupler point alone will not carry it past the corners of that triangle; there you must also control how the links fold in order to pass through. To keep the motion well-behaved, confine the coupler point to either the upper or the lower half of the straight line, or guide it through the midpoint so that it does not slip onto the other branch. Reference https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hart%27s_inversors Related Models Case This model is compatible with the case included in my first set . Use well-dried PETG to have better dimensional accuracy. Use 0.1 mm or 0.08 mm layer height to have smoother surfaces. Use slow printing speed for overhangs. Select “Random” seam position to have smoother rotation. Randomly distributed seam should be easily worn out after some wearing.Printing Sanding and Filing Note that, in this model, the rotation of the bases for bearings is intentionally made not too smooth. Sometimes, the gears suffer from the stringing effect and/or elephant foot effect, resulting in a too tight fit to the shafts (they are designed with a 0.15 mm radial clearance). If you see rough surface on the shafts due to stringing, sand off the roughness with a small piece of sand paper. If you feel the gears do not rotate smoothly due to an elephant effect, widen the hole slightly by using a thin round bar file. Without those issues, the parts should rotate very smoothly with minimal friction. Assembly Secure the links onto the shafts with the retaining rings. description: Help students pause, breathe, and reset with this simple Box Breathing Pause Card from 3DprintEDU. This 3D printable calm corner tool gives children a tactile path to follow with their finger while practising a simple breathing routine. Students can trace the square, moving from corner to corner as they breathe in, hold, breathe out, and pause. Each Pause Card uses a raised O as the starting point, making the collection consistent and easy for students to use independently. This post includes 2 card variations , so you can choose the version that works best for your classroom, calm corner, counselling space, or sensory toolkit. Great for: Classroom calm corners SEL routines Mindful moments Counselling offices Occupational therapy spaces Sensory bins Morning meetings Transitions and reset breaks Teacher wellness toolkits Home regulation spaces This is part of the growing 3DprintEDU SEL Pause Cards Collection , a set of classroom friendly 3D printable tools designed to support breathing, focus, and emotional regulation. Print notes No supports needed Flat print Quick classroom friendly print Great in one colour or AMS colour swaps Works well in bright, calming, or school themed colours How to Use Begin at the raised O , which is designed to be the consistent starting point across the SEL Pause Cards collection. Place your finger on the O and slowly trace along the square path. Use equal 4 second intervals for each part of the breathing cycle: Inhale for 4 seconds as you move from the O to the next raised circle. Hold for 4 seconds while resting your finger on the raised circle. Exhale for 4 seconds as you move to the next raised circle. Hold for 4 seconds while resting your finger on the final raised circle. Continue tracing around the square for a few rounds, moving slowly and breathing calmly. The raised circles give students tactile pause points, helping them slow down, focus, and reset. For younger students, an adult can guide the rhythm by counting aloud: Breathe in, 2, 3, 4. Hold, 2, 3, 4. Breathe out, 2, 3, 4. Hold, 2, 3, 4. Designed by 3DprintEDU , by a teacher, for teachers. description: This is PiDeck V2 , the next evolution of my original 7-inch cyberdeck design! This upgraded version takes the core concept of the first PiDeck and refines it into a sleeker, more reliable, and feature-rich portable terminal - but this time without integrated PowerBank. Disclaimer: This project is not for beginners . It was designed specifically around parts I already had on hand, so the tolerances and mounting points are very specific. You will likely need to tweak the design to fit your exact components. To make this easier, I have provided the CAD files (.step) so you can modify the housing to your needs. Key Improvements & Features Power Supply (Geekworm PD Module): The Raspberry Pi 5 is notoriously picky about its power source. To eliminate the low voltage warnings and power delivery issues of the first version, V2 ditches the internal power bank. Instead, it features an integrated Geekworm PD module , allowing you to power the deck reliably from any standard USB-C Power Delivery wall adapter or high-output PD power bank. Integrated Camera : This version now supports a Raspberry Pi 1.3 camera module , seamlessly integrated into the chassis. An optional clean backplate without the camera hole is also included in the files. Quick-Access Magnetic Flap: The rear panel features a magnetic flap that lets you access the Raspberry Pi's internal I/O ports instantly. Optimized & Thinner Chassis: The entire design has been streamlined. It features a slightly thinner profile. model_name: Wind Turbine Project | Functional Simple Turbine
description: This is a heavily modified and fully functional remix of the excellent "Basic Wind Turbine" by kjt270000 . This remix transforms the original core concept into a practical, power-generating system designed specifically for apartment balconies and off-grid experimentation. This project includes completely redesigned mounting hardware, weatherproofing additions, structural reinforcements, and a complete perfboard electronics enclosure to harness the wind and charge an 18650 lithium-ion battery. 🛠️ What's New in this Remix? Two Optimized Sizes Medium Version: Retains the 24mm motor from the original model. Ideal for standard winds and smaller spaces. Large Version: Upgraded to house a 32mm motor, significantly increasing power generation potential for easier battery charging. Balcony-Ready Mounting System The mounting system has been completely engineered from scratch to easily clamp onto a typical balcony barrier. The Mast: Designed to use a standard 32mm (external diameter) PVC pipe with a 2.5mm wall thickness as the main tower. Free Rotation Yaw: To ensure the turbine can freely track wind direction (yaw) without friction, the design incorporates a standard bearing (27mm External Diameter / 15.5mm Internal Diameter) at the pivot point. Structural & Weatherproofing Upgrades Motor Cover: Added a top cover for the motor housing to improve weather resistance. (Note: While it provides splash and light rain protection, leaving the turbine out in heavy, continuous rain is still not encouraged). Tail Support: A new stabilizing brace was added to the tail section. This prevents the tail from sagging or bending under its own weight over time due to the natural layer orientation of FDM printing. Smart Cable Management On both versions, the main pivot body features a specific internal routing path. The cables run straight from the motor, inside the PVC pipe, and out the bottom. This prevents the wires from wrapping around the mast as the turbine rotates. ⚡ Electronics Overview (No Custom PCB Required!) Hardware Components List Core Modules & Power 1x 18650 Lithium-Ion Battery (3.7V, unprotected cell is fine since the circuit has protection) 1x 18650 Single Cell Battery Holder 1x TP4056 Lithium Battery Charging Module (Ensure you get the version with the built-in protection circuit—it has OUT+ and OUT- pads in addition to B+ and B-). 2x MT3608 DC-DC Step-Up Boost Converter Modules (Often marked as HW-045). Basic Electronic Components 4x Rectifier Diodes (1N4007 are standard, but 1N5819 Schottky diodes are highly recommended here for better efficiency and lower voltage drop). 1x Electrolytic Capacitor (Values around 470µF to 1000µF, rated for at least 16V or 25V). 1x Perfboard / Prototype PCB (Standard dot-matrix board, cut to fit your 3D printed enclosure). Miscellaneous Hookup wire (22-24 AWG stranded wire is ideal for flexibility) Solder How It Works (The Circuit Logic) Input & Rectification: The wind turbine motor generates erratic, fluctuating voltage (and possibly AC depending on the motor). The four diodes act as a Bridge Rectifier , ensuring the electricity flows in the right direction regardless of which way the wind spins the turbine. The Capacitor smooths out this rippling voltage. Boosting to Charge: The turbine might not always generate the 5V needed to charge the battery. The first MT3608 boost converter takes the smoothed voltage and steps it up to a steady 5V. Battery Management: The 5V feeds into the TP4056 module , which safely charges the 18650 battery and protects it from over-charging and over-discharging. Output Power: The 18650 battery outputs around 3.7V. The second MT3608 boost converter takes this battery voltage and steps it up to a stable 5V (or 12V, depending on what you are trying to power with the turbine). Step-by-Step Assembly Guide Important Pre-step: Before soldering the MT3608 modules into the final circuit, connect a temporary power source to their inputs, hook a multimeter to their outputs, and turn the little brass screw on the blue potentiometer until they output exactly your desired voltages (e.g., 5V for the first one). Step 1: The Rectifier Circuit (Power Input) Solder the 4 diodes onto the perfboard in a bridge rectifier configuration. Connect the two wires coming from your wind turbine motor to the AC input sides of the diode bridge. Solder the electrolytic capacitor across the positive and negative outputs of the diode bridge. Note: Capacitors have polarity; ensure the negative stripe side connects to the negative trace. Step 2: Voltage Stabilization (First Boost Converter) Connect the Positive output of the capacitor to the VIN+ on the first MT3608 module. Connect the Negative output of the capacitor to the VIN- on the first MT3608 module. Tune this module to output exactly 5V. Step 3: The Charging Circuit Connect the VOUT+ of the first MT3608 to the IN+ (or standard positive input pad) of the TP4056 module. Connect the VOUT- of the first MT3608 to the IN- of the TP4056 module. Solder the positive (red) wire from the 18650 battery holder to the B+ pad on the TP4056. Solder the negative (black) wire from the battery holder to the B- pad on the TP4056. Step 4: Output Power (Second Boost Converter) Connect the OUT+ pad from the TP4056 to the VIN+ pad of the second MT3608 module. Connect the OUT- pad from the TP4056 to the VIN- pad of the second MT3608 module. Adjust the potentiometer on this second MT3608 to your final desired output voltage (e.g., 5V for charging a phone, 12V for LED strips). Solder your final output wires to the VOUT+ and VOUT- pads of the second MT3608. Enjoy building, and may the wind be in your favor!

The key innovation is a fully 3D-printed flex sensor that uses conductive TPU filament - as the sensor bends, its electrical resistance changes, allowing precise measurement of finger flexion. description: 5-Speed Manual Gearbox with Reverse This is a fully functional, highly detailed 5-speed manual transmission model (plus Reverse) designed for educational demonstration, engineering enthusiasts, or anyone who loves mechanical design. Every major internal component of a real manual transmission is represented here, including the input shaft, counter shaft, main output shaft, synchronizer hubs, synchronizer rings, sliding sleeves, and a reverse idler gear. The multi-colored gear assembly makes it incredibly easy to visualize how shifting gears changes the drive ratios from the input shaft to the output shaft. Parts & Components List All components are designed to print at 100% scale (1:1) for a perfect mechanical fit. The model is organized into the following components: Shafts: INPUTSHAFT (Input Shaft) Counter (Counter Shaft) Shaft (Main Shaft) Output Gears: 26 34 38 44 44 reverse Synchronizer Assembly: HUB GEAR 17 14 (Synchronizer Hub) HUB GEAR 20 17 (Synchronizer Hub) SLEAVE GEAR (Synchronizer Sleeve) SYNC RING (Synchronizer Rings) Reverse Mechanism: IDLEAR GEAR V2 (Reverse Idler Gear) Display Stand & Hardware: Stand Part 1 & Stand Part 2 Stand Holder Part 1 & Stand Holder Part 2 14mm bolt & Pin SNAP RING & SNAP TO IDLER SHAFT Assembly & Printing Tips Color Coding: For the best visual effect, consider printing the matching gear sets on the main shaft and counter shaft in distinct colors (as shown in the project photos) to easily identify each speed. Tolerances: This is a mechanical model with interlocking parts. Ensure your printer's flow rate and X/Y tolerances are well-calibrated so the gears spin smoothly and the synchronizer sleeves slide without binding. Post-Processing: A small amount of plastic-safe lubricant (like silicone grease) on the shafts and gear teeth can drastically improve the smoothness of the manual shifting action.

My Educational Mechanical Examples Series This model is one of my educational mechanical mechanism examples on 80mm x 80mm base plates. You can find all models of the series in this collection => [Mechanical Mechanism Examples] The present model This is an educational model of self-centering chuck. Brief Description A self-centering chuck is a device often used with a lathe . A lathe is a machine tool that rotates a workpiece and presses a cutting tool against it to remove material, producing shapes that are symmetric about the axis of rotation. During turning, a workpiece often has to be re-clamped from a different side, and each time this is done the rotational center of the workpiece must be made to coincide exactly with the rotational center of the lathe. A self-centering chuck moves several jaws — arranged symmetrically around the lathe's axis — inward or outward together without breaking that symmetry, continuously varying the radius of the circle traced by their gripping faces. Because the jaws remain symmetric, a rotationally symmetric workpiece held in a self-centering chuck settles naturally with its own axis aligned to the lathe's axis, requiring no fine adjustment. The self-centering chuck shown here has three jaws, whose positions are set by a ring into which an Archimedean spiral is cut. An Archimedean spiral is a spiral whose adjacent turns are spaced a constant distance apart. When the ring turns at a constant rate, the point where the spiral crosses a given radius travels along that radius at a constant speed. The underside of each jaw carries a straight rack that meshes with this spiral, so as the ring turns and the crossing point moves, the jaw — whose motion is constrained to the radial direction — is carried along the radius by that motion. On the plane through the middle of a jaw, the mechanism is this simple, but the finite width of the rack teeth makes the story a little more complex. As the figure below shows, each rack tooth has to curve to follow the spiral. The curvature of an Archimedean spiral is not constant — it is tighter on the inside and gentler on the outside — so as a jaw travels along the radius, the curvature of the spiral tooth it meshes with changes as well. To keep the rack teeth from interfering at any position the jaw can reach, each tooth is shaped for the worst case: its inner edge is cut to the largest radius of curvature that occurs over the tooth's range of travel, and its outer edge to the smallest. This makes the valley between teeth wide and deep enough everywhere to clear the spiral ridge without interference. To keep all three jaws at the same distance from the center, the rack on each jaw is offset in phase by one third of a tooth pitch, as shown in the figure above. Only when the jaws are fitted in the correct order do the three jaws sit at equal distances from the center. In the photograph above, each jaw is stepped, growing thicker toward the center, as the left figure below. A jaw of this kind is called an inside-diameter (ID) step jaw. It is designed for two modes of use: gripping a workpiece placed between the three jaws by closing the jaws onto its outer surface, and supporting a hollow workpiece from within, by inserting the raised central step into the bore and opening the jaws against the inside of the hole. Both modes were demonstrated in the youtube video above. The model also includes, as optional parts, an outside-diameter (OD) step jaw, which instead grows thicker toward the outside (central figure), and a flat jaw with no steps (right figure). The OD step jaw is used to hold a workpiece whose diameter is too large to be gripped by the central part of the jaws. A working chuck on a lathe hides all of its mechanical detail inside a steel body; here, laid open, the spiral and the racks show plainly how symmetry is turned into motion. Related model In the model of Groove Cam , the follower motion was limited along an arc by the swinging arm. In the present model, the teeth on the bottom surface of the jaws can be regarded as followers running in the Archimedean spiral groove. There, the followers' motion is limited along straight lines by the linear guide, instead of arcs. The model of Archimedean spiral gear, included in "Educational Gear Examples 2" shows a combination of Archimedean spiral with a pinion gear, instead of rack. Case This model is compatible with the case included in my first set . Printing Use the models named ???-printable.stl for printing . The models named ???-assembled.stl are provided just to show how they should be assembled. Use well-dried PETG to have better dimensional accuracy. Use 0.1 mm or 0.08 mm layer height to have smoother surfaces. Use slow printing speed for overhangs. Select “Random” seam position to have smoother rotation. Randomly distributed seam should be easily worn out after some wearing.Printing Sanding and Filing Note that, in this model, the rotation of the bases for bearings is intentionally made not too smooth. Sometimes, the gears suffer from the stringing effect and/or elephant foot effect, resulting in a too tight fit to the shafts (they are designed with a 0.15 mm radial clearance). If you see rough surface on the shafts due to stringing, sand off the roughness with a small piece of sand paper. If you feel the gears do not rotate smoothly due to an elephant effect, widen the hole slightly by using a thin round bar file. Without those issues, the parts should rotate very smoothly with minimal friction. Assembly Place the knob on the shaft and secure it with the retaining ring. Place the ring gear. Push the legs of the linear guide into the holes on the base plate. They will snap into place. While turning the ring gear counter-clockwise, slide the jaws into the linear guides one by one to make them mate with the spiral, referring to the number of dimples on the jaws. The one with single dimple should be the first, one with two dimples the second, and one with three dimples the last. Since three jaws have their teeth at different phases, if they are placed with wrong order, they will not be at same distance from the center. The order of insertion is what matters — any jaw can go into any guide, as long as the single-, double-, and triple-dimple jaws are inserted in that order. To replace the jaws to those of different type, turn the ring gear clockwise fully until the jaws come out from the linear guide. Then slide the replacing jaws in following the step 4. description: SpaceX Starship V3: The Future of Space Exploration Elevate your workspace with this detailed SpaceX Starship V3 display model! Whether you are an aerospace enthusiast or just love a striking centerpiece, this design captures the essence of modern spacecraft architecture. Designed for display, this model brings engineering art to your desk. Detailed Description This Starship V3 model is engineered for aesthetic appeal. Its improved toughness and dimensional accuracy ensure that your panels look sharp and professional. History: The Path to Starship V3 SpaceX was incorporated on March 14, 2002, by Elon Musk. Inspired by his desire to make humanity multi-planetary, Musk shifted his focus from the internet to aerospace after being discouraged by the high costs and lack of innovation in the industry. The Starship program represents the culmination of SpaceX's iterative "fail fast, learn faster" philosophy: Early Iterations: Development began with small, low-altitude "hops" using the Starhopper prototype in 2019, followed by high-altitude test flights of various "SN" (Serial Number) vehicles. Many ended in fiery explosions, but each provided invaluable data on structural integrity, engine performance, and landing maneuvers. The Integrated Flight Era: Starting with the first fully integrated launch in April 2023, SpaceX began testing the combination of the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage. The program moved through multiple vehicle "Blocks," constantly refining hardware, software, and pad infrastructure. Recent Milestones & V3: After years of rapid progress—including catching boosters with the launch tower arms and perfecting in-space engine relights—SpaceX debuted the Starship V3 on May 22, 2026. This 12th major flight test featured upgraded Raptor 3 engines, a more robust hot-staging ring, and enhanced satellite deployment capabilities. While the booster experienced a hard splashdown during this debut test, the Ship reached its target and successfully gathered critical data, proving the resilience of this new, massive design.
