description: This is the new version of my popular Instax Mini 12 keychain. It features a functional button that pushes out the film, letting you place a small picture inside—perfect for a heartfelt gift or to keep your loved ones close wherever you go. but in this version everything got better. What's new: No Glue Needed - Completely redesigned snap-fit system. Parts lock together without super glue. Better Mechanisms - The lever and button were rebuilt from scratch. They're much stiffer and shouldn't break. Film Bottom Lock - This was a big complaint with the V12. Now when you push the photo back into the slot, it stays there. Even if you flip the camera upside down. Perfect for keychain use. Film Top Lock - Press the button fast and hard enough and the film locks at the top too. Another thing people asked for. Improved Film Ejection - Much smoother push mechanism overall. More Detailed - Slightly bigger than V12 but way more accurate to the real Instax Mini 13. Important: Once you close the camera using the snap-fit, it's permanent. Don't try to reopen it or you'll break it. This isn't a design flaw - it's by design so it stays secure as a keychain. Picture Dimensions (Dimensions: 24x29mm ) For Commercial Use: If you have my commercial membership and plan to sell these, I recommend adding super glue to the snap fits for extra durability. Personal use? The snap fits are solid on their own. How to Assemble: Step 1 Gather all parts. Step 2 Very gently and lightly press these pieces until you hear a click. (If you don't want to risk breaking them, skip this step; they will eventually come loose as you press the film.) Step 3 Position the lever and the button/pin as shown in the image (do not try to press the button as the system will not work until the cover is in place) . Now insert the film, making sure that these two knobs are facing downwards; this will lock the film inside the Instax. Step 4 (If you want, you can use super glue on this step where the pins are, so the Instax is more secure, but this is no longer necessary because of the snap lock pins.) Place the front cover by fitting the 3 middle pins into the holes on the back of the front cover and press one side at a time so that the front cover locks in place. Step 5 Take and attach the two snap lock pins either to the middle back of the Instax or to the back cover, the order doesn't matter. Step 6 (This is another step where you can use super glue) Now attach the back part and press (you might need to apply some force here, don't worry, nothing will break (I hope)). Step 7 If you did everything right, you now have a cute and cool new Instax Mini 13 Keychain, enjoy :) Don't forget to share your builds!

description: EN: This is a 1:150 scale Boeing 737 MAX 8 model. Assembly requires glue. I found that using a combination of super glue for the internal structure and UV-curable glue for the exterior parts produces the best results. Assembly instructions can be found at the bottom of the description. It might sound like an upgrade, but the interior wasn't exactly in the greatest condition (the leather on many of the seats was already cracked), thanks to the wonderful maintenance standards of U.S. airlines. I decided to make a MAX 8 instead because there are simply more resources and references available for it. ZH： 去年我乘坐过一次阿拉斯加航空的 737 MAX 9，不过这次体验有点一言难尽，因为航司把原本计划执飞的带翼梢小翼的 737-900——我订票时特意选的、并且真正想坐的机型——换成了 MAX 9。听起来是一次升级，但多亏了美国航司幽默的维护水平，机舱内饰的状态实在拉跨（好多座位的皮都裂开了）。最终我还是决定制作 MAX 8，主要是因为关于这个机型的资料和参考图片更多。 EN: I included two print profiles: Blank: A single-color version of the model. You can paint it yourself or apply any decals you like. Lion Air: The only difference is that the engines have an orange (more red than orange to my eyes) color. I also attached a PDF file, which contains a livery of Lion Air and includes three different sizes, since print settings may affect the final dimensions. I recommend referencing photos of a real Lion Air 737 MAX 8 to determine the most accurate decal size for your print. Registration number PK-LQP is enclosed in a black box, due to the catastrophic accident. RIP to all victims, and hope all airplane manufacturers will do the right thing in the future. ZH： 我提供了两个打印配置： 白版（Blank）： 单色版本模型。您可以自行上色或贴上任何喜欢的贴纸。 狮航版（Lion Air）： 模型本身唯一的区别是发动机采用了橙色（感觉更偏红而不是橙色）。我还附上了一份 PDF 文件，其中包含狮航涂装贴纸，并提供了三种不同尺寸，因为不同的打印设置可能会影响贴纸的实际尺寸。我建议参考真实狮航 737 MAX 8 的照片，以确定最适合你打印模型的贴纸尺寸。注册号PK-LQP被特意放在黑框中，以标记那场灾难性的空难。愿所有遇难者安息，也希望未来所有飞机制造商都能做人事。

About Models: These models are designed to represent real animals as naturally as possible, with focus on accurate size, shapes, proportions, colors, fine details, and natural movement or pose. Some models include articulated, hinge, or flexi parts for motion and flexibility, while others are non-articulated and focus on realistic appearance. Some parts, such as legs, can be carefully adjusted with gentle heat for a more natural pose, but too much heat can damage or deform the model. Print: All settings are pre-configured and optimized for a balance between detail, print time, strength, functionality, and easy support removal. I recommend printing the models at their original scale. Scaling down may cause issues such as fused moving parts, small hinges not working correctly, or fine details not printing properly. Difficulty Guide: The difficulty icon is a general overall guide and may vary depending on your printer, filament, slicer settings, calibration, and experience. It mainly reflects print complexity, filament changes, possible waste, fine details, support use, and support removal. Multicolor prints may create more waste on single-nozzle AMS or AMS Lite systems, such as A1 with AMS Lite, compared to dual-nozzle or lower-waste systems like X2D or H2C. Level 3 / Supports: For higher difficulty models, especially Level 3, I recommend using Support Material for PLA. It can make support removal much easier, cleaner, and safer for delicate parts. This is especially helpful when the model has many supports, thin details, legs, antennas, or other fragile areas. Articulated / Hinge Versions: For models with moving parts, hinges, or flexi sections, please open the included 3MF file, ideally in Bambu Studio. Exporting to another slicer may cause hinge problems. My hinges are created and tested by me, usually designed to print without supports, and are added this way so they can be moved, adjusted, customized, or removed when scaling the model down. STL / 3MF Note: STL files are usually provided without moving parts. The prepared articulated or hinge version is inside the 3MF file. This helps avoid problems with small scaled-down models, where moving parts, gaps, or hinges may fuse or fail. If needed, you can remove the hinges and print the model as a solid version. Safety Notice: Some models may have sharp edges or small parts. Avoid printing them too small and do not leave children unattended with them, as there is a choking risk. If you adjust parts with heat, always proceed carefully and use heat gently. Support / Links: I truly appreciate every comment, rating, or photo of your print it really motivates me to keep creating. model_name: Miniature Parsons Chair Base For Upholstering
description: This is a hybrid project - most of the 3d printed parts don't even show in the finished piece! This base is made to let you upholster your own 1:12 scale miniature Parsons chair without having to model the supporting structure by hand from other materials. The description here isn't as long as with the model I shared earlier this year: Scale Miniature Chair Base for Upholstering , because this one is my original design and I've written a, hopefully detailed enough, assembly tutorial which you can find linked below. If you've never done miniature upholstery before and don't feel confident, that's understandable but I bet you'll find it easier than it looks. You might also enjoy the armchair project linked above, or find it helpful to skim this tutorial for it: https://1inchminisbykris.blogspot.com/2013/01/chair-upholstering-tuttorial-how-to.html. I'm providing some selected excerpts from the tutorial so you know what kind of supplies you'll want to have for this project, without having to download the file. I've gotten some lovely feedback and compliments on the armchair model, which really helped me stay motivated through the creation and testing process for this one. I hope you enjoy this project if you decide to give it a try, and I look forward to seeing your creations! Let me know if you have any struggles and I will try to help (I check in here a couple times a week most of the time). What to gather up once you've printed the files: Tools: Sharp scissors, craft knife, tweezers (Optional: pinking shears, applique or nail scissors with a curved blade) Glues: glue stick, preferred structural/assembly glue, preferred fabric/craft glue Textile materials: something for batting (i prefer cotton), something for upholstery material (still prefer cotton) Other handy stuff if you have it already: A piece of photo paper to put under templates while gluesticking them, rubber brayer to smooth fabric on templates, Fray Check. More detailed remarks on materials: Quilting cotton or muslin in a small print. I recommend this for beginners particularly as it's much easier to glue than synthetics, both for sticking purposes, and for not making the fabric look stupid and jacked up. You don't need a lot of fabric. I didn't even have an eighth yard left of that pink flowered fabric I used. Batting/padding. I use Warm & Natural cotton batting usually, and it's my favorite since it's easy to shape and kind of smoosh into position even if it's not perfect at first. I've also upholstered with synthetic felt or fleece, or even untextured paper towels for very small scale work. If you don't mind doing more layers, you'll be fine using a thinner batting. You could also make the cushions less dramatically stuffed. Probably the most important thing is choosing a batting material you like working with, that won't look lumpy or show through the fabric in a way you don't like. Glue. For this project I used an Elmers Craft Bond extra strength glue stick, Gorilla brand wood glue, because it sets up pretty quick and sticks to PLA better than you'd expect, and Bearly Art craft glue. Bearly Art is a bit pricey in my opinion, so I don't necessarily love to recommend it to others. Suggested alternate adhesives: Most of the Aleene's product line. Beacon FabriTac. The main things you want to accomplish adhesive-wise are listed below by use case: For the thin plastic panels use a glue stick to attach the fabric, because it's an easy way to get good enough coverage to keep the fabric from wrinkling. Suggestions: most glue sticks are probably fine. For structural gluing of PLA panels to PLA, or for gluing raw fabric edges to PLA where it'll be covered later , use something that grabs well and cures firm. Suggestions: most of the Aleene's product line but especially turbo tacky. Beacon FabriTac. Gorilla wood glue. For gluing fabric to fabric , use something that won't dry stiff in a place you want the fabric to look plush or flat. Wood glue will dry hard and you want a more flexible hold. It's smart to test the glue on your particular fabric to make sure it cooperates and doesn't bleed through and look awful. Suggestions: Bearly Art if you got the bucks, Beacon FabriTac, Aleene's.

Brown trout are another common species of trout targeted by anglers, and the newest flexi model in my collection. Originally native to Europe, western Asia, and northern Africa, this species has been transported worldwide to such a degree that it is one of the top 100 invasive species in the world. With such a wide dispersal, many forms and subspecies have formed ranging in appearance and behavior. Some are anadromous meaning they swim out to sea to spend most of their lives, returning only to spawn. During spawning season, males develop a kype, or hooked bottom jaw to help them fight other males for breeding territory. While this characteristic is not unique to this species, it's something I wanted to include in the model to capture the appearance of trophy brown trout caught by anglers. Large specimens can reach 40 lbs and 31 inches. Brown trout are generalist predators meaning they'll eat a wide array of bugs, invertebrates, frogs, and even mice. This model uses interlocking scale units to swim and is printed in 2 halves, aligned with the registration pin and secured by glue on the flat faces. Dies ist die legendäre Black Pearl , das schnellste Schiff der Karibik, inspiriert von den Filmen! Ich habe sie mit höchster Detailtreue nachgebildet. Das Besondere: Dieses Modell ist darauf ausgelegt, wasserdicht zu sein und tatsächlich zu schwimmen! Aber wie bei jedem legendären Schiff gibt es einen Haken, eine Herausforderung, die nur die tapfersten Baumeister meistern können. Die Merkmale: Höchste Detailtreue Schwimmfähig Wasserdichtigkeit Die Herausforderung: Aufgrund der hohen Detailtreue und der unterschiedlichen Gewichtsverhältnisse des 3D-Druckmaterials im Vergleich zum "echten" Schiff ist die Black Pearl im Wasser extrem kopflastig und instabil. Ohne Anpassung wird sie sofort umkippen. Du musst sie ausbalancieren! Schritt-für-Schritt-Anleitung zur Trimmung: Gewichtsanbringung: Um sie aufrecht zu halten, musst du Gewichte an der Unterseite des Rumpfes anbringen. Du kannst kleine Bleikügelchen, Metallplättchen oder Angelblei verwenden. In unserem Beispielbild haben wir kleine Gewichte am Kiel angebracht, um den Effekt zu zeigen. Feinabstimmung: Experimentiere mit der Position und der Menge der Gewichte. Füge kleine Mengen hinzu und überprüfe, wie sich das Gleichgewicht im Wasser ändert. Perfekte Stabilität: Das Ziel ist es, den Metazentrum/Schwerpunkt so zu justieren, dass das Schiff aufrecht im Wasser schwimmt, ohne zu kippen. Dies ist eine echte Ingenieursleistung! Der “Kleine Fehler” PS: Ich habe einen winzigen, aber deutlichen Fehler in das Modell eingebaut. Schau genau hin. Kannst du ihn entdecken?. Schreib deinen Tipp in die Kommentare! Dies ist ein Projekt für Fortgeschrittene, das Geduld und Präzision erfordert. Aber das Endergebnis ist es wert! Hast du das Zeug dazu, die Black Pearl zu meistern?

description: Bring a clean tactical landing zone to your grimdark sci-fi battlefield with this detailed Empty Imperial Landing Platform terrain piece. This model is designed as a large octagonal sci-fi platform with a grated surface, reinforced outer frame, riveted armor panels and a central winged skull emblem. The piece includes a wide front ramp and a fully open landing area, making it easy to use with vehicles, walkers, objective markers or infantry during gameplay. Its empty layout gives you maximum flexibility on the table, while the strong industrial design makes it fit perfectly into imperial outposts, military bases, spaceports or fortified battlefield zones. Unlike cluttered platform terrain, this version is kept clean and open, without crates, barrels or fixed accessories. This makes it easier to place miniatures, vehicles and mission markers directly on the platform and keeps the model highly practical for actual tabletop use. All my models are real test prints, not just digital renders. I always try to find the best balance between print time, level of detail and filament usage, so the terrain looks impressive on the table without becoming unnecessarily difficult or wasteful to print. I also put a lot of effort into optimizing the files, removing print issues and making the models as user-friendly as possible. My goal is to offer terrain that prints cleanly, feels solid, and can be used straight from the printer or painted with simple drybrushing techniques. Designed with FDM printing in mind, the piece is suitable for PLA filament printing and looks great in simple grey material without any color changes. description: A miniature model of Dalaran from WoW that floats using the Bambu Lab Magnetic Levitation DIY Kit! Model based on the Broken Isles version of Dalaran as it exists (or existed…) in-game Levitates using the Bambu Lab Magnetic Levitation DIY Kit, but you can of course print this for use without the kit. The small building models would be good as standalone DnD miniatures models too. Two versions - a multicolour version which despite having 13 different filaments, is split up so it can still be made with a printer with a single AMS. And a single colour version for a quicker print or for something that can be painted later. Highly detailed, with as much detail as you could possibly want printing with a 0.4mm nozzle at this scale. The actual city, not including the MagLev base, when assembled is roughly 170 x 130 x 170 mm. Making this is more of a 3D printing “quest” rather than a simple print especially if printing the multicolour version and getting it to float perfectly with the MagLev kit. Check out the assembly instructions below on how to assemble once printed. Be extra careful whenever handling any of the thin parts especially if printing in PLA Matte, they can break easily. You have been warned. The single colour version's 3MF doesn't have the base I designed, and I've used the base shell from MakerWorld for it in the photos, which you can download from here: https://makerworld.com/en/models/759193-base-shell-for-magnetic-levitation-kit?from=search#profileId-693690 There is a third print profile which has individual spires in case you need to reprint, and also has more trees for both adding weight, and making the model look a little more like the game version. Print Settings IMPORTANT: If possible, download and print this from a computer rather than using Bambu Handy, and increase Z-hop when retract to 0.8mm and Z-hop Type to Spiral in the printer's extruder settings. This is needed for better print quality for any plate that has multiple thin spires. This also helps if you are having print failures with the thin spires. See the print profile descriptions or 3MFs for full print settings. If printing this on a non-Bambu Lab printer, I would highly recommend you to download the Bambu Studio 3MF and use Orca Slicer which retains all the print settings. Even if you do want to change things for yourself, this will be a good starting point. Filament The multicolour version uses a lot of different filaments. description: 🍄 Shrieker Fungus Miniature – Screaming Fungal Colony This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The miniature consists of three large mushrooms growing together as a single fungal colony , with one dominant central Shrieker and two smaller mushrooms positioned to either side. The central mushroom is the tallest and most prominent. It has a thick, vertically ridged stalk that widens slightly toward the base and supports a broad, heavy mushroom cap. The stalk is textured with deep organic grooves and fibrous folds, giving it the appearance of tightly bundled fungal tissue. Set into the front of the central stalk is a large vertical mouth , stretched wide open as if the fungus is screaming. The mouth is an organic cavity formed directly within the flesh of the stalk, with thick wrinkled edges and a deep hollow interior. There are no eyes, nose, or humanoid facial features . The broad central cap has a rounded, irregular shape with a slightly drooping edge. Its surface is rough and uneven, covered with numerous small swollen fungal nodules and wart-like growths. The underside displays clearly defined radial gills extending outward from the stalk. Two smaller Shrieker mushrooms flank the central specimen. Both have thick, ridged stalks and broad caps with the same rough, nodular texture. Their different heights and slightly angled growth create an asymmetrical, natural fungal cluster. Small openings and subtle organic features can appear within their stalks, but the large screaming mouth of the central mushroom remains the main focal point. The color palette consists of muted purple, burgundy, brown, dirty beige, and fleshy pink tones . The caps are predominantly dark purple and reddish-brown, while the stalks are pale brown and beige with purple discoloration around the roots and organic folds. All three mushrooms grow directly from the base, with their stalks firmly connected to the ground. Their lower bodies spread into thick fungal roots and mycelial growths that merge naturally into the terrain. The base represents a damp cavern or forest floor with dark earth, small stones, patches of moss, clusters of tiny purple fungi, and scattered organic growth. Silent. Until disturbed. Fine mineral textures and weathered grooves help sell the illusion that the creature is simply another part of the cavern ceiling, making it an iconic ambush predator. Beneath the mantle, numerous muscular tentacles extend downward in graceful curling poses. Each appendage is thickened and reinforced for reliable 3D printing while preserving the organic movement that gives the Darkmantle its unsettling appearance. Near the upper edge of the mantle, a ring of small, watchful eyes peers from beneath the stone-like folds. Their subtle placement reinforces the creature's alien anatomy without disrupting the convincing stalactite silhouette. The scenic base features sharp stalagmites and rugged cavern stone, creating the impression that the Darkmantle is descending into an underground chamber. These integrated rock formations provide excellent structural support while enhancing the miniature's subterranean atmosphere. The pose conveys patient inevitability. This is not a monster rushing into battle. This is a hunter that has already waited hours for its next victim. ✨ Key Features Darkmantle inspired by Monster Manual 2024 Realistic stalactite-inspired mantle with layered rock textures Multiple thick tentacles sculpted for stable 3D printing Subtle ring of watchful eyes beneath the mantle Dynamic descending pose full of subterranean menace Scenic cavern base with stalagmites and durable structural support 🎨 Great for Painting Perfect for subterranean palettes: dark greys, charcoal blacks, muted browns, and subtle mineral highlights. Dry brushing beautifully enhances the rocky mantle, while washes emphasize the tentacle textures. Gloss varnish on the eyes and tentacles can create a damp cave-dwelling appearance. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Scaled for standard tabletop RPG play , including Dungeons & Dragons . Perfect as an Underdark ambush predator, cavern encounter, dungeon hazard, or atmospheric subterranean monster. It waits without breathing. Without moving. 🐾 Vizsla The Vizsla is an elegant, athletic breed celebrated for its striking golden-rust coat, affectionate nature, and exceptional versatility. Originating in Hungary, the Vizsla was developed centuries ago as a hunting companion, prized for its ability to point and retrieve game across fields, forests, and wetlands with speed, endurance, and precision. Graceful yet powerful, the Vizsla combines remarkable athleticism with a deeply loyal and people-oriented temperament. Often called the "Velcro dog" because of its desire to stay close to its family, this breed thrives on companionship and human interaction. Today, Vizslas are cherished as devoted family dogs, energetic sporting partners, and loving companions who excel in both active lifestyles and affectionate homes. 🐶 Appearance & Personality Coat: Short, smooth, and dense coat with a beautiful golden-rust color that is unique to the breed. Their coat is low-maintenance and naturally glossy. Build: Medium-sized, lean, and muscular with an elegant yet athletic frame. Built for speed, stamina, and agility rather than bulk. Expression: Warm, intelligent, and gentle. Their expressive amber eyes reflect the breed's affectionate and eager-to-please personality. Ears: Long, silky ears that hang close to the cheeks, contributing to their refined appearance. Tail: Traditionally docked in some countries, though naturally long where docking is prohibited. Carried with a slight curve and used actively during movement. Temperament: Affectionate, energetic, and highly intelligent. Vizslas are exceptionally loyal and form deep bonds with their families. They are friendly, sensitive, and thrive on positive interaction, making them wonderful companions for active households. 🎾 Activity & Companionship Vizslas are high-energy dogs that require plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation. They excel in activities such as running, hiking, agility, scent work, obedience, field sports, and retrieving games. Originally bred as versatile hunting dogs, they enjoy having a job to do and flourish when given regular challenges and training. Vizslas crave human companionship and are happiest when included in family activities. They generally do not enjoy being left alone for extended periods and thrive in homes where they receive plenty of attention and interaction. 💪 Health & Care Exercise: High — Vizslas need substantial daily physical activity combined with mental enrichment to remain healthy and well-balanced. Coat care: Low — their short coat requires only occasional brushing to remove loose hair and maintain its natural shine. description: This latest addition to the collection is easily one of my favorites. Eddie Van Halen revolutionized rock guitar playing, and his primary weapon of choice was the Frankenstrat (also known as "Frankenstein" or "Frankie"). Hand-built by Eddie in his garage in the mid-1970s, this DIY masterpiece forever changed instrument design and birthed the modern "Superstrat". Below is a little bit of history on this remarkable guitar. Technical Specifications & Assembly The Body & Neck: Eddie bought an unfinished Northern Ash Strat-style body and a maple neck from Charvel/Boogie Bodies for around $130. He purposely chose a body with a cosmetic wood knot because it was cheaper. The Electronics: He used a hammer and chisel to carve out the bridge cavity to fit a high-output Gibson PAF humbucker taken from an ES-335. He screwed the pickup directly into the wood and simplified the wiring to a single master volume knob. He even labeled the volume knob with a dial that said "Tone". The Dummy Elements: To confuse competitors and copycats, he installed a non-functional neck single-coil pickup and a broken 3-way selector switch into the middle slot, neither of which were actually wired to anything. The Tremolo System: Originally built with a standard Fender tremolo, Eddie worked closely with inventor Floyd Rose in 1980 to implement the revolutionary Floyd Rose dual-locking tremolo. This allowed Eddie to perform his signature, pitch-dropping "dive bombs" without falling out of tune. The 1971 Quarter: Eddie famously screwed a 1971 quarter directly into the guitar's wood underneath the back of the bridge to act as a physical stop, preventing the tremolo from pulling up. Evolution of the Iconic Paint Job The Frankenstrat's aesthetic evolved over time using strips of masking tape and layers of standard spray paint: Black and White (1977–1978): The original coat was painted black. Eddie applied masking tape lines and sprayed over it with white paint. When the tape was peeled away, it left a striking geometric design. This version is featured on the cover of the 1978 debut album Van Halen . The Red Overwrite (1979): As other guitar manufacturers began copying his black-and-white design, Eddie decided to change it. He re-taped the body and sprayed it with red Schwinn bicycle paint To make this model complete. description: Bone-Pile Mimic (Full DMs documentation included) Huge monstrosity (shapechanger), typically neutral evil What appears to be a mound of ancient battlefield remains is actually a patient and ravenous predator. Broken shields, rusted helmets, scattered weapons, and the bones of dozens of dead adventurers form its outer shell. A treasure chest often rests at the top of the pile, positioned as irresistible bait. When disturbed, the entire mound convulses. Ribs bend into grasping limbs, skulls turn toward nearby creatures, and the central mass tears open into an enormous tooth-filled maw. Long pseudopods of fused bone and dark flesh drag victims into the creature while sharpened fragments erupt from the ground to pin down anyone attempting to flee. Unlike an ordinary hoard mimic, the Bone-Pile Mimic is highly aggressive. It does not wait for prey to approach one at a time. Once awakened, it attempts to immobilize several enemies, separate them from their companions, and slowly drain their life through barbed skeletal growths. The bones covering the mimic are not merely camouflage. Many retain fragments of their former owners’ memories. Faint whispers, final screams, and promises of hidden treasure can sometimes be heard coming from inside the pile.

The sword remains firmly connected to the ground for a strong and stable miniature design. His opposite arm extends outward with an open hand in a calm but commanding gesture, as though addressing mortals, issuing a divine challenge, or preparing to unleash supernatural power. His stance is broad and confident, with both feet firmly planted on the rocky terrain. The flowing robes sweep naturally around his legs without obscuring the overall anatomy or silhouette. The result is not an armored angel or a conventional giant, but a towering divine humanoid: beautiful, physically overwhelming, and unmistakably celestial. Strength beyond mortality. The Sunken Watch of Weeping Stone Before you sits a grim testament to a forgotten age: a once-proud gatehouse reduced to a husk of its former self. The structure, cast in a weathered, slate-grey resin, depicts two heavily damaged, circular towers flanking a pulverized central archway. The stone is heavily eroded, giving it a rugged, ancient texture. The left tower has crumbled almost to its base, its crenelations completely shattered, while the right tower stands precariously, a jagged stump with only one remaining arrow slit. The ground around the structure is a choked expanse of rubble, loose scree, and massive, irregular stone blocks that have spilled from the walls. The path leading through the gate is a worn, uneven track littered with debris. Set deep within the collapsed central arch is a rusted, skeletal portcullis, lowered and sealed, barring all passage. The entire piece rests upon a meticulously detailed diorama base, featuring patches of withered static grass, scattered pebbles, and larger, moss-covered rocks, grounding it firmly in a desolate environment. Atmosphere & Lore (Dark Fantasy): This ruin feels cold and forsaken. The air around it seems still, heavy with the scent of old stone and decay. The shadows within the archway are deep and unwelcoming. Whatever tragedy befell this outpost—a dragon's breath, a siege by undead hordes, or a magical catastrophe—it left an indelible stain of despair. It is not merely an obstacle; it is a narrative hook, waiting for adventurers to approach and disturb the silence that has held for centuries.

It works perfectly as cover for gunfights, line-of-sight interruption, objective scenery or a flavorful terrain element for pirate-themed tabletop battlefields. Its detailed but practical design makes it especially useful for games like Freebooter’s Fate , where characterful terrain and clever positioning play a major role. The long, narrow footprint fits naturally along docks, beaches, harbor fronts, island settlements or ramshackle fortifications and helps create an immersive pirate setting without taking up too much space on the table. All my models are real test prints, not just digital renders. I always try to find the best balance between print time, level of detail and filament usage, so the terrain looks impressive on the table without becoming unnecessarily difficult or wasteful to print. I also put a lot of effort into optimizing the files, removing print issues and making the models as user-friendly as possible. My goal is to offer terrain that prints cleanly, feels solid, and can be used straight from the printer or painted with simple drybrushing techniques. Designed with FDM printing in mind, the piece is suitable for PLA filament printing and looks great in simple grey material without any color changes. description: A student gifted me this NeeDoh Nice Cube at the height of its popularity at the school, and I kept in on my desk for awhile. The problem was that every single person wanted to touch it and play with it - without asking - and it got grimey. Now, the NeeDoh sits in its little mini jail cell on my desk for eyes only, or, if you ask nicely, waiting for someone to use it during a test :) A lot of students asked in horror why I put the NeeDoh in jail. The top of the jail cell/cage comes off easily, but stays in place unless pulled out. Customize it directly in the MakerWorld / OpenSCAD customizer to fit straps, webbing, cords, paracord, loops or flat mounting tabs — no CAD software required. This model generates a real two-part buckle: male part with flexible snap arms and rigid center guide; female part with side-release windows. Main features 7 attachment styles, independently selectable for each side Choose a different tail style for the male and female parts: sewn slot belt pass-through adjustable tri-glide paracord holes, 2 or 4 holes closed loop / D-ring style single cord hole solid flat tab The tail shape automatically adapts to the selected attachment type: narrow rounded shape for cord use, full-width body for webbing, shaped tails for loops, paracord and flat mounting. Wide size range Designed for webbing widths from 10 mm to 60 mm , with adjustable overall thickness from 5 mm to 14 mm . Rigid center guide tongue — V2 The male part includes a rigid central guide tongue that helps insertion, reduces lateral wobble and protects the flexible arms from over-bending. On very narrow buckles, the guide is automatically disabled if there is not enough physical space. Improved snap-fit durability V2 includes several geometry improvements: rounded arm roots to reduce stress concentration; chamfered and rounded entry mouth for smoother insertion; side windows sized so the arms can relax when locked; adjustable latch geometry and arm stiffness. One-parameter fit tuning The most important parameter is clearance. Recommended starting point: default: 0.35 tighter fit: 0.25 – 0.30 looser fit: 0.40 – 0.45 Print, test, then fine-tune only this value first. Safe parametric sliders Critical parameters are internally limited to keep the geometry printable. If a limit is reached, OpenSCAD shows a NOTE in the console. Printing instructions Print the parts flat on the bed , exactly as generated in the both layout. This is important because the snap arms flex in the XY plane , so the stress stays within the printed layers. Do not print the buckle upright, otherwise the arms may break along the layer lines. Recommended settings: no supports required; PETG or PLA+ recommended; ABS / ASA for outdoor or hotter environments; 0.2 mm layer height; 3 perimeters; 25–40% infill. For this model, perimeters matter more than infill . Included files Full parametric OpenSCAD source file; ready-to-print STL pair for 25 mm webbing : male part with sewn slot; female part with tri-glide attachment. V2 changelog Compared to the previous version, V2 adds: rigid center guide tongue; improved side-release fit; rounded arm roots; smoother chamfered mouth; shaped tails for different attachment styles; description: Make your own text stamp for clay, soap, leather, play dough, fondant, and normal ink-pad stamping. Up to three lines of custom text, round or rectangular head, emboss or deboss, optional border, and a comfortable twist-lock handle. Prints support-free. Type your text and print a personal stamp. The rigid PETG/PLA version presses crisp, readable impressions into polymer clay, air-dry clay, soap, soft leather, play dough, fondant, and similar soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping, a tested option is to split the stamp face in the slicer and print the actual raised letters/rim in TPU, with the base and handle in PETG, so the letters flex slightly like a softer stamp face. Features: - Up to three lines of text, automatically centered. - Mirrored text by default, so the stamped impression reads correctly. Turn mirroring off to print a readable display plaque instead. - Two impression styles: "raised" presses your text INTO the material (debossed impression), "recessed" leaves your text standing proud (embossed impression). - Round or rectangular head with adjustable size and optional border ring - the border stamps a clean frame around your text. - Adjustable text depth (0.8-3 mm) for shallow or deep impressions. - Comfortable mushroom handle with a bayonet twist-lock: insert into the head back and twist clockwise to a firm stop. The locked handle cannot pull off, even when lifting the stamp out of sticky clay. Print one handle and many heads: name stamps, date stamps, logo text, gift tags. - Tested TPU-face workflow: print the raised letters/rim in TPU and the base + handle in PETG for a softer face that also works better as a normal ink-pad stamp. - Console warning if your text is too wide for the chosen head size. - Both parts print flat with no supports. The model checks your text width against the head size and prints a note in the customizer console if a line will not fit. Note: rigid PLA/PETG stamp faces are best for clay, soap, leather, dough, and other soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping on paper, the tested TPU-face workflow gives a more forgiving contact surface than a hard FDM face. Results still depend on ink pad, paper, layer height, and surface finish, so test first. Custom Fonts: You can use any font MakerWorld has installed , type it into font_name as "Family:style=Style". Examples: Liberation Sans:style=Bold (default) Liberation Serif:style=Bold (bookplate look) Liberation Mono:style=Bold (typewriter) Liberation Sans Narrow:style=Bold (fits longer text) DejaVu Sans:style=Bold DejaVu Serif:style=Bold Stick to Bold styles thin strokes don't stamp well and can be fragile. Customization Notes - line_1 / line_2 / line_3: your text; leave lines empty to use fewer lines. - font_name: keep the default Liberation Sans Bold for reliable width warnings; other bold fonts work, but check the preview. - mirror_text: leave ON for stamping. Turn off only for display plaques. - text_style: "raised" = pressed-in (debossed) impression, "recessed" = raised (embossed) impression. - text_depth: 1.5 mm default; use 2-3 mm for soft doughs, 1-1.5 mm for firm clay and leather. - head_shape / head_diameter / head_width / head_height: face size. Bigger faces fit longer text. - border_enabled / border_width / border_inset: frame ring around the text. - border_depth: rim height, independent of text_depth. Match text_depth for a classic one-level stamp, or make the rim taller than the text so it contains the material and controls impression depth like a cookie-cutter frame - useful for wax-seal-style stamps and uniform clay medallions. - fit_clearance: twist-lock clearance. Increase by 0.05-0.1 if the handle is hard to insert or twist; decrease toward 0.05 for a tighter lock. - part: "all" prints both pieces; "head" alone for extra stamp faces for a handle you already printed; "fit_preview" is preview-only - do not print. description: Windproof Heavy Duty Sand Pegs Stakes with 19mm HEX Designed For Extreme Beach Camping Stop watching your tent fly away in coastal gales. Built out of pure necessity, these heavy-duty screw-in sand pegs were designed to withstand the brutal realities of off-grid wild beach camping. When you are exposed to relentless 70–80 km/h winds , standard tent stakes just won't cut it. These aggressive, deep-threaded spiral anchors bite hard into loose ground to keep your shelter, tarp, or beach umbrella firmly rooted. Smart, Optimized 3D Print Design As a maker and avid camper, I designed these pegs from scratch to solve two major problems: weak ground holding and wasteful printing. The geometry has been carefully tuned for the 3D printing process: Zero Supports: Engineered to print completely support-free, saving post-processing time. Fast & Efficient: Optimized design drastically cuts down on print time and filament waste without sacrificing structural integrity or toughness. 3 Included Models & Sizes To ensure you have the perfect anchor for any beach topography, the package includes 3 distinct variations: 1x Medium Size: Great for compact packing, firmer damp sand, and standard setups. 1x XL Standard: Extended length for deep penetration into shifting, loose sand to provide massive pull resistance. 1x XL Wide-Thread: Features a significantly wider screw thread configuration. This is engineered specifically for extra strength and maximum surface area bite if you are dealing with ultra-fine, super dry, or powdery sand. 1x XXL Ultra Wide-Thread (19mm Hex): A beefed-up, heavy-duty version featuring our widest thread yet and a robust 19mm hex head for maximum torque and strength. (Note: Untested, feedback welcome!) Print Settings & Material Recommendations ⚠️ For Best Results: Print with high infill (minimum 40-50%) and at least 4-5 perimeters/walls to ensure maximum torsional strength when screwing them into the ground. ASA (Highly Recommended): If your stakes are going to sit in the blistering direct sun all day, ASA is the top choice . It offers excellent UV resistance and high thermal stability, ensuring the pegs won't soften, warp, or deform under intense beach heat. PETG (Budget/Alternative Option): PETG works perfectly fine with a simple trick! If you use PETG, dig a hole in the sand until you reach the damp, harder layer, screw the pegs in there, and then bury them back up with sand. As long as they are buried away from direct sunlight, PETG will stay cool enough to maintain its strength and hold your gear secure. Pro-Tip for Maximum Hold in Loose Sand: To get the absolute best anchorage on windy beaches, don't just screw them into the dry, powdery top layer. Dig a small hole until you reach the dense, wet sand underneath. Screw the anchor directly into that wet layer so the wide threads can lock into the compacted sand. If the sand is completely dry or you can't dig deep enough, pour a bottle of sea water over the area after screwing it in to tighten and pack the sand around the threads. Fill the hole back up and stomp it down! Update: New Model Added! (4. description: ITS FINALLY HERE! The highly anticipated Dewalt HD Industrial Storage rack for the Lowes Teeny Tote! *****PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT: As of right now, I've only got a print profile for the P2S because thats what I own. In order to upload profiles to MakerWorld for all other printers, the 3MF file has to be uploaded for an X1C (i guess that tells Makerworld that if it prints on an X1C, it prints on ANYTHING!) HOWEVER, with the mess of calibration lines and other B.S. that the X1C throws down on the front edge of the print bed, some parts WON'T FIT on the bed. If anyone has a workaround for that please let me know and I will get it uploaded for all Bambu Printers ASAP!) Perfectly fits nine of the Viral Tik Tok sensation Lowes Teeny Totes on three Heavy Duty shelves. Will also fit my version HDX Tiny tote ! So go print nine of those suckers after you print this rack! Or go do it now, I don't know how you plan your day! Either way, just make sure that if you don't have any official Lowes Teeny Totes (SEEN HERE) which are completely sold out at Lowes. ( Have you seen that those bad boys come in clear now too??) then go print mine! I promise you they are an EXACT 1:1 replica of the Home Depot HDX Tough Tote and the exact dimensions of the Lowes Teeny Tote so go ahead and mix & match too! I STILL HAVE MANY MORE PARTS, COMPONENTS, & ACCESSORIES TO ADD TO THIS SYSTEM! I will be adding more components from the Dewalt Industrial Shelving System ! and for every 20 boosts received on this model, I will add another component! (Think Extensions, Work Bench, Hooks, Pegboard, Gridfinity, DRAWERS.) That way I know there is genuine interest in this product and gives me an idea on where I should focus my limited time to make sure I release models that People ACTUALLY WANT! I recommend printing in PETG for the most strength but a GOOD PLA will absolutely work if you've got your settings dialed in! Assembly is pretty straight forward and I've included a ton of photos to give you an idea of how it goes together but I am still also working on a nice set of instructions. I had a crazy demand for this model so I wanted to get it uploaded ASAP! Assembly guide PDF and possibly a video will come in the next few days. the “filament rivets” are not absolutely necessary, you can just put a drop of crazy glue on the (8x) short filament “pins” to hold them in but the “rivet” method definitely gives it that authentic industrial rack look. The rivets/pins in the front and back cross braces are not absolutely necessary as the hooks lock in fairly well on their own. Again, it just adds to the final overall look of the model. DO NOT force the cross brace hooks into place. just put them into the hole you pick and then lightly press down to tighten them in. They don't “snap” or “click” into place and once you press them into position, the downward force of gravity will hold them in and they don't come out! If you want them to be even more secure, you can add a “filament rivet” to the hole in the front on each side of the cross beams. the rivet fits through the hole in the corner post and prevents the cross beam from sliding up and out. I really only added the rivets for aesthetics, the rack is MORE than strong and stable enough without them. As far as colors, Bambu PETG-HF Yellow is a good match. Bambu Sunflower Yellow PLA is BANG ON Dewalt. 1.Lay out the two end frames like this first: 2. Slide the Z-brace into the C-channel corner posts and line up the four 2mm holes (I tried to be generous with the hole size but I didn't want it to be loose so depending on your printer, settings & filament, you may need to drill out the holes ever so slightly with a 1.75mm or 2mm or 3/32" or 5/64" drill bit or something close. If you plan to use filament “rivets” then you want it to be fairly tight. If you plan to use CA (Crazy) Glue then its not a crucial since the glue will stiffen everything up once it dries. 3. Cut eight pieces of black PLA filament 25-30mm long and make them into “filament rivets." I use a mini torch or a lighter to heat up the first end and press it into my work surface to create the first “head.” Put the rivet through the 2mm holes with the unpressed end facing up. I then heat up that end with the torch and press it with my finger, HOWEVER, I am a real man, extremely badass, and I have a zero pain tolerance so you should use something like a flat screwdriver (or anything flat, really) to press the remaining side. BOOM! Filament rivet! Doesn't it look frickin' awesome? And TOUGH! Almost like Dewalt themselves made it! If you don't have a mini torch, Just use a full size propane torch. JUST KIDDING, that would be stupid, don't do that! But you can click THIS LINK to a Youtube Video to watch Barbs method similar to mine but she pulls it off with a soldering iron or glue gun. And the video is 10 years old! Ol' Barb is a LEGEND so make sure you tell her so in the comments of her video! Make sure to tell her where you came from too and how much her video is appreciated! Hopefully Barb is still alive! 4. The rest is pretty self-explanatory and I just want to get this model uploaded for you guys so just throw down a comment if you have any questions or if there are any issues with the model or upload. DON'T FORCE THE CROSS BRACE HOOKS DOWN!! They are just a light press fit, no click or snap into place. everyones print settings/filament/etc. is different so I left some tolerance. If the hook doesn't slide all the way to the bottom of the slot THATS OK! Don't force it! It will not fall out because of the way it is designed. if you want to add filament rivets to the holes in the cross beams just like the real full sized Dewalt rack then you can and I would because it looks BADASS! description: This one was quite the task! I originally did my clicker bar using these transparent bead storage cases which worked perfectly fine while making the odd one at home but I ran into a bit of an issue when we took it to our events. The first was they were quite small in height meaning I couldn't put a lot of keycaps in them, it also caused overflow into the other containers when people were digging around for the colour they wanted so I had random letters mixed in with each other. 😩 They were also a pain to put out on display because they came with an attached lid so I had to keep them closed after people left or use double the space to keep them open. Not great when you're already busy enough building the actual clickers and limited on table space! That got me motivated to upgrade the display - I looked around for a while but couldn't find anything that really matched what I needed so I set myself to work. The main issues I needed to resolve were: It had to be modular so I can always add extras for new keycaps if needed. Had to be held together somehow during the events so it doesn't get pushed over easily by people but needs to be able to accommodate for different sized bins and layouts due to table restrictions. A slot to show the letters/symbols as people often got lost trying to find letters if keycaps were flipped upside down in the box, worse if letters got mixed around already. Ideally stackable so I can just stack them together after events and pack it away in a box for ease of use. A lid preferably so they don't accidentally fall out or have other small objects fall into them. Features of the storage bins: Fully modular. x1, x4 and x9 bins. Bins are stackable. Please note x9 bin requires 256mm x 256mm build plates but you can print a x4 with x1 and combine to make a x9 for A1 Mini users. Two coupler versions for joining displays. Bins can be attached with the row or the quad coupler. There are both snug and loose fits so print the one best for your printers/filament calibration. Quad couplers are for holding 4 bins together or for joining large 9 bins with 4 bins. The row coupler is if you wanted to build horizontally/vertically only. Display slot version and one without. Slots are slide in and can be removed after event completion by placing it inside the bin with the keycaps for easy storage. Personally I like the slot version but I included one without in case others wanted to use these for other purposes. Stackable. Please note there is a small gap where they are stacked - this finger gap is INTENTIONAL so you can actually separate them easier without them getting stuck. (Mishaps have happened during testing...) Various lid options. x1 lids have handles and coupler holes, x4 lids have coupler holes, x9 lid have no holes. If using the handle versions for x1, please secure handles using GLUE. I could add more variations but I feel like for most people these versions should suffice. For handles I have a short and a taller version as well. There are two sizes to these in case you find them too tight to fit into the hole on the lids. Recommended Print Settings: Layer Height: 0.2mm Nozzle: 0.4mm Wall Generator: Classic Infill: 15-20% Gyroid Supports: Not required Speed: 20-50mm/s for layer 1, then 150-200 for the rest. The clicker bases and keycap models are my own and are available via my Patreon or on Etsy/Cults as a one off purchase with commercial licensing.

Overview This is a functionally optimized version of the CoolClip, completely redesigned. It allows you to easily attach a standard ice pack to a conventional or large room fan, instantly converting it into an active air cooler by guiding the airflow directly past the cooling element. Two Versions Included To ensure maximum compatibility with different fan types, two distinct versions of the clip are provided in the print profile: Round Grille Clip: Designed with a hook that securely attaches to fans with standard round wire grilles. Flat Grille Clip: Specifically shaped with a hook that perfectly fits fans with flat or wider plastic grilles/spokes. Design Improvements This model has been mechanically refined based on practical requirements: Optimized Fit: Tolerances have been fine-tuned, ensuring the clip holds a standard ice pack tightly and securely without play. Reinforced Geometry: Wall thickness has been strategically increased, and critical corners are structurally reinforced. This prevents material fatigue and breakage at bending points under mechanical stress. Large Fan Compatibility: The hook design accommodates the grilles of large (floor) fans, making it versatile for various fan sizes. 100% Support-Free: The design is optimized to print completely flat on the build plate without any support material. This ensures a shorter print time, less material waste, and a ready-to-use part. Print Guidelines (Bambu Lab / FDM) Supports: None required. Place flat on the build plate. Material: PETG, ABS, or ASA is strongly recommended over PLA. PETG provides the necessary elasticity for the clip mechanism and better withstands cold temperatures and constant condensation. Walls / Perimeters: 3 to 4 walls for solid mechanical strength. Infill: 15% - 20% (Gyroid recommended for even stress distribution). Usage Instructions & Condensation Management Choose the printed clip that matches your fan's grille (round or flat) and snap it onto a standard frozen ice pack. Hang the clip with the ice pack on the front or rear grille of your fan. Crucial: Always place a towel or drip tray directly beneath the ice pack. Condensation will inevitably form and drip down during operation due to the temperature difference.

description: ## Short Description Generate round spacers, rectangular shims, or tall standoffs with custom dimensions, hole sizes, clearances, and copy count. ## Full Description This parametric generator creates simple workshop spacing parts for 3D printers, enclosures, jigs, furniture fixes, craft builds, mounting jobs, and everyday repairs. Choose between a round spacer/washer, a rectangular shim plate, or a taller cylindrical standoff, then set the exact dimensions you need. The default model prints a small support-free batch of round spacers with central clearance holes and no unnecessary side notch. Switch to rectangular shim mode for flat plates with 0-4 mounting holes, or tall standoff mode for longer cylindrical stand-offs. A clearance parameter lets you slightly oversize holes for real-world FDM fit, and the copy count parameter lets you print one part or a small set at once. Optional finishing controls include chamfered spacer edges, engraved or raised top labels, and a countersunk top variant for flush-fit screw applications. This is intended as a practical custom-fit utility print. It is not a certified precision, load-rated, or high-temperature hardware replacement. For functional assemblies, print one test piece first and adjust the clearance for your printer, filament, and screw/bolt size. ## Customization Notes - Use `part_style` to choose `round_spacer` , `rectangular_shim` , or `tall_standoff` . - Use `copy_count` and `copy_gap` to print one part or a small batch. - For round spacers, tune `outer_diameter` , `inner_diameter` , and `spacer_height` . - For tall standoffs, tune `outer_diameter` , `standoff_height` , and `standoff_hole_diameter` . - For rectangular shims, tune `shim_length` , `shim_width` , `shim_thickness` , `hole_count` , `shim_hole_diameter` , and `hole_spacing` . - Use `clearance_extra` to add real-world hole clearance. Start around 0.20 mm for PLA, then test and adjust. - Use `chamfer_enabled` and `chamfer_size` to soften round spacer/standoff edges. - Use `label_enabled` , `label_style` , and `label_text` for engraved or raised top labels such as `M4 5mm` . - Use `countersink_enabled` , `countersink_diameter` , and `countersink_depth` for a countersunk top variant. - `edge_marker_notch` is off by default; enable only if you want a visible orientation/counting notch.

The original version still works, but that needs some ‘wearing in’ for it to function smoothly. Additionally, I tweaked the print profile a bit so that the seam is now less prominent (backside) Features Fully parametric and customizable Independently adjustable lid and base heights Separate lid and base (not print-in-place) Bigger boxes on smaller printers (only 1 part per build plate instead of the entire box) Reliable filament hinge No supports required Snap-fit locking mechanism Suitable for PLA, PETG and other common filaments Dimensions The model uses external dimensions as input parameters. All dimensions can be adjusted between 13 and 350 mm where applicable . Maximum dimensions are mainly limited by your printer size. External dimensions (customizable) In order to customize the design to your specific needs, hit the ‘customize’ button under the print profiles: The Parametric Model Maker will open in a new tab, where you can adjust the following settings: boxWidth : 95–350 mm boxDepth : 25–350 mm baseHeight : 17–350 mm. lidHeight : 13–350 mm Internal dimensions The usable internal dimensions are: Width : boxWidth − 8 mm Depth : boxDepth− 9 mm Base height : baseHeight − 4 mm Lid height : lidHeight − 4 mm Example (box in attached print profile): An external size of 125 × 80 × 70 mm (W × D × total height) could be configured with a 13 mm high lid and a 57 mm high base. This results in internal dimensions of 117 × 71 mm, with 9 mm usable height in the lid and 53 mm usable height in the base. After downloading, the model in Bambu Studio is 1 object. If you want to print the 2 parts separately (if they don't fit on 1 plate), you can use the ‘Cut’ menu in Bambu Studio to separate the parts. See image below for the settings to use: Filament hinge The hinge uses a short piece of filament as the hinge pin. A piece (30 mm) of standard (1.75 mm) filament can be used as the hinge pin. For assembly, I suggest the following: First, you take a piece of filament and test fit all the holes BEFORE assembly. As the tolerances are tight (intentional) a small printing artefact can cause headaches during assembly. By test fitting first, you smoothen the holes for the next step. Then, you fit the parts together and then slide in the filament pieces from the side. . . Locking mechanism The box uses a snap-fit latch to keep the lid securely closed while still allowing easy opening. 于是，我开始构思一个新的概念—— 焊接坞（SolderDock） 。 它不仅仅是一台焊烟过滤器，更应该成为焊接工作中所有常用工具的”停靠点”。 我希望它能够同时承担以下几个角色： 焊烟过滤 常用工具挂载 焊接工具收纳 模块化扩展平台 更重要的是，希望焊接结束后，我只需要移动一个设备，就能快速完成整个焊接环境的收纳，让工作台能够迅速从 焊接模式 切换到 装配、拼接、测量 等其它工作模式。 设计思考 既然希望所有工具最终都能围绕同一个主体展开，那么首先需要确定整个系统的核心。 观察整个焊接环境后，我发现焊烟过滤器本身就是体积最大的设备，也是所有工具中位置最固定的一部分，因此决定以焊烟过滤器作为整个”焊接坞”的核心。 随后，我开始寻找市面上的现成方案。 经过一段时间的调研后，我基本放弃了现有产品，原因主要有三个： 1. 体积与成本 过滤效果较好的产品通常体积较大，价格也相对较高，不适合作为桌面长期使用的中心设备。 2. 滤芯成本与维护 很多产品使用专用滤芯，不仅需要重新验证过滤效果，后期更换时也难以保证长期稳定购买，维护成本较高。 3. 扩展能力不足 市面上的焊烟过滤器几乎都是独立产品，并没有预留安装其它工具的可能，更无法作为整个焊接环境的中心。 因此，我希望最终的方案能够满足几个目标： 使用价格低廉且容易获得的标准滤芯； 成本尽可能低； 能够方便集成其它焊接工具； 保留后续模块化扩展能力。 实现方案 基础选型 整个设计首先从滤芯选型开始。 我希望直接采用已经成熟、供应稳定的标准滤芯，这样不仅能够降低成本，也方便后期长期更换。 最终，我选择了小米车载空气净化器所使用的滤芯。 原因很简单： 市场保有量大； 原厂、副厂滤芯供应充足； 更换成本低； 后续维护几乎没有压力。 确定滤芯之后，我曾考虑直接改造小米车载空气净化器。 不过很快发现两个问题。 第一，原机采用多面进风设计，作为焊烟过滤器时，无法将吸力集中到焊接区域。 第二，原机出风方向与理想结构并不一致，同时也没有预留任何工具挂载空间。 相比继续修改原机，重新设计整个外壳显然更加合理。 随后，我开始研究风扇和驱动方案。 最初计划单独购买离心风扇和驱动板，再重新设计整体结构。 但在比较价格时，我突然意识到： 直接购买二手小米车载空气净化器，反而比单独购买风扇和驱动电路更便宜。 于是最终选择拆解整机，仅保留： 风扇 驱动板 电源系统 除此之外，这块驱动板还带来了意外收获： 它不仅支持三档风速调节，还可以连接米家 App，通过蓝牙查看简单的空气质量信息，为整个产品增加了一些不错的交互体验。 结构设计 确定核心硬件后，整个设计开始围绕”焊接坞”这一理念展开。 优化风道 重新设计外壳，使进风口与出风口保持相对方向，让烟雾能够沿着更合理的路径流动，提高吸烟效率。 精准反向工程 由于原厂风扇安装孔位和接口均为异形结构，为保证装配精度，我通过 3D 扫描获取原始模型，并进行反向工程设计，使电机卡扣准确入位。 模块化扩展 外壳预留了大量标准 M3 安装孔，方便后续增加新的功能模块，也方便用户根据自己的需求进行扩展。 焊锡支架 顶部增加挡风罩，并将标准焊锡丝线轮集成其中，在保证风道效果的同时，也方便焊接过程中直接取锡。 焊锡分装收纳盒 整卷焊锡丝负责储存，分装盒负责使用。 通过可挂载的焊锡分装盒，让焊锡丝在 储存、收纳与焊接 之间自由切换。 PCB 夹具 通过金属万向软管安装 PCB 夹具，使夹具能够直接固定在焊接坞主体上，进一步减少桌面设备数量。 铜丝球清洁挂载 在侧面预留铜丝清洁球盒的挂载位置，将烙铁头清洁功能集成到焊接坞中，减少桌面独立设备。 电烙铁挂架 右侧设计了倾斜式电烙铁挂架。 这样的设计不仅符合日常使用习惯，还能够让烙铁余烟继续被吸入过滤器，同时降低误碰烫伤的风险。（这个设计来自一次真实的教训。） 图：电烙铁挂载图 快拆维护 采用快拆卡扣结构，更换滤芯无需拆卸整机。 同时，滤芯还能定期旋转角度，使滤材利用更加均匀，进一步延长使用寿命。 成品验证 最终，这套”焊接坞”基本实现了最初设定的目标。 电烙铁、PCB 夹具、焊锡等常用工具全部集中到一个主体上，现在只需一只手即可移动整个焊接环境，大幅降低了部署和收纳成本。 实际测试中，在关闭空调和风扇的室内环境下，焊烟能够在距离进风口约 12 cm 的位置被稳定吸入，满足日常焊接需求。 后续优化 目前，电烙铁和焊烟过滤器仍然采用独立供电。 下一阶段，我希望进一步整合供电系统，使整个焊接坞只需要一根电源线即可完成部署。 同时，也计划增加顶部辅助照明、更多可扩展模块以及统一的供电接口，让整个系统真正成为一个可持续扩展的模块化焊接平台。 本模型仅供个人下载使用，您不得以任何形式出售此模型的数字及物理打印版本。

🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

Custom Pet Wheelchair TPU / PETG This is a custom 3D printed pet wheelchair designed as a functional support frame for small pets with reduced rear leg mobility. The wheelchair combines rigid PETG structural parts with flexible TPU parts to provide strength, durability, comfort and better impact absorption. PLA can also be used as support material or support interface to improve surface quality and make support removal easier. The model is designed to be assembled with common hardware parts such as bearings, threaded rod, nuts, screws and an adjustable dog harness. Required materials: For 1 complete pet wheelchair: 608 2RS bearings 8x22x7 mm: 4 pieces M8 threaded rod: 1 piece, approx. 1 meter M8 nuts: 8 pieces M8 washers: 8 to 12 pieces M4 screws: approx. 20 pieces M4 nuts: approx. 20 pieces M4 washers: 20 to 30 pieces Adjustable padded dog harness: 1 piece PETG filament: for the rigid / structural parts TPU filament: for flexible parts / tires / comfort areas PLA filament: optional for supports or support interface For the M4 screws, it is best to buy a small assortment, for example with M4x12, M4x16, M4x20 and M4x25 mm, because the exact length may vary slightly depending on each part.s Important about the harness: The dog harness is not 3D printed and must be purchased separately. It is used to secure the pet comfortably to the wheelchair frame. The correct harness size must be chosen according to the pet’s body size, weight and comfort. Recommended print settings: Layer height: 0.20 mm Infill: 25% PETG walls: 4 to 5 walls TPU walls: 3 to 4 walls Recommended infill pattern: Gyroid Recommended speed: around 40 mm/s for safe and reliable functional printing First layer speed: around 20 mm/s Support interface speed: around 25 mm/s Support material: PLA can be used as support or support interface where needed Printing notes: For PETG structural parts, use enough walls to improve strength around screw holes, joints and bearing areas. For TPU parts, slower speeds are recommended to improve reliability and avoid extrusion issues. For parts with bearings, screws or tight fits, check the dimensions after printing and adjust tolerances if necessary. Assembly notes: Insert the 608 2RS bearings into the wheel hub area. Use the M8 threaded rod as the main wheel axle. Use M8 nuts to secure the axle system. Use M4 screws and M4 nuts for the joints and frame assembly. Attach the adjustable padded dog harness to secure the pet comfortably to the frame. Safety note: This model may require adjustments depending on the size, weight, body shape and mobility needs of the pet. Always check the fit carefully before use. The pet should be supervised while using the wheelchair. This is not a certified medical or veterinary device. Please consult a veterinarian or pet mobility specialist if the pet has serious mobility, spine, hip or leg problems.

# 🧰 bentopeps — Rugged Vial Box (Parametric) ### Build a rugged storage box that fits *your* exact kit — not the other way around. **bentopeps** is a fully parametric, snap-shut rugged box for **peptide & hormone vials, syringes, and alcohol wipes**. You tell it what you carry and it builds the box around you: a **bento-style grid** interior, a **personalised two-colour lid**, a **click-stop hinge** that holds itself open, and an **ergonomic thumb latch** — all auto-sized, all support-free. > 👉 **Press the “Customize” button** to open it in MakerWorld’s parametric editor and dial in your own box right in the browser — no software to install. Then download your `.3mf`/`.stl` and print. --- ## ✨ Highlights - 🧩 **Bento-grid interior** — drop vials, syringes, or wipe slots into a Row × Column grid; the box **auto-sizes** around your loadout. - 💉 **Holds your whole kit** — 3 / 5 / 10 ml vials (standing *or* laid on their side), open syringe bins, and vertical wipe slots. - 🏷️ **Personalised lid** — flush **two-colour text + graphics** (great with Bambu AMS), 40+ fonts including bold, aggressive display faces. - 🔗 **Click-stop hinge** — the lid **holds open** at set angles instead of flopping, and is engineered to survive **thousands of open/close cycles** in PLA. - 👍 **Ergonomic latch** — a smooth thumb-pry lip pops the lid with one finger; still snaps shut securely. - 🖨️ **Prints clean** — watertight and **support-free**; tuned for Bambu Lab and every FDM printer. --- ## 🧩 The Bento Grid (how the interior works) The inside is a grid of **`grid_rows × grid_cols`** quadrants. You drop a **component** into each cell, and the box grows to fit: | Component | What it is | Footprint | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | **vial1 / vial2** | pockets of your two chosen vial sizes | `cols × rows` | **auto-fills** the compartment; each can stand up **or lay flat** | | **syringe** | an **open deep bin** for U100 syringes | `count×20 × 130 mm` | floor→ceiling, no wasted solid; syringes lie in & stack | | **wipe** | a **vertical slot** for 50×50 mm wipe packets on edge | `(count×5) × 50 mm` | ~5 mm ≈ 10 wipes; +5 mm per count | | **empty** | a solid spacer | — | for gaps / future use | **How the sizing works (so it always fits):** - **Column widths** grow to the widest cell in that column; **row lengths** grow to the longest cell in that row — a clean table layout. So a 130 mm syringe makes its whole row 130 mm long, and the vial cell next to it **auto-fills** that length with more vials. - **Box height = your tallest item** (a standing 10 ml is 54 mm; a standing wipe is 50 mm — whichever is tallest sets the height so the lid still closes). - **Partition walls** turn each cell into a real compartment. `partition_level` sets their height: **0 = none, 1 = 25 %, 2 = 50 %, 3 = 75 %, 4 = full**. ``` grid_cols ───────────────► Example default 2×2: ┌──────────────┬───────────────┐ │ vial1 (3 ml) │ syringe bin │ r1c1 = vial1 (3 ml) r1c2 = syringe ×2 │ auto-filled │ ▭▭ open/deep │ r2c1 = vial2 (10 ml) r2c2 = wipe ×3 ├──────────────┼───────────────┤ │ vial2 (10 ml)│ wipe slot ▮▮ │ └──────────────┴───────────────┘ ``` ### 💊 Vial catalog | Vial | Size | Pocket | |---|---|---| | **3 ml** | Ø16 × 40 mm | Ø17 | | **5 ml** | Ø22 × 40 mm | Ø23 | | **10 ml** | Ø22 × 54 mm | Ø23 | Pick which two sizes you want with `vial1_type` / `vial2_type` (sizes are editable in **`[Content Catalog]`**). --- ## 🎛️ How to use the parametric controls Open **Customize** and you’ll see the settings grouped into sections. Here’s what each group does: ### `[Grid]` — the layout skeleton - **`grid_rows` / `grid_cols`** — how many quadrants (e.g. 2 × 2). - **`partition_level`** — divider-wall height, `0`–`4` (none → full). ### `[Row 1] / [Row 2] / [Row 3]` — fill each cell - **`r1c1` … `r3c3`** — the component in each cell: `vial1`, `vial2`, `syringe`, `wipe`, or `empty`. - **`r1c1_n` …** — the **count** (vials wide, syringe width, or wipe thickness). - **`r1c1_rows` …** — vial **rows deep** for *that* quadrant (`0` = use the default), so every cell can have its own R × C. ### `[Vial Types]` — vials behaviour - **`vial1_type` / `vial2_type`** — `3ml` / `5ml` / `10ml`. - **`vial1_orient` / `vial2_orient`** — `standing` or **`flat`** (lays the vials in round side cradles). - **`vial_pack`** — `fill` (maximise how many fit) or `exact` (place exactly your R × C). - **`vial_align`** — `spread` (outer vials hug the walls, evenly indexed) or `center` (centred block). - **`vial_wall_clear`** — gap kept to the walls so pockets never break out. ### `[Box Height]` - **`height_override`** — `0` = **AUTO** (sized to the tallest item). Set a value to force a total height. - **`extra_height`** — add head-room above the auto height. ### `[Output]` — what to render - **`show_bottom`** — the tray. **`show_top`** — the lid. **`show_combined`** — lid sitting on the box (preview). - **`show_contents`** — draws translucent mock vials/syringes/wipes so you can eyeball the loadout. **Turn it OFF before exporting** — it’s preview-only. - The **console report** tells you the grid, box W × L × H, what each cell holds, and warns if anything is too big for your plate. > 💡 **Tip:** export **once with `show_bottom`** and **once with `show_top`** — that’s your tray + lid. --- ## 🏷️ Personalise the Lid — flush two-colour Text & Graphics The lid top can carry a **flush, co-planar** label — *not* embossed or engraved, but a second-colour region in the same surface (perfect for **Bambu AMS / MakerWorld multi-colour**). **Text** and **Design** are independent — use either or **both**, each with its own colour and placement. **Orientation frame:** picture the closed box with the **latch toward you** (front) and the **hinge at the back**. Everything is placed in that frame — `halign` = your left/right, `valign` `top` = hinge / `bottom` = latch. ### `[Lid Text]` - **`lid_text_on`**, **`lid_text`** (+ optional **`lid_text_line2`**), **`lid_text_color`**. - **`lid_font`** — a dropdown of clean classics **plus aggressive / manly display faces**: Oswald, **Anton**, **Bebas Neue**, **Archivo Black**, **Black Ops One**, Bungee, Bangers, Teko, Russo One, Orbitron, Audiowide, Staatliches, Monoton, Permanent Marker, **Alfa Slab One**, **Ultra**, **Bevan**, **Passion One**, **Titan One**, **Squada One**, **Rajdhani**, **Chakra Petch**, **Wallpoet**, **Goldman**, **Michroma**, **Stardos Stencil**, **Special Elite**, **Rye**, **Metal Mania**, **Pirata One**, **UnifrakturCook**, **New Rocker**, **Germania One**, and more. - **`lid_font_custom`** — type **any** font name to use it instead (this is a searchable **font picker** in MakerWorld’s editor). - **`lid_text_weight`** — Regular / Bold / Black / … ⚠️ **Set this to `Regular` for single-weight display fonts** (Anton, Bebas Neue, Bangers, Black Ops One, Alfa Slab One, etc.) or they fall back to the default. - **`lid_text_size`** — a real font size in mm (`0` = no text); it **auto-shrinks to fit** so long words never run off the edge. - **Alignment + padding** — `lid_text_halign` / `lid_text_valign` **anchor the text to that edge and grow it inward** (right-align fills right→left, left-align fills left→right — never cut off). **`lid_text_pad_l/r/t/b`** inset each side in mm to nudge it perfectly. - **`lid_text_orient`** — `horizontal` or `vertical`. ### `[Lid Design]` - **`lid_design_on`**, **`lid_design`** — `molecule`, `helix`, `honeycomb`, `logo`, or full-lid tilings `helix-full` / `honeycomb-full`. - **`lid_design_orient`** — horizontal / vertical / corner-TL/TR/BL/BR, plus **`halign` / `valign` / `pad`** (same edge-anchored behaviour as the text) and **`lid_pattern_scale`** for size. - **`lid_design_color`** — the design colour. **Layering:** where text and a design overlap, the **text reads on top** (the design is relieved out from under the letters), each in its own colour. > 🎨 **To print in two colours:** render the lid (`show_top`) and **export as 3MF** — each colour region becomes its own material for the AMS. (A single-material STL is also fully watertight.) --- ## 🔗 Hinge & Latch — engineered, not guessed **Ergonomic latch pry-lip** — a smooth, rounded ridge you hook a thumb under to pop the lid. Hulled (no sharp edges), self-supporting underside, and clear of the snap bump so the **secure close is unchanged**. Set with `latch_relief` / `latch_relief_size`. **Click-stop detent hinge** — the open lid **clicks and holds** at set angles instead of flopping. A rounded nub on the lid drops into rounded dimples on the barrel ends — and because the detent lives on the **hinge end faces**, it needs **no supports at any angle**. - **`detent_angles_deg`** = `[90, 120, 140, 160, 180, 210]` (210 = full-open back-stop) — edit to taste. - **`detent_phase`** nudges the click angles; **`detent_nub_proud`** firms the click; **`detent_bore_extra`** adds local relief *only* if a test print snaps on too stiffly. - This design survived a **multi-pass adversarial stress-test** — it’s tuned to flex the long lid spring by only a few tenths of a millimetre per click (low strain) with filleted features for fatigue life. **Third (center) hinge** — on wide boxes the long barrel can sag, so a center support cradle is **added automatically** when the box `width ≥ third_hinge_width_threshold` (160 mm) or when you set `enable_third_hinge`. The lid still snaps on in one motion and prints support-free. > 🧪 **Pro tip:** print a quick **one-knuckle test coupon** first to feel the snap + click, then fine-tune `detent_phase` / `detent_nub_proud` before committing to a big box. --- ## 🖨️ Print settings & tips - **Material:** PLA is great; **PETG** is tougher for the hinge. - **Layer height:** 0.20 mm. **Supports:** ❌ none needed — everything opens upward. - **Orientation:** print the **tray on its floor**, the **lid on its rim / top-face-down** (the slicer plates them correctly from the exported files). - **Two-colour lid:** assign the text/design region a second filament in the AMS (use the **3MF**). - **Vial fit:** `vial_clearance` controls the radial gap; `vial_z_clearance` is the air gap above a vial so the lid clears a crimp/flip cap. - **Hinge stringing/snapping at layer lines?** Slow the top layers, raise min-layer-time to ~10 s, or bump temp +5 °C. --- ## 📦 What’s included - The **parametric model** (`.scad`) — the whole project, fully customizable on MakerWorld. - A set of **ready-to-print example STLs** (various grids). - The built-in **lid designs** (molecule / helix / honeycomb) and the optional logo. --- ## ❤️ About / License Designed from scratch by **Keaton Hoskins** — MakerWorld **@thehoskins**.
