🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

description: 32-slot Round Kumihimo disc for round bracelets This is a beginner friendly round Kumihimo disc to make round bracelets using the ancient Japanese artform of Kumihimo , which is done by weaving strings of silk, rope or yarn together using a disc to form a rope/bracelet with artistic patterns in the process. The disc has 32 marked notches to hold the strings in place and a rounded circle slot in the center for the weaving pattern to form. The notches are labelled 1-32 and the notes are marked every 8th slot with a large dot to indicate starting points for common 8-string weaves (at 8, 16, 24 and 32), as well as every 4th slot in between for 16-string weaves with a smaller circle (at 4, 12, 20 and 28). The labels are printed flat on the bed, so the disc is rotated upside down. If using an AMS, the labels are pre-colored and will be printed using a color for the disc and a second for the labels and markings. Without an AMS, the labels will still be visible through the trick of the labels being recessed by one layer height (0.2mm), this embeds the outline of the labels even without color as shown below. If desired, you could trace the etching using a permanent marker after the print. Instructions No assembly is required for the print. Simply print it, get some strings of silk, yarn or rope and you're ready to go. Patterns and instructions on how to use a Kumihimo disc to make rope/bracelets can be found online with several websites dedicated to it and many instructional videos. Weighted Bobbins for Kumihimo braiding My latest addition to the series is a set of Weighted Bobbin for Kumihimo braiding which make it easier to make neat braids by taking the pressure off my hands and instead the weight can do the tension holding on the center strand of the braid. model_name: SKADIS for P1S / X1C side panel - custom sized
description: 3D printed SKADIS for BambuLab P1S and X1C I thought to utilise the rather empty space of my P1S to mount a SKADIS board, but none of the available original SKADIS sizes fit the P1S / X1C side panel. Therefore, I created this model which fits on the side of a BambuLab P1S or X1C. 💡Features: almost everything is 3D printable, needs only 3 M4x10 screws (even those are optional) keyed dovetail connection between the boards for strong fit significant clearance between the board and printers side panel + TPU spacers to prevent scratching mounted using printed hooks on a stock printer setup rigid and universal The SKADIS itself was generated from the parametric model by user @Line Arc Line from printables ( Parametric SKADIS Board Generator ). Kudos to the designer! Dimensions of the final SKADIS: 32 x 42 x 5.3 mm Most parts can be printed out of PLA but the mounting hooks need to be printed out of PETG, ASA or another less brittle material than PLA . The reason is, that those parts need to be flexed quite a lot to snap into place during mounting. 📜Part list and filaments: You will need the following printed parts. All are present in the submitted print profile and split into plates ( see below ). 4x SKADIS plates labelled 1-4 - PLA or any other material 6x spacers with three pins - PLA or any other material 3x spacers with a M4 hole - PLA or any other material 3x thin washers with a M4 hole (can be replaced by metal washers as well) - PLA or any other material 9x spacer caps - TPU (optional) 2x top mounting brackets - PETG, ASA or other non-brittle material ( PLA won’t work! ) 2x bottom mounting brackets - PETG, ASA or other non-brittle material ( PLA won’t work! ) Non-printed parts 3x M4x10 screws 🖨️ Print instructions: Before you print all the pieces consider printing the TEST model first (see print profile). It's a quick 20 min to check if the settings fit your printer tolerances and setup. The provided print profiles have all settings dialed in and are ready to print (Bambu Handy App friendly). Just print each plate once and you should have everything you need: Plates 1-4 (PLA, ~350g total, 2h30min each): SKADIS parts labeled 1-4. Plate 5 (PLA, ~7g, 22 min): 6x stand-offs with pins, 3x normal standoffs and 3x spacers Plate 6 (TPU, ~4g, 22 min): 9x TPU caps for the stand-offs Plate 7 (PETG/ASA, ~12g, 30 min): 3x top and 3x bottom mounting hooks ( only two needed each, the other ones are spare ) 🔩 Assembly: A picture-assisted assembly and mounting guide is provided in the description. I strongly recommend to use that. You will find the text-based instruction below. Depending on the tolerances of your printer, the SKADIS pieces may go together either quite tight or be a little bit loose. I dialed the tolerances in for my P1S and the pieces grab onto each other quite well. Glue is not required for the assembly but is strongly recommended to prevent the whole thing from disassembling if you plan to hang something heavy from it. DO NOT use cyanoacrylate-based superglue especially if you printed the parts out of black (or dark) plastic. In my experience the glue emits some kind of vapour while drying which stains the plastic white. Instead, use a little bit of dedicated PLA glue or two-component resin glue. If the pieces go in quite tight you may use a rubber hammer to jam the pieces together which would probably hold quite well even without glue. Place piece 1 on a flat surface with the number 1 facing upward Hold piece 2 with the marking facing the top and slide into piece 1 from the top Repeat steps 1 and 2 for pieces 3 and 4 respectively Connect all pieces together by sliding the 1-2 piece into the 3-4 piece Insert the spacers with 3 legs into respective holes on the back of the board. The use of glue is advised if you are certain that you assembled the pieces right. Place the small spacers at the indicated spots at the front of the board. Insert the M4x?? screw from the front through the spacer and through the SKADIS hole. Screw in the remaining long spacers onto the M4 screws Cover all spacers with the TPU caps by inserting them into the respective holes 🪜Mounting: Remove the top glass of your P1S or X1C printer Hold the top mounting bracket with the SKADIS hook facing to the left. Flex the bracket and slide the right hand latch onto the frame where the glass sits on top. Straighten the left side of the bracket so it snaps into place. Repeat the same process for the other top mounting bracket Hang the assembled SKADIS onto the top brackets as indicated. Insert the bottom brackets into the indicated holes. Flex the right side of the bracket so it passes the bottom edge of the printer chassis and snaps into place. Repeat for the second bracket Now you are done and ready to go! Have fun! If you encounter any issues, feel free to comment or write me a DM, maybe I'll be able to help you. Post your makes, I'm curious how yours will look like ;) Cheers and all the best!😉 Fun fact: I finished the project in 2024 and it has been mounted on my P1S since without any issues. I just now finally found the time to document and release it properly. I hope you find it useful ;)

description: This is my personal take on the Noctua Air Amplifier. I wanted to take the original concept a step further by turning it into a functional, active desktop cooling solution using standard freezer ice packs. By extending the rear shroud, this design allows you to place two cooling packs directly into the intake airflow, significantly lowering the output temperature compared to a standard fan. Features: Dual Ice Pack Intake: The extended rear shroud accommodates up to two cooling packs with maximum dimensions of 26 x 84 x 155 mm each. Magnetic Quick-Change Lid: The rear intake is covered by a custom Noctua 120mm fan grill style lid. It is held securely by 8 magnets, allowing you to swap out warm ice packs for fresh ones in seconds without any tools. Additional Condensate Tray: Cold ice packs mean condensation. The included tray sits perfectly underneath to catch any dripping water and protect your desk. Bill of Materials (BOM): 120mm Fan -> Standard 120mm PC Fan (e.g., Noctua) M3x14mm Socket Head Screw (2x) -> For securing the fan shroud to the base/holder M3x4mm Heatset Insert (2x) -> Melted into the front shroud for the M3 screws M4 Screws & Nuts (4x or 8x) -> Option A: 4x M4x35mm screws + nuts (through-hole mount) OR Option B: 8x M4x10mm screws + nuts (separate front/rear mount) Neodymium Magnets 5x2mm (8x) -> 4 for the cooling shroud, 4 for the grill lid Printing & Assembly Tips: Material: PLA works perfectly fine, but PETG or ASA is highly recommended if you plan to leave it in a hot car or near direct sunlight. Magnets: Pay close attention to the polarity of the magnets before pressing or gluing them into the slots on the shroud and the lid! I recommend using a drop of superglue for every magnet.

La misura indicata è riferita al diametro interno del tubo da collegare, così puoi: stampare tutti i raccordi in un’unica stampa stampare solo quello che ti serve evitare modifiche manuali alla piastra scegliere rapidamente il diametro più adatto al tuo tubo Set composto da raccordi 1/2'' maschio NPT portagomma stampabili in 3D, progettati per collegare tubi di diverso diametro a componenti, adattatori, pompe, serbatoi o impianti che utilizzano filettatura NPT. 🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

I've always had a soft spot for the SKÅDIS pegboard system — cheap, endlessly flexible, and there's an accessory for pretty much everything. But there was one thing I could never find for it: a version of one of my favorite pieces of design history, an iconic modular storage unit from the late 1960s, originally made as a single molded block of compartments and hooks. You can actually buy the original — it's a single molded block holding all the compartments at once — but it's pricey and pretty bulky for what is, at the end of the day, a desk organizer. So I decided to reinterpret it for the SKÅDIS ecosystem instead: I redesigned the whole thing from scratch as a set of separate, 3D-printable modules, each with its own hook built directly into the print, so they clip straight onto a vertical 37×56 SKÅDIS panel. The result is a family of 13 individual modules . Arrange them close together in the original grid layout and you get a look that's a clear nod to the source of inspiration — or spread them out, mix them with other SKÅDIS accessories, or use just a handful of them, however suits your desk and your workflow. Since each piece hangs independently, you're never locked into one fixed configuration the way you would be with a single molded block! You can use PLA or PETG (I actually used Pla Tough). Some modules need supports, but they're minimal and pop off cleanly with no visible marks afterward, because it's all internal. Feel free to make it colourful by printing the models in different colors, or to repaint the pegboard and make it all the same color, to remind the original vintage piece! A fully 3D-printed folding wall shelf that tucks flat against the wall when not in use and deploys a load-bearing support arm when you need it — practical, space-saving, and finished with a honeycomb underside for style. -- Why I made this - Most wall shelves are permanent fixtures. I wanted something that earns its space — a shelf that disappears when you don't need it and holds its own when you do. This design is 100% 3D printed (minus the wall screws and anchors you'll source locally) and built around a real folding mechanism rather than a novelty hinge. -- What it is - The shelf folds on a set of printed hinge knuckles: fold it up and it sits flush against the wall, fold it down and a pivoting support arm locks it into a horizontal position capable of handling real everyday loads. The underside of the shelf panel features a honeycomb pattern — so the face you see when it's folded up looks intentional, not bare plastic. All the structural work is done by the shelf panel, the support arm, and the hinge knuckles. The only hardware you need are wall screws and anchors appropriate for your wall type. -- Design details **Folding hinge knuckles** — printed-in geometry, no metal hardware at the pivot **Pivoting support arm** — braces the shelf against downward load when deployed **Honeycomb underside** — decorative and visible when the shelf is stowed -- How to print - Print in PLA+ for a lightweight indoor shelf or PETG if you want better humidity and temperature resistance. Either material works well here. ORIENTATION MATTERS, ALWAYS ORIENT IN A WAY WHERE LOADS WONT SHEAR THE Z LAYERING OF THE PRINT. - **Shelf panel** — lay flat on the bed, largest face down. - **Support arm** — lay flat on face so layer lines run along the arm's length; this puts the strongest layer orientation against bending loads, which is exactly where you need it. - **Hinge knuckles** — This is the trickier one, check overhanging geometry in your slicer before printing; orientation matters. - **20-30% infill** on all structural parts and many walls 4-5 (support arm, hinge knuckles, and cradle). ### Tips - Run a test fit of the hinge knuckles before final assembly — tolerances can vary slightly between printers; a quick pass with a small file cleans things up in seconds. - When mounting to drywall, use wall anchors rated for at least the load you plan to put on the shelf — the print will hold, so make sure the wall fastening matches. - PETG is the better choice for garages, laundry rooms, or anywhere with temperature swings or moisture. ### Assembly / Instructions 1. Print all parts: shelf panel, support arm, hinge knuckles/wall brackets and cradle. Check orientation notes before slicing. 2. Dry-fit the wall bracket onto the shelf panel. Verify smooth pivot motion; lightly sand or file any tight spots. 3. Attach the wall brackets shelf panel and place against the wall, level it out and mark the holes for each wall bracket. 4. Drill out marked holes and install anchors. 5. description: Symmetric Pattern Generator Perfect for panels & drawer faces. I recently designed 3D printed drawers with Kumiko and Hexagon faces, and all of the generator I could find online never generator what I needed: Controllable frame dimensions / thickness Controllable pattern size or quantity to fill the frame in a perfectly symmetric way Controllable border padding Editable notch (optional) This script is perfect for anyone looking for an easy and quick way to generate patterns or panels. Very useful for laser cutting or CAD as well. Updates - 07/12/2026 You can now control the thickness of main branches & minor branches, especially useful for Kumiko patterns Added a modifier to add roundness where branches connect called “ Branch Gusset ”, makes it easier to print thin branches vertically when enabled Modified the Size Mode “by count” by adding a new modifier “Height / Width”. This let's you fill the panel with an exact amount of the patterns. Example: if you select “By count” → Fill pattern axis: Height" and select "Pattern count: 3", you will have exactly 3 pattern from bottom to top of the panel, very useful with hexagons patterns. Added a new pattern: Kumiko Asanoha v2 - this pattern removes the horizontal branches, making it easier to print vertically by removing bridges (could be handy in some situations) HOW TO USE Panel Size - Thickness Width & Height: control the size of the panel in mm Thickness: control the thickness of your frame Notch Add notch: toggle the notch function on/off Notch width / height: control the size of you notch Notch radius: Control the roundness of your notch ends Notch border: control the border thickness around your notch Border padding Border top / right / bottom / left: control the thickness of the padding around your frame Pattern style Pattern style: Select between 16 pattern styles (more to come) Size mode: this is the critical modifier: by size: the frame will be filled with repetitive patterns of the selected size. Very useful when making different panels where you want the pattern to stay consistent on different frame sizes. by count: the frame will be filled with exactly the selected “n patterns” number of the pattern. IF you select 7 “n patterns”, the frame will be filled with 7 patterns, the script will calculate the pattern size to make it fit exactly the width (working on making it height / width selectable). Use this if you want a perfectly symmetric pattern where left and right ends are identical (imagine a mirror in the middle of the frame). Pattern size: select the size of each pattern in mm (only when size mode is by size ) n patterns: select the exact amount of patterns to fill the frame width (only when size mode is by count ) Branch thickness: control the thickness of your patterns. For 3d printing, avoid going under 1.5mm Inner Thickness: control the thickness of inner branches (only currently used for the Boxes patterns) Export to SVG / DXF or more formats I designed this script to firstly export to DXF to work with Fusion360 and my laser cutting software. Unfortunately, MakerWorld limits the export to only STL (3MF is a zip archive of STL + print settings). If you are interested in exporting to more formats for your workflow, please send me a private message. Patterns To Do Still plenty of work to make this script the absolute ultimate: New patterns to come (especially Kumiko patterns) Link the inner thickness control to all the applicable patterns (Kumiko & lattice especially) Different styles of notches (rectangular for example) Side tabs: useful for frames that lock into a slot

description: Platethora , the open-source, public-domain, quick-release Plate system with a Plethora of applications. Platethora was inspired by systems like Gridfinity, the Honeycomb storage wall, and tripods. I aimed to create a quick-release plate you could use for anything you want, not just cameras. I tried to make the design as simple as possible while using also as little hardware as possible, but an M4x14-16 screw with a nylon nut is still required, although a regular nut with some superglue should also work. The main goal is for people to create their own bases and plates for whatever they need, which is why I shared the editable step files and put the whole project into the public domain, meaning you can do whatever you want with these files. I recommend printing in PETG in the orientation shown above. This isn't supposed to be a replacement for conventional tripods for cameras and such. It's supposed to be an option to be able to use tripods and quick-release plates with things you usually can't use them with. Things like lights and the other examples in the photos. If you have a really nice camera, then I encourage you to buy a nice tripod for it with a proper metal quick-release plate. But if you want something a little more out there, like helping hands that can be switched from being used on a flat surface to being used with a desk clamp, then I would argue my system is the better option. It's a solution for very specific problems, which is exactly what 3D printing is for.

description: Overview A customizable Skadis holder for round stuff, where you set the diameter and it does the rest. It hangs a row of round cups on an IKEA Skadis pegboard and holds just about anything cylindrical: glue sticks, markers, highlighters, screwdriver handles, small bottles, hobby paints, spray cans and WD-40. You really only set two things, the object diameter and how many cups you want. From there the customizer sizes the cups, packs them in next to each other and puts a Skadis hook behind each one at the nearest real slot. Heavy or wide cups get a second peg on their own so they can't tip out, and everything else is optional. Measure the object itself and type that number in, the model adds the fit gap for you so you're not left guessing tolerances (the optional floor hole works the same way). One thing worth doing before a big run: print a single cup first. Printer tolerances vary, so even if you know yours it pays to slice one cup at your diameter and check the object actually drops in before you print a whole row. A two-minute test is a lot cheaper than redoing a full board that came out a hair too tight. If the fit is off, nudge the Clearance a little (0.2 is snug, 0.3 is the default, 0.4 is looser) and reprint that one cup. Set the diameter — the customizer sizes every cup to fit. Highlights Diameter 10 to 80 mm, 1 to 12 cups in a row. Mixed sizes in the same row, so a wide can sits happily next to slim glue sticks. Heavy cups get a double peg automatically, and there's a thin-profile mode for short rows. Optional hole through the floor to pass a tool or screwdriver through. Native Skadis hook that fits both real Skadis (5 mm) and printed boards. Dimensions. The default 3 cup, 21 mm row comes out around 100 x 35 x 30 mm. Yours will depend on the diameter and count you choose. Compatibility. IKEA Skadis and Skadis-compatible printed pegboards (5x15 mm slots on a 40 mm grid). Cylinders up to 80 mm outside diameter. Printing. Print it standing up, with the panel flat on the bed and the cups opening upward. Any material is fine (PLA, PETG, ABS/ASA, PC). PETG is a solid all-rounder and PLA works perfectly well. Use a 0.4 or 0.6 mm nozzle and skip 0.8, which softens the detail and the fit. A bit of support on the rear pegs, none under the cups. Full customizer guide Every setting, if you want to fine-tune. What the settings control — diameter, clearance, wall, cup height, floor. Setting Default What it does Object diameter 21 mm The object's exact body diameter, 10–80 mm (any decimal). Measure it — the model adds the fit gap for you (set by Clearance). Count 3 Number of cups in the row, 1–12. Cup height 30 mm How far the cup wraps the object, 5–100 mm. Taller = steadier for tall/heavy items. Warns if a cup is too short for its diameter. Per-cup size off (0) Optional: give one cup its own diameter and/or height (0 = use the main size). Sits right under the main size. Pegs per cup auto (0) 0 = auto: 1 peg for light items, 2 for heavy/large. Or force 1–3. Heavy threshold 40 mm A cup at/above this diameter auto-gets a second peg. Single peg row off Thin-profile mode — forces all pegs into one row for the lowest backboard (best for short, light items). Clearance 0.3 mm The fit gap added to the diameter — applied to both the cup bore and the floor hole (a 30 mm object → a 30.3 mm bore). Measure exact and let the model add it. 0.3 (default) suits most prints — snug but slides in; 0.2 is very snug (only if you trust your printer); 0.4 plays it safe (looser). Wall 2.4 mm Cup wall thickness. Gap between cups 4 mm Spacing between neighbouring cups. Floor thickness 2 mm Every cup has a closed floor; this sets it. Floor hole 0 (off) The exact diameter of a tool/device to pass through every cup's floor (or to drain) — the model adds the same clearance as the cup. Any decimal. Per-cup override available. Plate thickness / margin / radius 3 / 5 / 7 mm Back panel: thickness, border around the cups, corner rounding. Board thickness 5 mm The Skadis board the pocket fits, 4–7 mm (standard Skadis is 5). Setup tips Measure exact, leave the tolerance to the model. Enter the object's true diameter, and if you use the floor hole, the true diameter of whatever goes through it. The model adds the Clearance to both, so you don't need to pad your own measurement. 0.3 (the default) suits most prints, snug but it still slides in. 0.2 is very snug, only worth it if you trust your printer. 0.4 plays it safe. One cup, two pegs. A single cup on one peg sits snug on the board, but with only one peg it can rotate a touch and a knock can twist it. For a steady single holder, set Pegs per cup to 2 so the two stacked pegs lock the rotation. (Auto already does this for heavy cups, and a row of three or more braces itself anyway.) Heavy or tall items. Keep it on auto (or force 2 pegs) and use a taller cup. Don't put a full can in single peg row mode, because it really wants the double peg. Thin profile. Turn on Single peg row for short items, like a tray of stubby markers, to get the lowest backboard possible. The pegs snap to the 40 mm Skadis grid, so a peg can sit slightly off a cup's centre and very close cups will share a peg. That's fine for light rows. Board grip. The default 5 mm board thickness fits standard Skadis. Drop it a little for a firmer grip on a thinner or printed board. How the pegs work Each cup gets a native Skadis hook that fills a 5x15 slot and catches behind the board. Heavy or wide cups (at or above the heavy threshold) automatically get a second peg stacked one slot below the first , a vertical pair that stops a full can from tipping out. Slim cups keep a single hook. Either way, every peg drops into a real slot at the same time. Turning on Single peg row overrides all of that and forces one thin row. The native hook catches behind the board. Hooks straight onto an IKEA Skadis board. Mixed sizes in one row Every cup uses the main diameter unless you give it one of its own. Set just the cup you want bigger and a wide can will still pack in tight next to a slim glue stick, with every hook landing in a real slot. The panel sizes itself to whatever row you build. Any size in one row — a fat can beside slim cups. anno_mixed.png Floor holes (optional) Cups are closed by default. You can open a hole through the floor, on every cup or just one, for a few reasons: to pass a screwdriver or tool through (handle in the cup, shaft poking out the bottom), to let a long object stick out the bottom, or to push something up from below to pop it out. Measure the exact diameter of whatever goes through and the model adds the same fit gap as the cup (the hole comes out as your diameter plus clearance), so it's a clean, snug pass-through. Print settings Setting Value Material Any. PLA, PETG, ABS/ASA or PC. PETG is a great everyday pick (fine indoors too) and PLA is perfectly fine. There's no real material limit here. The pricier engineering filaments just add heat and strength you probably don't need. Nozzle 0.4 or 0.6 mm (both print cleanly). Avoid 0.8 because it loses fine detail and the fit tolerances don't come out right. Layer height 0.2 mm Walls 5 at a 0.4 mm nozzle, 3 to 4 at 0.6 mm Infill 15 to 20% Supports None under the cups, light support on the rear pegs only Orientation Standing up, panel flat on the bed, cups opening upward Plate Single piece, no assembly More like this: part of my IKEA Skadis Organizers & Holders collection — more holders for the same board.

An open-source clamshell holder generator for openGrid , using the openConnect system. The holder can be used to mount objects either under a desk, often in combination with the Underware system, or on a wall. A common use case is holding power strips, but the dimensions and openings can be adjusted for a wide range of object shapes. Several example .stl files are included, with the parameters used to generate them in the file names. Customization guide: Measure the item. Set "item_width" , "item_height" , and "item_depth" . Adjust "item_corner_rounding" based on the item's shape. Add a little clearance if you want the item to slide in easily. For a heavy item, you may want to increase "holder_thickness" to make the holder sturdier. Set "holder_slot_position" . "Top" makes the item face forward when mounted on a wall, or downward when mounted under a desk. You can also choose "Front", which makes the item face sideways when mounted under a desk. Adjust the front opening. Use "front_opening_side_margin" and "front_opening_end_margin" . Larger margins create a smaller front opening, which may interfere with use, such as blocking the outlets of a power strip. Adjust the side openings. Use the "side_opening_x_margin" parameters. The side opening can be enabled on one side, both sides, or disabled completely. The position and size of the opening are highly customizable. Set "holder_slot_column_limit" . This value defaults to the minimum of 1, which saves filament and helps with heat dissipation. Increase it if you want the holder to cover more of the item. Set "slot_slide_direction" . "Left" and "Right" are usually used for under-desk mounting, while "Up" and "Down" are usually used for wall mounting. Choose the direction that lets the holder slide onto the openConnect slots from the accessible side. "generate_holder_part" : "Both" shows a good preview of the result, so it is recommended during customization. The "Left" and "Right" options allow different parameters for each part and automatically orient the model for 3D printing, which is convenient when exporting the result. The model is open-source under the CC-BY-SA license. Like all the OpenSCAD models I've designed for openGrid, it can be found in this GitHub repository . Feel free to use the code; feedback and suggestions are welcome.

description: 3D Printable Kerfmaker (Bridge City Inspired) Precision Joinery Without Measuring A kerfmaker is one of those simple woodworking tools that quickly becomes indispensable. It allows you to accurately size dados, grooves, rabbets, and other cuts to perfectly match the actual thickness of your material—without measuring, calipers, or complicated math. This is my own interpretation of the classic kerfmaker. I did not invent the kerfmaker , and credit for the original concept belongs to the woodworking community. My goal was to create a version that closely matches the functionality and style of the excellent Bridge City Toolworks Kerfmaker , while being easy to print, simple to assemble, and built with inexpensive, commonly available hardware. After searching MakerWorld, I noticed that many of the available printable kerfmakers were incomplete or required significant modification to become functional. This design is my attempt to provide a complete, easy-to-build solution that any woodworker with a 3D printer can make. Features Compact footprint 100 mm overall length 15.5 mm wide 38 mm tall Adjustable for a wide range of material thickness Captured hardware prevents nuts from spinning during adjustment Tight sliding keyway for accurate, repeatable settings Uses only four inexpensive pieces of hardware Perfect for table saws, router tables, dado setups, and joinery work Hardware Required You'll need: 1 × M4 × 16 mm flat head (countersunk) machine screw 1 × M4 × 20 mm flat head (countersunk) machine screw 2 × M4 hex nuts I used this metric hardware assortment: Metric Machine Screw Assortment Kit (Amazon) https://a.co/d/0eF5b6EH Any standard M4 hardware of the same sizes should also work. Assembly Assembly is straightforward and only takes a few minutes. The M4 nuts are captured inside the printed knobs during a pause in the print , creating comfortable hand-tightened knobs without requiring glue. The sliding fit between the parts is intentionally snug. The screw joining the two smaller pieces rides inside the keyway of the main body. The first 15–16 mm of travel may require some firm pressure as the screw head enters the slot. This is intentional and helps keep the assembly together during use. Once the screw passes this initial section, movement becomes much smoother while still maintaining a precise fit. If your printer runs slightly oversized, a light pass with fine sandpaper or a small file can make initial assembly easier. Why I Designed This I enjoy designing woodworking tools that solve practical problems in the shop. After looking around MakerWorld, I couldn't find a printable kerfmaker that checked all the boxes I was looking for, so I decided to design my own. My goals were to create a kerfmaker that was: Easy to print Easy to assemble Compact Durable Accurate Built using inexpensive, readily available hardware It's become a permanent addition to my own woodworking shop, and I hope it becomes one in yours as well. Disclaimer This is an original CAD model created by me. The kerfmaker concept has existed in woodworking for many years, and this design is inspired by the style and functionality of the Bridge City Toolworks Kerfmaker. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or produced by Bridge City Toolworks. If You Enjoyed This Model If you decide to print one, I'd love to see your build! Please consider: ⭐ Rating the model 📸 Posting a Make 🚀 Giving it a Boost if you found it useful Your support helps me continue designing and sharing new tools for the woodworking community.

description: ⚠️ Measure your power strip before printing! This is a parametric model. Do NOT print it using the default dimensions unless your power strip matches them. Before generating the model, carefully measure your power strip and enter its dimensions. 1. Add extra length The length of the enclosure should be slightly longer than the actual power strip. Since the power strip is inserted from the top at an angle, it needs some extra clearance during installation. If the enclosure is exactly the same length as the power strip, inserting it will be difficult or even impossible. I recommend adding at least 5 mm (typically 5–8 mm) to the measured length to ensure easy installation. Example: Measured power strip length: 250 mm Enclosure length: 255–258 mm The width and height can remain much closer to the actual dimensions, but the length should always include this additional clearance. 2. Check the cable exit position Before printing, check the distance between the top surface of the power strip and the top of the cable exit (see reference image). This check is important because the power strip is inserted from above. If the cable exits too close to the top of the power strip and your desk is thick, the cable may interfere with the underside of the tabletop during installation. You can verify the required height using this rule: Measure the distance between the top of the power strip and the top of the cable exit . Subtract your desk thickness . Subtract 6 mm (design clearance already accounted for in the model) . Available clearance = (top-to-cable-exit distance) − desk thickness − 6 mm If the result is positive or zero , the default height is sufficient. If the result is negative , increase the model height by that amount (absolute value). Example Top to cable exit: 20 mm Desk thickness: 25 mm Result: 20 − 25 − 6 = −11 mm → Increase height by 11 mm 3. Printing instructions This is a parametric model , meaning you only need to adjust three main values to fit your power strip: Length Width Height Once these values are set, the model will automatically adapt to your specific power strip dimensions. Two-part design The model is split into two separate parts : Top part Bottom part Both parts must be generated using the exact same dimensions to ensure a proper fit. Orientation for printing After exporting the models: The bottom part can be printed as-is. The top part must be rotated 180° before printing to ensure correct orientation and printability + This is necessary due to the geometry of the design. Assembly After printing, the bottom part must be permanently glued to the top part . Once glued, the two parts form a single rigid enclosure ready for installation into the desk. Important note This model was created in Fusion 360 , and while it is fully functional and parametric, this also means there are some design limitations related to the way parameters and exported bodies behave . For this reason, always double-check the exported geometry before slicing. If you follow the steps above, the model should print and assemble without issues. i may try to remodel this in open scad in the future About this model Turn any standard power strip into a clean, recessed desk power outlet. Instead of buying an expensive built-in desk power strip, this parametric model lets you install a regular power strip directly into your desk. Simply customize the dimensions to fit your own power strip, print the enclosure, cut an opening in the tabletop, and press-fit the insert into place. Why I designed this Most recessed desk power strips available online are: expensive available in only a few sizes often made by unknown brands with questionable quality Instead, I bought a high-quality standard power strip from a trusted manufacturer and designed this enclosure to create the same built-in look. The result is: lower cost better electrical quality freedom to choose the power strip you trust a clean and professional-looking installation If you build one, I'd love to see your Make!

description: Apothecary Cabinet Generator V1.1 This is a fully parametric apothecary cabinet generator that lets you make a custom little drawer cabinet without having to model the whole thing from scratch every time. You choose the cabinet size, drawer size, number of rows, number of columns, wall thickness, clearances, top cap, base style, drawer face details, and a bunch of other options. The generator builds the cabinet around the drawer size you choose, then also generates one matching drawer that fits that cabinet. This version uses one uniform drawer size across the whole cabinet. That means every opening is the same size, and the tool generates one matching drawer that you can duplicate in your slicer. So if you make a 4x3 cabinet, you print one cabinet and duplicate the drawer 12 times. Simple, clean, and way less annoying than generating a pile of separate drawer files for no reason. The cabinet is built around the drawer size you pick. Change the drawer width, height, or depth, and the whole cabinet recalculates around it. You can make tiny parts drawers, craft storage, dice drawers, bead organizers, mini hardware cabinets, display cabinets, or whatever other small nonsense needs organized. 🧰 Display / Export Modes Setting What It Does Both Shows the cabinet and one drawer side by side. Good for previewing the full setup. Cabinet Shows only the cabinet body. Use this when exporting the cabinet STL. Drawer Shows only the matching drawer. Use this when exporting the drawer STL. Fit Test Shows one drawer placed inside the cabinet so you can check the fit before printing everything. The Fit Test mode is useful before wasting filament on a big cabinet. You can choose which row and column the test drawer appears in and how far it is pulled out. 🗄️ Cabinet Grid Settings Setting What It Controls Columns How many drawer openings go across the cabinet. Rows How many drawer openings go up the cabinet. Drawer Width The outside width of the drawer body. The cabinet openings are calculated from this. Drawer Height The outside height of the drawer body. This controls the height of each opening. Drawer Depth The depth of the drawer body. This also controls how deep the cabinet needs to be. Drawer count is: Rows x Columns Examples: Cabinet Size Drawer Count 2x2 4 drawers 3x3 9 drawers 4x3 12 drawers 5x4 20 drawers 6x5 30 drawers You only need to export one drawer, then duplicate it in the slicer until you have the right amount. 📏 Clearance Settings Setting What It Does Fit Clearance XY Clearance around the drawer on the left, right, top, and bottom. This is what lets the drawer actually slide. Fit Clearance Depth Extra space behind the drawer so it does not bottom out against the back panel. Divider Thickness Thickness of the walls between drawer openings. Back Panel Turns the cabinet back panel on or off. Back Thickness Thickness of the back panel if enabled. Important part: Fit Clearance XY is per side. So if you set: Fit Clearance XY: 0.5 mm That gives the drawer: Side Clearance Left 0.5 mm Right 0.5 mm Top 0.5 mm Bottom 0.5 mm That means the actual cabinet opening becomes: Drawer Width + 1.0 mm Drawer Height + 1.0 mm Start with 0.5 mm for most FDM printers. If your printer is super dialed in, you can try less. If the drawers are tight, bump it up. Tiny drawers are tolerance nightmares (sometimes), because apparently plastic enjoys lying to us! 🏛️ Cabinet Style Settings Setting What It Controls Cabinet Front Frame Adds a raised frame around the front outside edge of the cabinet. Cabinet Frame Width How wide that front frame is. Cabinet Frame Projection How far the front frame sticks out from the cabinet face. Top Cap Turns the top cap on or off. Top Cap Thickness How thick the top cap is. Top Cap Side Overhang How far the top cap sticks out on the left and right sides. Top Cap Front Overhang How far the top cap sticks out over the front. Top Cap Back Overhang How far the top cap sticks out in the back. Set this to 0 for a flat back. Base Plinth Adds a raised front base piece under the cabinet. Base Plinth Height How tall the base plinth is. Base Plinth Projection How far the base plinth sticks out from the front. For a cabinet that sits flat against a wall, use: Top Cap Back Overhang: 0 That keeps the back clean instead of giving it a useless little roof spoiler. 🦶 Base Foot Styles Option What It Does No Feet No extra feet added. Clean flat cabinet. Four Block Feet Adds block feet at all four corners. Front Block Feet Adds feet only on the front. Good for a more decorative front-facing cabinet. Side Runners Adds long runner-style feet along the sides. Full Raised Base Adds one full solid raised base under the cabinet. Setting What It Controls Foot Width Width of each foot or runner. Foot Depth Depth of block feet. Foot Height How tall the feet or raised base are. 📦 Drawer Body Settings Setting What It Controls Drawer Wall Thickness Thickness of the drawer side walls. Drawer Bottom Thickness Thickness of the drawer floor. Drawer Front Thickness Thickness of the visible front face of the drawer. Drawer Front Overlap How much the drawer face overlaps the cabinet opening. Drawer Face Gap Gap between neighboring drawer fronts. Helps stop drawer faces from colliding. The drawer body is hollowed automatically. The front face is slightly larger than the drawer body so it covers the opening cleanly. The overlap is automatically limited so if you make a bunch of drawers side by side, the fronts do not crash into each other like badly parked shopping carts. 🎛️ Drawer Front Detail Switches Instead of a confusing preset menu, the drawer details are controlled with simple on/off switches. Switch What It Adds Use Raised Border Adds a raised rectangular border around the drawer face. Use Round Knob Adds a simple centered round knob. Use Bar Pull Adds a horizontal handle across the drawer front. Use Label Holder Adds a raised rectangular label holder. Use Card Catalog Face Adds a card-catalog style label frame and pull lip. Use Cup Pull Face Adds a wider raised pull plate style front. For the classic apothecary/card catalog look, I recommend: Setting Value Use Raised Border True Use Card Catalog Face True Use Round Knob False Use Bar Pull False Use Label Holder False Use Cup Pull Face False That gives it the old little-label-and-pull-lip look without turning the drawer into decorative soup. 🏷️ Raised Border Settings Setting What It Controls Raised Border Width Thickness of the raised border lines. Raised Border Raise How far the border sticks out from the drawer face. Raised Border Inset How far inward the border sits from the edge of the drawer front. Use this when you want the drawer face to look more finished and less like a plain cube pretending to have a personality. 🔘 Round Knob Settings Setting What It Controls Knob Diameter Size of the round knob. Knob Projection How far the knob sticks out. Knob Height Position Vertical position of the knob on the drawer front. Good for simple drawers or old cabinet-style fronts. 🧲 Bar Pull Settings Setting What It Controls Bar Pull Width Percent Width of the bar pull as a percentage of the drawer width. Bar Pull Diameter Thickness of the bar handle. Bar Pull Projection How far the handle sticks out from the drawer front. Bar Pull Height Position Vertical position of the bar handle. This makes the drawer look more modern or industrial. 📝 Label Holder Settings Setting What It Controls Label Width Percent Width of the label holder based on drawer width. Label Height Percent Height of the label holder based on drawer height. Label Frame Thickness Thickness of the label holder border. Label Raise How far the label holder sticks out. Label Height Position Vertical position of the label holder. Good for parts drawers, craft storage, bead storage, hardware sorting, and all the other tiny organized-chaos stuff. 🗂️ Card Catalog Face Settings Setting What It Controls Card Plate Raise How far the card catalog details stick out. Card Pull Lip Diameter Thickness of the little pull lip. Card Label Width Percent Width of the card label frame. Card Label Height Percent Height of the card label frame. Card Label Height Position Vertical position of the label frame. Card Pull Width Percent Width of the pull lip. Card Pull Height Position Vertical position of the pull lip. This is the best setting group for the classic apothecary look. It gives the drawer that old card-catalog vibe without needing actual metal hardware. 🥣 Cup Pull Face Settings Setting What It Controls Cup Pull Width Percent Width of the cup pull plate. Cup Pull Height Percent Height of the cup pull plate. Cup Pull Raise How far the cup pull plate sticks out. Cup Pull Height Position Vertical position of the cup pull. This gives the drawer a chunkier pull face. It works better on larger drawers. On tiny drawers, it can get crowded fast, because tiny drawers are dramatic. 🖨️ Printing Workflow Set your rows, columns, and drawer size. Set Fit Clearance XY to around 0.5 mm . Use Fit Test mode to check one drawer in the cabinet. Export the cabinet using Cabinet mode. Export the drawer using Drawer mode. Duplicate the drawer in your slicer. Example: Cabinet What To Print 4x3 cabinet 1 cabinet + 12 drawers 5x4 cabinet 1 cabinet + 20 drawers 6x5 cabinet 1 cabinet + 30 drawers ✅ Suggested First Test Setting Value Columns 2 Rows 2 Drawer Width 42 mm Drawer Height 28 mm Drawer Depth 55 mm Fit Clearance XY 0.5 mm Fit Clearance Depth 1.0 mm Divider Thickness 2.4 mm Drawer Wall Thickness 1.6 mm Drawer Bottom Thickness 1.8 mm Print a small 2x2 first before going huge. Once the fit is good, scale it up and go nuts. ⚠️ Current Limitation This version uses one drawer size for the whole cabinet. That means all openings are the same size. A future version may add different drawer sizes per row or multiple drawer types, but this one is meant to be clean, usable, and not an OpenSCAD crime scene with knobs.

description: This is a simple but very useful corner clamping assist designed for use with 1 inch wide Husky ratchet straps . The corner pieces hold the strap away from the edge of your workpiece, helping distribute pressure more evenly while also reducing the chance of the strap digging into soft wood, plywood edges, boxes, panels, or odd-shaped glue-ups. Why I Made This Ratchet straps can be very handy in the shop, but when used as clamps they tend to: Dig into corners Crush softer edges Slide out of position Pull unevenly around sharp corners Put too much pressure directly on one point These corner blocks help solve that by creating a rounded stand-off point for the strap, making the strap easier to control and much more useful as a woodworking clamping aid. Great For Cabinet boxes Drawer boxes Picture frames Plywood assemblies Large rectangular glue-ups Shop jigs Temporary holding while fastening Odd-sized projects where normal clamps do not reach Helping square up projects before screws, brads, or glue fully set Usage Notes These are intended as a woodworking clamping assist , not as a replacement for rated load-bearing tie-down hardware. Use reasonable pressure and check that the strap, workpiece, and printed parts are seated correctly before tightening. Do not use these for vehicle tie-downs, overhead lifting, load securing, or any safety-critical application. A differenza della filettatura NPT , la filettatura GHT è cilindrica/parallela e non conica. La tenuta non avviene stringendo progressivamente il filetto, ma tramite la guarnizione presente nel raccordo femmina , che lavora contro la faccia frontale del raccordo maschio (appositamente predisposto in questi raccordi). La filettatura GHT lavora normalmente con una guarnizione frontale, quindi il nastro PTFE non è sempre necessario e non sostituisce una guarnizione corretta. 🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

description: Comprehensive Guide to the Pocket Mechanical Switch Clicker Fidget 🕹️ Welcome to the ultimate Pocket Mechanical Switch Clicker Fidget project page! This model is specifically engineered for people who love the crisp, tactile sensation of mechanical keyboard switches. It functions as a heavy-duty, portable fidget toy that fits easily into a pocket, backpack, or pencil case. Whether you are trying to stay focused during class, brainstorming your next big project, or just looking for a satisfying way to pass the time, this 3-piece model is the perfect quick print. Key Design Features 💡 100% Support-Free: The geometry of this model utilizes careful bridging angles. You can print the entire file completely flat without generating any waste material. Ultra-Low Filament Consumption: Weighing in at less than 7 grams, you can print dozens of these using leftover filament scraps from the end of your spools. High Interlocking Tolerances: The button caps are designed with a standard cross-stem socket that snugly grabs onto your switches without slipping off during rapid clicking. Technical Print Specifications 🖨️ This model has been sliced and thoroughly tested on Bambu Lab printers to ensure perfect execution. Below is the exact configuration data used during the testing phase. Slicer Parameter Recommended Value Functional Purpose Printer Profile Bambu Lab P1S / X1C Targets standard CoreXY motion systems. Print Bed Type Textured PEI Plate Hides layer lines on the bottom face and improves bed adhesion. Filament Material PLA Basic (Green) Offers rigidity and prevents shrinking or warping. Layer Height 0.24mm Draft Optimizes print time while retaining tight tolerances. Sparse Infill Density 15% Provides a lightweight but structurally sound core. Infill Pattern Grid Ensures equal strength across the X and Y axes. Supports DISABLED (NONE) Eliminates post-processing cleanup and saves material. Wall Loops 2 Layers Keeps outer shells strong enough to withstand heavy finger pressure. Component Dimensional Data 📐 If you plan to modify or scale this project, please refer to the exact millimeter dimensions of the original source files below. Part Name Total Quantity Width (X) Length (Y) Height (Z) Base Part 1 Piece 41.21 mm 42.70 mm 9.00 mm Button Caps 2 Pieces 13.69 mm 17.99 mm 17.30 mm Required Extra Hardware & Materials 🛠️ To turn these plastic parts into a working clicker toy, you will need to source a few external items: Mechanical Keyboard Switches: This model accommodates standard Cherry MX style switches. For the loudest and most tactile click, look for Blue Mechanical Switches (such as dustproof clicky switches found online). “ https://www.amazon.com/Zhouwang-Blue-Mechanical-Switches-Dustproof/dp/B0FX2GT2XX/ref=sr_1_3?crid=3IEF9XUEI9D4Q&th=1 ” 3D Printed Alternative: If you do not have access to real keyboard hardware, you can search MakerWorld for a "3D printed mechanical switch" model and drop it right into the base. Adhesive (Super Glue): Because different brands of switches can vary by fractions of a millimeter, you may need a drop of standard plastic glue or super glue to lock the switches into the housing. Detailed Step-by-Step Assembly Guide 🧩 Follow these instructions carefully to assemble your clicker fidget safely and correctly. Clear the Build Plate: Let your heated print bed cool down entirely before removing the parts. Snapping them off while hot can warp the bottom plate. Examine the Parts: Check the inside of the square switch holes on the Base Part and the cross-shaped slots underneath the Button Caps . Remove any tiny stray plastic strings. Test Fit the Switches: Align your mechanical switches over the two square cavities in the base. Press straight down firmly until the side tabs click into place. Apply Glue If Necessary: If the switches slide out too easily when you pull on them, remove them. Place a tiny drop of super glue onto the inner side walls of the base cavity, then push the switches back in. Let it dry for 5 minutes. Attach the Button Caps: Line up the cross-shaped stem of the switch with the socket under the button cap. Press down evenly until the cap sits flush over the switch body. Frequently Asked Questions & Troubleshooting ❓ What should I do if the button caps are too loose? If your printer over-extrudes slightly, the cross socket might stretch. A tiny piece of paper placed over the switch stem before pressing the cap on will create a tighter fit. Can I print this in PETG or ABS instead of PLA? Yes! While PLA is recommended for its stiffness and ease of use, PETG will work great and offer higher impact resistance if dropped. Why won't my switches fit into the base? Ensure your first layer didn't suffer from "elephant's foot" (where the plastic squishes outward on the bottom layer). If it did, use a small craft knife to carefully scrape the inside edge of the square holes.

description: Membership Subscribe if you want to support me Keep the backseat entertained with this highly adjustable, universal car headrest mount. Designed to securely hold everything from a Nintendo Switch to a large iPad/Tablet , it’s the perfect companion for road trips. Key Features Universal Compatibility: Adjustable clamp system that fits smartphones, gaming consoles (Nintendo Switch), and tablets. True Quick-Release: Drop your device in and lock it in seconds, making it effortless to take your device with you when leaving the car. Innovative Fast-Thread Nut: The locking nut only has threads on one half. This means you can slide it freely into position and tighten or loosen it with just a quarter-turn ($1/4$ turn) . Full Adjustability: Easily adjust both the height and the viewing angle for the perfect ergonomic setup. Hardware Required To assemble the mount, you will need: 1x M5 x 35mm Bolt 1x M5 Nut (A locknut / nyloc nut is highly recommended to prevent it from loosening due to car vibrations). 100% 3D-Printed Option (No Metal Hardware Needed) If you don't have real hardware on hand, I have included a fully 3D-printable bolt and nut in the files. ⚠️ Important Assembly Note: The 3D-printed bolt is designed as a press-fit . Do not try to screw it into place—simply press it firmly together. Print Settings & Tips Material: Since this sits in a car, PETG, ASA, or ABS is highly recommended to withstand summer heat. Avoid standard PLA as it may deform on hot days. Orientation: Check the sliced preview or standard print profiles for the optimal printing orientation. Step-by-Step Guide Prepare the Parts: Gather the main arm, the tablet/Switch clamp components, and your hardware (or the 3D-printed press-fit bolt). Snap the Clamp Together: The main holding bracket and the adjustment nut snap directly together. No tools are needed for this part—just align them and press until they click. Orient the Fast-Thread Nut: When sliding the components onto the main threaded rod, make sure the innovative Fast-Thread Nut is positioned at the very top . Secure the Pivot: Use the M5 x 35mm bolt and nut (or the 3D-printed press-fit pin) to secure the tilt/angle mechanism. If using the 3D-printed pin: Remember to press it firmly into place rather than screwing it. Your headrest mount is now ready to be installed in the car! How to Setup & Use (Daily Operation) Once assembled, setting up your mount for the first time is incredibly easy, and daily use is lightning fast thanks to the quick-release mechanism. Initial Setup (First Time Only) Set the Height: Move the top nut (the Fast-Thread Nut) to the desired height where you want your device to sit, and twist it a quarter-turn to lock it in place. Insert Your Device: Place your iPad, Nintendo Switch, or phone into the bottom clamp. Secure the Base: Srew the bottom nut up against the device and tighten it gently. ⚠️ Note: Do not overtighten! Just tighten it enough so your device sits securely and cannot slide out. Daily Use (Quick Release) Once the bottom bracket is set to your device's size, you never have to adjust it again! Taking your device out: Simply loosen the top Fast-Thread Nut with a quarter-turn (1/4 turn) , slide it up, and take your device with you. The outer box is then generated around the drawer using the clearance and wall thickness settings. If your desk has a front edge, apron, trim piece, or thick lip that blocks the drawer from opening, increase this value. It makes the top of the box taller and drops the drawer opening lower. Example: Desk Lip Height Suggested Desk Lip Clearance No lip 0 mm Small lip 10–15 mm Medium lip 20–30 mm Big chunky desk lip 35 mm+ Drawer Fit / Clearance Settings 🛠️ Setting What It Changes Side Clearance Extra space on the left and right sides of the drawer Top Clearance Extra space above the drawer Bottom Clearance Extra space below the drawer Rear Clearance Extra space behind the drawer inside the box Front Reveal Lets the drawer sit slightly forward from the box opening These are the settings that keep the drawer from becoming a perfectly-sized plastic prison.
