description: Press the Customize button to customize! A fully parametric mesh strainer/colander: pick a rectangle or ellipse boundary, a solid border frame, and one of five interior grid patterns, and the interior mesh area bows upward into a dome, a straight-sided cone, or a volcano shape that dips back down to a small solid pad at the print plate. Add optional colander-style ear handles at the rim and mounting screw holes on the border. Looking for a flat mesh panel or an open-top mesh basket instead? Those are separate listings: Parametric Mesh Panel Generator and Parametric Mesh Basket Generator . Key Features Rectangle or ellipse boundary: set overall width and depth (or diameter, for a circle) directly Three bow shapes: rounded dome, straight-sided cone, or volcano (cone that curves back down to a small solid pad touching the print plate at the center) Curve-following holes: every hole is individually tilted to the bowed surface's own local angle at that point, instead of being drilled straight down through a curving wall Five grid patterns: square, diagonal (45 degree square), hexagonal honeycomb, triangular, and staggered circular holes, each with its true shape (not just a round approximation) carried onto the curved surface Colander-style ear handles: optional flat handles sticking out from the rim (1 or more, evenly spaced), each with an optional hanging hole Mounting screw holes: optional, placed at the 4 corners for a rectangle or evenly around a bolt circle for an ellipse, with an optional countersink for flat-head screws Solid border frame: frame around the outer edge, width set directly Auto-sized holes and struts: hole_size and strut_width default to 2.5x your nozzle diameter when left at 0, so a fresh copy prints cleanly without any tuning Pattern rotation: rotate the whole grid independently of the panel's default orientation Print Settings Setting Recommended Orientation Print exactly as generated - border flat on the bed, bow pointing up Supports Not required for bow_type = cone or volcano; a rounded dome needs supports right at its apex Perimeters 2-3 Infill 15-20% Material PLA or PETG Download the optimized print profile from this page, delete the sample models off the plate, and import your STL into it. How to Use Outer Shape: set shape to rectangle or ellipse, then outer_x, outer_y, and thickness. Border: set border_width. Bowed Mesh: pick bow_type (dome, cone, or volcano) and set bow_height. For a volcano, also set bow_volcano_ridge and bow_volcano_center_diameter. Side handles (optional): turn on side_handle_enable, set side_handle_count, side_handle_length, and side_handle_width. Set side_handle_hole_diameter above 0 for a hanging hole in each tip. Screw holes (optional): turn on screw_holes_enable, set screw_hole_count, screw_hole_diameter, and screw_hole_inset. Pick a pattern: choose pattern and, if you want a specific look, set hole_size and strut_width; leave both at 0 to auto-size from nozzle_diameter. Export the STL, delete the sample models off the plate, and import your STL into it. Customization Use the MakerWorld Customizer. All parameters are grouped and annotated. Outer Shape - shape: rect for a rectangle, ellipse for an ellipse or circle - outer_x: overall width, X axis (mm) - outer_y: overall depth, Y axis (mm) - thickness: panel material thickness (mm) Border Frame - border_width: solid border frame width (mm) Bowed Mesh - bow_type: dome (rounded, needs supports at the apex), cone (straight sides), or volcano (cone that dips back down to the plate at center) - bow_height: height the bowed mesh area rises above the border's top face, at its center (mm) - bow_volcano_ridge: fraction of the radius (0-1) where a volcano's peak ridge sits before curving back down to the plate; only used when bow_type is volcano - bow_volcano_center_diameter: diameter of the solid pad where a volcano's center touches the print plate (mm); the mesh between it and the ridge is perforated; only used when bow_type is volcano - bow_rim_width: solid margin around the base of the bow with no mesh holes (mm); 0 = holes cover the entire bowed area, right up to the rim - bow_segments: number of stacked segments approximating the dome's curve; higher = smoother, slower render Side Handles - side_handle_enable: add flat, colander-style ear handles sticking out from the rim - side_handle_count: number of handles, placed evenly around the rim (2 = opposite each other, colander-style) - side_handle_length: how far each handle extends beyond the outer edge (mm) - side_handle_width: width of each handle (mm) - side_handle_hole_diameter: diameter of an optional hanging hole through each handle's tip; 0 = no hole (mm) - side_handle_angle_offset: rotates the handle placement (degrees); 0 places the first handle along +X Screw Holes - screw_holes_enable: toggle mounting screw holes on/off - screw_hole_count: 4 places one at each corner (rect) or evenly around a bolt circle (ellipse); other counts are placed evenly around the panel - screw_hole_diameter: screw shaft clearance hole diameter (mm) - screw_hole_inset: distance from each hole's center to the nearest outer edge (mm); ignored when screw_hole_exact_spacing is on - screw_hole_exact_spacing: specify the exact hole-to-hole spacing directly instead of an edge inset - screw_hole_spacing_x: exact distance between opposite hole centers, X axis (mm); used only when screw_hole_exact_spacing is on - screw_hole_spacing_y: exact distance between opposite hole centers, Y axis (mm); used only when screw_hole_exact_spacing is on - screw_hole_angle_offset: rotates which rect corner is first (steps of 90 degrees), or the ellipse bolt-circle start angle (degrees) - screw_countersink_enable: add a conical countersink on the top face for a flat-head screw - screw_countersink_diameter: countersink diameter at the top face (mm); should be larger than screw_hole_diameter - screw_countersink_depth: countersink depth, cut down from the top face (mm) Mesh Pattern - pattern: square, diagonal, hex, triangle, or circle - hole_size: hole size (mm); flat-to-flat, edge length, or diameter depending on pattern; 0 = auto (2.5x nozzle diameter) - strut_width: wall width between holes (mm); 0 = auto (2.5x nozzle diameter) - pattern_rotation: extra rotation applied to the whole pattern (degrees) Printer - nozzle_diameter: drives the auto strut/hole sizing and minimum-feature warnings (mm) Bow Type Notes The model always prints "upside down" from how it's used: the border sits flat on the bed and the bowed mesh points straight up while printing, and you flip it over afterward so the bow becomes a concave bowl that drains through the mesh. That orientation is what keeps a cone or volcano fully supports-free, since the wall's cross-section only ever shrinks as it rises. A rounded dome is the one exception: it flattens out toward a horizontal cap right at the very apex and will typically still want supports there. A volcano's ridge and center pad need to stay proportioned so the funnel between them doesn't get steeper than 45 degrees from vertical; if you push bow_height very short relative to a wide bow_volcano_ridge, watch the console for a supports warning and increase bow_height (or reduce bow_volcano_ridge / increase bow_volcano_center_diameter) if it appears. Pattern Notes Every hole is individually tilted to match the bowed surface's own local angle at that point, so a hole never comes out as a stretched, off-angle slot the way a straight vertical drill would on a curving wall. Square, hex, and triangle holes keep their true shape on the curve, not just a round stand-in; only their placement follows the chosen pattern's grid. This is more render work than a flat panel, so very small hole_size / strut_width settings will render noticeably slower here. Side Handle Notes Handles are flat tabs at the same thickness as the border, flush with the rim, so they need no supports regardless of the bow. With 2 handles (the default) they land directly opposite each other; higher counts space evenly around the rim, and side_handle_angle_offset rotates the whole set. Keep side_handle_hole_diameter comfortably under side_handle_width so the hanging hole doesn't break out the sides. Screw Hole Notes The countersink is a cone that tapers from screw_hole_diameter at its base up to screw_countersink_diameter at the top face, so it meets the shaft hole below it with no step. Keep screw_countersink_depth comfortably under thickness so it doesn't cut all the way through. Sizing Tips If holes print closed or clogged, increase hole_size above 2.5x your nozzle diameter. If struts look flimsy or go missing, increase strut_width; anything thinner than 2.5x your nozzle diameter will not print as designed.

description: Kumihimo Marudai Bracelet/Rope braiding stand This is a beginner friendly Kumihimo Marudai stand to make bracelets or rope using the ancient Japanese artform of Kumihimo , which is done by weaving strings of silk, rope or yarn together using a disc to form a rope/bracelet with artistic patterns in the process. The Marudai (Japanese, lit. “ Round Stand ”) allows you to move multiple strings at once using even back and forth movements of string to interlace the strings to form the weave of the bracelet or cord. This results in a faster weave compared to a hand-held portable Round Kumihimo Disc for round bracelets , but is less portable due to its larger form factor. Marudai stand with weighted bobbins and counterweight Usage A Kumihimo weave being formed through the center hole and pulled down by a counterweight attached to it The Marudai is used together with a center weight to pull on the formed weave through the hole in the center, and smaller weighted bobbins , called tama, on each individual string around the outsides. Commonly, the ratio of the weight is that the center weight will be between ½ to ⅔ of the combined weight of the outside weights. This balance ensures that the woven pattern will be consistent between each movement and result in a uniform shape and pattern of the bracelet/ropes. There is no hard rule of which side of the spectrum you decide on, it can depend on the particular use case of the weave. Using a heavier center weight will increase the pulling force and can result in a looser weave, whereas less center weight will provide lower resistance and give a tighter weave. You may purchase weighted bobbins and counterweights online or use 3D printed ones such as my Weighted Bobbin for Kumihimo braiding - Tama . Many different patterns of braids can be formed using a Marudai, such as alternating lines, dotted patterns, spirals and more. Assembly The assembly is quick and easy and can be done without tools. Hardware required Printed base , I recommend printing the weighted base, which gives the stand a stronger support Printed top disc , pick from a series of different discs depending on your level of experience and convenience desired Numbered Top disc with 32 notches and markers for 8-string and 16-string braids Great for beginners or those transitioning from a Kumihimo hand disc due to the familiar style Numbered Top disc with 32 round guides and markers for 8-string and 16-string braids A nice balance between full notches and a fully round disc, giving the best of both worlds holding the strings loosely in position, but being able to move them with a push rather than having to lift them out of the notches to re-arrange for complex patterns Top disc with 32 round guides and markers for 8-string and 16-string braids Same disc, but without number labels Numbered Top round disc without indentations. Markers for 8-string and 16-string braids This is the traditional form of a marudai disc and allows for quick re-arranging of strands following a series of moves. This requires practice as the strings will only be held in place by gravity as they are not guided to a particular location Top round disc without indentations. Markers for 8-string and 16-string braids Same disc, but without number labels Connecting rods (4x) You can either: Get 1/2 inch (12.7mm) round dowel rods (such as round wooden dowels ) from your local hardware store and cut them to size (I recommend a length of ~9inches, or 20-25cm for each rod) Or print the provided rods (24cm in length - you may resize the length as desired and based on your printers print bed) Optional rod connectors to extend the heigh of the stand, by connecting multiple rods together to form a taller stand Assembly steps Place the bottom disc on the table or stable surface - this may either be the weighted bottom disc Weighted bottom disc or you can also decide to use one of the other pattern top disc as a bottom disc Round top disc being used as a bottom disc Push the four (4) connecting rods into the slots If you want to give it a stronger hold, you may use some glue and attach them permanently to the base Now attach the top disc to the top side of the connecting rods If you want to be able to change between different top plates, then I recommend not using glue for the top side. Optionally: if you want to make the stand taller , use the printable rod connectors to connect multiple rods to form a taller stand You may want to place additional weights onto the bottom to ensure the stand remains stable Rods extended using the optional rod connector Print Settings Supports / Brim: No Layer height: 0.20 mm Infill: 15% cubic for parts, 100% rectilinear for weighted base Walls: 2 Wall generation: Arachne for smooth curves Top/bottom pattern: Monotonic Orientation: Flat on the bed Material: PETG or PLA Kumihimo collection I've made a series of Kumihimo braiding related models to help me make neat Kumihimo braids, check them out: Weighted Bobbins for Kumihimo braiding To complement your Marudai, if you don't already have weights, you can print a set of Weighted Bobbin for Kumihimo braiding which make it easier to make neat braids by maintaining an even tension on the braid. Square Kumihimo disc for Flat bracelets If you're interested in making flat bracelets, you can check out my Square Kumihimo disc for flat bracelets which allows you to make some beautiful flat patterned bracelets. 32-slot Round Kumihimo disc for round bracelets If you are just starting out and want to make simpler bracelets, check out my 32-slot Round Kumihimo Disc for round bracelets which allows you to easily make Kumihimo bracelets with up to 16 strings (and if pushing it up to 20). 64-slot Large Kumihimo disc for complex pattern bracelets If you are looking for a way to make more complex patterns with more than 16 strings in a single weave, check out my 64-Slot Large Kumihimo disc for complex bracelets which allows you to make Kumihimo bracelets up to 40 strings, which is the practical limit for round Kumihimo braids.

description: A modular filament storage system inspired by one of the best designs on MakerWorld. Before anything else, I want to give full credit to Antiphrasis. Their modular filament rack has deservedly become one of the most popular storage systems on MakerWorld, with thousands of downloads, and it was their design that inspired me to explore a different engineering approach. After using their system myself, I became interested in solving one particular design challenge in a different way. Could I redesign the modular connection system so that each joint only required a single upright while still creating a strong, rigid structure? After building my own interpretation, I contacted Antiphrasis to show them what I'd created and to ask if they were happy for me to publish it on MakerWorld. Thankfully they gave me their blessing, so I'm delighted to be able to share it with the community. 🧵 Why I designed this version The original system is excellent and has proven itself over thousands of prints. Rather than trying to improve every aspect of it, I focused on solving one specific engineering problem: Creating a connection system that locks adjacent modules together while using a single shared upright instead of two. The result is a storage system that is solid and stable while reducing the number of uprights required and maintaining a clean, modular appearance. I genuinely recommend taking a look at Antiphrasis' original design as well, then deciding which approach best suits your needs. 📦 Modular by design Each module baes stores three filament spools. Using two base sections and two uprights creates storage for six rolls, with additional modules simply extending the system. Note: Always orient your bases in the same way The photographs show just a few possible layouts, including my own corner installation storing 36 spools along with additional shelving for boxed filament. 🖨️ Print notes Two print profiles are included: - PLA Basic - PETG No AMS required. description: Fly Swatter Fan – Holographic Fly Deterrent Help keep flies away from your food without chemicals or loud buzzing! This Fly Swatter Fan uses spinning TPU blades that display the holographic texture transferred from a textured PEI build plate. As the blades rotate, they create constantly changing flashes of reflected light that discourage flies from landing near your food. How It Works Flies have compound eyes that are highly sensitive to movement and rapidly changing light. As the holographic blades spin, they create constantly shifting reflections that can make the area appear unstable or difficult for flies to land in. Because of this, flies will often choose to fly somewhere else instead. Unlike sticky traps or chemical repellents, this design relies only on motion and reflected light to help discourage flies from landing near your food. Use a light-colored filament to maximize the holographic reflections. Balance the blades for smooth, quiet operation. This is my first design including motors so issues may arise and I love to hear feedback. If you enjoy this design, please leave a like, upload a Make, and share your print settings. tags: s26 ultra|spigen|samsung|camera bump|balancing pad|parametric|phone case|galaxy s26
description: Camera Bump Balancing Pad — Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (Spigen Case) My first MakerWorld upload — tips and feedback very welcome, especially on dual-nozzle print settings. The problem: Place a Galaxy S26 Ultra on a desk and it wobbles annoyingly when you touch the screen, because the camera module raises one side of the case. I decided to fix this with a printed pad, and ended up going further — matching the dimensions of my Spigen case camera bump and mirroring the three camera circles with customisable lettering. It turned out to be more involved than I expected, but I'm pleased with the result. Design notes: The pad prints with the lettering face-down on the build plate. The other face has a shallow recess (one layer deep) for double-sided tape, sized so the tape sits flush with no visible gap. I used Tesa 4970 tape (0.225mm thick) in a 0.15mm recess, leaving 0.075mm proud — enough to grip without a visible step. The model is split into two parts for dual-colour printing: Black part — outer wall, camera circles, solid body Grey part — infill band with letters showing through Importing into your slicer: select both STL files at the same time when importing — they share the same origin and will align automatically. Assign a different filament to each part. What you can customise: Letters (one per circle), font, and letter size Overall dimensions (width, length, height) Number of grey layers (controls colour band depth — increase if the dark colour shows through) Tape recess depth Colours are not set in the Customiser — assign your chosen filaments to each part in your slicer as normal. Plate choice: Because the first layer is the face, plate texture will determine the surface finish. I chose the engineering plate because it’s flat, but this does mean the print lines are more visible. I found I didn’t need glue and it helped not to use it. It came away easily once cooled and not using it helped the filament adhere. Filament choice: I had some small amounts of black and grey PETG I wanted to use up and was wanting to test various settings with PETG so chose that. I think matte PLA would probably look better and be simpler to get good results. Print settings — important: The lettering face is entirely first-layer, so first-layer calibration is critical. Key things that made a difference for me: Slow first layer speed (30–50mm/s) Concentric first layer pattern for the grey/light part Z offset calibration – I set both to -0.02 but this might not be correct for you I ran the high precision offset calibration Increasing the prime volume for the aux hotend – before I did this the first part of the first line would be missed My 3mf is included as a starting point but is configured for the X2D with dual nozzles — other printers will need their own settings. I fed the aux nozzle from an AMS HT with dried PETG, but getting consistent first-layer results from the aux nozzle is genuinely tricky. Printing both parts from the main nozzle with a filament swap will probably give cleaner results but with a little more waste. A 0.2mm nozzle would likely improve the detail and finish — I don't have one but it's worth trying if you do.

description: I needed a compact pill splitter with built-in storage for spare tablets. I didn't have any extra Bambu Lab scraper blades, which ruled out most pill splitter designs available on MakerWorld. The few designs that relied on a printed plastic blade didn't work for me either. My medication is very fragile, and every attempt to split it using a "printed blade" ended up crushing the tablet instead of cutting it. However, I still had a few spare Bambu Lab filament cutter blades that came with my P1S , so I decided it was time to design my own solution. The model is best printed in two colors, although you can also add a third color for the symbol on the top half. I wanted to be able to safely carry the container while traveling without the risk of accidentally touching the blade, so I designed the enclosure with built-in magnets. You'll need four 5 × 2 mm magnets , or alternatively eight 5 × 1 mm magnets . The enclosure also includes a separate storage compartment where you can keep whole tablets before splitting them in the cutting chamber. Joining the two halves of the enclosure may require a little force, but versions with larger clearances became too loose during use, so I intentionally chose a slightly tighter hinge. The tolerances were tested using Bambu Lab filaments. Assembling To install the blade, carefully hold the metal end between two fingers and insert the plastic part into the slot in the lid at an angle. Then use flat pliers to gently push the blade into its final position. Tip: You don't have to insert the blade all the way to the end of the slot. The slot is intentionally longer so you can adjust where the blade contacts the tablet. For smaller tablets (≤ 10 mm), the blade can remain fully inserted. For larger tablets (> 10 mm), moving the blade slightly backward allows it to strike closer to the center of the tablet. I recommend trying a few different positions to find the one that works best for your medication. Parts Bambu Lab filament cutter blade 4 × 5 × 2 mm magnets (or 8 × 5 × 1 mm magnets)

Both versions use Velcro to hold the Flow 2 itself to the mount; they only differ in how the mount attaches to your bag. This design is meant as a more affordable, printable alternative to mounts like this commercial option . Two Models — Pick Your Attachment Style Model 1 — Velcro Strap Mount Wraps a strip of Velcro around your backpack strap to hold the mount in place. Simple, low-profile, and doesn't require any extra hardware — just Velcro. (I think this can also possibly work with MOLLE, but I have not tested myself.) Model 2 — Peak Design Capture Clip Mount Designed to quick-release onto a Peak Design Capture Camera Clip . If you already run a Capture Clip on your strap, this lets you swap the Flow 2 mount on and off in seconds. I've printed and both, and they both will work well — but I personally feel more confident with the Peak Design version since the quick-release clip feels a bit more secure than Velcro alone against a strap. Velcro Sizing Both models are designed to fit Velcro up to 1" wide . Photos shown use 0.75" wide Velcro. For long-term/heavier-duty use, I'd recommend this 1" wide Velcro instead — it's what the mount was actually dimensioned around. Print Settings / Material Notes I printed my originals in PLA , and they've held up fine for my use. That said, since this mount is holding your Gimbal, you may want to print in something tougher and more heat-resistant if you're going to trust it fully — PETG or ASA would be a smart upgrade, especially if it'll sit in a hot car or direct sun. Compatibility Insta360 Flow 2 (secured via Velcro) Model 2 requires a Peak Design Capture Camera Clip Requests Want a different mounting style — belt clip, etc.? Let me know in the comments and I'll consider adding it as another model variant. Use at your own risk. I made this for myself, and I'm sharing it in case it's useful to someone else — but I take no responsibility for how it's printed or used. This is a plastic part: it can break, wear out over time, or fail if it's not printed correctly (wrong material, low infill, bad settings, etc.). Test it yourself before trusting it with anything valuable, and print in a durable material if you're relying on it for real use. Free to print, free to use — just know that if it fails, that's on you, not me.

Produktbeschreibung: 3D-gedruckter Kalibrierungs-Moppel / Mess-Säule (mit Magnet-Option) Dieses Set aus präzisen Kalibrierungs-Moppeln ist ideal für Maker, Ingenieure und Bastler, die eine visuelle Referenz für Höhenmessungen auf ihrer Arbeitsfläche oder direkt an Maschinen benötigen. Eigenschaften: Präzise Markierungen: Jede Säule verfügt über drei feine, schwarze Ringe, die exakt positioniert sind. Klare Referenzhöhen: Die erste Markierung befindet sich exakt 25 mm vom Boden entfernt. Die folgenden Markierungen sind im Abstand von jeweils 5 mm platziert. Das bedeutet, die Ringe markieren die Höhen: 25 mm, 30 mm und 35 mm . Integriertes Magnet-Fach: der druck ist so, dass bei Bedarf ein runder Magnet mit den Maßen 8x2 mm eingesetzt werden kann. Dadurch haften die Moppel sicher auf metallischen Oberflächen (wie z. B. magnetischen Druckbetten). Visuelle Kontrolle: Die Markierungen ermöglichen eine schnelle und einfache visuelle Überprüfung von Höhen und Abständen, zum Beispiel: Ausrichtung von Druckbetten Messung von Bauteilhöhen Referenzpunkte für Laser-Ausrichtungen (wie in den Beispielbildern gezeigt) 3D-gedruckte Qualität: Die gedruckte Oberfläche ist glatt, um scharfe und deutliche Linien zu gewährleisten. Vorteile: Sicherer Halt dank Magnet-Option: Durch den optionalen 8x2-mm-Magneten verrutschen die Säulen nicht auf metallischen Oberflächen, was die Messung noch präziser und komfortabler macht. Zeitsparende Höhenkontrolle: Vermeidet umständliches Messen mit einem Messschieber oder Lineal für schnelle Zwischenprüfungen. Universell einsetzbar: Perfekt für den 3D-Druck, Lasergravur, Modellbau und vieles mehr. Druck- & Montagehinweise: Magnet einsetzen: Beim drucken ist ein stop mit drin wo mann einen Magneten der Größe Ø 8 mm x 2 mm einlegen kann. Empfohlene Einstellungen: Schichthöhe: 0,16 mm oder 0,2 mm für präzise Höhen. Infill: 15–20 % reicht völlig aus. Support: Nicht erforderlich.

Membership Want to join an exclusive community and get early access to prints like this one and get commercial sales licenses? Join my membership The Ultimate Players Kit just got a huge upgrade. I've taken quite a bit of community feedback and transformed the Ultimate Players Kit into something truly special: an ancient tome guarding the knowledge of your character. Included is: A leather sculpted exterior No more arachne wheels Stats with included modifiers and saving throws Gold tracker Wider and deeper dice slots Plus it just looks cool as heck Class insignias for decoration Assembly Instructions Assemble the outer cover Using filament for the hinge pins, link the top cover to the spine, then the spine to the bottom cover. Add Connectors to the cover insides Using the included tool, attach the connectors to the insides of the covers. It is important that you add the connectors to the covers first, and not to the tray and tracker inserts. Add the inserts Snap in the tray to the bottom cover, then the tracker frame to the top cover, taking care that the untextured side of them both face into the spine. Add the corner decorations Using a drop or two of CA glue (super glue) or hot glue, affix the corner decorations. The decorations with only one lip goes on the spine side, and the decorations with corner lips go on the outside. Add your insignia I highly recommend using hot glue/hot melt for this. It will make for easier changing when you want to play a new character. Add the lock mechanisms The lock prints with in place supports that need to be removed (see pictures). Once removed, the receiver (the part of the lock without the prongs) gets added to the tray (bottom). Similar to the cover, add the connectors to the lock, then clip the lock to the frame. Be sure to attach the receiver so that the opening faces upwards (towards the clasp) Add the clasp to the tracker frame in a similar fashion to the receiver (connectors into the part, then clip the part to the tracker frame.) Be sure that when adding the clasp, the prongs are facing downwards towards the receiver. Finally, add the decoration to the locks. Build the trackers There are 8 slots for trackers, but only 7 rods. This is intentional, because I have left an open slot for customization in the future. The top half holds the stats, which gets 4 rods, and the bottom half holds skills which get 3 rods. Please see the model photos for which wheels go in which place. I highly recommend using a pick to micro adjust the wheels to get a nice fitment. It is important to note: the panels that cover the wheels are over sized. This is intentional. Because of the print orientation, they have quite a bit of flex allowed and they act as pins to hold the rods in place once assembled. Once all of the tracker wheels are on the rods, it is time to add the panels on top of them. This is the most fiddly, frustrating bit, but take heart: They do fit and it is very satisfying when they do. Print Settings I highly recommend using my print profiles rather than the STLs. I have done a lot of supports painting and speed changed for the metal parts. The wheel geometry has been re-worked so that arachne wall generation is no longer necessary. The covers and spine were designed to be printed standing upwards for optimal resolution of the texture. The rods should be printed with ~30% infill. This is to stop them flexing too much when spanning large gaps. The snap connector holes on the trays do not need supports. The lock mechanism has included supports in the model. A1 Mini Users This is likely going to be a challenging print for A1M. I recommend slowing your printer down and having a super clean plate: washed with hot water and dawn dish soap. Please also monitor your first layer and slow your print speed for the very tall prints. Upgrading from v2/v3 Most of the parts in this one are not compatible with v2/v3. However I took special caution when designing the windows for the wheels to keep them the same size as the previous version because the wheels are the most time intensive parts to print. As such, the wheels from v2/v3 will fit in this version The rods are slightly wider in diameter, so expect a tight fit, but width wise they do work (I have tested it myself.) I do highly recommend printing a new set of wheels however, the inner geometry has been reinforced for a more clicky wheel with less plastic deformation. Special Thanks A huge shout out to ElsnerPepperForge for the thorough beta testing. I could not have produced this without their help.

Hop into a day of wiggles and giggles with this charming Frog Roly-Poly Toy! 🐸 Designed as a self-righting wobble toy, this frog tumbles, rocks, and spins for a delightfully long time before bouncing right back up again. This innovative toy combines simple physics with playful interaction, creating a fun, hands-on experience for all ages while encouraging curiosity and exploration! ⚙️ Technical Features & Design Built to be an elegant, easy-to-print project, this model maximizes performance while remaining incredibly user-friendly: Streamlined Assembly: Putting your frog together is a breeze! This new model features a streamlined assembly process and now only uses one single connector. NO AMS Needed: A smart multipart design lets you print all parts separately, before assembling them in 7 simple steps. One-Plate Printing: The ONE PLATE versions let you print the entire multi-color model on a single build plate with only 3 filament swaps! Zero Hardware Required: Unlike traditional designs that need metal bearings or heavy screws, this frog relies entirely on its 3D-printed structure and solid infill to self-right. 🛠️ Step-by-Step Assembly Guide The assembly process is straightforward and consists of 7 simple steps . For the best results, having some CA glue (superglue) on hand is recommended. Step 1: Clean the Prints Carefully remove all support material from the printed parts. Ensure all mating surfaces are clean and smooth for a flush fit. Step 2: Prepare the Base Apply a small amount of CA glue on the cutout of the bottom piece. Step 3: Install the Base Connector Insert the hexagonal connector into the base. IMPORTANT: Make sure that its bottom side faces the bottom ! This is crucial for the final weight distribution. Step 4: Assemble the Body Apply a little more CA glue in a circular pattern around the base connector. Align both halves of the body and slot them together. Both seams need to face the back. Step 5: Insert the Belly Panel Take the belly panel and simply press it into its cutout. This step does not require any glue! Step 6: Assemble the Eyes The eyes consist of the inner and outer parts. They are not cross-compatible with each other, so take care not to mix them up. Insert the inner parts into the outer white parts. Step 7: Final Assembly In this final step, insert the completed eyes and the red mouth piece into the rest of the body. Step 8: Optional If you notice excess bits of green filament on the bottom piece of the belly, trim them off with flush cutters. A perfectly smooth bottom ensures the best, longest wobbles. Done! description: Enjoy some outdoor summer fun with this Propeller Launcher perfect for kids and people of all ages! With just a pull of the cord you can send the propeller flying upwards of 10 meters or even more! It prints in 3 easy pieces consisting of the launcher body, the propeller, and the rip cord. Support removal can be quite tricky so for the best results I highly recommend using a pair of nippers or needle nose pliers. A little cleanup with a hobby knife can also prove to be great. I hope you enjoy! For the best print results I highly recommend printing on a well maintained and cleaned build plate for proper adhesion. The main launcher body may be susceptible to tipping over during printing due to an unclean build plate. Simply wash the plate with soap and warm water or wipe it down with isopropyl.

description: This model is a low-power, custom-built toy blaster of my own original design . Ensured to have no internal functionality related to actual complicated gas powered, dangerous mechanisms, methods of modifying them, or inclusion of similar parts or aesthetics. This is strictly a slingshot mechanism , that is tensioned by a lever and connected by snap joints. Functionally and aesthetically, it is the equivalent of a foam dart blaster. All future projects strictly follow these standards, and I will now communicate this directly, not indirectly. — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — [ " Reaper-26" | Lever Action Blaster ] [ Assembly tutorial, More showcases, and rubber band sizes below ] After 4 months of designing and the headache of 100+ reprinted parts from failed tests, I am glad to finally share my hard work here, free of charge, of course. I am finally glad to get this off my back. I will try to upload another model in… 2-3 weeks?…. As long as everything works. This lever action blaster, which I have named the Reaper-26 , is a fully functional toy slingshot powered by rubber bands. I designed this to give a satisfying process of individual round loading and a lever action mechanism that makes handling it a satisfying process, even outside of launching toy bullets. The video below will demonstrate the satisfying clicking sounds the blaster makes when loading. Showcase and Assembly Video: Please watch the last 30 seconds of the video, it contains essential information about how to load it. Improper loading can cause jams and not allow more prop bullets to be inserted. For those who do not have access to YouTube, I am in the process of making an instruction PDF in 2-3 days, these take a lot of effort, almost as much as the video itself. List of features I want to highlight: Individual round loading An internal magazine, that stores fake bullets in the lower barrel. Fake bullet storage on the stock, allowing quick reloads after you empty the internal toy magazine Adjustable and variable rubber band hooks, which I implemented so that many different rubber band diameters can work (I hope this helps with accessibility). The slingshot, magazine, and trigger rubber bands can all be accessed externally without taking the whole thing apart , which is an improvement from my previous model. Unlike traditional bullet launching devices, this toy blaster is 65% more effective because it utilizes the entire projectile, rather than leaving the cartridge to waste. Distance: Averaging from various tests from eye level: 5.0-5.7 Meters 16-18 Feet The launching distance is the same as the my former Deagle. If yours does not reach this distance, then you need stronger bands or they are getting caught and causing friction. Thick rubber bands give more power, please don't use very thin ones. I saw a lot of people do that on my last model… Rubber bands used: Just because I used these exact ones doesn't mean you have to. In fact, these were just lying around my house, so maybe yours could perform even better. The rubber bands attached as part of the Makers Supply are as close to the dimensions as possible. Slingshot, trigger, and magazine feeder rubber bands (Blue) Height - 3-4mm Diameter - 50mm 5-7 rubber bands, with 3-5 being on the slingshot Internal feeder rubber band (Purple) Height - 1.5mm Diameter - 40mm One rubber band used I primarily designed this model to be as accessible as possible . It only requires rubber bands and one spool; every part snaps or slots together without the requirement of glue or screws . The snap joints allow you to disassemble the blaster whenever you want by using a lot of force. There are no permanent joints, but they are strong enough to where you cannot break them unintentionally. The project is for those seeking a more sophisticated and functional model with many parts. The assembly is a hands-on and enjoyable process in itself. If you enjoy working with intricate projects, snapping and slotting parts together, or building, then you will find the assembly enjoyable like I did. Membership Earn a stream of revenue and stand out from the crowd by selling my unique and interactive model for a premium, start now by signing up for my commercial license. Custom Toy Attachments: I loved how there were people on my former model who would tweak the parts aesthetically or functionality, and I want to support that. There is currently a snap joint on the top rail that can suit an attachment. I uploaded one design of my own as a print profile. But if you want to make one yourself and upload it, there is a file of the rail attachment piece, that you can easily add a model of whatever you want to. Once you are done, you can attach it as a print profile for others to try out! Reward the points to yourself, not me. Miscellaneous: The project unfortunately is too large to be printed with the A1 mini , I promise any dedicated A1 mini users that my next model will be supported by it, I plan to upload it soon in the near future (2-3 weeks if my idea works easily). I would like to thank @luca_dilo for the targets , I used his target print profile for his “Spring Gun V3” and they turned great. Go check him and his models out! These targets were actually my first ever multicolor print. Do not shoot or aim at people, pets, or cowboys without their permission (good luck getting it from your dog) Even though it is a toy, like most toys, it still poses danger to your eyes, so exercise caution. So, I want to improve the process by adding this section here. These are all the potential issues I can think of or have occurred to me in the past 4 months of designing. This is a complicated model so these might not be intuitive. Jams or cannot be loaded The projectile slips out when pushing back or unresponsive trigger Weak/no launching -You inserted the toy bullets in a way where they are angled slightly, and they are getting caught on something. When loading, make sure they get straightly positioned and resting on the elevator wall - The magazine tension is too strong (can also cause angled projectiles) - The loading door is not properly going back (The band is weak or broken) and is getting caught - You are not fully moving the lever into place ← too much tension can cause this - You are attempting to load while there is already a projectile in tension - Loading too quickly or aggressively -The trigger tension is too low and cannot hold the projectile in place while it is tensioned, or it does not have enough strength to go back into place -The trigger insert came out a little bit and the transfer bar is uneven. This can also cause an unresponsive trigger -There is already a projectile hidden improperly inside the barrel. Hold the trigger and shake to drop it out (this happens to me) - Way too much slingshot tension -The strength and number of your bands are the biggest factor, thin bands might not be strong enough to fire. - The bands are rubbing against the sides - You just need to add more, ideally you want 4-5 bands that extend to the furthest hook for maximum acceleration - You are not pulling the lever back into place - There is something hidden in the barrel (this happens to me) Also if you ever encounter any jams, removing the rubber bands on the slingshot easily loosens everything up. Rubber bands breaking: Use thicker rubber bands, I have been using this model consistently and tested it to ensure no breakage. Parts not joining well: Different printers and colors can cause size variation, which is frustrating as a designer, but I have added elements to prevent this. For the best chances to get your parts like mine, print yours in the same color. A P1S is also how I printed mine incase you have one. Original Description ------------------------------------------------------------------------ In the family we have many card games, we like them a lot. Many of these games have their own cases, made of reinforced cardboard or durable plastic. Sometimes, however, the packages are not so good, perhaps they are made of light cardboard and do not have a suitable container to protect the cards. If they then pass into the hands of children, these packages have a short life. I searched a lot among the various designer creations on the web, but often they weren't to my liking or maybe they needed hardware or other accessories to be assembled and I didn't like it. By chance I came across a box that more or less met my needs. The creator, Hugo, whom I thank very much for the work he has done, has made the fusion file with parametric model available. He does not require external accessories for assembly, so no screws, no pieces of filament or no iron wires to cut to size! I downloaded it, made some changes to make it more suitable for my needs (Fillet, Draft etc.), I made a couple of test prints and I realized I had found what I was looking for. It's perfect, my son and my wife approved, so I started creating various boxes of the dimensions we needed, I designed the internal modules to contain the cards and I personalized the lids with the logos of the various games. This one in particular is for the classic UNO game, a game that in my opinion should not be missing from the collection of anyone who loves playing cards. In my profile you will find other customizations and other sizes suitable for the various games we have at home. Good fun ------------------------------------------ In famiglia abbiamo molti giochi di carte, ci piacciono molto. Molti di questi giochi hanno le loro custodie, in cartone rinforzato o in plastica resistente. A volte però le confezioni non sono così valide, magari sono di cartoncino leggero e non hanno un contenitore adatto a proteggere le carte. Se poi passano nelle mani dei bambini queste confezioni hanno vita breve. Ho cercato molto tra le varie creazioni dei designer sul web, ma spesso non erano di mio gradimento o magari avevano bisogno di ferramenta o altri accessori per essere assemblate e la cosa non mi piaceva. Casualmente mi sono imbattuto in una scatola che rispondeva, più o meno, alle mie esigenze. Il creatore, Hugo, che ringrazio tantissimo per il lavoro che ha fatto, ha messo a disposizione il file di fusion con modello parametrico. Non necessita di accessori esterni per l'assemblaggio, quindi niente viti, niente pezzi di filamento o niente fili in ferro da tagliare a misura! L'ho scaricato, ho fatto qualche modifica per renderla più adatta alla mie esigenze (Fillet, Draft ecc..), ho fatto un paio di stampe di test e ho capito di aver trovato quello che cercavo. E' perfetta, mio figlio e mia moglie hanno approvato, così ho iniziato a creare varie scatole delle dimensioni a noi necessarie, ho disegnato i moduli interni per contenere le carte e ho personalizzato i coperchi con i loghi dei vari giochi. Questa in particolare è per il gioco UNO classico, un gioco che secondo me non deve mancare nella collezione di chi ama giocare a carte. Nel mio profilo troverete altre personalizzazioni e altre dimensioni adatte ai vari giochi che abbiamo in casa. Buon divertimento

description: Lubricating oil needs to be added to the rotating parts The prototype of this model is a work by (YY the length). I believe there are some irrational aspects in the prototype. Therefore, I conducted a redesign, and all the new designs are aimed at making printing and usage more convenient. This is not a simple replica, but an optimized parallel version. The following is a description of version differences: *Bearing-free design The bearing-free design is not simply about removing bearings. It requires ingenious design to achieve smooth rotation without bearings. The original version must use specific bearings. *Completely unsupported Completely unsupported is not simply a matter of changing the position of the model, but rather a redesign of the structure. The original version uses a lot of support. *The main structure is integrally printed and molded To reduce assembly difficulty and achieve an integrated main structure, various details need to be considered, necessitating a redesign of the structure. The original parts cannot be printed as a single unit, but are all separate, making assembly challenging. *The shell is intact, with the elastic band concealed A complete spherical shape also requires precise design, and it cannot be achieved simply by making some changes. The rubber band is hidden inside, making the shell more intact. The original version has its internal structure exposed. * Add angle limit to the interior of the rotating shaft A limit stop is incorporated inside the rotating shaft to maintain a consistent angle when pressed. The original version has no limit on the rotation axis, and it rotates randomly when pressed. *Gear cover with concealed buckle locking The gear cover features a concealed buckle design, which locks with a single press. The original version is complex to install, requiring materials to be inserted and fixed. Due to printing tolerances, it is sometimes difficult to insert them. * The innovative addition of a ring buckle allows for more playful ways to use it, and it can even be rotated without the need for a rubber band (completely without any additional accessories) The original version does not have this function *Introducing a smaller version with a diameter of 5cm. description: Oracle Red Bull Racing F1 – Fully 3D Printed 400% Scale Massive Build 🏎️🔥 This project is a fully 3D printed, massive 400% scaled-up version of the iconic Oracle Red Bull Racing Formula 1 car. Modeled carefully after the famous building blocks Speed Champions set, this model has been entirely optimized, engineered, and recreated from scratch for large-scale desktop 3D printing. Every single component is custom-printed, resulting in a colossal, highly detailed engineering masterpiece with approximately 250+ individual parts. Scaled up to a giant 400%, the finished model completely transforms the classic building block experience into a dominant display piece with an incredible shelf presence. Features ✨ Speed Champions Inspired: Modeled directly after the beloved, famous building blocks scale to bring that classic nostalgic build style to a massive format. 1:1 Decal Accuracy: Every single original decal and sponsor logo has been meticulously replicated and integrated into the parts for an authentic racing look. True-to-Life Textures: Reengineered down to the finest details, including the flexible, bendable halo safety ring and the specialized texture for the rubbery-grip racing tires. Massive 400% Scale Build: A giant, head-turning model that looks incredible on any desk, shelf, or workshop table. Fully 3D Printed Construction: Around 250+ individual parts engineered to lock together beautifully. AMS Compatible Design: Fully optimized for multi-material and multi-color printing—all major racing logos are ready to print straight from your AMS without any painting required! No Extraneous Hardware: No screws, magnets, or metal rods required for assembly. Printing Information 🖨️ A1 Standard Ready: The entire project has been thoughtfully sliced and oriented to fit perfectly on a standard Bambu Lab A1 or X1/P1 series build volume (256x256x256 mm). Smart Splicing: For the main large body piece that exceeds standard build plates at 400% scale, the model has been cleanly sliced in half with high-tolerance alignment pins for seamless reassembly. No massive XL printer required! Material: The main model is optimized for PLA filament. For the authentic flexible halo piece, printing in TPU 95A is highly recommended! Settings: 3 walls/perimeters are highly recommended to give the scaled-up connection pins maximum structural rigidity. Use a 10% Gyroid infill for the best balance of strength and material saving. Pre-Configured 3MF: A fully optimized 3MF file is included, cleanly grouping parts onto plates by color to minimize waste and maximize printing efficiency. Organization: Because this build contains over 250 components, sorting your printed parts by assembly sections as they come off the bed is highly recommended to make the process completely seamless. Assembly 🔧 Despite the high part count, the assembly process is extremely satisfying and rewarding. Watching hundreds of individually printed pieces slowly click together into a complete, giant F1 racer creates a genuinely unique building experience. Use original instructions from the smaller set to assemble! Assembly Difficulty: Medium Estimated Assembly Time: ~1.5 to 2 hours Pro-Tip: While the parts fit together with high mechanical tolerances, glue is recommended (I recommend Kraftprotz 3D Printing Glue) on key structural parts to ensure your massive model remains entirely rigid when handled or displayed. Important Notes ⚠️ This is a large-scale, multi-part engineering project. Printer tolerances can vary. Use XY compensation to get tighter or looser fitting pieces if need be. Proper printer calibration is recommended to ensure seamless brick-to-brick tolerances. Ensure your filament is dry to minimize stringing on fine logo details.

description: I am happy to present the “Infinity Infill Cube” , my very own version of the famous fidget combining my take on the hinge mechanism while showcasing 16 different infills with accompanying text . This model is simply a must to have next to your printer, as an infill display while also being the most popular and fun fidget . Overall, this model turned out way better than I expected and I could not be happier to share it with you all! Membership If you want to sell this model you can do so by joining the Membership for a commercial licence. The Model I started by making my own version of the Infinity Cube Fidget mechanism, trying to minimize the size of the hinges . For printability, the model contains a number of support “points” which makes the model printable. This results in some minor trimming being required after printing. Similarly, some “brim” structures are included in the print profiles, to minimize issues for people with bed adhesion issues. After making my own version of the Infinity Cube , I continued all work within Bambu slicer . Here I added 16 different “infills” to be shown within the fidget. In addition, the name of each “infill” was also added to the fidget. While I set out to make a multicolour version of this fidget (which looks great), I really ended up liking the single colour version the most. If you do not have a multi-nozzle printer, I really recommend printing the single colour version . Compared to most fidgets of this design , this model generates a heavy 50g fidget which takes a while to print (with my profiles). The weight was a result of the design choices, but I really think the “Infinity cube” feels better in the hands when heavy . While I provide a number of print profiles for the “Infinity Infill Fidget”, I can only provide a single .STL file of the “Base” Infinity Cube model. The model showcases 16 different infills available in Bambu Slicer: Gyroid - 15% Concentric - 40% Archimedes Chords - 40% Hilbert Curves - 30% 3D Honeycomb - 15% Honeycomb - 20% Octagram Spiral - 30% 2D Lattice - 15% Aligned Rectilinear - 30% Tri-Hexagon - 30% Cross Hatch - 20% Cubic - 30% Zig Zag - 25% Grid - 30% Adaptive Cubic - 30% Triangles - 30% Printing As all Infinity Cubes, this one might be a little demanding to print . That being said, I have had no issues at all. I expect that poor bed adhesion will be an issue, and have for this reason slowed down the first layer of the print profiles. I recommend printing the single colour version as the text looks the best in this version (in my opinion). If you have a printer with multiple nozzles , the multicolour prints are nice, although I which I could have made the font larger. If you decide to print the multicolour versions with a single nozzle, I have also added a print profile (Multicolour profile - Plate 3) which includes a second “Infinity Cube” used as a purge object (giving you 2 fidgets for the price of 1). Post-processing As with all versions of this fidget, playing around with it will make it move more smoothly . In addition, I would recommend some trimming with a sharp blade . In particular, the 4 brim structures needs to be removed . In addition, some trimming of the many minor support structures will make it both look and feel nicer. Overall, compared to other similar models I have printed, this one is relatively loose and smooth to move . Overall, I am just so happy with how this turned out! I am really looking forward to see photos of your colour combinations and hope you will enjoy this print as much as I have! If you make changes to the infills, I also look forward to additional print profiles !! description: Nosk is a terrifying shape-shifting spider creature from Hollow Knight, faithfully recreated as a detailed 3D printed figure capturing its iconic spider body, long curved legs, and the haunting false mask dangling from its chest. Its intricate details, from the flowing mane to the glowing red accents that make Nosk one of the most unsettling bosses in Hallownest… and… it glows oO I also realized I did not print out and attach the front arms before making the cover photo… sigh . After you print them, get some hot water (per instructions below) dip the end of the leg to soften and place where and how the arms should face. Then after it hardens, dip again in glue and secure it. INSTRUCTIONS This is an annoying one, but if you ever assembled my models; you know you are in for some frustration and glue on your fingers :D Print everything out, and assemble the legs. Remember if you are using superglue, very tiny amounts are needed to join the legs together. The legs come in two variations, with a cable run to pass a wire for the inner glow, and solid. The cable ones are much much more annoying to glue. The cable must be ultra fine, since you only have 4mm of space. I used aRGB and a addresable LED controller for mine (more details an pics to follow) once done, glue the torso together, inserting the orange belly. Try your best to keep it as aligned as possible. Later insert the legs and spines. If legs dont seem to fit, or the legs are not all aligned to the floor DO NOT PANIC! For this one, hot water, hair dryer or a blowtorch lighter is a must. Soften the plastic a bit and insert it to get the correct shape or bend the leg so it is flat to the ground. The holes were designed to be symmetrical, but after gluing, they are not going to be.. and thats fine, Nosk is weird, so heat it and bend his legs any way you want to make it unique (its a feature!) Any issues, shoot me a comment.

description: ⛴️ Deep Regrets and Even Deeper Regrets (expansion) insert / organizer This is an insert / organizer for the wicked fishing board game “Deep Regrets" (2025) and the expansion "Even Deeper Regrets" (2026) . It will also hold Kickstarter promo cards and the “Lamentable Tentacles” (2025) mini-expansion . 🪝Main features Supports sleeved cards No lid lift No supports needed (one part has a smallish support prompted by Bambu Studio but it could be turned off safely) Highly decorative yet functional parts that double for storage and enhance gameplay at the same time (check photos!) Some organizers out there put everything in the main box, but my design philosophy behind this model was to fit the game art and ideas. The inner boxes have beautiful art too, so I didn't want to neglect the expansion box either. Having a little more box estate space, I decided to have my insert function as in-game accessories too. The trays for the port cards resemble fish crates; the dink card holders are little anchovy / sardine cans! The regrets card holder can be opened and assembled to function as both draw tray and discard pile holder. The shoal trays feature portholes when you reach the bottom of a shoal deck, and so on… 🏗️ Print & assembly instructions You will need to glue portholes to the shoal/river trays. This is easy. I tried a multicolor approach on the same model but I noticed some quality issue since the bottom of the tray and the portholes are very thin. Printing the two pieces as separate models turned out much cleaner and better. I have used a brush-applied superglue to glue the pieces together and if done with just a little patience you won't be able to tell that the two were separate pieces. I highly recommend to print the portholes and the dink trays in some metal-like filament. I used Bambu Lab Basic PLA Brass for the portholes and Iridium Gold for the dink trays. For the latter you can probably use a silk filament with an aluminum finish as well. For these parts specifically I also recommend using ironing, but it's optional (I have set mine to 60mm/s and 30% for the metal PLA, but your settings may differ). Optional rubber or felt feet can be applied at the bottom of the pieces that go on the game board. At the bottom of the trays (river, shoal, loch) you'll notice some smallish hole/marks: I have put those as reference marks in case you decide to add rubber/foam feet to those models so they don't slide on the board. They're entirely optional. 🖌️ Optional weathering suggestions In the photos I published in the gallery you may notice that I decided to weather some of the models: this is entirely optional, but the components of this insert really lend themselves to this kind of treatment. If you want to try the same route, you can use some washes and other grime/mold effects as you like. The port crates feature some holes that can pass through a small rope (2-3mm thick: I have used 2.5) to create handles: these are non-functional and merely decorative but they're really a fun feature that's really easy to add. You will be able to store the trays normally even with these small appendages on. 📦 Packing instructions Check the images for visual references. Main box Place the 4 ship trays for the shoals and the river filled with cards as per game setup instructions (typically 13 per shoal slot and all, evenly distributed, for river slots): you'll shuffle these at every game together with the other cards that go in the other box but this separation is intended to optimize space. Design Story This project began as a challenge to create my own version of a sliding fidget from scratch. The first design used 20 sections. After receiving feedback asking for a higher piece count, I tested several new versions and adjusted the spacing, clearances, wall thickness, and internal rail. A 35-piece version was also tested, but the smaller sections did not hold onto the guide as reliably as I wanted. After more redesigning, 32 pieces gave the best balance of movement, strength, size, and printability. The final version uses a mostly concealed guide and catcher system so the outside stays clean while the mechanism remains secure. Features 32 moving sections Twisting sliding motion Internal guide and catcher system Print-in-place construction Designed for FDM printers No supports required Refined clearances to reduce fusing Rounded outer profile Printing Notes This model uses small moving gaps, so printer calibration is important. Avoid an overly compressed first layer, since excess elephant foot may join the sections together. Recommended Settings 0.16 mm layer height for the first print 0.12 mm layer height for finer surface detail Supports off Brim off Arachne wall generator recommended PLA or PLA+ recommended Check the sliced Preview to confirm that the moving gaps remain open TwistCore went through multiple prototypes, failed ideas, and geometry changes before reaching this version. It is the most complete and reliable design I have made from this concept so far.

description: A warm and cozy country loaf, fresh from the bakery! 🥖 Clicky Bread – Country Bread is a cute fidget toy inspired by rustic handmade bread. The round and hearty country loaf rests inside a tiny proofing basket with a soft liner, creating a warm miniature bakery scene. Warm and Rustic Country Bread Design The bread features a round and hearty shape inspired by traditional European-style country loaves. Its natural scoring pattern and slightly irregular surface give it a warm handmade bakery feel while keeping the design cute and easy to recognize. Proofing Basket-Inspired Base The base is inspired by a traditional proofing basket , also known as a banneton . These baskets are commonly used to support and shape bread dough during its final rise. For this model, the proofing basket has been reimagined as a cute miniature display base for the finished bread. The distinctive circular ridges around the basket also give the model an artisan bakery look. Separate Proofing Basket Liner The proofing basket liner is a separate part and can be printed in a different color from the basket. Assembly Install the mechanical keyboard switch into the proofing basket. Place the proofing basket liner in the correct position. Connect the country bread to the switch. Press the bread several times to make sure it moves smoothly and returns properly. For the keychain version, attach your own keychain hardware to the connection point. Super Leggiero is the first aircraft in the Ultralight Series , designed around the principles of minimum weight, efficient aerodynamics, and slow, floaty flight . With its ultralow wing loading and optimized airframe, it delivers long, graceful glides in indoor environments and calm, no-wind conditions. The Ultralight Series also introduces an expert hybrid construction technique , where the frame of the plane is printed directly onto lightweight tissue paper. This reduces the flying weight from 9 g to just 5 g —a 45% weight reduction —resulting in even slower flight, lower sink rate, and exceptional indoor performance. While the standard version is designed for simplicity and easy assembly, the hybrid version offers experienced builders the opportunity to explore the limits of ultralight 3D printed aircraft. Complete Lineup Ultralight Series Super Leggiero - 9 g Experimental Series Canard Glider — Experimental Series #1 Gossamer Albatross Glider — Experimental Series #2 Sky Series Cumulus 680 — slow, smooth, relaxed glides Cumulus 400 Speed Wing — faster flights Stratus 500 — balanced and versatile Stratus 500 A1 mini version - Original size Assembly guide: Camber bracket: Insert the front pin of the camber bracket into the fuselage. Insert the rear pin by bending the camber bracket into an S-shape . Then slide the rear pin into the fuselage. (See assembly video.) Make sure the camber bracket sits securely between the locating tabs on the wing. Vertical Stabilizer : Insert vertical stabilizer pins into the slots (1).Bend the locking tabs as shown to secure the stabilizer. (2) Polyhedral Wing bend: Bend both wingtips upward along the reinforced bend lines. Flying tips: Note that the plane is suited for NO wind or indoor conditions only Avoid throwing the glider too hard. If launched too fast, it will pitch up and stall . Instead, give it a gentle push and try to match the glider's natural flying speed. Launch the glider at a slight downward angle . This helps maintain speed and results in a smoother glide. Finetune the pitch by adjusting the elevator control surfaces. If the glider pitches up or stalls: add more down elevator . If the glider dives: add more up elevator . Enjoy your flights! 😊 Expert guide for Tissue Paper Hybrid Edition Note: This version requires patience and experience. It is recommended for advanced 3D printing users. 1. Prepare the paper Cut a sheet of tissue paper slightly larger than the print area. 2. Secure the paper Attach the paper to the build plate using magnets. I use Ø20 × 3 mm neodymium magnets from the Bambu Lab store. Make sure the paper is smooth and wrinkle-free. 3. Check magnet placement Before printing, verify that all magnets are outside the print path . 4. Print settings Disable Bed Leveling . Ignore the warning pop-ups. If possible, set Auxiliary Part Cooling to 0% . Excessive airflow can cause the tissue paper to flutter, reducing print quality. 6. Cut out the glider Use a sharp hobby knife and cut in the direction shown in the illustrations for the cleanest result. 7. Assemble Follow the standard assembly instructions. The tissue paper version is extremely delicate , so handle it carefully. 8. Fly! Congratulations—you've just built one of the lightest and best-flying printable gliders on Maker World. Enjoy! ✈️

description: Personalized name puzzle with big chunky letters and a matching pocket board or open tray. Type any name, pick letter size and thickness, print the board and letters in different colors. A classic first-birthday and toddler gift. Turn any name into a chunky letter puzzle. Type the name, choose the board style, and the model generates a matching board with letter-shaped pockets plus a full set of thick, rounded, easy-to-grip letters. Features: - Any name or short word up to 14 characters (spaces allowed). - Proportional letter layout: narrow letters like I sit close, wide letters like W get the room they need. Pockets always match the letters. - Two board styles: pocket board (a recess for every letter) or open tray (rimmed board the letters lie inside). - Chunky rounded letters: adjustable size (25-60 mm), thickness (8-25 mm), and outline rounding for that classic soft toy-letter look. - Adjustable fit clearance so pieces lift out easily without being sloppy. - Letters stand well proud of the board so small hands can grab them. - Both parts print flat with no supports. Print the board in one color and the letters in one or more colors for the classic pastel look - no AMS required, just print the letter plate in your second color (or print letters one at a time in different colors). The model reports the exact board size in the console. Long names make long boards: at the default 40 mm letters, names up to about 6 letters fit a 256 mm bed. For longer names, reduce letter_size or print the letters without the board. Child safety: this is a decorative/keepsake print. FDM prints can crack into small parts under abuse. Not recommended as an unsupervised toy for children under 3 years; always supervise young children. Print letters large (40 mm or bigger), use plenty of walls, and inspect prints regularly for damage. ## Customization Notes - name: the name or word (UPPERCASE looks best and prints strongest). - font_name: keep the default Liberation Sans Bold for guaranteed spacing. Other bold sans-serif fonts work (pockets always match the letters), but letter spacing is tuned to the default font - after changing it, check the preview to confirm neighbouring letters do not touch, and avoid thin or decorative fonts. - letter_size: glyph height in mm. 40 mm default is a good toddler size. - letter_thickness: how tall the pieces are. Default 15 mm; the pieces stand about 9 mm proud of the board pockets. - letter_rounding: fattens and rounds the letter outlines for a chunkier look. - letter_gap: space between letters; the model enforces a minimum so pockets never merge. - board_style: "pocket" cuts a recess per letter, "tray" makes one open rimmed recess. - fit_clearance: gap between letter and pocket. 0.5 mm default suits most printers; increase if pieces fit too tight. - part: print "board" and "letters" separately for two-color puzzles, or "all" for everything on one plate. "fit_preview" is preview-only - do not print it.

It was developed to evaluate how well ASAHI's EGO System androids could adapt to Earth's harsh environment, while also field-testing the company's first military-spec body, which had never before entered mass production or combat service. Rather than functioning as a conventional AI, the EGO System grants the android a highly developed sense of self-identity, enabling behavior and decision-making much closer to that of a human. In the X-AD-0, the system is specifically configured with one purpose: "Explore human buildings and living spaces from a human perspective—and survive." Il modello è composto da singoli pezzi che si incastrano tra loro in modo semplice e intuitivo. Una volta assemblata, la volpe si sostiene anche in piedi, diventando sia un piccolo puzzle educativo che un simpatico personaggio decorativo. È ideale per bambini, attività creative, giochi educativi, camerette, scuole, asili o semplicemente per chi ama stampare piccoli oggetti colorati e divertenti. Anche il riempimento/infill può essere aumentato per rendere i pezzi più robusti e resistenti, soprattutto se il puzzle viene utilizzato spesso. Con un infill più basso, invece, si ottiene una stampa più veloce e leggera. It's quicker, safer, and easier! 🌞 ⚠️ WARNING!⚠️ Parts can break off prematurely while removing the card from the build plate unless you take a few simple and easy steps first. Use a freshly cleaned textured build plate . Let it cool completely first , then slowly and carefully flex the plate. The card should pop off easily if it hasn't already self-released. Flush cutters or scissors highly recommended to remove parts from card. Don't want to use tools? Print as separate pieces instead. Troubles? Please see any of my other kit card models for tips and tricks. Why not here? The tree that's pictured in the instructions is from “ A Complete Guide to Heraldry ." This book of heraldic designs by Arthur Charles Fox-Davies was published in 1909 and was illustrated by Graham “ Herald Painter to the Lyon Court ” Johnston. description: Floating Hull Upgrade for Cargo Ship Set 60422 This model is a 3D printed replacement/upgrade hull designed for the cargo ship from set 60422. Before printing the full hull, I strongly recommend printing the calibration plate available in the print profiles. The calibration file contains five 4x4 test plates with different stud diameters. This 3D-printed toy key lock showcases the internal mechanics of a simple key lock. You could use it as a prop, novelty items or a interactive children's toy. The circular housing shows a core comprised entirely of matching plastic components. The lock features a guide for a physical key, a latch to secure the shackle, and a compliant zig-zag plastic spring that gives the shackle tension, a spring bar for the latch that gives it the necessary mechanical tension to hold the latch against the shackle cutout. In Collaboration with another maker we have a key and bitway for the lock. Go here to obtain the key and bitway. https://makerworld.com/en/models/3048389-working-old-fashioned-fantasy-key#profileId-3428902 The Lock parts are shown below Then you will install the following 3d printed parts to the base Lock Shackle is placed into the lock with the latch cutout to the left like shown. You will need to add the retainer ring and glue it on. Retainer ring for the Shackle. It is placed on the end of the shackle after you slide the shackle into the base collar provided. The retaining ring will need to be glued onto the end of the shackle. Don't be sloppy with the glue, Be careful not to get glue on the shaft of the shackle and accidently glue it to the collar in the base. One tiny drop will due. This retaining ring keeps the shackle permanently locked into the lock base. The Latch mechanism slides in from the right hand side of the latch holder. It has a keyway that it must slide into. HINT: Take a Crayon and color both sides of the latch to lubricate and help it slide better while in the latch holder, work it back and forth a few times. The compliant spring. Drop it into the channel provided in the base making sure it is placed in the orientation shown. I find a spring printed with PLA makes a better spring. Depending on what spring tension you prefer you could print the 5 loop version to give a more solid lock open The Latch spring is placed in its holder with the top end placed behind the latch to give it return tension. If you like you could add a small drop of glue to the latch spring holder clip or print the Latch spring ever so slightly thicker to make a tight fit. If you plan to use one key per lock then you could glue the bitway into its holder. The Bitway is cut in such a way to only allow its corresponding key to work in the lock. Check pictures. Now add the lid and snap it together. Take note of the keyway at the top of the lid and lock body. Match them up and snap it shut. description: STAX is a two-player abstract strategy game. Fast to learn, deep to master. Two colours of spheres, one rising board, and a single goal: line up your colour before your opponent does. Elegant on the table, ruthless in play. ⚙️ Setup Each player takes 15 spheres of one colour (30 total) and keeps them in the moat running around the board. The playing field is a 4×4 diamond of shallow cradles. Decide who goes first, that's the whole setup. 🎯 How to play Players alternate turns, placing one sphere at a time. On your turn you may either drop a sphere into any empty cradle on the base, or nest a sphere on top of a completed 2×2 block of four (any colour mix) to begin a higher level. Every new sphere settles into the hollow between the four below it, so the structure naturally climbs: 4×4 base → 3×3 → 2×2 → a single peak. 🏆 How to win Be first to complete a line of your own color on one level: 🔹 four in a row on the base (row, column or diagonal) 🔹 three in a row on the 3×3 level 🔹 all four spheres of any 2×2 level Lines only count at the same height — a vertical stack does not win. ⛰️ Reaching the peak The full pyramid is exactly 30 spheres the same as your total supply. If it's built all the way up with no colour line, the winner is decided at the top: the majority colour of the 2×2 level below the peak places the final sphere and wins. (A 2–2 split at the top is a rare draw.) 🧠 Make your strategy Every sphere you place can become a step your opponent climbs on, so building upward is as dangerous as it is powerful. Winning is about seeing one move ahead and completing your own line while quietly blocking the one your opponent is building. 🖨️ Printing notes The spheres print in two halves and snap together for a clean, seamless finish, no supports needed. Print 15 in each of two contrasting colours (the metallic silver and speckled grey pairing looks fantastic). Board and moat print as one piece.
