description: 此模型是一个H2D/H2S/H2C上盖玻璃增高架，可增高27mm，侧边IKEA Skadis洞洞板，也能有效防止料管摩擦上盖玻璃。 特点： 两盘打印，打印时长10H，耗材使用量（PETG 465g）、（ABS 385g）。 27mm增高高度，完美避免料管摩擦上盖玻璃。 两侧单排Skadis尺寸洞洞板，通用的附件可快速拆装。 榫卯组装结构，组装快速牢固。 H2D原机尺寸测量，完美兼容H2系列机型。 打印注意事项： 打印测试机型为H2D，耗材类型为Bambu PETG，打印参数为0.2mm层高默认参数，12%填充。 为兼容多材料打印成功率，在PETG打印后留有细微间隙，并使用Bambu ABS默认参数进行打印测试，玻璃盖板稍紧但可正常使用。 请在打印之后，静待1-2小时后取下，以免快速冷却产生形变。 经过长期测试，PETG材质打印的增高架可在打印高温材料时正常使用。 IKEA Skadis拓展： 兼容IKEA Skadis洞洞板配件，可拓展性强。 孔洞不与内部连通，不影响仓温。 配件列表： 官方刮刀支架 官方胶水支架 50*50*80、80*115*65、80*155*65收纳盒 打印版清洁器支架 TPU进料辅助器支架 进气格栅预留： 预留进气格栅活动空间，不影响开合。 螺丝位预留： 保留与原机相同的螺丝位，使打玻璃盖板与增高架不干涉。 盖板磁铁位预留： 预留玻璃盖板上磁铁位置，使玻璃盖板能完全平放在增高架上。 开盖检测传感器： H2系列打印机具有玻璃盖板开盖检测，原理为霍尔感应。 在与玻璃盖板相同的位置预留磁铁槽位，使用一颗8x3mm并用胶水粘上即可使打印机不提示开盖，磁铁凸起为正常。 如您安装磁铁后还是会出现提示，也可以在传感器位置用胶带将磁铁粘上。 组装方法： 按照对应图案摆放至打印机顶部。 使用榫卯卡连接，并按压到底。 盖上玻璃盖板测试是否安装正确。 如有需要可使用EVA胶带达到原机使用效果。 经过测试张贴泡绵胶带可大大提高稳定性与摩擦力，同时能消除附件矿量，玻璃盖螺丝预留位置也可直接覆盖泡绵。 顶面可选用泡绵胶带增强密封与摩擦力（宽度40mm，厚度1mm），按照尺寸进行裁切。 裁切宽度分别为40mm/30mm/15mm。 购买链接： 淘宝链接 、 AliExpress链接 （40mm宽*1mm厚） 泡绵胶带为非必要，您不是用它也可以获得高质量的增高架。 2026.6.27修改：修改磁铁孔位为8mm，深度1.5mm，减少因位移导致的开盖检测提示，也可直接将磁铁贴在传感器上彻底杜绝。

model_name: X2D Top Glass Lid Riser for External Filtration
description: Bambu Lab X2D Top Glass Lid Riser – External Filtration Solution The X2D Glass Lid Riser is designed to lift the printer's glass lid, creating additional internal clearance that improves airflow. When paired with external ventilation or filtration systems, the riser supports more effective air movement by taking advantage of the natural air circulation . This makes it especially useful when printing engineering materials such as ABS or ASA, where controlled airflow and fume management are important. Beyond airflow improvements, the increased clearance also helps reduce friction between the PTFE tube and the glass lid and minimize long-term wear on both components. Installation is completely tool-free and follows the same simple setup process as our P2S glass lid riser, making it quick and easy to install or remove whenever needed. Installation Guide 1) Connect the frame pieces: Use the dovetail connectors to join each part together. Make sure all joints are fully seated and aligned for a secure fit. 2) Install the front covers: Slide the covers into the designated slots on the frame. By default, the covers with editable text should be installed on the front side. The vent port can be installed on either the front-left or front-right side. 3) Final check: Once all parts are assembled and in place, your X2D Glass Lid Riser should look like the finished setup shown. Ensure everything is properly seated and stable before use.

description: AMS HT Side Mount für Bambu Lab H2 Serie Diese Halterung ermöglicht es, das AMS HT seitlich am oberen Rahmen eines Druckers der H2-Serie zu befestigen. Dadurch kann TPU direkt über die Bypass-Öffnung des AMS HT zum Druckkopf geführt werden. Der große Vorteil dieser Positionierung ist der extrem kurze und nahezu geradlinige Filamentweg. Das reduziert den Wiederstand beim fördern des Filaments auf ein Minimum und verbessert insbesondere den Druck mit sehr weichen TPU-Filamenten, die empfindlich auf lange oder stark gekrümmte Filamentwege reagieren. Zusätzlich kann das AMS HT während des Drucks weiterhin als Filamenttrockner genutzt werden. So bleibt das TPU während des gesamten Druckvorgangs trocken, was die Druckqualität zusätzlich verbessert. Einfache Konstruktion Die Halterung besteht aus drei Steckteilen, die ohne Schrauben oder weiteres Montagematerial zusammengesteckt werden. Diese Bauweise bietet mehrere Vorteile: Sehr einfacher und zuverlässiger Druck. Nur eines der drei Bauteile benötigt eine winzige Stützstruktur. Die Halterung lässt sich jederzeit wieder zerlegen und dadurch besonders platzsparend verstauen. Hinweis: Je nach verwendeten Material und Kalibrierung des Druckers und Filament, kann es sein, dass die Steckverbindung schwergängig ist. Versuche nicht die Teile mit Gewalt zusammen zu stecken! In diesen Fall ist es hilfreich die Steckverbinder mit etwas Schlafpapier nach zu arbeiten. Etwas Gleitmittel wie Balistol oder WD40 kann ebenfalls helfen. Einfache Montage Für die Montage muss lediglich der Glasdeckel des Druckers entfernt werden. Anschließend wird die Halterung einfach über den oberen Rand des Druckers gesteckt. Das AMS HT wird danach nur auf der Halterung abgestellt - ganz ohne zusätzliche Befestigung. CUSTOMIZABLE DIY FILAMENT/BOOK SHELF SEVERAL RISER OPTIONS CUSTOMIZE TO FIT YOUR SPACE NOTE: REQUIRES SOME WORK WITH WOOD As part of my new print room, I designed this DIY shelf system to maximize the space I had available for my filament storage dry boxes and keep them organized. At the same time l wanted something truly unique and nice to look at. I decided to share it here in case others want to try it themselves. Please read all of the information and the attached instructions before starting. Overall, it may not be a huge cost savings compared to an Ikea or other purchasable bookshelf (though the larger it is the more it will save), but being able to make it the exact length and height you want is not possible with those options. Plus, the looks of this are so much better IMO. The riser options include: Diamondplate Pattern Lattice Pattern Square & Compass Vertical Bolts (these are only recommended for middle risers) FYI If you are interested in the filament labels or drybox kits shown in the pictures, you can find them here: https://makerworld.com/en/models/1193463-filament-labels-with-logos https://makerworld.com/en/models/2561229-4l-dry-box-kit-for-outer-spool-desiccant-trays ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ PURCHASED PARTS SHELVES The shelves themselves are made of ¾” wood and the risers are designed to fit a shelf depth of 234mm (9-3/8”). Your shelf length will be whatever length you want for your needs (more on that in the instructions below). This means you can source the shelving a number of different ways. Buy standard ¾” shelf boards and trim them to size. The ends are covered and the back not visible so you could get them pre-finished if you can make clean cuts. Buy a ¾” MDF sheet and cut or have the hardware store cut to the correct depth and whatever length you decide, then paint as needed. This is the option I chose. Buy a ¾” plywood sheet and cut or have the hardware store cut to the correct depth and whatever length you decide. Then you would need to add edging to the front edge to cover the layer lines before painting. HARDWARE Threaded wood inserts – ¼” or M6 x ¾” or 20mm (9) Inserts are required PER SHELF I used these: https://a.co/d/0hchaaFy Flattened or Button Head Screws – ¼”x1-1/2” or M6x35 (18) screws per intermediate shelf, (9) screws per top and bottom shelf I used these: https://a.co/d/00rvAgmG IF you are going to use the Square and Compass Risers, you will also need (4) M5 heat press inserts (any length up to 12mm max) and (4) M5x20mm Socket Head Screws PER RISER to connect the pieces together. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- PRINTED PARTS You will need the following printed parts from the print profile of your choice: RISERS – Selection and quantity are up to you. Generally, you will need 2 risers per shelf and if you feel it needs a middle riser. Bolt Risers are only recommended as a middle riser and require 3 per riser. Square and Compass Risers include 3 pieces per riser that need assembled – main riser, top, and bottom. RISER CONNECTORS – These slide onto the shelf and connect to the risers. You will need 2 side connectors (and 1 middle connector if you chose a middle riser) per shelf. The top shelf has special Top Riser Connectors. Bolt Risers do not need any Riser Connectors but are only recommended as a middle riser. BOLT SPACERS – These get bolted to the shelves to interconnect the risers and riser connectors. You will need the same quantity as the screws – 18 per intermediate shelf, 9 per top and bottom shelf. FEET - You can attach any feet of your liking to the bottom using the ¼" threaded holes. The ones in the picture which I recommend I had previously released here: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2498728-hd-adjustable-leveling-foot Now let’s talk about print orientation. There are 2 print profiles – one with the risers and connectors oriented flat on the bed, and one with risers and connectors oriented vertically. Depending on your filament of choice, printing orientation will change how the color looks. Square & Compass Risers and Bolt Risers must be printed vertically unless you are willing to get creative with supports. Vertical printing creates a higher resolution but is much more challenging to print. The hardest part with vertical printing is the Riser Connectors because the opening for the shelf requires supports. You can use a special support material but this adds layer time which can cause a “benchy hull” line from the big difference in layer time. Not using special support material (like I didn’t) creates a rough interface. Not too big of a deal since it is sitting flat against the shelf, but I had to make little trim pieces to cover the exposed outer edge. Those are included if you need them. If you like the look or the filament color doesn't change, another option would be to print the risers vertically and the connectors flat. This would be kind of the “best of both worlds”. I chose a shiny filament, so orientation made a big difference in the color. Here is a comparison of the two print orientations: ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- FILAMENT SELECTION The majority of the loading is in compression (buckling) so material requirements aren’t too bad. I recommend a MINIMUM of a PLA+ that has decent impact strength. A good Tough PLA+ like the one Bambu has, Sunlu’s PLA+ 2.0, or Polymaker Polylite PLA PRO would be decent options. I would avoid basic matte or silk PLA’s as their brittleness and layer adhesion may not make it appropriate. PETG will generally hold up a little better but is more difficult to print. I chose Tinmorry Space Grey Metallic PETG because it gave me a nice “steel” look and I printed vertically. Seams and retraction were a big challenge however and took me a couple tries. I have attached the assembly instruction and basic assembly dimensions. Length is based on the one I built and fit the dry boxes shown in the pictures perfectly, but you can adjust to the length you want for your needs. Thank you and if you decide to do this project, I hope you enjoy it as much as I did.

PTFE Clips Helps prevent PTFE tubes from rubbing against the top glass These lightweight PTFE tube clips are designed to help keep the tubing from wearing on the upper glass panel on enclosed Bambu Lab printers. They have been tested on the Bambu Lab X2D and are designed for standard 4 mm PTFE tubing , so they may also fit other compatible Bambu Lab models. Why I designed them As the toolhead moves around the printer, the PTFE tubes naturally twist, bend and change position. Some tube-management solutions hold multiple tubes tightly together to create a neater appearance. While this may look tidy, it can also introduce unnecessary tension, stress or twisting into the tubing as the toolhead travels. These clips are designed to support each tube individually. This helps reduce wear on the PTFE tubes from the top glass while still allowing the tubes to move as designed. Key features Helps prevent PTFE wear from rubbing on the top glass Designed for standard 4 mm PTFE tubing Tested on the Bambu Lab X2D Allows each tube to move independently Applies only light tension to the tubing Lightweight and low profile Quick snap-on installation No tools or printer modifications required Small and fast to print How many should I use? I currently use four clips , which provides good support and separation. More clips can be installed if additional support is required, but avoid using so many that the tubing becomes stiff or restricted. Recommended print settings These were successfully printed using: Layer height: 0.16 mm Walls/perimeters: 3 Bed temperature: 60°C Part cooling fan: 0% for the first 2 - 3 layers, then a maximum of 25% Brim: Not required Supports: Not required Keeping the cooling fan low helps prevent these small parts from cooling too quickly, warping or lifting from the build plate. Material recommendations PLA is suitable for normal use where the heated chamber is not being used. For printers operating with a heated chamber, use a more temperature-resistant material such as: PETG ABS ASA Another suitable heat-resistant filament PLA may soften or deform when exposed to elevated chamber temperatures for extended periods. Installation Carefully snap each clip over a PTFE tube. Position the clips along the tubing where support is required. Move the toolhead through its full range of travel. Check that each tube can still bend and move freely. Reposition or remove clips if any tension or restriction is present. Important notes These clips are intended to gently guide the PTFE tubes, not lock them rigidly in place. After installation, confirm that: The tubes still move freely The clips do not contact the cable chain The tubing is not stretched, kinked or twisted The toolhead can reach the full build area The clips remain clear of all moving components Compatibility Tested on: Bambu Lab X2D Tube size: 4 mm PTFE Other models may be compatible but have not yet been tested Support the design

model_name: Silika Gel Behälter - ideal für Vakuumbeutel
description: Hallo Druckfreunde! Heute teile ich meine Silika Gel Box für Vakuumbeutel . Feuchtigkeit ist ja bekanntlich der größte Feind von perfektem 3D-Druck. Warum dieses Design den Unterschied macht: Smarte Slicer-Optimierung: Die Wände dieses Behälters werden flach liegend gedruckt. Das sorgt für einen schnellen, stabilen und druckerschonenden Druckprozess. Funktionales Gyroid-Infill: Durch das Weglassen von Deck- und Bodenschichten wird das Gyroid-Infill als hochfunktionale Außenhaut genutzt. Das Ergebnis: Eine perfekte 360°-Durchlüftung für die Silikakugeln, ohne dass diese herausfallen. Visuelle Feuchtigkeitskontrolle auf einen Blick: Wenn du transparentes Filament für das Infill verwendest, kannst du den Zustand deiner Silikakugeln (Farbwechsel bei Sättigung) perfekt durch das Gyroid-Muster hindurch ablesen – direkt durch den Vakuumbeutel, ohne ihn extra öffnen zu müssen! Platzsparend & Effizient: Nutzt den ungenutzten Raum in der Mitte der Filament-Spule optimal aus und ersetzt die meist schon gesättigten Silkapäckchen. Gedruckt habe ich die Box in zwei Farben (macht ein AMS notwendig) und mit PETG . Ich empfehle PETG, da es flexibel und robust für den Einsatz mit Silika Gel ist. Die sichtbare Gyroid Schicht ist mit einem transparenten PETG gedruckt. Desweiteren gibt es auf Druckplatte 2 einen kleinen Helfer, der euch bei der Montage unterstützt. Dieser kann auch mit PLA gedruckt werden und ist für die Funktion der Box nicht notwendig. Montagehinweis: druckt alle nötigen Teile für den Behäler aus druckt den ‘Helper’ aus schiebt den ‘Helper’ über das Grundgerüst, wie im Bild unten zu sehen biegt die Wände leicht vor und schiebt sie dann, durch die Führung, bis in den Boden dann noch den Deckel einschrauben, gerade aufsetzen… fertig!!!

description: Description This model works with a X2D or a P2S, adding only 53mm to the depth of the printer, and it vents the printer to connect to a 3.75 inch (100mm) or 75mm diameter hose. For the X2D, the fan, control board, air filter and hardware from the factory installed External Exhaust Fan can be reused for this model, but you will need to get 22 BT2x5 self-tapping screws (or equivalent) and an M3x12 screw for the Latch pivots (listed in the Bill of Materials above). For the P2S, it works with the components provided by the Bambu P2S External Exhaust Fan Kit and supports the External Exhaust Air Filter (listed in the Bill of Materials above). Note: Before you order the External Exhaust Fan Kit from Bambu inspect the back of your printer. If there is no exhaust port on the back panel, then you have an early version of the printer and will need to order the External Exhaust Fan Kit + Rear Panel option from Bambu (which doesn't cost extra). And install the new rear panel before you can install the External Exhaust Fan upgrade. Instructions installing the rear panel are here . NOTE: 5 output stage options are currently offered, distributed across several print profiles: Low Profile Vertical Active Fan Vent P2S X2D Vx.3m, Plate 4 - 3.75 inch hose adapter Low Profile Active P2S Fan Vent Vx.3mf, Plate 3 - Fan Grille Low Profile Fan Vent P2S 75mm Hose Adapter Vx.3MF, Plate 1 - 75mm hose adapter Low Profile Fan Vent P2S X2D Rt Angle Hose Adapters Vx.3MF, Plate 1 or 3 - 3.75 inch adapter Low Profile Fan Vent P2S X2D Rt Angle Hose Adapters Vx.3MF, Plate 2 or 4 - 75mm adapter This model is divided into 4 parts: the Base Module, Vertical Extension, Fan Module, and Output Stage (Hose Adapter/Fan Grille). This partitioning allows easy modification of any component without needing to reprint the other components. For example, the Hose Adapter can be easily replaced to support different hose sizes. Let me know in the comments the Inner Diameter (ID) of the particular hose that you need. Assembly Base Assembly The first step is to assemble the Fan Vent Base. The two types of clips (as shown in Figure 1 ) are inserted into the Fan Vent Base (Low Profile Fan Vent P2S V4.stl) in the positions indicated in Figure 2 . Figure 1 : Low Profile Fan Vent Clips Be sure to orientate all the clips to point in the same direction, as indicated by the green arrow in Figure 2 . Then insert the BT2x5 self-tapping screws, provided with the Bambu kit, from the opposite side (see the green arrows in Figure 15 ) and secure the Clips with the screws. Figure 2 : Base Clip Attachment Finally apply the pre-cut black Foam Tape provided with the Bambu Kit to the Base. Confirm the correct position before pasting to avoid errors. Ensure the foam is aligned with the edge, and paste the four strips of top foam one by one as shown in Figure 2 . If you have an X2D and can't peel the tape of the factory fan cover, search for "1mm foam tape" on Amazon, they offer many options. If available, insert the External Exhaust Air Filter . Fan Module The next step is to assemble the Fan Module. Latches Each Latch consists of two parts: Body and Latch. First install the Latch Body part ( Figure 3 ) on the fan Module connector, then insert two BT2x5 self-tapping screws as indicated by the green arrows and tighten them on the both sides to attach it to the Latch Body. Note: The screws act as shafts. Do not over-tighten them otherwise the Latch will not work smoothly. Figure 3 : Latch Body Installation Next install the Latch Latch part ( Figure 4 ) on the fan Module connector, then insert two BT2x5 self-tapping screws as indicated by the green arrows and tighten them on the both sides to attach it to the Latch Body. Figure 4 : Latch Latch Installation Now use the same process to attach the Latch components on the opposite of the Fan Module for the Base, and on the top and bottom of the Fan Module for the Hose Adapter, as shown in Figure 5 . Figure 5 : Hose Adapter Latches Fan Installation Before continuing remove any leftover support material from around the inside of the Connector Holes ( Figure 6 ) and the ‘top’ inside surface of the PCB case (as indicated by the blue arrow in Figure 6 ). And ensure that PCB connectors fit through the holes, and the PCB fits snugly against the top surface of the PCB case. Route the fan cable through the Fan Cable Hole as shown in Figure 6 and Figure 8 . Figure 6 : PCB Case Then press the fan into the Fan Module with the orientation shown in Figure 7 , while pulling on the fan cable. Note that the gasket that wraps around the fan is facing out. Also the airflow direction arrow on the side of the fan must be facing out as well. The surface of the fan should be flush with the surface of the fan module. Figure 7 : Fan Orientation PCB Installation Connect the Fan Cable to the PCB then fit the connectors into the connector holes ( Figure 6 ) and rotate the PCB so that it flat against the bottom of the PCB case. Finally use a BT2x5 self-tapping screw to secure the PCB to the Fan Module. Only one screw is necessary, because the left side of the PCB is held in place by its connectors. Figure 8 : PCB Installation Now press the PCB Cover into the PCB Case. Make sure that the Connector Baffles (as shown in Figure 9 ) are over the connectors. Also make sure that there is no left over support material in the slots that the cover will clip into, otherwise it will not seat tightly. Figure 9 : PCB Cover Output Stage There are 5 Output Stage options. The Output Stage printing choices are discussed at the beginning of this Description, for the various options. Only print the Plate associated with the option that you choose! For all options, you will need to press the Hose Adapter Gasket into the Hose Adapter Module so that it seats as show in Figure 10 . Note: There may be some elephant foot around the outside edge of the gasket, scrape it if necessary to allow the gasket to be pressed into the Hose Adapter. Also, one end of the gasket is chamfered on both edges. The chamfered edges should be facing out when inserted. The Gasket is printed with the chamfered edges facing up. Figure 10 : Hose Adapter Fan Grill Similar to the Hose Adapter ( Figure 10 ), press the Hose Adapter Gasket into the Fan Grille so that it seats as show in Figure 11 . Note: There may be some elephant foot around the outside edge of the gasket, scrape it if necessary to allow the gasket to be pressed into the Fan Grille. Also, one end of the gasket is chamfered on both edges. The chamfered edges should be facing out when inserted. The Gasket is printed with the chamfered edges facing up. Figure 11 : Fan Grille Right Angle Hose Adapters Similar to the Hose Adapter ( Figure 10 ), press the Hose Adapter Gasket into the Right Angle Hose Adapter so that it seats as show in Figure 12 . Note: There may be some elephant foot around the outside edge of the gasket, scrape it if necessary to allow the gasket to be pressed into the Right Angle Adapters. Also, one end of the gasket is chamfered on both edges. The chamfered edges should be facing out when inserted. The Gasket is printed with the chamfered edges facing up. Figure 12 : 3.75inch and 75mm Right Angle Hose Adapters The Right Angle Hose Adapters can be attached with the hose facing up, down, forward, or backwards. The Low Profile Fan Vent P2S X2D Rt Angle Hose Adapters Vx.3MF file includes two versions of the 3.75 inch and 75mm adapters: One with normal Tree supports and the other using tree supports and PETG as an interface layer. I added the PETG interface versions, which add about 3.5 hours to the print time, to see if they would significantly improve the surface quality. I didn't see a improvement that I was hoping for, especially considering the additional print time, but I left them in the file. Final Installation If attached, tear off the sticker on the printer’s rear panel exhaust port. If there is no exhaust port on the back panel, they you will need to order the “External Exhaust Fan Kit + Rear Panel” option from Bambu. Figure 14 : Sticker Removal Base Module Hold the Base Module and align the clips with the slots on the rear panel. Press the Base Module firmly against the rear panel to compress the foam gasket, then slide it to the left (as indicated by the red dashed arrow in Figure 15 ). You should feel the module snap into place to the preset installation position of the rear panel. The green arrows indicate where the BT2x5 self-tapping screws are inserted to secure the clips. Figure 15 : Base Module Installation Vertical Extension A single M3x10mm screw through the Extension Mounting Screw Hole (Green Arrow in Figure 16 and Figure 17 ). is used to attach the Vertical Extension to the Base Module. Figure 16 : Extension Mounting Screw Hole Remove the Allen screw from the center/top of the back plate. Fit the Vertical Extension to the Base Module (Red Arrow) and use an M3x10mm Screw and the same hole that you just removed the screw from (Green Arrow in Figure 17 ) to attach the Vertical Extension to the back panel. Figure 17 : Base Module Installation Fan Module Fit the Fan Module to the Vertical Extension, then use the top and bottom latches to secure it in place (Green Arrows in Figure 18 ). After installation, connect the 6PIN cable between the fan connector to the corresponding connector of the buffer. Figure 18 : Fan Module Installation Output Adapter Finally fit the selected Output Adapter to the Fan Module, then use the front and back latches to secure it in place. Figure 19 shows the installation of the Fan Grill. Figure 19 : Output Adapter Installation Output Options Figure 20 : Hose Adapter options: 3.75 inch and 75mm Figure 21 : Right Angle Hose Adapter options: 3.75 inch and 75mm Figure 21 : Fan Grille And as always, if this design proves useful to you please boost me. model_name: Low Profile P2S Chamber Exhaust Fan Kit ver1.0
description: This is a lower profile Chamber Exhaust Fan than the official Bambu “ P2S Chamber Exhaust Fan Kit ”. It uses the same $20 Bambu P2S chamber exhaust fan kit parts . Though design may appear similar to the Original Bambu Chamber Exhaust Fan in some ways, it is an entirely different, scratch built design. This design is not in any way associated with Bambu, so use this design at your own risk. No warranties are given. This project was a collaboration with MadMopar (over on MakerWorld). MadMopar had the original idea for a lower profile exhaust duct for the P2S, ran multiple prototypes, provided suggestions and feedback to refine the design, and also provided all the images of the printed design. So a big thanks goes out to MadMopar ! PLEASE NOTE: This profile does not include the poop chute shown in the pics (and the baseplate included here is not compatible with that poop chute design). This model only includes a basic (flat) plate for the poop chute. If you want to use Mc2.project3D's “ Inspectable Waste Chute – Series P / X / H2 ” which is shown in the pics , you will be able to find a remixed backplate and slide which are compatible with that designat the link below (due to the MakerWorld Exclusive License): https://makerworld.com/en/models/2920654-baseplate-only-for-the-inspectable-waste-chute#profileId-3267976 Between MadMopar and myself, many hours have been spent polishing the design, testing and improving it. I feel it is completed, and the one of these ducts in operation currently (with the 2" duct) has been performing well. But if you make or use this design and see anything that could be improved, please provide feedback (positive or negative). I cannot guarantee that the changes will be made, but I will check the comments. I don't own the P2S myself, so if you have a problem, providing pics and accurate measurements would be very helpful. Functionally, this design differs from the official Bambu Chamber Exhaust Fan design in the following key ways: This design has a lower overall profile, which can help in setups with limited room behind the printer. This design uses magnets to hold the duct on, instead of the latches on the stock Bambu design. It was thought that the magnetic attachment would make the duct easier to install or remove when there is limited space behind the printer. This design shifts the whole Exhaust Fan to the left a few mm, which allows for more poop chute options. This does however move the poop chute mount a bit away from the printer, which could be a problem with some poop chute designs (YMMV). This design has an optional TPU gasket, or can be used with 1/16" (1.58mm) thick foam tape, between the backplate and printer, to reduce air leakage. This design does not have room for a HEPA filter , which the official Bambu Chamber Exhaust design does allow for. This design is strictly for venting the chamber either outside or to a separate air cleaner. This design is a bit more complex and expensive to build, since it uses 16x 10x3mm cylinder magnets to hold the duct on, and requires more filament. Currently there are only ducts for a 2" or 2.5" (inside diameter) hose, with options for ducts that angle out at 45°, 90° and straight out from the printer. The 2.5" ducts are untested , and you can find them at the following link: https://www.printables.com/model/1754424-25-ducts-for-bambu-p2s-and-p1-exhaust-see-descript I may add additional ducts in the future, but I plan to upload the STEP models for this design to help with remixing the design. I may upload this in the future to MakerWorld, so I kindly ask that you please do not upload this design to MakerWorld. Thanks for understanding. To build this, the following hardware is needed (in addition to the Bambu P2S Exhaust Fan Kit): 2x M3x20 FHCS (Flat Head Cap Screws) 2x M3x14 (upto 20mm long) FHCS 4x M5x10 Self-Tapping Case Fan Screws 16x 10x3mm Cylinder Magnets 1/16" foam tape (optional) and not needed if using the TPU Gasket Superglue Printing: There are two main profiles available for the main parts. One of the main profiles is set up for ABS and uses brims and mouse ears to help with bed adhesion. The other main profile is set up with PETG, and does not use brims. Both profiles use a textured build plate, however both also specify an Engineering Plate for the optional TPU gasket. The Engineering Plate for TPU is just a suggestion, but I recommend using a smoother plate with glue as a release agent, since TPU tends to aggressively stick to the textured plates. There are additional profiles for the 2" ducts. Any future duct sizes will also have a separate profile. The image below shows the layout of the profile. The only options, aside from the TPU gasket, are the three L-Clip choices. The L-Clips mount into the baseplate, and help to hold the vent fan to the back of the printer, along with 2 screws around the poop chute. The L-Clips are available in different lengths, depending on how the vent fan is configured. There are different L-Clip sizes for using 1/16" foam tape, the optional TPU gasket, or no tape and no TPU gasket (which will probably allow more leakage of air). These options are described below the image: Referring to the above image, the L-Clip options are: A. L-Clips used with 1/16" foam tape (plate 04) B. L-Clips used without the foam tape or TPU gasket (plate 05) C. L-Clips used with the TPU gasket on plate 06 (plate 04) The 3mf profiles included were set up using Bambu Studio v2.7.1.57 and include the following: 92mm_Fan_Cover_v95_PETG_no_Ducts.3mf (base profile without brims, for PETG) 92mm_Fan_Cover_v95_ABS_w_BRIMS_no_Ducts.3mf (base profile with brims, for ABS) v6Z_2in_Ducts_only.3mf (45°, 90°, dual, and straight through 2" ducts) V1F_2-5in_Ducts.3mf (UNTESTED 45°, 90°, and straight through 2" ducts) The individual STEP models will be added later, when the license is changed to allow for remixing. Assembly: First decide if you plan to use the optional TPU cover, or 1/16" foam tape before gathering the parts. This will determine which type of L-hook is used, and which plates need to be printed. See the above information under “Printing” to decide which size L-Clips you need to use. Start by installing the L-Clips into the baseplate. These will need a bit of glue to hold them in place. Next, remove the two screws around the poop chute. These will be re-installed in the following steps, through the baseplate. If the TPU cover (shown in orange) is going to be used, install it on the baseplate: Install the baseplate onto the back of the printer. First start the right side L-Clip hooks in the corresponding holes on the printer metal backplate, then start the left side hooks. When both are in place and the baseplate will sit flush to the printer, slide the baseplate leftward until it stops. At this point the holes on the plate should align with the holes for the screws around the poop chute which were removed in step 3. These two screws can now be re-installed through the baseplate to help secure it to the printer. Install 8 of the 10x3 cylinder magnets into the cover as shown. Pay special attention to the polarity of these magnets, and how they are installed, so they will attract the magnets which will be installed in the duct. It can help to mark one pole of the magnets with a sharpie before starting, so there is a visual indicator of their polarity. I recommend installing the magnets so the poles are all pointed in the same direction, which will make things easier later. A drop of superglue will help secure them. Install the fan into the cover of the printer, using the M5x10 self-tapping fan screws. Make sure the fan power cable wraps either around the top or bottom side of the fan, and will not become pinched. Connect the fan cable to the board from the P2S Exhaust Fan Kit. Use the 3 screws included with the P2S Exhaust Fan Kit to install the board into the cover. You can use the small wire management slot (circled in green) to manage the extra wire. Double check that the wiring is connected and none of the fan wires are pinched (or will get pinched during the next assembly steps). Install the cover (with the fan and board previously installed) onto the baseplate using the M3 flat head screws: Install 8 of the 10x3mm cylinder magnets into the fan duct. Pay special attention to the polarity of the magnets here, since they should all be set up to attract the magnets already installed in the fan cover. It may help to set the magnets onto the fan cover magnets, prior to installing, so you can verify they will attract and not repel. If your magnets are not all set up as north or south on the fan cover and duct, be sure to orient the duct in the final position before installing magnets in it, otherwise it may attract on some and repell on others. It can also help to mark one pole of the magnets with a sharpie before starting, so there is a visual indicator of their polarity. A drop of superglue may help them stay. Install the duct onto the fan cover. Please provide feedback on this design (positive or negative), so it can be improved, thanks! Ultimate Spool Holder A simple, robust wall-mounted spool holder designed to be practical, easy to print, and easy to assemble. This design was created with real-world printing in mind: no exotic materials, no supports, and no oversized build volume requirements. Caution: This design requires 2 ball bearings! I used standard 22mm skateboard bearings. Features Easy to print in PLA or PETG No supports required Fits on a single build plate Compatible with any printer Clean wall-mounted installation Suitable for many 1kg filament spools (Spool Inner diameter must be between 52 and 58 mm) Printing Recommended materials: PLA, PETG Supports: None Assembly Assemble the main axle thread using the small cube as a guide (glue is not necessary). Depending on the material and print settings, you may have to sand the thread a little bit for it to fit. Insert the 22mm bearings Push the axle through the bearings Screw the axle in the base until it is tight Screw the base where you want using a 3mm wide screw Install the springs (glue should not be necessary) Insert the whole thing on the wall mount. Why this design? The provided external spool holder has a lot of friction with cardboard spools, causing noise and giving the filament feeder more work. model_name: Snapmaker U1 + Sunlu Filadryer S4 Feeder Adapter
description: Humidity, my worst enemy… Snapmaker sent me the U1, and unfortunately, I'm not able to get good prints with printers that have open-air spools (because of the humidity at my location). So I looked for the best way to deal with it, and none of the projects I found were good enough. The closest one used a Sunlu Filadryer S4, so that was my baseline to start this project: Snapmaker u1 + Sunlu Fliladryer S4 Setup Compact setup Air-tight (at least as much as the original S4) It has the feeders as close as possible to the spools → Easier loading and unloading This is a DIY project, so you will need some tools and materials: M3 x 6 Screws, 4 of them with nuts and washers 2 x PTFE connectors. The ones that allow the 4 mm PTFE tube to pass through Drills (3.5 mm for the screws, and one for the size of your PTFE connectors) Extra PTFE tubes (4 mm OD, 2.5 mm ID) to replace the ones that go from the original feeder location to the back of the printer. Feeder extension cable. This might be the trickiest. They can be found as GH1.25 or JST GH1.25. Be sure they are 15-pin and male-female configuration. The length depends on your setup; measure both sides from the feeder's original location to the back of the Sunlu S4. I recommend 50 cm. I'll leave some links in the comments. I don't have measurements of the process, because I did it on the go and wasn't planning to upload it anywhere. But I have some pictures taken from the video I recorded: Depending on your setup, you would want to place the S4 on the right or the left of the U1. Therefore, you need to install the feeders on the side of the S4 that faces the back (as shown in the pictures above). You need to measure the distance between the feeder inputs, and drill the holes in the S4 to install the PTFE connectors. Then, assemble the feeders in the printed holder, and place it with the holes aligned to the filament input. Mark the Holder holes, and drill the 3.5 mm holes for the screw assembly. Assemble it, place the numbers from the inside, and then the funnels (optional, but recommended) Then, place the U1 and S4 in the final position, measure, cut, and install the PTFE tubes from the printer to the feeder. Don't make them too short or they might bend; leave some extra for them to wiggle around with smooth curves. That's about it. As I said, I made it on the go, so I'm not sure if I'm forgetting something 😂

description: VERSION FRANÇAISE Support AMS HT pour Simple AMS Flipper de Jakob — fixation directe sur l'ossature, réversible G/D Mon nouveau AMS HT venait d'arriver, il me fallait un support compatible avec le Simple AMS Flipper de Jakob : 🔗 https://makerworld.com/fr/models/1815860-h2-simple-ams-flipper Pourquoi ce design plutôt que le support officiel de Jakob ? Le mien s'accroche directement sur l'ossature du Flipper, en s'appuyant sur la structure triangulée du bras — comme on le voit sur le rendu CAD ci-dessus. C'est une approche différente, pas un remplacement : à toi de voir laquelle correspond le mieux à ton montage. Caractéristiques Fixation par clipsage / insertion sur les triangles du bras, aucun outil ni visserie nécessaire Réversible gauche/droite : un seul design en miroir, mais je fournis directement les 2 fichiers STL prêts à imprimer (pas besoin de mirrorer toi-même dans Bambu Studio) Compatible avec le bras droit court (version ventilée) — même système de fixation par triangles Profil pensé pour rester compact et garder le Flipper pleinement fonctionnel une fois l'AMS HT en place Hauteur du support calculée pour laisser entièrement libre la fenêtre de visualisation intérieure de l'imprimante Matériau recommandé Imprimé et utilisé en PETG-CF chez moi — bon compromis rigidité/qualité de finition, et la teinte cuivrée rend plutôt bien sur la pièce. A peine de fléchissement malgré les + de 2kg de poids : Impression Le fichier nécessite des supports, mais l'orientation a été pensée pour les limiter au maximum : la pièce est positionnée à l'envers sur le plateau (dessus contre le plateau) Mise à jour : amortisseurs TPU anti-vibrations Pour limiter les vibrations entre le support et la carrosserie de l'imprimante, j'ajoute deux petits amortisseurs en TPU qui s'insèrent par friction (sans colle) sur le cadre bas du support, au point de contact avec l'imprimante. Le support n'étant pas forcément parfaitement parallèle à la carrosserie, chaque cale a un côté de 8 mm et l'autre de 10 mm : il suffit de la retourner pour s'adapter à l'écart réel de ton montage. Ce support fait partie d'un écosystème de pièces développées pour le Simple AMS Flipper H2D : TPU Flipper mount: Right bearing roller mount F eet for Flipper without top glass AMS HT-Direct mount on Flipper arm Simple AMS TPU Feed Assist for AMS Flipper simple Si ce mod te rend service, un boost fait toujours plaisir 🙂 Et si tu l'imprimes, je serai heureux de voir vos prints et photos de montage, ça fait toujours plaisir 🤩 ENGLISH VERSION AMS HT mount for Jakob's Simple AMS Flipper — mounts directly on the flipper frame, left/right reversible My new AMS HT had just arrived, so I needed a mount compatible with Jakob's Simple AMS Flipper: 🔗 https://makerworld.com/fr/models/1815860-h2-simple-ams-flipper Why this design instead of Jakob's official AMS-HT mount? Jakob's AMS-HT bracket attaches to the printer's frame. Mine clips directly onto the Flipper's own arm, using its triangular truss structure — as shown in the CAD render above. It's a different approach, not a replacement: pick whichever fits your setup better. description: Bambu A1 and A2L Swiveling PTFE Tube Guide - Parametric, with Print-in-Place Ball Joint A small ask : if you print this and find it to your liking, please rate my model. Ratings contribute to model visibility. Thank you ! If you've ever glanced over mid-print and noticed your drybox or your AMS Lite slowly sliding toward the print bed - pulled there by a taut filament tube - this one's for you. PTFE tube management is one of those details that seems trivial until it isn't. A loose or unsecured tube puts real tension on whatever it's attached to: a desktop spool holder, an AMS Lite, or a drybox on a shelf. Some existing guides rely on a dovetail joint or a friction fit that works fine in theory - until the repeated motion of printing slowly works the joint loose, and by the time you notice something is wrong, your setup has already been dragged somewhere it shouldn't be. I learned this the hard way so I designed my own. My design uses a fully print-in-place ball joint: it articulates freely so the tube always follows the print head without resistance, but the ball is physically captured inside the housing - there's no clip, no friction fit, nothing that can pull apart under load. The lever is printed horizontally so its strength doesn't rely on layer adhesion at all. And the C-clip uses a carefully angled opening that holds the tubes in place during normal use. Fully Parametric Configure four values to match your setup: Guide placement - top of the printer (usually for external spools) or towards the front (usually for a side-mounted AMS Lite) Guide diameter - size the C-clip to your tube count and diameter Lever length - a short lever works for most prints; increase it if you frequently print very tall models and need more slack Ball joint offset - position the guide towards the front, center, or back of the top bar Pre-configured standard variants are published alongside this model, so if your setup is typical you can go straight to printing without touching a single parameter. Printing note After printing, gently move the lever in the joint until it becomes loose and starts swiveling. Longer lever variants require a small horizontal bridge support under the lever. The included print profiles handle this automatically. Happy printing !

description: X2D Support Test – Multi-Material Support Benchmark Dieses Modell wurde speziell entwickelt, um die Qualität von Supportstrukturen und Multi-Material-Drucke objektiv zu bewerten. Durch die verschiedenen Überhänge, Aussparungen, Brücken und Kontaktflächen eignet sich der Test hervorragend, um die Druckqualität unterschiedlicher Materialkombinationen zu vergleichen und optimale Einstellungen für saubere Support-Oberflächen zu finden. Was wird getestet? Oberflächenqualität über Supportstrukturen Maßhaltigkeit kritischer Geometrien Qualität von Überhängen und Brücken Trennbarkeit der Supports Einfluss verschiedener Interface-Materialien Druckzeit und Materialverbrauch Vorteile von Multi-Material Supports Durch die Verwendung eines separaten Support-Interface-Materials lassen sich deutlich sauberere Unterseiten und Kontaktflächen erzielen als mit Supports aus dem gleichen Material. Besonders bei anspruchsvollen Überhängen können dadurch: glattere Oberflächen bessere Maßhaltigkeit weniger Nacharbeit einfachere Supportentfernung erreicht werden. Empfohlene Druckvarianten Variante 1 – Nur Support-Interface in anderem Material (empfohlen) Hier wird das Modell und die eigentlichen Supportstrukturen mit dem Hauptmaterial gedruckt. Lediglich die Support-Schnittstellen (Support Interface Layers) werden mit einem zweiten Material erzeugt. Beispiel: Modell: PLA Supports: PLA Support Interface: PETG Diese Methode bietet in der Regel das beste Verhältnis aus Druckqualität, Materialverbrauch und Druckzeit. Variante 2 – Komplette Supports in anderem Material Alternativ können sowohl die Supportstrukturen als auch die Support-Schnittstellen vollständig aus einem zweiten Material gedruckt werden. Beispiel: Modell: PLA Supports + Interface: PETG Diese Variante kann die Trennbarkeit weiter verbessern, erhöht jedoch den Materialwechsel erheblich. Wichtig: Durch die vielen Werkzeugwechsel zwischen den Materialien verlängert sich die Druckzeit deutlich und es entsteht zusätzlicher Materialabfall durch Spülvorgänge. Für die meisten Anwendungen ist daher Variante 1 die sinnvollere Wahl. Empfohlene Materialkombinationen PLA ↔ PETG PETG ↔ PLA ASA ↔ Support Material ABS ↔ Support Material Viel Spaß beim Testen! Teile gerne deine Ergebnisse, Einstellungen und Materialkombinationen in den Kommentaren, damit andere Nutzer von deinen Erfahrungen profitieren können. Hinweis Die Vorschaubilder und Darstellungen in diesem Eintrag wurden mithilfe von KI-generierten Grafiken erstellt und dienen ausschließlich der Veranschaulichung des Druckkonzepts. Das tatsächliche Druckergebnis kann je nach Drucker, Material und Einstellungen abweichen.

model_name: Will it stick? Adhesion / Warping Torture Test
description: Everyone runs their own warp/adhesion tests. Nobody else ever learns from them. Every time someone figures out whether a filament sticks to a plate, that answer stays in their head, and the next person burns time and filament rediscovering it. You end up getting people in discord or reddit or forums having their own tiny bit of anecdotal evidence, and everyone cargo cults it. Will It Stick fixes that: print one standard model, report what happened, and your result joins a free, searchable matrix of build plate × filament × surface prep results at willitstick.fyi . Because every data point comes from this exact model, results are directly comparable across plates, materials, and brands; one shared test instead of a thousand private ones nobody can see. One short print, three answers 1. First-layer adhesion: did the first layer grip without sliding or lifting? 2. Warping: are the corners and long edges still flat when the print finishes? 3. Ease of removal : does it release cleanly once cool, without damaging the plate? Your result feeds the community adhesion matrix at willitstick.fyi ; crowdsourced, like-for-like data on which filaments stick to which build plates, with which surface prep. Every result comes from this exact model, so combos are actually comparable. Submitting takes about two minutes and no account: snap one photo, record pass/fail for the three checks at https://willitstick.fyi/submit . Full protocol (with photo examples) at https://willitstick.fyi/how-to-test ⚠️ Because this model is deliberately brutal, a failure doesn't mean your plate or filament is bad! It's a way to compare plate performance with evidence instead of feels. Print Settings: A 3mf for OrcaSlicer 2.4.1 is available in “Download STL/CAD files” Layer Height 0.2mm Walls 4 Top Layers 2 Top Shell Thickness 0.4mm Bottom Layers 2 Sparse Infill Density 50% Sparse Infill Pattern Aligned Rectilinear Infill/Wall Overlap 20% Example results: printed with (extremely warp-prone) Bambu Lab PA6-GF The forbidden dorito: A much more slight warping failure (glue helps!): And a perfect pass: There's also useful overview information for each plate in the database! btw, the firethorn is the only plate so far that didn't warp with Bambu PA6-GF without glue . description: This is a simple magnet fit tolerance test kit for common round magnets used in 3D printed projects. Instead of guessing the perfect hole size for your magnets, print the test strip that matches the magnets you have, press your magnets into the different holes, and choose the fit that works best for your printer, slicer settings, filament, and material. The kit includes separate test pieces for: 3×2 mm magnets 4×2 mm magnets 5×2 mm magnets 6×2 mm magnets 8×2 mm magnets 10×2 mm magnets Each size is a separate part, so you do not need to print the whole kit. Just print the strip for the magnet size you actually have. Each strip includes multiple hole diameters around the nominal magnet size, with the tolerance clearly labelled above each hole. For example, the 6×2 mm strip tests hole sizes from 5.95 mm to 6.25 mm. The magnet pockets are designed for 2 mm thick magnets. The back of each pocket is intentionally thin so the magnet can be pushed back out after testing. Why use this? Magnet fit can vary a lot depending on: Printer calibration Filament type Material shrinkage Nozzle size Slicer settings Hole compensation settings Whether you want a press fit, loose fit, or glue-in fit For best results, print the test strip in the same material you plan to use for your final project. For example, if your finished part will be PETG, print the test strip in PETG. If your final part will be ABS, print the test strip in ABS. Included sizes 3×2 mm magnet test Tests: Ø2.95, Ø3.00, Ø3.05, Ø3.10, Ø3.15, Ø3.20, Ø3.25 4×2 mm magnet test Tests: Ø3.95, Ø4.00, Ø4.05, Ø4.10, Ø4.15, Ø4.20, Ø4.25 5×2 mm magnet test Tests: Ø4.95, Ø5.00, Ø5.05, Ø5.10, Ø5.15, Ø5.20, Ø5.25 6×2 mm magnet test Tests: Ø5.95, Ø6.00, Ø6.05, Ø6.10, Ø6.15, Ø6.20, Ø6.25 8×2 mm magnet test Tests: Ø7.95, Ø8.00, Ø8.05, Ø8.10, Ø8.15, Ø8.20, Ø8.25 10×2 mm magnet test Tests: Ø9.95, Ø10.00, Ø10.05, Ø10.10, Ø10.15, Ø10.20, Ø10.25 Printing notes These are quick, simple prints and should not need supports. Recommended settings: Layer height: 0.16 mm or 0.20 mm Walls: 2 or more Infill: 10 to 20% Supports: No Brim: Not usually needed Orientation: Print flat on the build plate Material: Use the same material you plan to use for your final magnet project For the most accurate results, avoid scaling the model. 1 colour or 2 colour printing This model can be printed in either one colour or two colours . For a simple print, use one colour. The labels are still useful as raised or engraved text. For better readability, print the text in a second colour. A dark base with light text works especially well. How to use Choose the test strip that matches your magnet size. Print it in the material you plan to use for your final project. Press your magnet into each labelled hole. Find the fit you prefer. Use that hole diameter in your own CAD model. A tighter fit may work well for press-fit magnets. A looser fit may be better if you plan to use glue. Notes If you need a different magnet size, leave a comment. I can make additional sizes if people would like them.

model_name: Minimal Filament Respooler for AMS Lite V2
description: This is a filament respooler that uses the structure of the Bambu Lab AMS Lite. It is an improved and updated version of my previously released model. A Bambu Lab AMS Lite is required to use this model. The printed parts cannot be used on their own. By utilizing the AMS Lite’s structure, filament can be transferred to another spool smoothly and reliably with only a small number of printed parts. The complete set requires approximately 90 g of filament to print. It supports manual operation with the included hand crank, as well as electric screwdrivers, electric drills, and ratchet wrenches. A dedicated storage case is also included to keep all the parts neatly organized when not in use. All parts can be printed on an A1 mini. Instructions 1. Assemble the Hand Crank The hand crank is assembled from three printed parts. The small hexagonal adapter is used when respooling with a ratchet wrench and a 10 mm socket. 2. Install the Holder on the AMS Lite Remove one rotary spool holder from the AMS Lite. Insert the printed inner holder onto the exposed AMS Lite shaft. This holder does not rotate, so the fitting is intentionally designed to be tight. 3. Install the Spools Screw the respooling core into the empty spool and tighten it securely. Install the empty receiving spool on the side fitted with the printed inner holder. Install the spool containing the filament on another spool holder of the AMS Lite. Pull out the filament and secure its end to the empty spool. 4. Respool the Filament For manual operation, attach the hand crank. When using an electric screwdriver, insert the hex driver bit fully into the drive socket. When using an electric drill, attach a 10 mm hex bit. When using a ratchet wrench, insert the included adapter and then attach a 10 mm socket. Important Notes An AMS Lite is required to use this model. This respooler does not include a mechanism for automatically distributing the filament evenly across the spool. Guide the filament from side to side by hand while respooling to prevent it from accumulating in one area. When using a power tool, always operate it slowly at a low speed.

model_name: Printer test model when buying used printers 50g
description: Ever buy a used printer and not be confident that it works as advertised? Don't take that gamble! Send the seller this test model to run prior to you arriving, and request that they leave it on the build plate as proof that the printer works as advertised. There is no denying that the printer printed it, if its still stuck to the build plate when you arrive! This model is not a calibration model , it does not test over hangs, extrusion, nothing like that. This test was designed to make sure the printer can print most of the build plate, as well as show that the Z axis is clean and not bend. You can scale it up or down, but going too small will make that first layer pretty thin. I recommend scaling so the bottom is only 1 layer thick. That will show you how even the bed is and if the printer can print big flat models. The vertical part will show the z axis wear and tear, as well as show layer shifts, VFAs, ghosting and overall print quality. Check around the engraved letters for ghosting and VFAs, check around the corners to see proper extrusion and cornering and ringing, check the circle section to see if there are visible layer shifting. Finally check the pyramid top to ensure it can complete a top without knocking the entire model below over. Again, this is not a test of calibration, just a simple test model for you to be confident that the used printer you are buying can perform basic 3D printer tasks. description: Tired of small, overflowing purge bins, this modular flexible tube allows you to route waste directly into any container for uninterrupted long-term printing. By combining a secure mounting bracket with a customizable segmented design, you can easily adjust the length and angle of the chute to fit your specific workspace layout. It is the ultimate "set it and forget it" upgrade for Bambu users who want a cleaner, more efficient waste management system. This is a “poop chute” or purge waste collection system that has been customized for use with the Bambu Lab H2 series printers, H2S, H2D, H2C. Here are some valuable features: Infinite Customization: It has a segmented "link" design allows you to add or remove sections to reach a waste bin at almost any height or distance from your workbench. Zero-Clog Geometry: The wide, rounded internal path of the segments prevents the "accordion" effect where purge poops occasionally snag on sharp corners or narrow bottlenecks. Workspace Flexibility: Unlike rigid chutes, the articulated tube can be snaked around power cables, enclosure legs, or other tools sitting behind your printer. Toolless Maintenance: Once the adapter is mounted, the tube segments easily snap together or apart, making it simple to clear a rare jam or adjust the routing without tools. High-Volume Ready: By bypassing small, printer-mounted bins in favor of a floor-side box, you can run massive multi-color prints without worrying about a backup at the purge exit. It includes these parts: Mounting Bracket : This part attaches to your printer and has a simple dovetail that can accept an adapter. It attaches to the back of your H2 printer using the same screws that are already there. Just unscrew the two screws, top and bottom, and use those screws to attach the mounting bracket. This part is adapted from Molodos' H2 Series Poop Bin (2 Sizes) Adapter : One end of this part has the male end of a dovetail that hangs on the mounting bracket. The other end attaches to the segmented tube. Segmented Tube . This part snaps onto the Adapter. You can also snap an unlimited number of these parts together, in order to route your waste tube wherever you need. The fit is tight. But each segment can still be articulated. I did not change anything about this model. It is included in this collection (aggregation) in the interest of providing a complete solution. Although this solution articulates, no one piece has any moving parts. So you should probably be fine printing with PLA. I used PETG. The main plate on the print profile includes a “starter kit” with a mounting bracket, adapter bracket, and one segmented tube. The second plate includes just one segmented tube. The idea here is that you can tell Bambu Handy to print multiple copies when you print, so you get as many as you need. If you use Bambu Studio (which gives you many more options, I recommend manually copying and pasting. You can fit a lot more on the build plate than you get by using “Fill bed with copies,” which is pretty clumsy. “Clone” works pretty well.

description: After repeatedly receiving the EufyMake E1's "Taper Warning" while using traditional ring-style Stanley cup jigs, I designed a full sleeve that encloses the tapered base of the tumbler. By presenting the machine with a perfectly cylindrical surface, the warning disappears and the cup mounts much more securely. It has worked reliably on my 1200ml Stanley-style cups and has made printing with the rotary much easier. Most Travel Cup jigs only use a locating ring around the base. While they support the cup, the E1 can still detect the taper and display its familiar "Taper Warning" , preventing accurate setup. This jig solves that problem by using a full-length sleeve instead of a ring. The sleeve completely surrounds the lower tapered section of the tumbler, creating a perfectly cylindrical surface that the E1 recognises as level. Features ✔ Eliminates the EufyMake E1 taper warning ✔ Full sleeve design for maximum stability ✔ Keeps the tumbler perfectly centred ✔ Slides on and off easily ✔ Designed specifically for 1200ml Stanley-style travel cups ✔ No modifications required Tested With This model was designed around the following tumbler: 1300ml Egotier 94373 stainless steel travel cup with handle Printing Recommended settings: Layer Height: 0.20 mm Walls: 3 Infill: 15–20% Supports: None Material: PLA Notes Because many travel cups are manufactured by different factories, small dimensional differences may exist. This model has been tested with the Egotier 94373 travel cup. If your cup differs slightly, a small scale adjustment (±1%) may be required.

model_name: PLA/PETG Dual-Material Support Test Model X2D
description: A stress test model designed to validate using PLA as a support material for PETG prints (or vice versa) with supports built directly on the model -- not from the build plate. The model includes multiple hole types, side cavities, and a bottom pocket to test support placement in challenging geometry. The result is clean top and bottom surfaces with supports that take one firm pull to remove. Designed for: Bambu X2D, H2D, and H2C (dual nozzle required) Why this method works well for complex models: Tree supports from the build plate are great for many prints, but for models with internal cavities, bottom pockets, or tight geometry, getting supports in and out cleanly gets tricky. This method places support only where it's needed, directly on the model, leaving clean surfaces on both top and bottom contact points with minimal removal effort. Important: When you set the “Support/raft interface” setting under “Support”, Bambu Studio will pop up a warning suggesting it change your settings. Press NO. Pressing Yes will switch you to tree supports from the build plate and undo everything. This is the most important step. Notes: PLA supports on a 70°C PETG bed temp caused no issues Adhesion between PLA and PETG is better than expected -- enough to hold during printing, clean enough to pop off with one pull Dedicated support filaments work too, but regular cheap PLA does the job just as well

Le caratteristiche principali di questo design: Gestione lineare del tubo (Nessun bisogno di scollegare nulla): Molti progetti online richiedono di scollegare il tubo in PTFE dall'AMS HT quando il TPU Assistant non è in uso, ad esempio per inserire il tappo di sigillo e avviare la funzione di essiccazione dell'Hub. Questo spesso comporta il dover riporre il tubetto rimosso per non perderlo. Con questa configurazione, grazie alla distanza ridotta e all'allineamento, non è mai necessario scollegare il tubo . Il condotto rimane stabilmente al suo posto e sigillato, semplificando i passaggi: basta spingere il filamento dall'AMS HT direttamente nel TPU Assistant e si è pronti a stampare. Inclinazione ed Ergonomia dei Tasti: La staffa è posizionata più in basso e inclina il TPU Assistant verso lo sguardo di chi si trova davanti alla stampante. In questo modo la pulsantiera e i LED di stato sono facilmente visibili e comodi da raggiungere direttamente dal fronte. Geometria del percorso posteriore e specifiche tubi: Essendo una staffa ribassata, la distanza geometrica verso l'ingresso della stampante aumenta leggermente rispetto alla configurazione standard, richiedendo un percorso totale fisso di 200 mm . Nota per la community: Bambu Lab raccomanda solitamente 160 mm, ma non c'è assolutamente da preoccuparsi per il caricamento . Il sistema del TPU Assistant è infatti progettato per funzionare ufficialmente anche sulla H2D , che è una stampante molto più grande della X2D e ha un percorso interno del filamento nativamente molto più lungo. Visto che il sistema gestisce quel tragitto maggiore senza problemi, i 4 cm esterni in più introdotti su questo setup vengono digeriti dall'estrusore in totale sicurezza. Per installare il sistema avete due opzioni precise: Setup Diretto: Vi servirà uno spezzone di tubo in PTFE tagliato esattamente a 200 mm . Con Adattatore 4-in-1: Se utilizzate un connettore 4-in-1 come il mio (lungo circa 6 cm), dovrete compensare la misura tagliando il tubetto in PTFE a 140 mm (140 mm + 60 mm = 200 mm). Design Essenziale: La struttura è pensata per essere il più compatta e leggera possibile, riducendo la quantità di filamento necessaria e i tempi di stampa. 🔄 IMPORTANTE: Calibrazione post-installazione Come raccomandato dalle linee guida ufficiali Bambu Lab, dopo aver installato la nuova staffa e posizionato il tubo da 200 mm (o 140 mm con adattatore), è fondamentale lanciare la calibrazione del modulo . Questa procedura serve a far leggere al sistema la nuova lunghezza del percorso, misurando l'attrito per calibrare al millesimo la forza della spinta automatica. 👉 Potete seguire la procedura ufficiale passo-passo a questo link della Wiki Bambu Lab: Guida alla Calibrazione del TPU Assistant . 🛠️ Note di Stampa e Tolleranze Materiale di Test: Il progetto è stato sviluppato, stampato e testato in PETG . Nota sulle tolleranze: L'asola di incastro per il TPU Assistant è calibrata in modo preciso sul PETG. Se decidete di stamparlo in PLA o ABS/ASA, tenete conto che il diverso ritiro termico dei materiali potrebbe influire leggermente sulla tolleranza dell'incastro (potrebbe risultare impercettibilmente più stretto o largo). model_name: Ultimate Top Layer Calibration (No Ironing Needed)
description: Tired of waiting hours for "Ironing" to finish, or dealing with the rough, inconsistent top surfaces on your prints? This comprehensive Top Layer Calibration Matrix helps you systematically find the perfect balance between Top Surface Line Width and Top Surface Speed for any filament. Dial in a flawless, smooth, and shiny top finish purely through optimized extrusion mechanics! This test utilizes a grid layout (Columns 1–5 and Rows A–K) featuring both flat rectangular sections and concentric circular test pads (as previewed in the slicer toolpath view). This allows you to evaluate how different settings handle straight infill lines versus tight, curved perimeters. How It Works (The Matrix Grid) The model is divided into a 5x11 grid matrix. Each cell modifies two critical variables to let you visually and texturally pick your winner: Columns (1 – 5): Top Surface Line Width 1: 0.30 mm 2: 0.35 mm 3: 0.40 mm 4: 0.45 mm 5: 0.50 mm Rows (A – K): Top Surface Speed A: 25 mm/s B: 50 mm/s C: 75 mm/s D: 100 mm/s E: 125 mm/s F: 150 mm/s G: 175 mm/s H: 200 mm/s I: 225 mm/s J: 250 mm/s K: 275 mm/s How to Use This Model Download & Slice: Open the provided .3mf file or arrange the model flat on your build plate. Apply Settings: Ensure you use a multi-modifier layout or a calibrated project file where each block/cell is mapped to its respective speed and width coordinates listed above or just hit SLICE without changing any parameters . description: Give your Bambu Lab printer a retro gaming makeover! I couldn't find a PS Vita inspired bezel for my X2D or P2S, so I decided to design one myself. description: This is a dedicated mount that uses the A1 mini's Z-axis cover to attach the BMCU 370C to the right side of the printer. Most existing mounts position the BMCU behind the printer, feeding the PTFE tube from the rear toward the front. However, if your setup has limited rear clearance, this can create an excessively tight bend in the PTFE tube. To solve this problem, this mount routes the filament from the right side of the printer toward the left, allowing the PTFE tube to follow a smoother, more natural curve even in tight spaces. After testing several designs, I found that positioning the filament path at approximately a 45° angle while placing the BMCU slightly farther from the printer provided the best tube routing. The main model is based on this design. The Long 45° Version is the main model. The Ultimate Tracking Tower creates a dense, three-dimensional field of black-and-white tracking markers around the scan volume. Rather than placing every marker on a flat sheet or directly on the turntable, the tower distributes reference points across a broad lower section, a raised central stem, and two faceted upper sections. This arrangement keeps usable markers visible from a wider range of scanner and camera positions. How It Works Users position the tower beside the object being captured or attach it directly to a magnetic turntable. During scanning, the system recognizes the visible markers as stable spatial references for tracking, pose estimation, and frame-to-frame alignment. The wide lower panels provide a large marker field near the turntable. The narrow stem raises additional reference points above the base without creating a large visual obstruction. The faceted upper sections present markers on several different planes and viewing angles. As the object rotates, or as the operator changes position, newly visible markers replace any that become hidden. This continuous marker coverage helps reduce tracking loss, alignment drift, repeated scan passes, and interruptions caused by target reacquisition. Advantages Over Conventional Marker Holders Flat marker boards provide reference points on only one plane and become less effective when the scanner moves outside their ideal viewing angle. Low-profile marker pucks can disappear behind taller objects. Simple cylindrical towers often place markers at similar angles and may provide limited geometric diversity. The Ultimate Tracking Tower addresses those limitations through: **Multi-height marker coverage.** Markers remain available near the turntable, beside the object, and above the object’s lower silhouette. * *Multi-angle visibility.** The faceted upper geometry presents targets toward several scanner positions instead of concentrating them on one flat surface. **Reduced object occlusion.** The narrow central stem raises markers while minimizing the amount of the object that the tower blocks. **A stable reference volume.** The combination of horizontal spread, vertical separation, and angular diversity provides the scanner with a stronger three-dimensional tracking reference than a flat board or basic marker post. **A weighted, magnetic base.** The base incorporates **four 2-inch-diameter by 4-mm-thick round magnets**. The magnets add useful weight, lower the center of gravity, and improve resistance to tipping. They also affix the tower securely to magnetic turntables, preventing unwanted movement during rotation while allowing users to reposition or remove the tower quickly. Recommended Finish The finished tower uses: SEM Products High-Build Primer Surfacer Part Number: 42013 Color: Gray This coating serves an optical and functional purpose, not merely a cosmetic one. Its high-build formulation helps fill and soften visible print-layer texture, while its sandable surface supports a cleaner final profile. The primer-flat finish also reduces concentrated reflections that can interfere with projected patterns, camera exposure, marker recognition, and optical measurement. Once the coating has fully cured, users can apply the required black-and-white tracking markers to the prepared surfaces. Why Medium Gray Is Better Than White or Black Many users assume that white or black must provide the best marker-tower color because those colors represent the brightest and darkest possible backgrounds. As general-purpose recommendations for structured-light scanning, laser scanning, and photogrammetry, both assumptions are wrong. White is too bright . Strong scanner illumination can make a white tower produce glare, clipped highlights, and excessive reflected light. A large white surface can drive automatic exposure downward, reduce available highlight headroom, and weaken separation from white marker centers or light-colored objects. Black is too dark . Black absorbs more projected light and returns a weaker optical signal. It can crush shadow detail, create tracking difficulties for optical systems, and visually merge with black plastic, rubber, carbon-look material, and other dark objects. Matte medium neutral gray provides the best overall balance . It is dark enough to control glare, light enough to remain visible to optical systems, and neutral enough to avoid unnecessary color bias. The midtone preserves more usable dynamic range than either white or black, supports more stable automatic exposure and white balance, and allows the black-and-white tracking markers to remain the dominant high-contrast features. For a general-purpose marker tower, the combination of **SEM 42013 High-Build Primer Surfacer, a matte gray finish, distributed marker geometry, and a weighted magnetic base** provides a more stable, versatile, and scan-friendly solution than conventional flat boards, unweighted towers, or extreme white and black finishes.
