tags: bambu|BAMBU LAB|TPU|tpu spool|tpu spool holder|tpu spool mount|wallmounted tpu|tpu wallmount|tpu holder|tpu bearing|tpu 608|spool|spool holder|spool holder bearings
description: This is the ultimate, fully customizable, wall mounted spool holder which should be suitable for the softest of filaments. It has been tested with: Bambu 95A Bambu 90A Bambu 85A Bambu TPU for AMS Siraya tech flex TPU Of course it should work with all standard filaments too. It features a total of six “tool” holders. The central two (one on each main arm) below the hub are designed to take the flap brake. The flap brake will only work with these two. The other holders are used for the friction brakes. This is the third version of my wall mount and based on the original one which was super smooth but had little control, could run backwards and overrun. I did update it with some brakes which helped but they weren’t very adjustable at all and adding a flap brake just wasn’t practical. I am still in a testing phase but even without adjusting between filaments this version has worked flawlessly so far. I hope it does for you too! Upgrading? For people who already have that old version, this version can re-use at least some parts you already have printed: The original wall brackets will work (although they will be tighter than the new ones). The PTFE tube holder is unchanged. The rear joining bracket is unchanged The wall template is unchanged, no need to redrill anything! Printing Suggestions. The 3MF file contains the settings and support methods I used for this print. Filament: Bambu PLA Metal Iridium Bambu PLA Metal Iron Grey Sparse infill 25% (15% will work just fne) Sparse infill pattern Gyroid Place brim ears on all four parts the two piece arms. In Bambu slicer the brim ears tool set to auto does a great job. You will need to set the brim type to “painted”. Materials you will need: Plugs and screws. Check the screw heads will sit in the countersunk hole and clear the dovetail on the arm. Plugs – if required – I used Fischer 4no. 6x30, 6mm drill bit Screws – 4no. 4x35 – make sure the head will sit within the recess A small amount of PTFE tube. (This is not essential, you can bypass the PTFE holder in use if you choose) Two 608 bearings – these are pretty good: https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B08ZN94S5L?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title but almost any 608 bearing should be fine. Fleece fabric Tessa tape,19- 20mm ideally 51608-00001-00 Or Cable tie Velcro with the soft side as the brake 10-20mm wide Super glue. Installation and assembly: This video should help you understand how it works when assembled, I’d recommend you have sound turned on whilst I’m fitting the brake. Sorry.. VERY boring video :( https://youtube.com/shorts/ZhJ1bJGjlVE?feature=share Choosing parts: Note that I have named all the parts in the 3MF file. I will refer to them here. There are two types of spool arms. One set is only printable on a large bed printer such as the H2D. The other set should be printable on most printer beds and offers a different aesthetic if you use two colours. Photos/videos are of the two part type. Choose how many tool arms to print and of which type (more on this later!). If in doubt just print one standard tool arm “ARM TYPE1 MEDIUM”, one flap brake arm “ARM TYPE 3 Flap Brake”. Note: Arms can be inserted upside down in the front arm holder. Choose which tool to print, again, if in doubt I would suggest “Brake Tool TYPE 1” which has the ridges around and no chamfer. Choose a cover plate type (you may not want cover plates at all!) Note that the large cover plate has a bambu logo which looks nice if printed in a different colour. Choose your axle cap design round or hex – photos are of the hex type. You can choose not to print the flanges. The hub does not require either of them but you won’t get the non-reverse function of course. There is a filament guide included “Flimanent Guide OPTIONAL”. This helped to stop filament loop drops in version 1. I still have it mounted in this version (in the photos) but I haven’t used it nor needed it so far. I would suggest you don’t print it unless you have problems and think it will help. Wall mounting: I would recommend printing the template and using that to position the drill holes. Accuracy IS important. Check that your screw heads will sit within the counter sunk holes. The wall brackets have a little vertical movement in them. Screw the brackets to the wall. Assembly: The two part version is very easy to put together but make sure you trim any access filament (the brim) off the joint on both sides! You can only push the two parts together from one side. Lay the main arm flat on a table and push the small arm on until the whole thing is flush. It may require some force, it’s designed to be tight. A light tap with a hammer can help. Join the parts of the PTFE tube holder together to match the photos. Attach the PTFE tube holder to one of the arms. Take the rear bracket and insert it, bevel edges forward onto the same arm. Now take the other arm and carefully seat it on both the rear bracket and the PTFE tube carrier. Now slide the whole assembly onto the wall brackets to check alignment. It should slide on easily. Assemble the hubs. Remove any support material, use snipe nose pliers to remove the support in the axel socket. Check the supported edge looks flat with no bits of support left and test fit the flanges (if you are using them) to make sure they are flat and flush when seated. Push an axel in each hub as far as it will go. Put a spacer sleeve on next, then your bearings which should be a fairly snug fit. Finally your choice of axel cap. The cap should take quite a bit of force to get on. If it is loose you might want to add some glue. Fitting the flanges Test fit the flanges again. They should be fairly loose fitting without glue. This is by design. Remove them, run a bead of superglue all the way around the edge of the hub, stick the flanges on and leave to dry. Check they are well stuck! Almost done! The hubs should fit together without any effort. Obviously they need to come apart to insert your spools so don’t glue them! Put them together and try dropping the hub into the wall mount. It should drop in and pull out with almost no effort. If it sticks or doesn’t seat correctly there may be some support materials in the arm sockets. If there isn’t try taking the hib in and our a few times. If it doesn’t and the arms didn’t slide into the the wall brackets with ease then you may have an alignment problem. Check your drilling template against the holes in the wall. How things work and Tuning: Flap Brake (s): The function of the flap brake is primarily to stop the spool from running backwards. You will need the smaller ARM TYPE3 (they aren’t handed) and one flap brake for the side you intend to use it on. Fit the brake to the arm (it should fit fairly tightly). When correctly aligned the outer ARM hex faces should line up with the Flap Brake male end hex faces but the most important part is that the flat end of the flap must line up perfectly with the deep flat edge of the scoops on the flange plate. Once fitted the arm can be adjusted by pulling it in and out. Insert it roughly into position so that the end just sits in a scoop The designed position is when it “ticks” fairly quietly in the forward direction and stops the spool turning in the reverse direction. Tuning the flap brake: “Turn” any other brakes off! Use your hand to manually turn the spool forwards and check that there is little to no resistance and you can hear the flap ticking on the disc. Then try to gently spin with spool in reverse. It should be stopped almost immediately as the flap connects with an edge. Note - If you want you can put flap brakes on both sides of the holder. Note – The flap brakes can actually be used as friction brakes too if you push the tool arm in further – it will just be more noisy! Main friction Brakes: Generally I would recommend installing just one or two but you can use up to four. NOTE: Why four? Partly – just in case and you might only have access to one side of the holder but you may like to have one on each side to keep the spool aligned or all four installed to keep everything aligned with a light pressure on all of them. There are two brake types, one is designed for Tessa tape or Velcro style cable ties to wrap around. The other can also take tape but can be used on it’s own – you can just angle the chamfered part against the spool. Tuning the main friction brakes: You can push and pull the arms and you can also angle the tool head on the arm which should allow to you to really fine tune the amount of friction you are applying perfectly to suit the filament type. My personal preference is to use Tessa tape, it sticks on and the surface is very smooth. Tool arms: The arms are handed for left and right There are three types. Short – This makes the tool easy to remove but doesn’t provide much resistance to stop the tool head from being moved when tilted. Medium – Recommended. Some give but plenty of resistance. However it is quite hard to pull the arm out without breaking it. Long – Loads of resistance, almost impossible to remove the arm. Basically a permanent position once you push the head all the way on. Happy Soft Filament printing! Minor update 14-7-2026: The flap stop could catch on the edge of a flange when a spool is dropped in to the arms. This version adds a chamfer to the flanges to make it smoother and less likely to catch and rotate the flap stops.

description: I love maCyo42's AMS Riser V3. I put it on my P2S and it does a great job. I've already put up a remix that allows you to mount an AMS-HT on the side using the slots he designed it with. Unfortunately his riser blocks direct access through the top of the P2S for an overhead TPU spool holder. I have never gotten TPU to print properly on my P2S. I don’t print it often enough to buy the Bambu TPU filament feeder. It kind of annoys me that my A1 is able to print it so much easier. I could print a top spool mount for it but that would involve taking down the riser and AMS 2 Pro to use it each time. So I decided to design a front mount system to feed down into the P2S and not have to remove the riser and AMS 2 Pro each time. This heavy-duty, cantilever shelf bracket is designed specifically to solve that problem. It allows you to securely mount a Bambu Lab AMS HT (1.21 kg) and filament spool (up to 1.3 kg) directly above and in front of your printer, keeping your top-front feed path completely clear and accessible. No more moving risers, no more shifting your AMS units around just to print a quick TPU gasket or dampener. Many 3D-printed brackets fail because they are printed in multiple pieces or oriented incorrectly, creating a mechanical "hinge" that sags under a continuous 2.5 kg load. This design completely eliminates that failure point: One-Piece Diagonal Print: Optimized to fit barely but perfectly across a standard 256mm x 256mm build plate . By rotating it 45 degrees and printing it flat on its side, the perimeter walls run continuously from the anchor lip to the front tip. DON’T MOVE THIS ON THE PLATE, IT’S A NIGHTMARE TO GET IT TO FIT PROPERLY! Zero-Joint Cantilever: With no split joints or seams in the middle, the continuous extrusion lines effortlessly handle the forces of the shelf. Advanced Geometry: Features a massive single-diagonal structural gusset to direct the load straight back to the frame anchor and fillets on many internal 90-degree corners to eliminate stress concentration points. Recommended Print Settings Remember, you are relying on this part to securely hold an expensive AMS HT unit. I’ve tested using my settings and found it to be effective and sufficiently strong enough to hold the weight. I STRONGLY ADVISE PRINTING WITH MY EXACT SETTINGS IN PLA-CF. DON’T REARRANGE THE PRINT, IT’S EXTREMELY DIFFICULT TO GET IT ON THE PLATE WITHOUT GETTING AN OVER THE PLATE MESSAGE! To ensure this bracket holds up, use the following settings in Bambu Studio (I've already done that for you): Orientation: Print flat on its side, rotated diagonally to fit the bed. Do not use brims since we’ve hit the maximum length of Wall Loops: 6 to 8 walls (Crucial for structural rigidity). Infill: 40% to 45% (Gyroid recommended for optimal resistance against downward bending forces). Filament Choice: I’ve used PLA-CF and regular PLA, both work well for stiffness, I recommend using PLA-CF to give you the absolute best rigidity and long-term resistance to material creep under a sustained 2.5 kg load. Wall Generator: Arachne (to ensure seamless gap filling at the truss intersections). 👍 Support the Design! This project took multiple design iterations and a lot of geometry tweaking to maximize the 256x256mm print envelope. Its also a niche product that's never going to get a lot of downloads or boosts since it appeals to a limited group of people. So, if this bracket saves you the headache of rearranging your AMS stack every time you want to print TPU, please consider leaving a Like, a Download, or throwing a Boost my way! Your support directly funds the filament and prototypes for my next functional prints.

Choose between the cable inlet for a wired setup or the Pogo-Pin magnetic connector for wireless operation and print the corresponding parts. Insert 4x M3 heat-inserts into the grip. The fit is designed to be tight, holding the cable securely in place. For the wireless version: The Adafruit PowerBoost 1000C is recommended, as it supports charging, boosting, and bypassing power from the connector, all on a single board. Solder the USB-A port to the Adafruit PowerBoost 1000C. Solder the Pogo-Pin magnetic charging connector to the 5V/GND pins of the PowerBoost 1000C. Make sure to get the wiring polarity correct! Feed the Pogo-Pin connector through the grip, then insert the battery, and finally the PowerBoost 1000C. The USB-A port sticks out slightly at the top but fits through the hole in the main body. description: Hello! I’m excited to introduce my desiccant drying system specifically designed for the Creality Space Pi x4 filament dryer. I dedicated a lot of time and effort to developing this model, going through numerous iterations until I reached this version. After experimenting with a model I found in MakerWorld and encountering several issues, I decided to create my own. My goal was to design a strong, modular system that ensures unobstructed airflow. I also wanted something at incorporated a pour spout without taking up a lot of space or using a lot of filament. This filament drying system is stackable, robust, and easy to use. It’s large enough to accommodate two boxes and a frame on each side of the Space Pi x4. It measures 1500mm by 150mm by 60mm, features 2mm holes and a pour spout in one of the corners. Each box can hold a maximum of 500 grams of desiccant, but I recommend not exceeding 300 grams to expedite drying times and prevent overloading the frame. I successfully dried approximately 400 grams (200 grams per side) of wet desiccant in about 6 hours at 85 degrees Celsius, which is significantly faster compared to other solutions. Please note that to achieve the optimal drying temperature of 85 degrees Celsius, I highly recommend printing this model in ASA filament. I’ve shared my personal settings in the profile I published, which is in ASA. For faster prints, I used a .6mm nozzle, but if you prioritize quality, you can print it with a .4mm nozzle. Make sure to adjust the print settings accordingly. Turn off all cooling, lower the volumetric flow to 12 cubic millimeters per second, heat up the chamber to 65 degrees Celsius, and heat the build plate to 100 degrees Celsius. If you don’t have a heated chamber, heat soak it for at least 30 minutes before printing to minimize the risk of warping. Additionally, ensure that you use a textured PEI plate or an engineering plate. Wash it with soap and warm water, and apply a glue stick. ASA emits toxic fumes so use air filters and a proper mask when printing with ASA. Your health is too important to risk it! Customizable Navigation Bar Holder / GPS Bar Clamp A customizable two-piece navigation bar holder for motorcycle GPS, phone, tablet and DMD-style mounts. This model is designed as a parametric OpenSCAD / MakerWorld Customizer file. You can adjust the bar diameter, clamp tolerance, block size, bolt spacing, nut pockets and corner radius directly in the MakerWorld customizer. Key Features Fully customizable bar diameter Designed for navigation bars, GPS bars and handlebar-style mounting points Bar runs through the short side of the block Two-piece clamp design: front and back part Both parts are placed print-ready with the groove facing upward M4 bolt holes Optional M4 hex nut pockets in the back part Rounded corners Adjustable clamp undersize for a tighter or looser fit Suitable for common adventure motorcycle navigation bars Common Diameter Examples Recommended starting values: BMW / adventure GPS bar: Bar_Diameter = 12.0 Clamp_Undersize = 0.30 Hardware M4 Bolt 25mm M4 nyloc nuts Some BMW navigation bars: Bar_Diameter = 16.0 Clamp_Undersize = 0.30 Hardware M4 Bolt 30mm M4 nyloc nuts Always measure your own bar with calipers before printing. Small differences matter for clamp fit. Important Assembly Note Both parts are shown in print orientation with the bar groove facing upward. For assembly: Place the back part against the navigation bar. Flip the front part over. Put the front part over the bar. Insert the M4 bolts. Tighten gradually and evenly. The two half-round grooves will clamp around the bar. Parameters Main customizer parameters: Bar_Diameter Nominal diameter of your motorcycle navigation bar. Bar_Offset_X Moves the bar groove left or right from the center of the block. This is useful when the navigation bar needs to sit slightly off-center. Default value: 0.0 mm Range: -10 mm to +10 mm Clamp_Undersize Reduces the actual groove diameter for a tighter clamp. Example: Bar_Diameter = 12.0 and Clamp_Undersize = 0.30 creates an effective 11.7 mm clamp . Block_Length Overall length of the clamp block. Block_Width Overall width of the clamp block. Half_Thickness Thickness of each half. Set to 0 for automatic thickness. Corner_Radius Controls the rounded corners. Bolt Parameters Bolt_Size Selects the bolt size used for the clamp. Options: M3, M4, M5 The model automatically adjusts the bolt hole diameter and nut pocket size based on this setting. Bolt_Clearance Adds extra clearance to the selected bolt diameter. Example : Bolt_Size = M4 Bolt_Clearance = 0.5 This creates a 4.5 mm bolt hole. Increase this value if your printer makes holes too tight. Manual_Hole_Diameter Manual override for the bolt hole diameter. Set this value to 0 to use automatic hole sizing based on Bolt_Size and Bolt_Clearance. Use this only if you want full manual control over the hole diameter. Hole_Spacing_X Horizontal spacing between the left and right bolt holes. Measured center-to-center. Hole_Spacing_Y Vertical spacing between the upper and lower bolt holes. Measured center-to-center. Back Nut Pocket Parameters Nut_Pockets Enables or disables hexagonal nut pockets in the back part. Options : true Adds hex nut pockets to the back part. false Creates normal through-holes only. Nut_Pocket_Clearance Adds extra clearance to the automatic nut pocket size. Increase this value if your nuts are too tight. Decrease this value if your nuts are too loose. Manual_Nut_Flat_To_Flat Manual override for the hex nut pocket size. Measured flat-to-flat. Set this value to 0 to use automatic sizing based on Bolt_Size and Nut_Pocket_Clearance. Manual_Nut_Depth Manual override for the hex nut pocket depth. Set this value to 0 to use automatic depth based on Bolt_Size. Increase this value if your nuts sit proud of the surface. Advanced Parameters Preview_Cutaway Creates a cutaway preview to inspect the internal groove and holes. Options: false Normal printable model. true Cutaway preview mode. Use false before exporting for printing. Facet_Count Controls the smoothness of circular features such as the bar groove, bolt holes and nut pockets. Options : 32, 48, 64, 96, 128 Recommended value : 96 Higher values create smoother curves but may generate larger files. Print Settings Recommended material: PETG ASA ABS PETG-CF Suggested settings: 4–6 walls/perimeters 40–60% infill 0.2 mm layer height Print both parts with the groove facing upward Use supports only if your slicer requires them for the nut pockets For motorcycle use, avoid PLA because heat and sunlight can deform the part. Hardware Recommended hardware: 4x M4 bolts 4x M4 nuts or nyloc nuts Optional washer under bolt heads Optional thin rubber strip or double-sided tape around the bar for extra grip Disclaimer This is a DIY 3D printed motorcycle accessory. Use at your own risk. Check fitment and strength before riding. Re-check bolt tightness after the first ride and inspect the part regularly for cracks or wear. Credits Created as a customizable navigation bar holder for motorcycle GPS / DMD-style mounting setups.

I made this design because all of the files online seem to have thousands of holes and I do not believe that is necessary. When you end up realising you need one of these, it is because you have wet filament. What does wet filament hate? Retractions... So I made this to use as few retractions as possible. I have used this design for two years and it works a treat and has fit 95% of spools. I place it in the centre of a spool then vacume seal them to keep the moisture out. Uses only 22 grams of filament! Ø Diameter = 56mm! No support required and orientated to print. I do not recomend printing it from PLA, PETG is best. This is the first STL I have ever uploaded! description: I am a big fan of star wars and the mandalorian.. Here are the things you'll need for the build: water bottle - my affiliate links on aliexpress.. https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_c4KHeTTF nylon ribbon straps 38mm - my affiliate links on aliexpress.. https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_c3ToSnqZ water sipper nozzle - my affiliate links on aliexpress.. https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_c3CnCPsZ https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_c2QrQKgN drill bit - to drill a hole in the water bottle cap compression springs - 7x12mm I printed mine using PLA for the metalic color but for durability you might want to print it using PETG or ABS.. For the straps i made 2 version.. 1 with the sipper tube holder.. the belt straps are 1meter long each.. it should fit a child.. you might want to extend it a bit around20-40cm for adults.. The whole backpack weight about 1kg without water in it.. It uses about 1.1kg filament.. I used PLA silk silver for the jetpack.. model_name: V40 Mini Frag Grenade | 100% New Design
description: Want a realistic life-size V40 Mini Grenade with a flying handle? This model is 100% brand new from the ground-up with stronger parts, easy screw-on assembly, and enhanced realism. What is the v40 Mini Grenade? The V40 Mini Grenade is an unusually compact fragmentation hand grenade developed in the Netherlands that is roughly the size of a golf ball. Weighing just 4.8 ounces, it allowed soldiers to carry the weapon in much greater quantities than standard fragmentation grenades. It gained historical fame for its utilization by U.S. special operations units during the Vietnam War. Spring options (for flying handle) Metal Spring (recommended) – if you have a metal spring, even a pen spring will usually work, then print the metal spring profile. It is designed to work with the Bambu Store's 0.5x7x12mm spring (linked lower on the page). If you use a pen spring, you can usually cut it in half and get two springs. Plastic Spring – if you don't have a metal spring, but still want the handle to fly off, then print the plastic spring profile. If the spring eventually wears out, just print a new one and pop it in. Don't leave the spring under tension when not using it as it will wear out much faster. Avoid Matte and Silk filament for the spring itself, Basic and Metal work better. No Flying Handle - if you don't want the handle to fly off and just want a grenade model, simply print either version and don't put in a spring. Bambu Filaments used Metal Iron Gray black Matte Yellow Polymaker Army Green ( Amazon link ) Bambu Matte Dark Green is the closest Bambu filament Metal Spring Version Assembly 1. Insert the peg into the grenade topper as you see below. 2. Then insert a metal spring int the same way. 3. Lastly, screw the topper onto the body of the grenade – it helps to do this upside down or sideways so the spring doesn't fall out. Plastic Spring Version Assembly 1. Insert the printed plastic spring into the grenade topper as you see below. Make sure the peg at the top of the spring is sticking out the top, rotate it until it pops out if not. 2. Lastly, screw the topper onto the grenade body – its easiest if you do this upside down or sideways.

model_name: US WWI Mk1 Grenade Prop | Realistic Flying Handle
description: Want a replica of a US WW1 grenade? This is the original "pineapple" grenade from WW1 that was the predecessor to the Mk2 grenade we all know from WW2. This grenade has a spoon handle that flies off when you pull the pin, just like the real thing would. Background: Introduced in 1917, the US Mk1 Grenade was the first fragmentation hand grenade developed by the United States for use in World War I. It was notoriously complicated to operate in the field, often requiring the user to manually ignite the fuse before throwing. Due to soldiers struggling to arm it under pressure, the Mk 1 grenade was quickly recalled and replaced by the improved Mk 2 grenade fuze in 1918 (which this model depicts). Spring options (for flying handle) Metal Spring (recommended) – if you have a metal spring, even a pen spring will usually work, then print the metal spring profile. It is designed to work with the Bambu Store's 0.5x7x12mm spring (linked lower on the page). If you use a pen spring, you can usually cut it in half and get two springs. Plastic Spring – if you don't have a metal spring, but still want the handle to fly off, then print the plastic spring profile. If the spring eventually wears out, just print a new one and pop it in. Don't leave the spring under tension when not using it as it will wear out much faster. Avoid Matte and Silk filament for the spring itself, Basic and Metal work better. No Flying Handle - if you don't want the handle to fly off and just want a grenade model, simply print either version and don't put in a spring. Bambu filaments used Basic Bronze Dark gray filaments are also period appropriate Silk+ Silver Assembly takes seconds Metal Spring Version 1. Insert the peg into the topper while its upside down. 2. Then insert the metal spring in the same way. 3. Then screw the grenade topper onto the body of the grenade. Doing so upside down is easiest. (this depicts a Mk2 grenade with the yellow stripe, but this Mk1 screws together in the same way) Plastic Spring Version 1. Insert the printed spring into the topper. Make sure the peg pops out, rotate it if it doesn't until it does. 2. Then simply screw the topper onto the grenade while upside down. (this depicts a Mk2 grenade with the yellow stripe, but this Mk1 screws together in the same way)

model_name: Frodo's Sting sword The Lord of the Rings
description: This is the elven sword Sting , Frodo's sword from The Lord of the Rings film trilogy. The sword is designed in a full-scale 1:1 size and has an overall length of 559 mm . Both the blade and the guard feature the original Elvish inscriptions. Maegnas aen estar nín – dagnir in yngyl im = "Sting is my name; I am the bane of spiders." The core of the sword consists of a 490 mm long M5 threaded rod , which mechanically connects all parts into one solid assembly without the use of glue. A safety M5 nut is embedded in the Blade_up part. A second safety M5 nut is inserted into the Grip part, which is designed for two-color filament printing using an AMS system. A standard M5 nut is embedded in the Pommel_A part. The assembly procedure and part layout can be seen in the exploded_view drawing located in the gallery of this model. For an impressive effect, the blade is printed using fluorescent PLA filament that glows blue in the dark after being exposed to light, just as Sting glowed blue in the movies when orcs were nearby. For the blade, I used Spectrum PLA Glow in the Dark Blue filament. To further enhance the display and allow the sword to be hung on a wall, I also designed a dedicated wall mount. The wall mount features beautiful golden ornaments and the inscription from the One Ring: The base of the wall mount is printed in two separate parts, which are fastened together using three M5×30 socket head screws and nuts . A separately printed ring featuring the inscription from the One Ring, along with the golden ornaments, is glued into the base. The sword itself is supported by two M6 L-hooks with a length of 60 mm . The assembly and all individual parts can be seen in the exploded_view image located in the gallery of this model. The threaded rod, screws, nuts, and L-hooks can be purchased at any Hobby market. The print profile is well-tuned and easy to print, making this project suitable for everyone. I hope this sword brings you joy, and enjoy its blue glow during the evening hours—it is truly an impressive sight, just like in the The Lord of the Rings movies. Happy printing!

For assembly: Like i said you are going to need some glue ( cyanoacrylate) , a 28mm x 500mm stick and some electric tape to wrap around the handle but that is opcional. For assembly you are going to need to follow this steps, the first is to glue this two parts to the main body. The we can join the two parts of the “blade” with help of the 3 pegs to align the pieces together. The we can add the blade to the main body. After that we can add the small chain blades. Now we can add the sick to the main body, as a recomendation just put glue in the end of the hole, since it a very thight fit the two part might be glue together before it inserted all the way thought. The we can add this part, it doesnt need a lot of glue, just a couple of drops. The the we can add the final part. And this should be all, now you can add the electric tape to the handle if you want.

description: "Why does that pirate have a ship's wheel attached to his belt?" "Arrr... it's driving me nuts!" Now you can finally tell one of the oldest pirate jokes... while being the punchline. Recommended Finish Print using a light brown filament . Apply a dark wood stain or dark brown varnish . Immediately wipe away most of the finish with a paper towel or soft cloth. CYBERPUNK OUTCAST FLINTLOCK MUSKET (DART BLASTER) "In a dark cyberpunk future, everything and everyone belongs to the corporations. Only the outcasts have never been owned. Corporations can lock your implants, freeze your bank account, and disable your smart rifle. But they cannot disable steel, black powder, and flint. Free people are forced to fight with the weapons of the past. A flintlock requires no firmware, no subscription, and answers to no one but its wielder." Inspired by this concept, the CYBERPUNK OUTCAST FLINTLOCK MUSKET is a fully 3D-printable elastic-powered toy dart blaster that combines the appearance of a cyberpunk firearm with the operation of a traditional flintlock musket. Rather than simply resembling a flintlock, it recreates the complete firing sequence with a functional cock, frizzen, powder pan, trigger, sear, and half-cock safety. The blaster is muzzle-loaded. Insert the dart into the barrel, seat it with the ramrod, cock the lock, aim, and fire. The entire loading and firing sequence is designed to resemble the operation of a historical flintlock while using a completely different internal propulsion system. The model features a compact folding design. Both the stock and the front assembly lock securely in their folded and deployed positions, allowing the blaster to be stored or transported in a much smaller package while remaining ready for use within seconds. Designed primarily for PETG printing, the model is almost entirely 3D printed. No metal springs, screws, glue, filament retaining pins, or other additional hardware are required. The only non-printed components are the elastic bands used for propulsion and mechanism operation. In addition to the original HEX 13 mm dart version, the project also includes a separate conversion profile for standard 0.5-inch foam darts. Features Fully functional flintlock-style firing mechanism Functional half-cock safety Muzzle-loaded operation with ramrod Folding stock with adjustable length of pull Folding front assembly for compact storage 99% PETG 3D printed No metal springs, screws, glue, or additional hardware. The only non-printed components are the elastic materials; the carriage guide rails also require lubrication during assembly. Includes a conversion profile for standard 0.5-inch foam darts Compatible with Bambu Lab P1 and A1 build volumes, as well as similar-sized printers (not compatible with the A1 Mini) Ammunition & Performance The primary configuration is designed to fire lightweight HEX 13 mm PETG or TPU printed darts weighing approximately 1–2 g. Typical performance: Muzzle velocity: approximately 40 ft/s (12 m/s) Effective range: approximately 3–10 m Shot dispersion at 3 m may reach approximately 0.25 m A separate conversion profile is included for users who prefer standard 0.5-inch foam darts. This project is intended primarily as an engineering and mechanical showcase that faithfully recreates the operation of a flintlock mechanism using almost entirely 3D-printed components. It prioritizes authenticity of operation and mechanical complexity over maximum performance. Before You Print Please review the listed performance characteristics before starting the project. If you expect significantly higher power, accuracy, or range, this model may not match your expectations.

description: This is my biggest project so far and it was a really good way to use for the first time my new H2S, i know that no everybody has the bigger size printers so i made a 84% scale version that is compatible with 256x256mm bed sizes , the materials and the assembly is the same as the bigger variant and to be honest the bigger one might be a bit excesive. Other thing that im not really sure if the bigger variant is going to be compatible with all the H2 series and A2L since they all have slightly diferent print sices and its all very confusing. For assembly: Same materials for big and small variants. You are going to need some glue ( cyanoacrylate). A tube or stick that is 32mm in diameter and 160~180cm long, The lenght of the tube might vary depending of how tall you are and how big you want the model to be , i recomend having some lenght to spare and them cutting down if its to long with the top part of the model already assembled,i used a PVC pipe for this that was petty rigid. Some el ectric tape to wrap around the handle but that is opcional . And some 6mm max in diameter flexible tube or cable but that is also opcional . We are going to start ading the top part to the end of the tube and glue it in. Then we are going to start joining the two central parts, they have holes for pegs but you dont have to use all of them. Afther that we can add it to the tube trie to add glue so it glued to the top part but also to the tube. Now we can add the claws that also use pegs and the screw, is better to do this step now becuase later we are not going to have the angle to insert the screwand might get tricky. After that we can add the two lower parts. Now we can add the blades and box thingy , the blades also use some pegs. Now that we have all the top part conected we can cut the tube if its a bit too long if not we can add the final bits, you can mix and mach the rings and the colums if you want to get diferent combinations and have for example more rings, the model its designed so the lower part of the tube sticks out a bit so the printed part not gets damage when resting the axe on the ground. And this is petty much it, now you can add the final details like electric tape to the handle and the small flexible tube or cable can be inserted and wrap around the handle using the two small holes.

description: Introducing my latest gun and by far my largest time-investment in a model - the FN Twin Mag Electric Water Gun! Check out all of my Fortnite Guns! 2026: Fortnite Twin Mag SMG Electric Water Gun 2026: Fortnite Wrecker Revolver 2025: Fortnite P90 Compact SMG 2025: Fortnite Mammoth Pistol 2025: Fortnite Holo Twister Rifle 2025: Fortnite Scoped Burst SMG 2025: Fortnite Havoc Shotgun 2024: Fortnite Gatekeeper Shotgun 2024: Fortnite Scar After many many hours spent modeling, testing, printing, remodeling, and retesting, I am proud to release the Twin Mag SMG Water Gun. This model uses two items from the Bambu Store - their Electric Spray Kit #02 and steel 5x35mm pins. 100% PETG Highly Recommended for this model! You can print stress free using my custom profiles organized by color. Every piece has been carefully individually sliced: Blue Parts: Top Rail Black Parts #1: Small Black Pieces Black Parts #2: Large Black Pieces Brown Parts: Handguard and Bracket Red Parts: Accent Pieces Blue Parts No Watergun/No Holes: This is the top rail without dowel holes if you want to glue things shut without the water gun kit. You could probably combine the two black plates if you try, but I wanted to split up the main long print and a bunch of small pieces just in case. This model will push the limits of what your 3D Printer can create. By the end, you will have a product that make you forget it started as a roll of filament. Every millimeter of this model has been considered and designed for 3D printing. You will need several items that are not 3D printable: Electric Water Spray Kit #02 (~$11 per kit from Bambu) (2) 5mm x 35mm Pins (~$1 for 5-pack from Bambu) Gel Super Glue Short Piece of Filament Scissors or Flush Wire Cutters Refer to the assembly PDF for easy instructions! The Glue Help piece is not part of the final product, it is to help align the brown handguard horizontally when upside-down on a table during assembly only. No glue ever touches the Glue Help piece. This model can also be assembled without the electric spray kit or dowels; you just need to use glue to connect the top rail to the body and print the blue rails with no holes. You can also print the normal blue rails, there will just be visible holes for the dowels. Please keep in mind you are not printing one model - you are printing 20 models and a couple may require a skip/reprint/re-do. Hopefully not though! I know there will be plenty of people that will click print on each plate and have zero problems with their perfectly dialed in printer and filament just like my other models! I put a lot of effort in these uploads to make printing as smooth as possible and easy to assemble. These easy to print and easy to assemble uploads are not necessarily easy or quick to design! I also continue to upload these for ‘free’ besides some Bambu points, passing on other popular release types. In return, I simply ask for your continued thumbs up, comments, pictures, and boosts!

description: ⚔️ Devil May Cry - "Manga Cut" Weapon Collection (NO AMS Required!) ⚔️ Benvenuti cacciatori di demoni! Questa collezione esclusiva unisce lo stile iconico della saga di Devil May Cry al design affilato e dinamico del Manga Cut . Cinque pezzi unici che fondono i volti dei protagonisti più amati della serie direttamente con le sagome e le impugnature delle armi più leggendarie del gioco. La particolarità di questo progetto? È ottimizzato per la stampa 3D FDM tradizionale ed è stampabile al 100% SENZA AMS! Otterrai uno spettacolare effetto bicolore in stile manga semplicemente impostando un cambio filamento (pausa al livello) nel tuo slicer. 👥 I Personaggi e i Modelli Inclusi Ogni pezzo è curato nei minimi dettagli per esaltare il contrasto tra bianco e nero, unendo i volti allo stile unico delle armi: Modello V (Stile Sparda): Il misterioso V con la sua trama di tatuaggi, integrato su una lama che richiama l'elsa della leggendaria spada Sparda e la sigla DMC . Modello Nero (Stile Red Queen/Blue Rose): Il giovane cacciatore Nero , fuso con i dettagli meccanici e industriali delle sue armi. Modello Dante (Stile Rebellion): L'iconico Dante con il suo sorriso beffardo, sormontato dall'indimenticabile elsa a forma di teschio alato della spada Rebellion . Modello Vergil (Stile Yamato): Il carismatico ed elegante Vergil , caratterizzato dall'impugnatura con la tipica nastratura (Tsuka) della sua letale katana Yamato . Modello Lady (Stile Gunslinger): La letale cacciatrice umana Lady , la cui impugnatura riprende le linee e le canne delle armi da fuoco. 🛠️ Molteplici Utilizzi Grazie al design versatile, non stai stampando dei semplici pezzi da esposizione. Ecco come puoi utilizzarli: Segnalibri "Manga Cut": Perfetti da infilare tra le pagine dei tuoi manga di DMC o dei tuoi libri preferiti. Portachiavi / Daily Carry: sfruttando il foro passante integrato sulla sommità dell'impugnatura, diventano dei fantastici portachiavi. Espositori da Scrivania: Stampali a grandezza naturale e posizionali su uno stand per decorare la tua postazione da gaming. Accessori per Cosplay: Utilizzali come gadget da fiera, scambiabili o come accenti decorativi. 🖨️ Guida alla Stampa (Ottimizzato NO AMS) Il modello è progettato a livelli per permettere a chiunque di ottenere la colorazione bicolore (Bianco/Nero) senza possedere sistemi multi-colore come l'AMS di Bambu Lab. Altezza dello strato (Layer Height): 0.12 mm (o 0.08 mm per un dettaglio ancora maggiore sui volti). Infill: 30% (Giroide consigliato). Materiale: PLA Nero e PLA Bianco. Come ottenere il bicolore SENZA AMS: Carica il file 3mf nel tuo slicer Inizia la stampa con il filamento NERO per la base e lo sfondo. Individua l'altezza in cui iniziano i dettagli in rilievo del volto (gli ultimi strati superiori). Inserisci una Pausa (M600 / Change Filament) a quel preciso layer. Quando la stampante si ferma, sostituisci il filamento nero con quello BIANCO e riprendi la stampa. description: This one is for Squidward who relentlessly pushed for me to make the model, and then was so grateful when I got started! I hope you enjoy it! I designed this mask a bit different from my others and I am happy with the outcome. Essentially, I incorporated the mesh eyes directly into the mask so they don't need to be added or printed separately. If you would prefer to print it all in one color (to save time and money), you should be able to easily paint the mesh portion black with some black acrylic paint. I also experimented with how the horns are printed and attached to the head to make them more integrated into the design and also to avoid needing supports on them. My first version was a bit to tight to fit on my head, but it fit on everyone else's in my home. In this version I tweaked the hole size for the head and flattened the bottom of the print a bit to improve printability and eliminate some of the supports. I believe this should fit any head pretty easily now. One under appreciated part of my work is figuring out how to get a model absolutely maximize the space of a p1s sized printer. In this case of this print, lots of adjustments were made to get it just right. For this hobby (designing and 3d printing models) I certainly go through phases. After filling up all the wall space in a room with Hollow Knight masks, I prioritized new areas. This was a nice break from my current phase which has been pond fountains, I think I have one more of those left in me before switching again. I am experimenting with designing a toy for kids during long car rides, I am excited about it and hope to share it soon!

description: Instant Ronin Double Tanto - Magnetic Knives Channel your inner samurai with the Instant Ronin - Double Tanto (Magnetic Edition) ! This isn't just a pair of sleek 3D-printable props—it's a fully mechanical, dual-sword ecosystem. By utilising a precise arrangement of 5-off 6mm x 3mm magnets per sword, these Tantos completely ditch traditional metal springs for solid-state physics. But here is the real kicker: One sword acts as the activator for the other. Mating the companion sword into the other triggers the magnetic mechanisms, releasing the internal locks and allowing for an instant, seamless locking - and the reverse when withdrawing. Absolutely zero glue required. Every magnet pocket has been engineered for a perfect, satisfying, push-fit. Print two, link them up, and prepare to lose hours of your life to the ultimate fidget experience. Features Triple-Action Magnetic Mechanics: Uses opposing and attracting magnetic fields to safely lock the blades closed, assist the deployment, and lock them open. 5-Magnet Precision Layout: Optimised specifically for standard, high-strength 6mm x 3mm cylinder magnets (5-off per sword). 100% Glue-Free Assembly: Meticulously tuned tolerances mean every magnet snaps tightly into place. Save the superglue for fixing the things you break with the Tanto. Zero Mechanical Springs: No metal springs to find, bend, fatigue, or lose tension over time—magnetism doesn't wear out! Dual-Tanto Blade Profile: A sleek, aggressive geometric aesthetic that looks as sharp as the mechanism feels. Maximum Fidget Factor Magnet Assembly Guide ⚠️ Crucial Tip: Because these are a push-fit, double-check your magnet orientation before you press them home. Getting a backward magnet out of a tight 3D-printed pocket is a special kind of pain you don't want to experience. Use a spare magnet as a reference tool! Follow this exact sequence to ensure the polarity works flawlessly, see my sectioned CAD image and assembly pictures to help with the below: The Master Slider Magnet [1]: Push a magnet into the bottom pocket of the Blade Slider . This can face any direction you like. Once it’s in, this magnet is the "Master" that dictates the rest of the build. The Extended Lock [2]: Press a magnet into the lower forward pocket of the Handle . This magnet must REPEL Magnet #1. (This repelling force is the secret sauce that lifts the slider up into the notch to lock the blade open!) The Retracted Lock [3]: Press a magnet into the bottom rear pocket of the Handle . This magnet must ATTRACT Magnet #1, snapping the blade securely closed so they doesn't slide apart when closed. The Kinetic "Spring" Caps [4]: Press one magnet into each of the two Circular Caps at the top hilt. Both of these magnets must REPEL each other, creating that crisp, snappy detent.

Once you are ready to connect the LED strip inside the blade to the Hilt, you must pay careful attention that the wire does not get caught in the threaded connection. Make sure all excess wire is tucked into the hilt and doesnt get crushed between any connection points. description: Clicker Cosplay Mask – The Last of Us Description & Origin Bring the fungal nightmare of the post-apocalypse to life with this highly detailed, screen-accurate Clicker Cosplay Mask . Inspired by the terrifying infected creatures from HBO’s The Last of Us and the iconic Naughty Dog video game franchise, this model captures the grotesque, organic geometry of the Cordyceps brain infection bursting from a human skull. The front of the mask features the signature split, cauliflower-like fungal blooms completely overtaking the upper face, layered over an underlying structure of exposed, decaying teeth and infected skin tissue. Designed with cosplay comfort in mind, the rear of the print is ergonomically contoured to comfortably sit against a human face, making it the ultimate centerpiece for your next convention, Halloween costume, or horror display. Functional Use & Wearability This is a wearable cosplay prop. The internal face cavity is smooth to allow for the addition of foam padding, and the side profiles include clean integration points for a leather or elastic head strap. Because a full Clicker transformation leaves the host blind, this mask is designed for authentic tracking. However, for safe convention wear, the open mouth cavity and deep recesses within the fungal plates can easily be lined with black mesh fabric from the inside—allowing you to see out and breathe comfortably while keeping the actor's face completely hidden from the outside. Sizing, Scaling, and Customization Because everyone's head shape is unique, proper sizing is crucial before you send this multi-hour print to the plate. To ensure a perfect 1:1 fit over your face and brow, I highly recommend using my custom Cosplay Calipers Sizing Tool to grab your exact physical dimensions. If you need to scale the mask up or down, or if you need to slice it to fit a smaller printer bed, check out my step-by-step video guide: How to Size, Scale, Cut, Pin, and Orient Armor in Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer . Print Settings & Material Recommendations To capture the hyper-organic, textured look of the Cordyceps fungus without glaring layer lines, I highly recommend printing this at a 0.12mm or 0.16mm layer height with organic tree supports. For the absolute best results, post-processing durability, and crisp detail retention, I exclusively recommend using SUNLU Filament . For a Paint-Ready Base: Use SUNLU PLA Plus (PLA+) Filament in Gray or White. It provides incredible impact resistance for convention wear and sands beautifully. For Rugged Outdoor/Con Wear: If you want extra temperature resistance against hot summer conventions, step up to SUNLU PETG Filament . Note: If you plan on modifying this model into a multi-color print using an AMS setup, be sure to watch my tutorial: How to Remesh and Color Prints Effectively in Bambu Studio . Assembly Instructions Depending on your printer build volume, you may choose to print this mask in sections. For a permanent, rock-solid bond that won't snap when under tension from the head strap, I highly recommend using ARKA KRAFTPROTZ UNIVERSAL Superglue . It fuses the printed seams flawlessly, ensuring your mask survives the chaos of a busy con floor. Creative Remix Ideas & Potential Uses Looking to use this geometry for something other than a costume? Here are a few creative ways you can remix or repurpose this file: Halloween Prop Decor: Scale it down, hollow it out, and turn it into a creepy, glowing LED wall sconce or a lampshade. Aquarium/Terrarium Decor: Print it using aquarium-safe materials to create an apocalyptic, overgrown centerpiece for a reptile enclosure or fish tank. Gaming Room Display: Mount the mask onto a plaque or a custom mannequin head stand to create a premium gaming room prop display. model_name: Mandalorian Grav Charge With Lightup Mod (Breach)
description: This is my version of the Grav Charge and holder from the show The Mandalorian. I designed it looking at pictures from the show to be as accurate as I could but also be a light up prop. To that end I designed it around these little magnet operated light up warning lights: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CMTJQRYX . The lights have a reed sensor in them that when the magnet is on the back they don't do anything but when you remove the magnet they light up. And the pattern is similar to the actual grav charge, close enough without needing expensive electronics or wiring anything. The back of the holder has some indents of 15mm magnets. Glue some magnets to the back and that will be strong enough to keep the light off. When you pull the grav charge off the holder the reed switch turns the unit on and the lights start to flash then after about 10 seconds go to the circular pattern. I added magnets on the bottom of the grav charges themselves also so you can still stick it to something like in the show but without affecting the light. Place it back on the holder and it turns back off. I went with these lights because they also turn themselves off after a couple minutes so they won't kill the battery if you leave them out. Print Details I printed the body and holder in Bambu ABS - Silver. The body has scarf seam turned on in its object settings which leaves less of a seam on the outside but does sometime affect the color slightly in that spot. If you are going to paint them leave scarf seam on, if you are going to leave them as is you may want to turn that off so the color is more consistent but the seam will be more noticeable. The cover is Bambu PETG Translucent Clear that I then used a red Sharpie oil based paint pen on because I couldn't find a good clear red filament. The combination ended up looking really good so that's what I would recommend or even possibly just a red marker. For printing the cover I have the speeds set to 20mm/s and a custom Bambu Transparent PETG setting that turns off cooling. It's the only way to get a mostly clear lens but you can of course use standard settings, the lens just might not be as clear and the LEDs won't be as distinguishable. Or you can buy a after market clear lens sized for about 28mm. I tried to optimize the print so no supports are required and the 2 x 4 magnets on the bottom should be press fit although I'd add a dab of glue behind them. The holder for the light also is press fit but you can also glue that in to be more secure. Since the lights turn themselves off the batteries should last for years so personally I glued them in.

description: Wax seals are fantastic at adding a level of class to letters, in sealing envelopes, or for attatching tags to brithday and christmas presents. Personally I plan on using them for creating immersive TTRPG props for my D&D game, so that I can hand them printed notices ( like these free ones ). Unfortunately, having a wax seal stamp design for every occasion, affiliation, or character can get expensive… so why not design and 3D print them? This is my first attempt at creating a design using one of my illustrations for Fantastical Geographic's debut . This design uses measurements taken from a proper wood and metal wax seal stamp so that the proportions of your seal will be similar, but also so that you can simply swap out the head and handle as you see fit as these are modeled separately. Or if you have a lot of metal stamp heads already you could simply want some fancy handles to accompany them instead of swapping things out. The head design and print profile have been optimized for 0.2mm nozzles as my experiments showed this yielded the best results. The head prints face up and uses ironing to create a smooth stamping surface for easy release, however, it is IMPORTANT to note that your ironing settings may need adjusting as this varies depending on printer, filament type, filament brand, and filament color! I've opted for PLA as it's the most accessible for many printers. If you are interested in reading my experiments I will be uploading a full write-up on my website of how I achieved the cleanest wax seal and release of the stamp (link to come). The TLDR is: 0.2 mm nozzle Head printed face up with ironing on 0.08mm layer height. 50% Infill 100% cooling Release Agent - A thin layer applied with an old brush Pre-cooling - Place the stamp in the freezer for 10-15 minutes (make sure to apply release agent first) Wait - Leave the stamp in the wax for about 1 minute before gently peeling off Additional Notes: I have included a 0.4mm nozzle profile, however, I was not able to get the ironing as smooth as the 0.2mm. It is there primarily for printing the handle, which doesn't require the high detail. These results were achieved with a tuned PLA filament profile for my machine. Your mileage may vary.

Fan made design Liberator carbine from Helldivers 2 Its pretty much all there with the exception of the pouch. Not quite good enough yet to get that part done properly. Fully assembled it is almost 24 inches long. Features: Working picatinny rail with attachments. Sights can be quick swapped with each other or a scope if you go with 8x2 magnets. 2 different threaded muzzle options 2 sight options 1 scope option 1 under barrel “flashlight / laser combo” (2 parts held together with magnets) 1 under barrel grip Most parts are separated out for easy color printing. I'll provide an AMS profile for some of the main parts & accessories if you want to go that route. (Grip, main sight, flashlight attachment & buttstock) Assembly: *Assembly is pretty straight forward but there are a lot of pieces. See images for the renders that show where everything goes. Yellow parts in the images are all the connecting / guide pins. You will want to assemble the 3 main sections first. Front, Mid, rear using the larger connecting pins. *Be sure to remember to put in the barrel insert into the mid section prior to any gluing (if you are doing that). Slide rear top (as I call it *on plate 4) into the mid section using connecting pin. Little holes on the top need to be towards the rear of the gun. Buttstock will hold the main rear and top rear sections together with connecting pins. Buttstock covers - There are small alignment holes for pins on the rear top. Add in pins to rear top (may be tight). Place covers onto pins. They only go on one way, see images for reference. Buttstock straps - These should fit snuggle into the openings on the covers. I'd start by inserting the strap on the right side of the gun fist, then push the left side up and in. Straps may need some filing. Mine fit in nice and required no gluing. Magazine connects to the bottom of the rear section using connecting pins. Magazine end cap and loop need to be glued on. Grips & trigger guard - There is an indent in the grip and the upper grip where the trigger guard sits. Due to the design you need to assemble these at the same time. Put 2 pins in the upper grip place it flat side down (in not already attached to mid section). Hold flat side of trigger guard in the grip with one hand while pushing the grip onto the pins guide the angle side of the trigger guard into the indent on the upper grip. Seems difficult when typing it out but its easy. Do test a test fit before gluing anything. I filled my trigger guard down a bit to get perfect fit before gluing. Top picatinny rail is held in my the screw pins. I added the screw pin down into the rails first, then aligned the pins above the holes & pushed them all the way into the main body of the gun. Mine were snug and required no glue. Bottom and side picatinny rails are all the same size & go in as descried above. Cover plates - These are glued on after everything is assembled. Under barrel plates hide some of the seam lines. Top 2 for the bolt area are aesthetic. If you want to use the top 2 be sure to glue them in before you glue in the bolt pin. Slide picatinny mount onto the rails. Add in magnets, make sure you get polarity right on the accessories for easy swapping. There are pins to secure the mount to the rails. Slide the pin in and place on the cap on the other side. You can glue them if you like, I chose not to since the mounts were snug on the rails for me. *Only 2 mounts are in the profile. Print more if you need them. Notes: Most larger flat pieces have 3 walls and 10% infill. I've also slowed the outer / inner wall speeds down to 60-80mm/s to try and negate seeing lines. Smaller items have brims and .16 layer heights to keep the details. Supports are enabled on individual objects where needed. Magazine & magazine end cap have a ton of triangles so you will see that warning. Simplify them at your own risk. Screw pins - I printed them facing up because I didn't want texture to show. Feel free to rotate them 180 if you have smooth plate. Magnets: if you use them for all accessories you will need 16 or 20 8x2 magnets. Be sure to get your polarity correct for easy swapping. If not using magnets you can print our 8mmx4mm plugs. I'm probably missing something but will update notes as needed. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HELLDIVERS SWAG o7

description: Model for Thor's Hammer from Thor: Love and Thunder. Hammer head splits into different pieces like in the movie and are held together using magnets. Print orientation in the .3mf matches the orientations I used when I printed it, but you might need to test printing in different orientations if the fit between two of the hammer head pieces isn't lining up well. The magnets used are 10x2mm and are superglued into the holes. You'll need around 210 magnets. Depending on the infill percentage and what you intend to do with the hammer (display vs carry around), you might need to adjust the strength of the magnets. I used 20% infill for a display build and the hammer stays together, but the pieces can come apart come apart when yanked. 20% infill gives the hammer a nice weight to it, but 10-15% might be better for balancing with the magnet strength. I printed all the pieces on an Ender v2 with a smooth plate. I used Cura to slice it so it just had straight supports. I used a generic coffee brown PLA for the handle and generic silk silver PLA for the hammer head pieces. The Bambu filaments selected below should match the generic ones I used. I tested some of the prints on my Bambu P2S and they printed fine. I used tree supports on the starting textured plate to test the prints. I would recommend a smooth plate since most of the head pieces print on one of the hammer faces so smooth will look better. I transferred all the settings I used in Cura into the .3mf, but did slow down the print settings for the P2S with silk. Leather strap was found at craft store and cut to fit the hole in the hammer hilt.

model_name: Halo Energy Sword - life-sized and light up!
tags: halo|halo energy sword|elite|elite energy sword|arbiter|master chief|halo cosplay|energy sword
description: Ever wanted a life-sized Halo energy sword? Me too! I was surprised that I couldn't find a print for this, so I made one myself. Coming in at just over a metre long, this is a faithful replica of the iconic Halo weapon. It looks great printed in either translucent blue or clear PETG, with light channels down the middle of each blade and compartments on both blades for electronics (batteries - sized for 18650 cells, control boards etc). Everything is designed to key together to allow for easy printing and assembly. This print takes up 5 full plates on my P2S and took a few days to print, with around 1.5kg of blade material. Each plate is as packed as it can reasonably be. It can of course be printed on smaller printers like the A1 and can be scaled down appropriately to suit this. Key assembly steps: Print and attach hilt sections together. I printed these in a grey PLA+, then stuck them together with CA glue. The fit is tight and may need a bit of force. There is a channel down the inside of the hilt to route wires for lights or switches. Optional - sand, prime, paint hilt. I painted with a base of black acrylic and then steel / silver acrylic on top, then sanded paint down in places to give a weathered look. Print blade base parts and attach to hilt. The fit between the hilt and blade base is a bit looser than any of the other joins, as this gives a bit more tolerance for any accumulated accuracy errors throughout the print. The intended attachment method is to use an M8 nut / insert / T-nuts heat-set into the handle, and an M8*40mm bolt through the blade into this nut / insert. You could however just use a suitable epoxy to bond the two parts well. Either way, this should be a secure connection once properly glued / torqued down. Attach blade pieces to blade base, finishing up with the optional reinforcing bar (secured using M3 heat inserts and M3*10mm bolts into the blade sections). You could use a suitable glue to attach these together, though the keyed fit is pretty tight. Optional finishing steps. I used a UV-set clear resin to fill the join lines between sections and make things look a bit more continuous. This certainly isn't a magic fix as it is obviously still printed in pieces, but it does help! You can then install electronics if desired. I found LED rope or LED-strips worked well (ideally with high density RGB COBs. If they're too far apart you get a less diffuse effect). The original energy sword sculpt was done by the extremely talented Sigil0fSaturn on the Sketchfab site, linked here ( Energy Sword - Halo Prop - Download Free 3D model by Sigil0fSaturn (@Sigil0fSaturn) [8dda2fc] )

description: Disclosure Day Device - Movie Accurate Replica This is the most geometrically accurate 3D printable replica of the Disclosure Day Device available online. This specific combination creates the unique, shifting facets that give the device its iconic look—a detail that other creators completely miss because they don't take the time to figure out how the original designers actually constructed the figure. Screen-Accurate Details The Glyphs: The symbols engraved on the upper facet were fully recreated from scratch using high-resolution reference images, ensuring every line, dot, and proportion is completely true to the screen. Print-Optimized: Designed with structural durability in mind, guaranteeing a flawless print that captures the sharp edges and dramatic transitions of the prop. If you are looking for a true, movie-accurate replica born from genuine engineering and deep analysis rather than a rushed approximation, this is the model for you.

This is a 1:2 scale AK-47 (AKM variant) display model Introduced in 1959, the AKM was a modernized evolution of the original AK-47 and became one of the most widely produced rifle designs in history. Its stamped receiver reduced weight, simplified manufacturing, and improved production efficiency while retaining the rugged reliability for which the platform is known. description: A fully 3d printed Single-shot Cap-powered BB pistol! Fully 3d printed springs. Has 10 bodies to print, can fit on an a1 build plate at minimum. Semi-auto hammer and trigger system though it is single shot. hammer action works well. The larger spring is the hammer spring, simply slot into the holes in the hammer and the main body. The smaller spring is the Trigger spring, do the same. The two main halves of the pistol snap together, may need a spot of glue on the joints. To use, get a standard 8-shot ring cap, then cut off an individual cap using a utility knife, being careful with fingers. Break the barrel (shown in images) by pressing the barrel release latch (shown in images as well) on the left hand side of the pistol body, then lift the barrel, tilting it upwards from the end near the hammer. To lock the barrel, manually push the barrel release latch now protruding from the right hand side back into its original position. this can be fiddly ads the hole is quite precise. Load the singular cap into the recess at the end of the barrel, making sure it sits snug. This is a muzzle loader-so from the muzzle, cut out a small square of tissue. Place it on the muzzle and get a standard 6mm BB. place the BB on top of the tissue wad and using a blunt skewer, ram the BB and the wad into the barrel until you feel it stop (do not ram too hard as the cap holder will snap). Then you are ready to fire! *DISCLAIMER* I am not at fault for misuse of this toy causing damage to living beings and surroundings. tags: spear|bronze age spear|spear of king fuchai of wu|spearhead
description: This spearhead model is inspired by the famous Spear of King Fuchai of Wu (吴王夫差矛) . If you're interested in the history behind the original artifact, you can read about it on Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spear_of_Fuchai The spearhead is modeled at approximately the same size as the original artifact and is just over 300 mm long. Since it exceeds the printable height of many printers, it is split into two pieces that are joined with the included connector. I recommend printing one spearhead piece per build plate, even though it may be tempting to place both pieces on the same plate. There are two reasons for this: Print stability – The spearhead is very thin and tall. When both pieces are printed side by side, the nozzle may strike one of them while traveling between parts, causing a print failure. (I learned this the hard way.) If you decide to print both at once, place them end-to-end (like - -) rather than side-by-side (like =) to reduce the chance of collisions. Surface finish – I found that the surface texture is noticeably smoother when only a single part is printed on the build plate. Printing multiple parts at once produced a slightly different finish. This may depend on your filament or printer, but for the best-looking result, I recommend printing the pieces individually. The spearhead shown in the photos was printed using ERYONE Gold Silk PLA at a 0.16 mm layer height. The gold color is intentional —newly cast bronze weapons had a golden appearance.The greenish appearance of the surviving artifact is due to the patina formed during more than two thousand years of corrosion. The pole is designed as 25 mm in diameter and is divided into 150 mm (approximately 6 in) sections. Each section uses M20 × 1.5 threads, allowing you to print as many sections as needed and screw them together to create a spear of your desired length. I printed the pole sections with Fuzzy Skin enabled to create a nice visual contrast with the smooth, polished spearhead. The pommel completes the assembly. To avoid support, a threaded connector was included and the pommel can be threaded onto the end of the pole using that connector. Printing Notes Supports is required for the lower spearhead section only. The upper spearhead section, pole sections, connector, and pommel print without supports. For maximum strength, glue the two spearhead halves together after inserting the connector. Note: The cover image was created using AI.

description: 一、模型设计概述 本模型基于《我的世界》游戏内二维像素剑造型进行3D重构。区别于仅做平面拉伸的同类模型，该设计利用高低落差的阶梯式结构，塑造出三维立体的体素浮雕质感。在无需多色打印的条件下，依然可通过光影呈现丰富的层次感。 剑柄部分针对握持的人体工学进行了重新设计。参考游戏内官方3D化逻辑，将原二维扁平剑柄进行90度旋转并合并重组，消除冗余块面，使握把具备真实的立体体积和圆润的握持手感。剑柄底部设计有贯穿的镂空结构，可穿入挂绳，用于悬挂或作为背包挂饰。 二、打印与组装参数 文件拆分 ：剑身与剑柄已完成分体处理，默认分布在1-2两盘，可分开独立打印。 公差与组装 ：经多重精度测试，公差控制精准。装配预期为无胶水拼装（摩擦力卡合结构），无需额外使用粘合剂。 打印设置测试 ：内部已进行多组打印参数实测，以保障最佳打印质量。 三、耗材适配与操作提示 多色与单色适配 ：模型未预设固定配色，任何基础色彩耗材均可直接打印。纯色打印即可凸显像素浮雕质感；若配备多色打印系统（如AMS），或具备后期手涂上色能力，由于全模型皆为方块构造，表面涂装和分色操作非常简便，可根据游戏原作色彩自行调配。 耗材翘边预警 ：模型默认未在剑身部分添加辅助裙边（Brim）。若使用PETG或ABS等收缩率较高的材料，打印时 必须 在切片软件中手动开启裙边功能，否则极易发生翘边；若使用PLA材料，则无需额外处理。 打印尺寸限制 ：针对A1 mini 等较小打印平台的机器，无法直接打印原比例尺寸模型，可通过切片软件等比缩小后输出缩小版本。 四、文件开源与兼容性说明 本模型同步提供 STEP 格式开源文件，可在网页端下载。用户可将其导入任意CAD软件中进行结构修改，用于创作个人二次开发版本。 注意 ：此STEP文件暂无法在 Bambu Studio 切片软件中直接打开。如需在常见切片软件中预览和打印，请直接下载模型提供的 STL 格式文件。

description: The tip of your index finger still tingles from the electric shock of the loose neural interface ⚡, Kael, a back-alley ripperdoc in Neo-Arcology’s lower level, just set this unprimed prototype dagger he pulled from a sunken smuggling craft on his workbench. He only took this 500-credit odd job to find a missing cargo crate dropped into the Neo-Pacific trench, spent three days modding his cheap dive cybernetics to slip past the sealed force field around the wreck, and found nothing in that reinforced cabin but this dagger locked to the hull with cryo-seal. The moment his skin touched the hilt carved into a lion’s head, a deep, bone-shaking roar exploded in his cochlear implant, carrying the rumble of the void between stars that no human was supposed to hear 🌀. The secondhand shoulder cyber he installed last week suddenly burned, the stray void micro-organisms that seeped in with the seawater were crawling up his neural line toward his brain, those alien parasites that turn humans into mindless abominations in a week, the kind the corporate enforcers kill on sight. Then the spiral carvings on the blade started glowing a faint pale blue 🔮, the parasites veered off his neural tract like they were pulled by an invisible magnet, crawling right into the blade’s grooves and locking themselves there. The neon sign outside his shop flickered three times before it died, the hum of corporate enforcer hovercars rumbles past the alley, getting closer by the second. Kael shoves the dagger into the sheath strapped to his boot, touches the back of his neck where the implant was already starting to fester, and finds smooth cool skin instead of oozing rot. He squints at the faint ancient galactic script carved along the edge of the blade, and realizes this wasn’t a lost cargo—it was a lure, and he just took the bait that the last void hunter left behind. The roar in his ears softened into a quiet hum, and somewhere above the clouds, a rift in reality just started to crack open 🔪

Wind blowing scrap metal across K's visor, she looks at the pink-blue gradient halo of the distant planet's atmosphere, which matches the blade perfectly. She taps the hollow handle with her fingertip, only she knows that the residual consciousness chip of the dead hacker is hidden in the blade's cavity 🔋. This dagger is inspired by the legendary Sword of Goujian, the famous bronze sword of the King of Yue. I tried to preserve the distinctive flat ring pommel and the overall shape of the original hilt. However, I added larger fillets around the edges of the hilt so it can be printed without supports. I also found the original round handle to be too small for a comfortable grip, as the historical sword was intended to be wrapped with silk or leather. To improve ergonomics, I increased the handle size and changed its cross-section from round to elliptical, making it much more comfortable to hold while maintaining the spirit of the original design. The blade and handle are designed as two separate parts, allowing you to print them in different colors. For my print, I chose a gold filament to represent newly cast bronze. Although ancient bronze artifacts are often seen with a green patina today, that color is the result of corrosion over centuries—freshly cast bronze has a beautiful golden appearance. Assembly is straightforward: Carefully align the blade with the slot in the handle. Press the blade fully into place. The fit is intentionally tight to provide a secure connection. If you would like a permanent assembly, it is recommended to apply a small amount of super glue before inserting the blade. Once assembled, the thin blade fits very tightly, and removing it later may be difficult without damaging or breaking the blade, especially for the filament I used. description: The cold stale wind of the abandoned spaceport vent brushes against the back of Linna’s cybernetic neck, the jagged bone handle of the dagger bites perfectly into his modified palm, the familiar tingle of the crystal veins crawling up his wrist hums in time with the blade’s pulse 🤚. Three standard days ago, he took a shady merc job to retrieve an “anomaly” from a derelict human research outpost that had been abandoned for three hundred years, drifting on the edge of the asteroid belt 🌑. He found the blade tucked into the hollow cavity of a fossilized alien spine, its gradient pink-blue color and twisted bone texture didn’t match any geological record of the asteroid, marking it as a visitor from the deeper void. He only thought it was a valuable oddity to sell to the rich collectors in the cyber city, enough money to replace his failing artificial heart, he never thought it would take root in him ✨. He killed three inquisitors at the spaceport port of entry yesterday, when the last one’s blood sprayed across the blade, it all soaked into the carved patterns instead of staining the surface, the cold blue base of the blade blushed soft pink, just like the veins that are now crawling up his own arm 🩸. His synthetic lung is leaking oxygen after taking a stray bullet, the inquisitors’ footsteps are getting louder, the crunch of their boots on metal debris echoing through the vent. The whisper in his skull is getting clearer now, he doesn’t recognize the language, but he understands every word: take me back to the star core, take me home. Linna tightens his grip on the clawed blade, grinning around the taste of blood in his mouth, he realizes now that he was never the one holding the dagger—he’s just a new bone for the void star skeleton, growing to carry it home 🗡️. The flashlight beam cuts into the end of the vent, and Linna presses the tip of the blade to the back of his own neck, waiting.🔦

model_name: Caine from The Amazing Digital Circus
description: Cosplay Caine the Ring Master from The Amazing Digital Circus (TADC) Printed in white PETG, with 2 walls, 2% lightning infill (basically hollow) to make it was light as possible. These files are for printing the teeth/jaws. They're split into 3 segments for each jaw; front, left, and right. And should fit on an Ender 3, or any 220 printbed or larger. The segments dovetail together, but I still recommend glue or plastic welding for the strongest attachment possible. It is designed to clip onto the brim of a baseball cap, and the aliceband isn't meant to sit it normally would on your head, but add better stability to the brim, because the center of gravity is farther forward than you would expect. I ultimately glued some nickels to the back to bring the center of gravity farther back for balance. However, if I were to do it again, I would add strategic infill to the farthest back section (in the slicer) for counterweight and to reinforce the clip connector holes, which I broke. I also recommend adding springs to the back of the jaws to space them apart, and keep them from hitting each other. I played around with various 3D printed springs, which I included. However, I ultimately broke the connectors while switching them, and just 3D printed a straight, flat rectangle piece that I plastic welded to them. Really, anything will work, as long as you attach something to them to keep them apart. I also recommend connecting the front of the jaws using fishing line. I included some small holes where fishing line may be attached, however they came out too small in my print, perhaps do to my printer settings in the slicer. I ultimately tied the fishing line around the seems where the segments meet, where it would be completely hidden. I would also recommend using a touch of hot glue on the knots, to absolutely make sure they stay. And of course you can adjust the length to choose how open the mouth hangs open, just make sure both lines are the same length. I choose to space them so that the bottom jaw doesn't rest on my shoulders, so it all turns with my head, but it also closes if I shrug my shoulders. For my cosplay, I used contact cement to glue a large stripe of red craft foam around the "gums" for texture and to hide the seams, and then I sealed it with Mod Podge for toughness and luster. A hair dryer can also be used to help shrink wrap the foam to the print, but be careful not to let the plastic get too hot or it could warp. I just painted the inside gums red, since they're less visible, and I was very concerned about weight since I was going to be wear it for long hours. Absolutely NO A.I. was used to make these models nor the images. Do not reupload my files somewhere else. I will upload them where I want. DO NOT SELL THEM! I made these models from scratch, and choose to upload them for free for the cosplay community for free. Remixes are welcome, especially as this can be improved, but please give attribution, and posted under the same CC BY-NC-SA license terms. description: UPDATE: I made a version that supports an aluminum rod! This version uses a ½" aluminum rod that is 56" long. I recommend taking a 6ft aluminum rod and cutting it down. The parts are all assembled the same way as the original with the same guide, but I recommend using epoxy instead of glue. I wanted the aluminum rod to go all the way into the spearhead, but a ½" rod is too thick to fit, and any rod thinner than ½" is not rigid enough. If anyone has a good idea for reinforcing the spearhead, let me know! Just created a Makerworld account! (Idk why I didn't do it earlier) This is just the same model that I originally posted on Printables. NOTE: The model is around 76 in (1.93 meters) long, but the real in-game spear is around 85 in (2.2 meters). I scaled it that way because I wanted a spear that would fit me, and I'm just not as tall as Kratos. Every single part of this spear, except the spearhead, is threaded, so you don't need an aluminum rod. For the spearhead, I just used PVA glue, and it worked pretty well, but you can use 3D gloop if you want a stronger bond. I'm still working on painting my spear. All of the parts need support, and I'd recommend a brim as well, just to be safe. I might consider making a version of this spear with an aluminum rod on the inside if anyone wants a stronger spear, so let me know in the comments if you would like that :) When printing, each piece is labeled with a number.
